en:
In 1719 miners draining a long-flooded shaft at Falun found a body in the water, with neither clothes, hands nor face showing decay. Margaret Olsdotter recognised it as her fiancé Mats Israelsson, who had vanished forty-two years before. Raised into the air, the corpse dried as hard as wood; Linnaeus, who saw it, noted that it was not petrified, only coated with vitriol.

Falun grew up around the Great Copper Mountain, Stora Kopparberg, where local farmers were gathering ore around the year 1000, by some estimates earlier. In 1347 King Magnus Eriksson drafted a charter for the mine. Free miners held shares in proportion to the smelters they owned, an arrangement seen as a forerunner of the joint-stock company; the Stora company, descended from it, is often called the oldest still operating. The rock was worked by fire-setting: fires lit at the end of the day burned through the night, and next morning the cooled, cracked rock was broken loose with wedges and sledgehammers, about a metre of advance a month. The ore was then roasted in open hearths, and the thick, poisonous smoke marked Falun for centuries. In the seventeenth century this was Sweden's largest workplace, with about a thousand workers, and at its peak around 1650 it produced over three thousand tonnes of copper in a year, at times two thirds of the world's copper. The Privy Council called it the kingdom's treasury and stronghold, and its output helped fund Sweden's wars in its great-power era. The red sludge from the tailings, heated and mixed with linseed oil and rye flour, became Falu red, the paint that let wooden houses imitate the brick facades of the upper classes.

Nearly five hundred years of mining had riddled the mountain with shafts. On Midsummer 1687 a large part of the mine collapsed, leaving the great hollow called Stora stöten, 95 metres deep and 1.6 kilometres around. It was a holiday, and no one was working underground. Linnaeus called the mine one of the great wonders of Sweden but as horrible as hell itself.
zh:
1719年，人们抽干法伦一条淹了多年的竖井，在水里发现一具尸体，衣服、双手和面孔都没有腐烂的迹象。玛格丽特·奥尔斯多特认出他就是自己的未婚夫马茨·伊斯拉埃尔松，他四十二年前就失踪了。尸体被抬出水面后慢慢干硬得像木头；亲眼见过的林奈指出，它并没有变成石头，只是裹满了硫酸盐。

法伦大铜矿所在的大铜山（Stora Kopparberg）周围，长出了法伦城。约1000年前后，据估计或许更早，当地农民就在山上采矿石。1347年，马格努斯·埃里克松国王为矿山起草了特许状：自由矿工按各人拥有的冶炼炉分得股份，这种安排被看作股份公司的前身，由它传下来的斯道拉公司常被称为现存最古老的股份公司。岩石靠火烧法开采：每天收工时点火，整夜燃烧，次日早晨岩石冷却开裂，再用楔子和大锤撬下，一个月大约掘进一米。矿石随后在露天炉灶里焙烧，浓重有毒的烟雾成了法伦几个世纪的标志。17世纪，这里是瑞典最大的工场，约有一千名工人；1650年前后极盛，一年产铜逾三千吨，一度占到全世界铜产量的三分之二。瑞典枢密院称它为王国的钱库和堡垒，瑞典大国时代的战争多靠它出产的铜支撑。矿渣堆里的红色矿泥加热后与亚麻籽油和黑麦粉调和，就成了「法伦红」颜料，让木头房子刷成上层人家砖墙立面的模样。

近五百年的开采把整座山掏得千疮百孔。1687年仲夏节，矿山大部分塌陷，留下深95米、周长1.6公里的大坑，叫「大塌陷坑」；那天是节日，井下没有人干活。林奈说，这座矿是瑞典的大奇观之一，却「和地狱本身一样可怕」。

en:
Kronborg stands on a sandspit at the narrowest neck of the Sound, where four kilometres of water separate Zealand from Scania and every Baltic ship had to pass. Eric of Pomerania's fortress Krogen, built in the 1420s, controlled the Baltic entrance together with the castle at Helsingborg on the Scanian shore and backed the collection of the Sound Dues. The toll was levied on the captain's own statement of his cargo's value, and the king kept the right to buy the cargo at that price, which stopped captains from stating too little.

After the Northern Seven Years' War Frederick II rebuilt Krogen into the showpiece of his reign. Flemish architects directed the work, and the walls were faced with sandstone from Scania and roofed in copper. In 1577 the fortress took the name Kronborg. The Ballroom, 62 metres long, was the largest hall in northern Europe when it was finished in 1582. For it Dutch weavers summoned to Helsingør made forty-three tapestries of the Danish kings, only fifteen of which survive. In 1590 James VI of Scotland, newly married to Anne of Denmark, lodged here and tipped the household two thousand gold dalers. On the night of 24 September 1629 two workmen's carelessness burned most of the castle; only the chapel escaped, saved by the strength of its vaults, and the interiors came back baroque and never as lavish. When Carl Gustaf Wrangel's Swedes took the castle in 1658 they carried off the courtyard fountain, Frederick II's canopy, woven with gold and silver thread, and a number of the Ballroom's ceiling paintings.

Danish legend says that Holger Danske, a warrior in Charlemagne's army, sleeps in the cellars beneath the castle and will wake to save Denmark if the country is ever in danger; a statue of him lies in the casemates. After 1658 Kronborg was increasingly a fortress rather than a royal seat. A crownwork was added in the 1680s, chained convicts worked on the fortifications from 1739, and Queen Caroline Matilda, sister of George III, was held here from January to April 1772 after Struensee's fall.
zh:
克隆堡建在厄勒海峡最窄处的沙嘴上，西兰与斯科讷之间四公里宽的水面，是波罗的海每艘船的必经之门。波美拉尼亚的埃里克在15世纪20年代修起克罗根要塞，它与对岸斯科讷的赫尔辛堡城堡一同控制着波罗的海的入口，支撑海峡税的征收。关税按船长自报的货物价值计征，国王保留按报价买下这批货的权利，船长也就不敢少报。

北方七年战争后，腓特烈二世把克罗根改建成他统治年代最得意的工程。主持工程的是佛兰德建筑师。墙身贴上从斯科讷运来的砂岩，屋顶覆以铜皮，1577年要塞改名克隆堡，意为「王冠堡」。舞厅长62米，1582年落成时是北欧最大的厅堂。应召来到赫尔辛格的荷兰织工为它织成四十三幅历代丹麦国王挂毯，存世的只有十五幅。1590年，刚与丹麦的安妮成婚的苏格兰国王詹姆斯六世驻跸堡中，临走给堡内仆从打赏了两千达勒金币。1629年9月24日夜，两名工匠一时不慎，城堡大半焚于大火，只有礼拜堂靠着坚固的拱顶幸免；内部重修成巴洛克样式，再没恢复旧日的奢华。1658年，卡尔·古斯塔夫·弗兰格尔的瑞典军攻陷城堡，掠走庭院喷泉、腓特烈二世那顶以金线银线织成的华盖，还有舞厅的多幅天顶画。

丹麦传说说，查理曼军中的勇士霍尔格（Holger Danske）就沉睡在城堡下的地窖里，国家一旦有难，他便会醒来相救；堡下的炮台洞室里立着他的雕像。1658年之后，克隆堡越来越像要塞而不再是王宫：17世纪80年代增建了「王冠工事」，1739年起戴镣铐的苦役在工事上服刑，英王乔治三世的妹妹、王后卡罗琳·玛蒂尔达则在1772年施特林泽倒台后，于1月至4月间被关押在此。

en:
Visby walled itself in limestone: a ring originally about 3.6 kilometres long with 29 large towers and 22 small ones that ride on the wall like saddles. The oldest stone is the Kruttornet at the old harbour, a freestanding tower of the 1100s and the oldest surviving secular building in the Nordic countries. It had no door, only a small hatch some ten metres up the wall, reached by a ladder that was pulled up behind the defenders. A sea wall ran from it to a matching tower about 1250. The land wall followed in the 1270s and 1280s, five or six metres high with a walkway for archers behind openings and arrowslits; it was probably tied to the quarrel between the town and the Gotland assembly that became a civil war in 1288. In medieval Sweden only Visby, Stockholm and Kalmar had city walls. In the 1350s the wall was raised three or four metres and more than twenty saddle towers were added.

At the seaward Maiden Tower they told of Nils the goldsmith's daughter, walled up alive for betraying Visby to Valdemar Atterdag in 1361, though the tower was not built until the 1400s. When Valdemar took the town he had a stretch of wall torn down as a token of submission, and the breach was closed again in 1363. In 1525 troops from Lubeck stormed Visby, and fires set by the defenders destroyed three churches. In 1533-34 the Danish governor Henrik Nielsen Rosenkrantz tore down St John's and St Peter's, or at least their towers, to strengthen his castle, Visborg, and St Mary's remained the town's last functional church. In the sixteenth century caponiers, half-round works for flanking fire, were added at the east wall. By then the wall served mainly as a toll barrier, and when the inland tolls were abolished in 1810 it was already a known landmark.
zh:
维斯比城用石灰岩把自己围了起来：城墙原长约三千六百米，原有29座大塔，另有22座骑在墙上、形如马鞍的小塔。最古老的石头是旧港口边的火药塔，建于12世纪，是一座独立的塔，也是北欧现存最古老的世俗建筑。塔上没有门，只在离地约十米处开了一个小口，要靠梯子上下，守军进去后把梯子抽走。约1250年，一道海墙从它延伸到另一座同样的塔。陆地城墙筑于13世纪70至80年代，高五六米，墙上有供射手行走的通道，墙上隔一段开口，口间是窄窄的箭缝；筑墙很可能与城市同哥得兰乡庭的冲突有关，这场冲突在1288年演成内战。整个中世纪的瑞典，只有维斯比、斯德哥尔摩和卡尔马三座城市拥有城墙。14世纪50年代，城墙加高了三四米，并增设二十多座骑墙塔。

朝海的少女塔流传着一个故事：金匠尼尔斯的女儿在1361年把维斯比出卖给瓦尔德马·阿特达格，被活活砌进墙里，不过这座塔到15世纪才建成。瓦尔德马占领全城时，下令拆去一段城墙作为降服的象征，这个缺口1363年被补好。1525年，吕贝克军队攻入维斯比，守军放的火烧毁了三座教堂。1533至1534年，丹麦总督亨里克·尼尔森·罗森克兰茨为加强维斯堡城堡的防御，拆毁圣约翰和圣彼得两座教堂，至少拆掉了两座塔楼，圣马利亚成了城里最后仍在使用的教堂。16世纪，东段城墙增建了供侧射的半圆形暗堡。到那时城墙主要靠充当关卡存留下来，1810年国内关税废除时，它已是一处人所共知的古迹。

en:
In 1745 thirty cats were fetched from Kazan to hunt mice in the unfinished Winter Palace, where the cats descended from one Peter the Great had brought from Holland already lived. The palace on the Neva embankment is the last of several winter residences built on the river. Peter had a small wooden winter house and the stone Wedding Chambers, Governor Menshikov's gift for his marriage to Catherine; Georg Mattarnovi then built a larger palace beside the Winter Canal, where Peter died. Empress Anna Ioannovna found the old house too small and had Bartolomeo Rastrelli rebuild it, work that began in the spring of 1732 and gave her some seventy state halls, more than a hundred bedrooms, a theatre and a chapel. Elizabeth was no fonder of it. On 1 January 1752 she decided to enlarge it, and Rastrelli ended by designing a new palace, 215 metres long and thirty high, with about 1,500 rooms, 1,945 windows and 117 staircases. Elizabeth died before it was finished, Peter III took delivery of it on 6 April 1762 and was overthrown that summer, and Catherine II completed the building and dismissed Rastrelli.

Catherine filled the palace with pictures. In 1764 the Berlin merchant Gotzkowsky's debt to Prince Dolgorukov was settled with some two hundred paintings, mostly Dutch and Flemish, which hung in the empress's private apartments. She gave those rooms the French name Hermitage, a place of solitude, and a separate building for the pictures went up east of the palace a few years later. She also placed the rooms of her favourite Grigory Orlov directly below her own, and had a pavilion built for him, joined to her apartments by a gallery on an arch. Before the great fire some two thousand people lived in the palace, and anyone properly dressed could walk in, even to see the Diamond Room, part of the empress's private quarters. Envoys on audience days climbed the Jordan Staircase, then called the Ambassadors' Staircase, and passed through the enfilade of state rooms facing the Neva to the throne hall. Giacomo Quarenghi's new Great Throne Hall opened in 1795.
zh:
1745年，为捕捉尚未竣工的冬宫里的老鼠，人们从喀山运来三十只猫；宫里原有的猫，是彼得大帝从荷兰带回的一只猫的后代。涅瓦河畔的这座宫殿，是河边接连修建的几座冬季宅邸中的最后一座。彼得先有一座小小的木制冬屋和石造婚礼宫，后者是总督缅什科夫送给他和叶卡捷琳娜的成婚礼物；后来格奥尔格·马塔尔诺维在冬宫运河边建起更大的宫殿，彼得就在这里去世。安娜·伊凡诺夫娜女皇嫌旧宫太小，命巴托洛梅奥·拉斯特雷利改建，1732年春动工，给她安排了约七十座典礼大厅、一百多间卧室，还有剧院和礼拜堂。伊丽莎白同样看不上它。1752年1月1日她决定扩建，拉斯特雷利最后设计出一座新宫：立面长215米、高30米，约有1500个房间、近两千扇窗和117座楼梯。伊丽莎白没能等到竣工；彼得三世1762年4月6日接收宫殿，当年夏天就被推翻，最后由叶卡捷琳娜二世把工程收尾，并辞退了拉斯特雷利。

叶卡捷琳娜把宫殿变成了藏画之所。1764年，柏林商人戈茨科夫斯基欠多尔戈鲁科夫公爵的债，以二百多幅画抵偿，大半是荷兰和佛兰德斯画派，这些画挂在女皇的私室里。她给这几个房间起了个法文名字「艾尔米塔什」，意为退隐独居之处；几年后，宫殿东面另建了一座专放藏画的楼。她还把宠臣格里戈里·奥尔洛夫的房间安排在自己的寝室正下方，又给他造了一座亭阁，用一道架在拱上的廊子与她的寝宫相连。大火之前，宫里常住约两千人，凡衣着得体者都可入内，连属于女皇私人寝宫的钻石厅也能参观。外国使节觐见时先登约旦阶梯（当时叫使节阶梯），再穿过一溜面朝涅瓦河的典礼大厅，走向宝座厅；贾科莫·夸伦吉修建的新大宝座厅1795年启用。

en:
Above twelve Doric columns of the Brandenburg Gate a goddess of victory drives four horses of beaten copper toward the city. The gate replaced a baroque customs gate of 1734 on the road from Berlin to Brandenburg an der Havel. Frederick William II, who came to the throne in 1786, wanted a Berlin with the monuments of Vienna, Paris and London, and his royal architect Carl Gotthard Langhans took the Propylaea of the Athenian Acropolis for his model, working from the published drawings of Le Roy and of Stuart and Revett because he had never seen Greece. Raised mostly in Elbe sandstone, with five passages between the columns, it was one of the first Greek Revival buildings in Germany. The metopes repeat the Parthenon's fight of centaurs and Lapiths, those on the west side after models by the sculptor Johann Gottfried Schadow, and reliefs in the passages show the labours of Hercules, meant as an allegory of the deeds of Frederick the Great. The gate opened to traffic in 1791 as the Peace Gate, for Prussia's intervention in Holland.

The quadriga was designed by Schadow and hammered out of copper sheets by the coppersmith Emanuel Jury and others; in 1793 the king, on the Academy's advice, decided against gilding it. After Jena and Auerstedt Napoleon marched in through the gate on 27 October 1806 and had the group taken down that December. Packed in twelve crates, it went by water through Hamburg to Paris, where it was restored in the Louvre but never mounted on the Porte Saint-Denis, where Napoleon finally meant it to go. Meanwhile Berliners saw only the bare iron mounting spike above the columns, and felt it as a deeper insult than the empty roof. In 1814, after the Prussians entered Paris, Blücher reported the quadriga found and the king ordered it home. On 7 August Frederick William III rode through the gate at the head of his troops as the wrappings fell from the restored chariot, and Berliners nicknamed the returned chariot the Retourkutsche, 'return carriage'. Karl Friedrich Schinkel then gave Victoria a new oak wreath around the Iron Cross, with the crowned Prussian eagle above it.
zh:
勃兰登堡门的十二根多立克柱上方，一位胜利女神驾着四匹锻铜的骏马朝向城内。大门取代了1734年建在柏林通往哈弗尔河畔勃兰登堡大道上的一座巴洛克式税关城门。1786年即位的腓特烈·威廉二世想让柏林拥有维也纳、巴黎、伦敦那样的纪念建筑，王室建筑师卡尔·戈特哈德·朗汉斯以雅典卫城的山门为范本，他本人没有去过希腊，依据的是勒鲁瓦以及斯图尔特和雷维特出版的图录。大门主要用易北砂岩建成，柱间五条通道，是德意志最早的希腊复兴式建筑之一。檐壁上的排档间饰模仿帕特农神庙上半人马与拉庇泰人的战斗，西面的几块依雕塑家约翰·戈特弗里德·沙多的模型制作；通道里的浮雕表现赫拉克勒斯的功绩，用来比喻腓特烈大王的功业。1791年大门开放通行，定名「和平门」，纪念普鲁士出兵荷兰。

门顶的四马战车由沙多设计，铜匠埃马努埃尔·尤里等人把铜板锻打成型；1793年国王听从美术学院的意见，决定不鎏金。耶拿和奥尔施泰特战败后，拿破仑1806年10月27日率军穿过勃兰登堡门进入柏林，同年12月下令拆下战车。战车分装十二箱，经汉堡走水路运往巴黎，在卢浮宫修复，最终没有安到拿破仑最后属意的圣但尼门上。这期间柏林人只能看见门顶竖着一根光秃秃的安装铁桩，比起门顶空空，这根「尖刺」更让他们觉得屈辱。1814年普鲁士军队进入巴黎后，布吕歇尔报告战车已经找到，国王下令立即运回柏林。8月7日，腓特烈·威廉三世率军穿过大门，修复的战车同时揭幕，柏林人把归来的战车戏称为「回程马车」（Retourkutsche）。申克尔随后为维多利亚重制了标志：新的橡叶环环抱着铁十字，上方立着戴王冠的普鲁士雄鹰。

en:
Ambras Castle began as a present for a secret wife. Ferdinand II, second son of Emperor Ferdinand I, had married Philippine Welser, an Augsburg merchant's daughter, in secret, and when he became sovereign of Tyrol in 1564 he set two Italian architects to turn the old fortress on the hill above Innsbruck into a Renaissance residence for her. The marriage stayed officially secret until 1576. Philippine was a commoner, and the valley loved her: even nobles brought their petitions to her, and people addressed them to 'Merciful Miss'. She laid out a herb garden and mixed medicines with her physician. She died in 1580.

Ferdinand was one of the great collectors of his age, and he built the Lower Castle as a museum for his collections. The Chamber of Art and Curiosities is the only Renaissance Kunstkammer preserved in its original place, with corals, clocks, automata, goblets of rhinoceros horn and portraits of 'wondrous persons' such as a hairy family and Vlad Dracula. In 1589 he added a hall for his 'heroes', the armour of famous commanders shown to their eternal memory, described as the first systematic display of its kind in museum history; the court giant Bartlmä Bon's armour is among the rest. In the Bacchus Grotto in the park, a visitor's account says, guests were welcomed with a drinking test: hidden chains held them fast until they had drained a cup of wine, probably by means of the iron trap chair kept in the Kunstkammer. The Spanish Hall, built for court festivals, has an inlaid wooden ceiling and 27 full-length portraits of the rulers of Tyrol.

After Ferdinand's death his son Charles, Margrave of Burgau, had little interest in the castle or its collections, and they decayed. In 1606 he sold them to Emperor Rudolf II, a great collector himself, who left his uncle's treasures where they were. Later, with Ambras seldom lived in, valuable books, manuscripts and drawings were lost, and Leopold I moved some of the most valuable books and manuscripts to Vienna. In 1805, with Austria beaten by France, Napoleon recognised the collection as private Habsburg property and had it carried to safety in Vienna.
zh:
阿姆布拉斯宫起初是献给一位秘密妻子的礼物。斐迪南二世是皇帝斐迪南一世的次子，他秘密娶了奥格斯堡商人的女儿菲利皮内·韦尔泽；1564年成为蒂罗尔的领主之后，他命两名意大利建筑师把因斯布鲁克上方山头的旧堡垒改建成文艺复兴式府邸，给她居住。这桩婚姻直到1576年才不再保密。菲利皮内是平民出身，谷地里的人却爱戴她：连贵族也向她递请愿书，人们称她「仁慈的小姐」。她辟了一座药草园，同自己的御医一起配药。1580年她去世。

斐迪南是那个时代首屈一指的收藏家，他专门修了下堡当博物馆。艺术与奇珍室是唯一保存在原处的文艺复兴奇珍柜，里面有珊瑚、钟表、自动机械、犀牛角杯，还有「奇人」的肖像，比如一家毛人和弗拉德·德拉库拉。1589年他又加建一座陈列「英雄」的厅馆，收着名将的甲胄，说是要让他们永远被人记住，被描述为博物馆史上第一次这样系统的陈列；宫廷巨人巴特尔梅·邦的甲胄也在藏品之中。据一位来访者的记述，园中的巴克斯石窟会用一场饮酒考验迎接客人：暗藏的锁链把客人扣住，要喝干一杯酒才能脱身，用的很可能是奇珍室收藏的那把铁制机关椅。西班牙厅是为宫廷庆典而建，木嵌天顶之下排着27幅蒂罗尔统治者的等身肖像。

斐迪南死后，儿子布尔高藩侯卡尔对宫殿和藏品没什么兴趣，任其败落。1606年他把它们卖给皇帝鲁道夫二世。鲁道夫自己就是大收藏家，仍把叔父的珍藏留在原处。后来宫中少有人居住，不少珍贵的书籍、手稿和手绘稿遗失，利奥波德一世又把其中一部分最珍贵的书籍和手稿迁到维也纳。1805年奥地利败给法国，拿破仑认定这批藏品是哈布斯堡的私产，下令把它安全运抵维也纳。

en:
For nearly three centuries a wooden crane, more than twenty-five metres high, stood on the stump of Cologne Cathedral's south tower, and it came to stand for a city that had stopped building. The church was conceived as a giant stone reliquary. The bones of the Three Kings made Cologne one of the great pilgrimage goals of the Middle Ages, so the chapter planned a French High Gothic minster modelled on Amiens. Archbishop Konrad von Hochstaden laid the first stone on 15 August 1248, with trachyte from the Drachenfels for the walls. Master Gerhard, who planned the chevet of seven chapels, is said to have died after a fall from his scaffolding under mysterious circumstances. His successors raised the choir and consecrated it in 1322. Its 104 stalls, the largest set in Germany, kept one seat for the emperor and one for the pope, and the upper windows hold glass portraits of forty-eight kings. As the pilgrim streams thinned after the Reformation, the chapter formally ended its funding in 1560.

The Dom remained a torso: a finished choir walled off from a nave raised barely halfway and closed by an emergency roof. French revolutionary troops entered Cologne in October 1794 and used the church as a stable and storehouse for a time, while the chapter had the shrine of the Three Kings carried to safety in Westphalia. Then the Romantics made completion their cause. Joseph Görres called the building a national shrine in 1814. The Cologne art dealer Sulpiz Boisserée, who had been sketching the fabric since 1808, found the medieval facade plan of 1370 in Darmstadt and Paris, in 1814 and 1816, with Johannes Fuhrer. In 1821 the pope restored the Dom as a cathedral and the Prussian state took over the cost of its upkeep, and Boisserée began publishing a series of engravings that showed the church finished. The crane stayed on the stump.
zh:
近三百年里，科隆大教堂南塔的残顶上一直立着一架高逾二十五米的木起重机，它成了一座停了工的城市的标记。这座教堂从设计之初就是一具巨大的石造圣物匣。三王圣骸使科隆成为中世纪最主要的朝圣地之一，教士团于是决定仿照亚眠大教堂，修建一座法国盛哥特式教堂。1248年8月15日，大主教康拉德·冯·霍赫施塔登放下第一块基石，墙体用德拉亨费尔斯山的粗面岩砌成。设计了七座小堂环绕的东端圣坛的格哈德师傅，据说是在神秘的情形下从脚手架上坠亡的。继任者们砌起唱诗班席，1322年祝圣启用。席位一百零四个，是德国最大的一组，其中一个留给皇帝，一个留给教宗；高窗上嵌着四十八位国王的彩绘玻璃像。宗教改革后朝圣的人流减少，1560年教士团正式停止拨款。

此后大教堂一直是副躯干：完工的唱诗班席被一道墙与只砌到一半高、盖着应急屋顶的中殿隔开。1794年10月法国革命军进入科隆，教堂一度被当作马厩和仓库，教士团则把三王金盒送往威斯特伐利亚避难。后来浪漫派把续建当成事业：戈雷斯1814年称它为民族圣地，科隆艺术品商人苏尔皮茨·布瓦塞雷自1808年起一直在描绘建筑现状，1814年和1816年与约翰内斯·富勒一起，在达姆施塔特和巴黎找回了1370年的立面设计图。1821年，教宗下诏恢复它的主教座堂地位，普鲁士国家承担起维护费用，布瓦塞雷开始陆续出版描绘教堂完工样貌的铜版画。南塔上的起重机没有撤下。

en:
The Amsterdam bourse opened for just one hour a day, from eleven to twelve, so that every goods broker had to be on the floor at the same time; the city council had ruled that trade was to be done only inside the bourse building. Before the Koopmansbeurs, the Merchants' Exchange, opened in 1611, merchants struck their bargains in the open air on the Nieuwe Brug by the IJ and in bad weather crowded into the Jerusalem Chapel or a church. In April 1607 the town council voted a bourse 'for the convenience of the merchants', and in the spring Hendrick de Keyser, the city's master sculptor and stonemason, went to London with the master mason Cornelis Danckertsz de Rij to study the exchange there. The building went up across the Rokin just south of the Dam, resting partly on the vaults of a sluice and partly on piles fifty to sixty feet long.

Most deals were in commodities, but the floor also traded shares in the East India Company and, from 1621, the West India Company, plus forward contracts, insurance and shipping deals, along with news from distant markets. An ordinance of 1619 even barred brokers from lingering near the building or the Dam after hours. In 1688 Joseph de la Vega, a Sephardic Jewish merchant, wrote Confusion de Confusiones, the first full-length work about the Amsterdam exchange, its traders and shareholders.

A legend attached itself to the bourse. In 1622 Balthasar Paul, a stonemason's journeyman from Namur, plotted to burn Amsterdam down, the bourse included, and died on the scaffold on the Dam; in the legend, an orphan boy found a ship loaded with gunpowder under the bourse and raised the alarm by drumming, and in thanks the orphan boys were allowed to drum at the bourse during fair week. In 1668 the city architect Daniël Stalpaert lengthened the courtyard from twelve arches to seventeen and put a statue of Mercury between two arched openings in the new front.
name_zh: 阿姆斯特丹证券交易所
zh:
阿姆斯特丹证券交易所每天只开一小时，从十一点到十二点，好让所有货物经纪人同一时间都在场内；市议会规定，生意只准在交易所大楼里做。1611年商人交易所落成以前，商人们在艾湾畔的新桥露天议价，遇上坏天气就挤进耶路撒冷礼拜堂或借教堂落脚。1607年4月，市议会决定「为商人之便」修建交易所；当年春天，城市雕刻兼石匠师傅亨德里克·德·凯泽（Hendrick de Keyser）与泥瓦师傅科内利斯·丹克茨·德赖前往伦敦，考察那里的交易所。大楼建在水坝广场南侧，横跨罗金（Rokin），一半架在水闸的拱顶之上，一半立在五六十英尺长的木桩上。

场内成交以货物为主，但也买卖东印度公司股票，1621年起又加上西印度公司股票，另有远期合同、保险和货运合约，远方市场的消息也在此汇集。1619年的一项法令甚至禁止经纪人在交易时间之外靠近交易所和水坝广场。1688年，塞法迪犹太商人约瑟夫·德拉维加（Joseph de la Vega）写成《混乱中的混乱》（Confusion de Confusiones），这是第一部完整讲述阿姆斯特丹交易所、场内交易者和股东的著作。

交易所还附着一桩传说：1622年，那慕尔来的石匠帮工巴尔塔扎·保罗密谋纵火烧掉阿姆斯特丹，交易所也在目标之列，事败后在水坝广场被处死；传说则讲成一个孤儿院男孩在交易所下面发现一艘满载火药的船，击鼓报警，孤儿院的男孩为此获准在集市周于交易所击鼓。1668年，城市建筑师丹尼尔·斯塔尔帕特（Daniël Stalpaert）主持改建，庭院拱廊从十二拱加长到十七拱，新门面中央两个拱形门洞之间立起墨丘利神像。

en:
Legend says that when the St Elizabeth's flood receded, people saw a cradle floating on the water and expected the worst, but a cat was leaping from corner to corner to keep it upright, and the sleeping baby's bedding stayed dry. Kinderdijk takes its name, the story runs, from a cradle washed ashore in 1421. The flood itself was real. On the night of 18-19 November 1421 a storm broke the dikes in a number of places, villages in the Grote Waard were lost, and between 2,000 and 10,000 people died.

The polders are land kept dry by dikes, sluices and mills. From the eleventh century religious orders took the lead in banking off silted ground along the coasts, in Zeeland on behalf of Flemish abbeys. In Holland the drained peat soil subsided, so ditches and polders had to be organised, and from the thirteenth century local polder boards joined together. The first official water board was Rijnland, set up in 1255 by Count Willem II. The earliest written mention of a windmill used to control water dates from 1407, near Alkmaar.

Draining inland lakes began with small experiments. The Achtermeer, a 35-hectare lake south of Alkmaar, was pumped dry in 1533 under a patent granted to Jan Jansz and Willem Jansz. It is the earliest known droogmakerij, a polder made from a lake bed. Investors then took on the Beemster, a lake connected to the Zuiderzee, between 1608 and 1612. When a breach in the Zuiderzee dikes let the water back in, the ring dike was raised a full metre above the surrounding land. The dry lake bed was laid out in a grid of roads with canals running parallel, and divided among the investors. Its farms grew crops for the long voyages of the East India Company. The Purmer followed in 1622, the Wijdewormer in 1626, the Watergraafsmeer in 1629 and the Schermer in 1635.
zh:
相传圣伊丽莎白洪水退去后，人们看见一只摇篮漂在水上，以为婴儿凶多吉少，却见一只猫在摇篮的各个角上来回跳跃，使它保持直立，熟睡的婴儿连被褥都没有湿。小孩堤防（Kinderdijk）据说就得名于1421年一只被冲上岸的摇篮。洪水本身确有其事：1421年11月18日至19日夜间，风暴冲决了多处堤坝，大瓦尔德的村庄被淹没，死亡人数在两千到一万之间。

荷兰圩田是靠堤坝、水闸和风车保持干燥的土地。从十一世纪起，宗教团体带头在沿海筑堤围起淤积的滩地，泽兰一带则是替佛兰德的修道院做。在荷兰，排水后的泥炭土不断下沉，必须整治沟渠、修筑圩田；十三世纪起，各地的圩田管理机构开始联合。第一个正式的水利委员会是1255年由伯爵威廉二世设立的赖恩兰水利委员会。风车用于控制水位的最早文字记载是1407年，在阿尔克马尔附近。

排干内陆湖泊是从小规模试验开始的：1533年，阿尔克马尔以南三十五公顷的阿赫特梅尔湖按照颁给扬·扬松和威廉·扬松的特许被抽干，这是已知最早的湖底圩田（droogmakerij）。投资者随后在1608至1612年间向与须得海相通的贝姆斯特湖动手。须得海的堤坝决口、湖水倒灌后，人们把环形围堤加高到比周围地面整整高出一米。干涸的湖底铺成道路的网格，水渠与道路平行，分给投资人。这里的农场种出供东印度公司远航用的作物。普尔默湖1622年、维德沃默湖1626年、瓦特赫拉夫斯米尔湖1629年、斯海尔默湖1635年相继排干。

en:
Every block of marble quarried at Candoglia for the Duomo was stamped AUF, ad usum fabricae, 'for the use of the works', and so crossed the country free of every toll. Archbishop Antonio da Saluzzo began the cathedral in 1386 on the most central site of Roman Mediolanum, where the public basilica had faced the forum. His cousin Gian Galeazzo Visconti soon took control, wanting a building in step with the newest European fashion, and gave the Fabbrica del Duomo, the building office, exclusive use of the quarry.

The French architect Jean Mignot, summoned from Paris to judge the rising piers, declared the work so far in 'peril of ruin', built 'without science'; the walls stood, but the insult spurred the engineers to improve their instruments and techniques. In 1488 Leonardo and Bramante both entered models for the cupola, and Leonardo withdrew. Archbishop Carlo Borromeo removed the lay tombs from the church and consecrated it in 1577. At the left of the altar stands Marco d'Agrate's Saint Bartholomew Flayed, the saint carrying his own skin over his shoulders like a stole. High above the altar, a nail of the True Cross, which tradition says Saint Helena found, hangs from the keystone of the vault, made visible from the nave by a red light. Each year on 3 May the archbishop takes it down and shows it to the faithful with the Nivola, a seventeenth-century mechanical lift. In 1774 Giuseppe Perego's gilded copper Madonnina was raised on the main spire, and the Milanese count a day when she is visible through the mist as fair weather.

The facade was the great unfinished argument. Pellegrini drew a Roman scheme with columns and obelisks, and Buzzi returned to Gothic. Napoleon was crowned King of Italy at the Duomo in 1805 and ordered the facade finished, promising that the French treasury would repay the Fabbrica; the money was never paid, but Carlo Amati completed the facade in 1813, and a statue of Napoleon was set on one of the spires. Behind it open five naves, about 45 metres high, the highest Gothic vaults of a completed church.
zh:
为米兰主教座堂从坎多利亚采石场运来的每块大理石，都烙着「AUF」，即拉丁文「ad usum fabricae」，意思是「供工程使用」，运过各地关卡一概免税。1386年，大主教安东尼奥·达·萨卢佐在古罗马梅迪奥拉努姆最中心的位置动工，那里原来是面向广场的公共巴西利卡。他的表弟吉安·加莱亚佐·维斯孔蒂很快接管了工程，想要一座跟上欧洲最新潮流的建筑，并把坎多利亚采石场的独占使用权给了大教堂工程局。

从巴黎召来评判正在升高的巨墩的法国建筑师让·米尼奥断言，已建部分有「坍塌之险」、做法「不合科学」；墙没有塌，这番羞辱却逼着工程师改进仪器和技法。1488年，列奥纳多·达·芬奇和伯拉孟特各自为穹顶制作模型参选，列奥纳多退出。大主教卡洛·博罗梅奥把俗人陵墓清出教堂，并在1577年为教堂祝圣。祭坛左侧立着马尔科·德·阿格拉泰的《剥皮的圣巴多禄茂》，圣人把自己的皮像披肩一样搭在肩上。祭坛上方高处，相传由圣海伦娜发现的十字架圣钉挂在拱顶的拱心石上，一盏红灯使中殿里的人都看得见它。每年5月3日，大主教用一架十七世纪的机械升降具「尼沃拉」把圣钉取下，给信众瞻仰。1774年，朱塞佩·佩雷戈设计的镀金铜圣母像安放在大尖塔顶上，米兰人把能在薄雾中望见她的日子当作晴天。

立面是争论最久的难题。佩莱格里尼画了一份有圆柱和方尖碑的罗马式方案，布齐又改回哥特式。1805年，拿破仑在米兰主教座堂加冕为意大利国王，下令完成立面，并答应由法国国库偿还工程局的开销；钱从未拨付，卡洛·阿马蒂却在1813年把立面建成，一座尖顶上还安放了拿破仑的雕像。立面之后是五廊的室内，中殿高约45米，拱顶是已建成教堂里最高的哥特拱顶。

en:
In the Great Council hall a frieze of doges' portraits runs beneath the ceiling, and the place of Marino Faliero, who attempted a coup in 1355, is filled by a black cloth. The portraits are imaginary, painted after the fire of 1577 destroyed the earlier ones. The Doge's Palace held government offices, a jail and the doge's residence. The palace of 1444 was the Gothic building begun around 1340 on the lagoon side, two colonnaded storeys under a massive upper wall of inlaid marble. Doge Francesco Foscari later extended it along the Piazzetta, and its ceremonial entrance is the Porta della Carta. After a fire in 1483 Antonio Rizzo rebuilt the east wing in the new Renaissance manner, with the Giants' Staircase, where doges were crowned. Sansovino's colossal Mars and Neptune stand at its head.

On 20 December 1577 a third fire destroyed the Scrutinio Room and the Great Council Chamber, with works by Gentile da Fabriano, Pisanello, Bellini, Carpaccio and Titian. The rebuilding kept the Gothic style, despite neoclassical designs submitted by Palladio. Tintoretto and his son Domenico painted Paradise across the end wall, 24.51 metres long and 7.65 high, which the Italian wikipedia calls the largest canvas in the world.

The palace had its prison too. The Wells, below the level of the water, were damp and dark. The Leads, under the lead roof, were kept for prisoners of higher status. Giacomo Casanova, sentenced to five years there in 1755, broke through the lead plates with a spike and crawled over the roof. He lowered himself into the palace, passed through its corridors and talked a guard into letting him out, then left by gondola. A covered bridge built in 1614 joined the palace to the New Prisons across the canal; the name Bridge of Sighs came in the Romantic age, from the idea that prisoners sighed at their last sight of the lagoon. When the republic fell in 1797 the French destroyed the medieval sculpture of Doge Foscari kneeling before the lion of Saint Mark over the Porta della Carta.
zh:
大议会厅天花板下的檐壁上，历代总督的肖像依次排开，1355年谋反的马里诺·法列罗那里却只挂一幅黑布。这些肖像都是想象像，1577年大火烧毁了原来的画，之后才重画。总督宫里有政府机关、监狱和总督的住所。1444年的总督宫是约1340年起在潟湖一侧动工的哥特式宫殿，两层柱廊之上是一道镶嵌大理石的厚重墙体。后来总督弗朗切斯科·福斯卡里把它沿小广场方向扩建，礼仪大门是「纸门」。1483年大火之后，安东尼奥·里佐按新兴的文艺复兴样式重建东翼，建起巨人阶梯，总督在这里加冕；圣索维诺所作的巨大战神与海神像立在梯顶。

1577年12月20日，第三场大火烧毁了评议厅和大议会厅，真蒂莱·达·法布里亚诺、皮萨内洛、贝利尼、卡尔帕乔、提香等人的画作同归于尽。重建时保留了哥特样式，尽管帕拉第奥提交过新古典式的设计。丁托列托和儿子多梅尼科在尽头的墙上画了《天堂》，长24.51米、高7.65米，意大利文维基称它是世界上最大的画布。

总督宫里还有监狱。「井狱」在水面之下，潮湿昏暗；「铅狱」在铅皮屋顶下，关押身份较高的囚犯。贾科莫·卡萨诺瓦1755年被判五年徒刑关在这里，他用一根铁钎撬开铅板，爬上屋顶，从天窗下到宫里，穿过走廊，说动守卫放他出去，然后乘贡多拉离开。1614年，一座封闭的廊桥跨运河把总督宫和新监狱连了起来；叹息桥这个名字出现在浪漫主义时代，说是囚徒在这里最后一次望见潟湖，发出叹息。1797年共和国灭亡，法军砸毁了纸门上方福斯卡里总督跪在圣马可之狮前的中世纪雕群。

en:
Dante used the Venetian word arzanà in the Inferno, and the pitch boiling in the fifth pit of hell is compared to the pitch the Venetians boiled in winter to mend their unsound ships. The word comes from the Arabic dar al-sina'a, house of craft. The state dockyard in the Castello district, traditionally founded in 1104 though no evidence gives so exact a date, grew into possibly the largest industrial site in Europe before the Industrial Revolution, about 48 hectares behind a rampart three kilometres long, some 15 per cent of the city. After the New Arsenal of 1320 it could build and repair the whole state navy and the larger merchantmen; hulls went up frame-first, a canal carried each one past the workers, and up to a hundred galleys stood in different stages of building and upkeep. Timber came from the state forest at Montello, and the rope-walks used hemp brought mostly from the mouth of the Don, in the Sea of Azov.

Before the land gate, built around 1460 on the pattern of a Roman arch at Venetian-ruled Pula, four stone lions were set in 1687. One of them, the Piraeus Lion, carries runic graffiti, probably cut by Scandinavian mercenaries in the eleventh century. In 1593 Galileo became a consultant to the yard and helped with problems of oars and ballistics; the shipwrights' knowledge later fed his book on the strength of materials. The doge's ceremonial barge, the bucentaur, was held in the Arsenal too. Every Ascension Day it carried the doge out to throw a gold ring into the Adriatic, wedding Venice to the sea; Casanova noted that the slightest headwind could drown the doge with all his lordship and the ambassadors. The last and most magnificent, first sailed in 1729, was 35 metres long and rowed by 168 oarsmen.

Even in decline the yard was valued: when Peter I of Russia built galleys for the Sea of Azov, he called in Venetian shipwrights. After the republic fell in 1797, ships on the stocks were broken up and more than 5,000 guns from the Arsenal were sent to Toulon. The bucentaur was smashed and burned in 1798 to recover its gold.
zh:
但丁在《神曲·地狱篇》里用了威尼斯方言词arzanà（军械库），地狱第五恶囊里沸腾的沥青，被他比作威尼斯人冬天熬来修补破损船只的沥青。这个词来自阿拉伯语「工匠之家」。城堡区的国家船坞传统上认为建于1104年，不过没有证据能给出这样确切的年份；它后来可能成了工业革命以前欧洲最大的工业区，占地约48公顷，围墙长约3公里，约占全城面积的15%。1320年新军械库建成之后，国家的整支舰队和较大的商船都能在这里建造和维修；船身采用先立骨架的造法，一条渠道把船身依次送过工匠身边，常有多达一百艘桨帆船处在不同的建造和维护阶段。木材取自国家在蒙泰洛的专属森林，绳索工场所用的麻多半来自亚速海边的顿河口。

威尼斯军械库的陆地正门约1460年建成，仿照威尼斯治下普拉的一座古罗马凯旋门，1687年门前安放了四尊石狮，其中的「比雷埃夫斯之狮」侧身刻有如尼文，多半是11世纪斯堪的纳维亚雇佣兵的手笔。1593年，伽利略受聘为军械库顾问，帮忙解决船桨和弹道方面的难题；船匠们的经验后来写进了他关于材料强度的著作。总督的礼舟也存放在军械库。每年耶稣升天节，礼舟载着总督出海，把一枚金戒指投入亚得里亚海，表示威尼斯与大海成婚；卡萨诺瓦写道，稍有顶风，就能让总督连同全体显贵和使节一起淹死。最后也最华丽的一艘1729年首航，长35米，由168名桨手划动。

即便在衰落年代，船坞仍受看重：俄国的彼得一世营造亚速海桨帆船时，请来了威尼斯船匠。1797年共和国灭亡后，船台上的船被拆毁，军械库五千多门火炮被运往土伦。那艘礼舟1798年被砸碎焚烧，为的是回收上面的金子。

en:
Santa Maria del Fiore stood without its dome for decades. Begun in 1296 to replace the old church of Santa Reparata, its walls were faced in bands of white Carrara, green Prato and red Siena marble. Above the crossing yawned a gap about 43 metres wide, and the plan inherited from Arnolfo di Cambio and Neri di Fioravanti called for an octagonal dome higher and wider than any ever built, with no Gothic buttresses. Tuscany had too little timber for the usual wooden centring.

In 1418 the wool guild held a competition. The two main rivals were the goldsmiths Filippo Brunelleschi and Lorenzo Ghiberti; Brunelleschi won, but Ghiberti was made co-director on the same salary. When Brunelleschi fell ill, or feigned illness, Ghiberti briefly took over and supposedly had to admit that the job was beyond him. Brunelleschi raised two brick shells with nothing supporting them from below, laying the bricks in a herringbone pattern that passed the weight of each fresh course to the nearest vertical ribs, and he invented hoists to lift 37,000 tons of material, including over four million bricks. On 25 March 1436, New Year's Day in the Florentine calendar, Pope Eugene IV consecrated the cathedral while Guillaume Dufay's motet Nuper rosarum flores was performed. Brunelleschi died in 1446, a few months after work on the lantern began, and lies in a simple tomb in the crypt. The gilded copper ball on the lantern was made by Verrocchio, in whose workshop the young Leonardo da Vinci sketched Brunelleschi's hoists. Lightning knocked it down in 1600, and a larger one replaced it two years later.

On 26 April 1478, during Mass, assassins struck at the Medici brothers. Giuliano was stabbed to death; Lorenzo escaped into the sacristy and barricaded himself in. When Baccio d'Agnolo began a gallery around the drum, Michelangelo is said to have called the dome a cage for crickets, and the work stopped after one of its eight sides. Grand Duke Cosimo I had the inside of the dome painted: Giorgio Vasari began the Last Judgment in 1572 and died before it was done, and Federico Zuccari finished its 3,600 square metres in 1579.
zh:
圣母百花大教堂有几十年没有穹顶。它1296年动工，取代旧的圣雷帕拉塔堂，外墙以白色卡拉拉、绿色普拉托和红色锡耶纳大理石相间镶成。十字交叉处上方空着一个约43米宽的缺口；承袭自阿尔诺福·迪·坎比奥和内里·迪·菲奥拉万蒂的方案，要建一座比以往任何穹顶都更高更宽的八角穹顶，还不许用哥特式飞扶壁。托斯卡纳的木材又不够搭传统的满堂脚手架。

1418年羊毛行会悬赏征集方案，两个主要对手是金匠菲利波·布鲁内莱斯基和洛伦佐·吉贝尔蒂。布鲁内莱斯基胜出，但吉贝尔蒂也被任命为共同负责人，薪水相同。据说布鲁内莱斯基病倒（也有说是装病），吉贝尔蒂一度接手，结果不得不承认自己干不了。布鲁内莱斯基造起内外两层砖壳，施工时下面不设任何支撑，砖按鱼骨纹砌，把新砌砖层的重量传给最近的竖向肋条；他还发明了吊机，吊起3.7万吨材料，其中砖有四百多万块。1436年3月25日，佛罗伦萨历的元旦，教皇恩仁四世为大教堂祝圣，纪尧姆·迪费的经文歌《玫瑰新开》（Nuper rosarum flores）在典礼上演唱。采光亭动工几个月后，布鲁内莱斯基于1446年去世，葬在地下室一座简朴的墓里。采光亭顶上的镀金铜球出自韦罗基奥之手，年轻的列奥纳多·达·芬奇当时在他的作坊里，画下了布鲁内莱斯基吊机的草图。1600年雷电把铜球击落，两年后换上了一只更大的。

1478年4月26日，弥撒进行时，刺客对美第奇兄弟下手。朱利亚诺被刺死；洛伦佐逃进圣器室，从里面把门堵住。巴乔·达尼奥洛开始在鼓座外加建回廊时，据说米开朗基罗评论这座穹顶像一只蟋蟀笼，工程只做了八面中的一面就停了。大公科西莫一世下令绘制穹顶内壁：乔治·瓦萨里1572年动笔绘制《最后的审判》，没画完就去世了，费德里科·祖卡里1579年完成了这3600平方米的画面。

en:
In 1586 Domenico Fontana moved the Egyptian obelisk of Nero's circus into the square before St Peter's, on the orders of Sixtus V. As the lifting ropes began to smoke from the friction, a Sanremo sailor, Benedetto Bresca, noticed it and intervened quickly, and for that his town earned the privilege of supplying the palms for Palm Sunday.

The church it stood before began as Constantine's basilica on Vatican Hill, over the tomb of Peter outside the city walls. Charlemagne was crowned emperor there in 800, and a red porphyry disc in the later floor marks where he is said to have knelt. By the 1400s the old church was falling into ruin, and Alberti wrote that the wind had already pushed a long wall more than six feet out of true. Julius II decided to pull it down, which shocked many people of the time, since the building stood for papal continuity back to Peter. Bramante's design won the competition, a Greek cross under a dome like the Pantheon's, and the foundation stone was laid in 1506. To pay for the work the Archbishop of Mainz promoted indulgences and appointed the Dominican Johann Tetzel, whose salesmanship provoked a scandal that led to the Reformation. Raphael planned a nave of five bays; Charles V's army sacked Rome in 1527, and the next plan was never carried out.

On 1 January 1547 Michelangelo, then in his seventies, took charge, writing 'I undertake this only for the love of God and in honour of the Apostle'. He redesigned the dome as two brick shells, the outer one with 16 stone ribs, and Giacomo della Porta and Domenico Fontana closed it in 1590. Carlo Maderno added three bays to the front, and Urban VIII consecrated the church on 18 November 1626. Bernini's bronze baldachin over Peter's altar, close to 29 metres high, took its twisted columns from the old church's. Michelangelo's Pietà stands in the first chapel of the north aisle, and Queen Christina of Sweden, who gave up her throne to become a Catholic, is buried in the basilica.
zh:
1586年，多梅尼科·丰塔纳奉西斯都五世之命，把尼禄马戏场的埃及方尖碑移到圣伯多禄大殿（圣彼得大教堂）前的广场。吊索因摩擦开始冒烟，圣雷莫的水手本尼代托·布雷斯卡发现后迅速出手，他的家乡因此得到为圣枝主日供应棕榈枝的特权。

广场后的大殿起初是君士坦丁大帝建在梵蒂冈山丘上的老殿，坐落在罗马城墙外的伯多禄墓上。800年查理曼在这里加冕为帝，后来的地面上有一块红色斑岩圆盘，据说是他当时下跪的地方。到15世纪，老殿濒于倾颓，阿尔贝蒂写道，风已经把一道长墙推得偏离垂直线六英尺以上。儒略二世决定拆掉老殿，当时许多人深感震惊，因为这座建筑代表着从伯多禄传下来的教皇世系。伯拉孟特的方案在竞赛中胜出：希腊十字平面，上覆万神殿式的穹顶，1506年奠基。为了筹款，美因茨大主教推销赎罪券，指派多明我会修士约翰·台彻尔，他的推销引发丑闻，并导致宗教改革。拉斐尔设想了五间的长厅；1527年查理五世的军队洗劫罗马，之后的方案没有实现。

1547年1月1日，已年过七旬的米开朗基罗接掌工程，写道「我接手这件事，只是为了天主的爱和宗徒的荣耀」。他把穹顶重新设计成双层砖壳，外层有16道石肋，1590年由贾科莫·德拉·波尔塔和多梅尼科·丰塔纳封顶。卡洛·马代尔诺在前面加了三间，1626年11月18日教皇乌尔巴诺八世为大殿祝圣。贝尔尼尼在伯多禄祭坛上方铸起近29米高的青铜华盖，扭柱取自老殿的柱式。米开朗基罗的《圣殇》供在北侧廊第一间小堂里；放弃王位皈依天主教的瑞典女王克里斯蒂娜也葬在大殿。

en:
From the great gallery at the centre of the palace the park runs away in a line of fountains to an artificial cascade on Monte Briano. The water came from the Fizzo springs at the foot of Monte Taburno, 38 kilometres away, through the Carolino Aqueduct, mostly underground. Where it crosses the Valle di Maddaloni the channel runs over a three-tier tufa bridge 529 metres long and 55.8 metres high, modelled on the aqueducts of ancient Rome and the longest bridge in Europe when it was built.

The palace itself stands in the plain 35 kilometres north of Naples, a five-storey rectangle of 247 by 190 metres with about 1,200 rooms. Charles VII of Naples, later Charles III of Spain, laid the first stone on 20 January 1752, his thirty-sixth birthday. He wanted a new administrative centre for the kingdom, with court, government and troop barracks under one roof on the model of Versailles, in a place regarded as safe from Vesuvius and from sea raids and away from crowded, revolt-prone Naples. Luigi Vanvitelli designed it, and by 1760 over two thousand workmen and slaves were on the site, using tuff, lime and travertine from the neighbourhood. Charles never slept a night in it: in 1759 he left for the crown of Spain, and his son Ferdinand IV inherited an unfinished house. Vanvitelli died in 1773 and his son Carlo carried on. The court began to live there in 1789, when Giuseppe Maria Galanti reckoned that the work had cost seven million ducats.

Queen Maria Carolina wanted an English garden, on the advice of her sister Marie Antoinette and of the British envoy Lord Hamilton. The English gardener John Graefer began it in 1786 and obtained seeds and specimens from Japan, China and Australia; his camellias came to Europe directly from Japan. A silk mill at San Leucio worked on water from the same aqueduct. When the Parthenopaean Republic was proclaimed in 1799 the palace was expropriated like the rest of the crown's property and its furniture was looted, to be recovered after the Restoration. Under the French, Joachim Murat lived here, turned the Alexander Hall into a throne room and hung an apartment with San Leucio silks.
zh:
从王宫正中的大长廊望出去，花园沿着一排喷泉伸向布里亚诺山上的人工瀑布。水来自塔布尔诺山脚下的菲佐泉，由38公里长的卡罗利诺水道送来，水道大半埋在地下。越过马达洛尼谷地的一段，水渠架在三层凝灰岩拱券桥上，桥长529米、高55.8米，仿古罗马水道而建，建成时是欧洲最长的桥。

卡塞塔王宫本身立在那波利以北35公里的平原上，是一座247米长、190米宽的五层矩形建筑，约有1200个房间。1752年1月20日，那不勒斯国王卡洛七世（后来的西班牙国王卡洛斯三世）在他36岁生日那天奠基。他想为王国建一个新的行政中心，以凡尔赛为样板，把宫廷、政府和卫戍部队集中在一座建筑里，选在人们认为维苏威火山波及不到、海上袭击够不着的地方，远离拥挤又容易闹事的那波利。路易吉·万维泰利主持设计，到1760年工地上已有两千多名工匠和奴隶，使用附近出产的凝灰岩、石灰和洞石。卡洛没有在王宫里住过一夜：1759年他动身去西班牙继位，未完工的宫殿留给了儿子费迪南多四世。万维泰利1773年去世，由其子卡洛接手。宫廷1789年开始住进来，朱塞佩·玛丽亚·加兰蒂估计这时工程已花去700万杜卡特。

王后玛丽亚·卡罗利娜听从姊姊玛丽·安托瓦内特和英国公使汉密尔顿勋爵的建议，要建一座英式花园。英国园艺师约翰·格雷费尔1786年动工，从日本、中国和澳大利亚弄到种子和标本，他的山茶花直接从日本运到了欧洲。圣卢乔的丝织厂也借用同一条水道的水力。1799年帕特诺珀共和国成立，王宫同王室其他产业一起被没收，家具遭劫掠，复辟后才追回。法国人统治时期，若阿基姆·缪拉住在这里，把亚历山大厅改成了王座厅，还用圣卢乔的丝绸裱糊了一套房间。

en:
The Malta forts ring the Grand Harbour, one of the safest anchorages between Sicily and the African coast. Its core was Fort St Angelo on the Birgu headland, a medieval castle known as the Castrum Maris, the castle by the sea; after 1530 the Hospitallers cut a dry ditch through its rock and made it the grand master's seat. Across the water, at the tip of the Sciberras peninsula, an Aragonese watchtower had been replaced by the star fort St Elmo, and it took the first blow in 1565. About 150 knights and 600 soldiers held out for 28 days under fire from guns on Mount Sciberras, and when it fell on 23 June the garrison was almost wiped out. The corsair Dragut was fatally struck by debris from a shot, fired by an Ottoman gun in one account and by Spanish gunners at St Angelo in another. In July a sea attack on Senglea ran into a battery at the foot of St Angelo, which sank all but one of the boats.

Afterwards the knights girdled their new capital Valletta with bastions drawn by the papal engineer Francesco Laparelli, and kept building for two centuries. The Cottonera Lines were meant to shelter 40,000 islanders and their animals in a siege, but work stopped when Grand Master Cotoner died in 1680 and the lines were finished only in the 1760s. Fort Ricasoli, paid for by a gift of 20,000 scudi from the Florentine knight Giovanni Francesco Ricasoli, guards the harbour mouth and is the largest fort in Malta. On Gozo the island's governor, Chambray, paid for Fort Chambray, a citadel meant to take in the islanders and their livestock, with a town inside its walls that was never built.

The rebels of 1775 chose 8 September, the anniversary of the end of the Great Siege. Led by the priest Gaetano Mannarino, they seized St Elmo and St James Cavalier; the Order retook the cavalier within the hour and the fort was handed back within days. In June 1798 Napoleon landed, and Grand Master Hompesch gave up the fortified harbour within days, without a siege. The French garrison held the forts through the two-year Maltese blockade and surrendered them to the British in 1800.
zh:
马耳他堡垒群环绕着大港，那是西西里与非洲海岸之间最稳妥的锚地之一。核心是比尔古角上的圣安杰洛堡，中世纪时是一座叫「海边城堡」（Castrum Maris）的城堡；1530年后，医院骑士团凿开岩石修成干壕，把这里作为大团长驻地。对岸希伯拉斯半岛尖端，一座阿拉贡人的瞭望塔已被改建成星形的圣埃尔莫堡，1565年它首当其冲：约150名骑士和600名士兵在希伯拉斯山的炮火下坚守28天，6月23日城陷，守军几乎全军覆没。海盗头目德拉古特被一发炮弹的碎屑击中致命，一说是奥斯曼炮手所发，另一说是圣安杰洛堡的西班牙炮手所为。7月，对森格莱阿的海上进攻撞上了圣安杰洛堡脚下的炮台，除一条小艇外全被击沉。

此后骑士团按教皇派来的工程师弗朗切斯科·拉帕雷利的设计，给新都瓦莱塔围上棱堡，两百年里仍在增筑。科托内拉防线打算在围城时收容四万名岛民和他们的牲畜，但1680年科托内大团长去世后停工，直到1760年代才建成。里卡索利堡由佛罗伦萨骑士乔瓦尼·弗朗切斯科·里卡索利捐出两万斯库多修建，扼守港口咽喉，是马耳他最大的堡垒。在戈佐岛上，总督尚布雷出资修建尚布雷堡，打算容纳岛上居民和牲畜，堡内规划的新城却始终没有盖起来。

1775年的起事者特意选在9月8日，那是大围攻解围的纪念日。他们在神父加埃塔诺·曼纳里诺带领下占领圣埃尔莫堡和圣詹姆斯骑士楼；骑士团一小时内夺回骑士楼，圣埃尔莫堡几天内交还。1798年6月拿破仑登陆，大团长霍姆佩施几天内就献出设防港口，未经一场围城战。法国守军靠着堡垒撑过马耳他人两年的封锁，于1800年把它们交给英国人。

en:
The story goes that Emperor Matthias, hunting here, found an artesian spring and cried 'Welch' schöner Brunn!', what a fine spring, which gave Schönbrunn its name. The estate lay on the floodplain of the Wien river outside Vienna. In 1569 Maximilian II bought it and fenced it as the court's hunting ground; Eleonora Gonzaga, widow of Ferdinand II, later added a palace wing to the old Katterburg. The Ottoman siege of 1683 left it all unusable, and Leopold I commissioned a new palace for his heir Joseph from Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach. Fischer's first plan would have outdone Versailles but could not be paid for; the far smaller palace built over the ruins was ready to live in by the end of the century.

Charles VI cared little for Schönbrunn and in 1740 gave it to his daughter Maria Theresa, who made it the summer seat of the imperial family. Her architect Nikolaus von Pacassi raised the palace by a storey and renewed most of the interior in what is almost the only Austrian rococo. On 13 October 1762 the six-year-old Mozart met the archduchess Maria Antonia here, the future Marie Antoinette. The biographer Eric Blom tells how she helped him up when he slipped on the polished floor, and she is supposed to have received a proposal of marriage in return. On the hill behind the palace the Gloriette was finished in 1775 as a monument to the just war, built from the columns and cornices of an old gallery at Schloss Neugebäude that Maria Theresa wrote was of no use where it stood.

Napoleon stayed at Schönbrunn in 1805 and again in 1809, when French troops held Vienna. On 12 October 1809 the 17-year-old Friedrich Staps was arrested in the courtyard with a kitchen knife hidden among his petition papers; Napoleon asked whether he would be grateful if pardoned, and Staps answered that he would kill him all the same. Two days later Austria signed the Peace of Schönbrunn, giving up Salzburg, its Adriatic coast and West Galicia. In 1810 Francis I married his daughter Marie Louise to Napoleon.
zh:
相传皇帝马蒂亚斯出猎到这里，发现一眼自流井，脱口赞道「好一眼美泉」，「美泉」之名就这样得来。庄园位于维也纳城外维也纳河的滩地上。1569年，马克西米利安二世买下这片地，圈起来做宫廷猎场；斐迪南二世的遗孀埃莱奥诺拉·贡扎加后来给旧的卡特堡添建了一翼宫室。1683年奥斯曼围城，这些建筑被毁得无法使用，利奥波德一世委托约翰·伯恩哈德·费舍尔·冯·埃拉赫为继承人约瑟夫重建新宫。费舍尔的初稿本要压过凡尔赛，却付不起钱；在废墟上建起的小得多的宫殿，世纪末已可入住。

卡尔六世对美泉宫兴趣不大，1740年把它赐给女儿玛丽亚·特蕾西亚，她把这里定为皇室的夏宫。她的建筑师尼古劳斯·冯·帕卡西把宫殿加高一层，并更新了大部分内饰，成了奥地利几乎仅有的洛可可范例。1762年10月13日，六岁的莫扎特在这里见到了大公女玛丽亚·安东妮娅，就是后来的玛丽·安托瓦内特。传记作者埃里克·布洛姆讲过一则轶事：莫扎特在光滑的地板上滑倒，她把他扶起来，据说他还因此向她求婚。宫后的小丘上，1775年建成了荣耀亭（Gloriette），作为正义战争的纪念碑；所用的柱子和檐口，拆自新建宫（Neugebäude）的一条旧回廊，玛丽亚·特蕾西亚在批示里写道，这些石料留在原处没有用处。

拿破仑1805年和1809年都住在美泉宫，1809年法军占领着维也纳。1809年10月12日，十七岁的弗里德里希·施塔普斯在院子里被捕，请愿书里藏着一把厨刀；拿破仑问他若被赦免会不会感激，施塔普斯回答说照样要杀他。两天后，奥地利签署《美泉宫和约》，割让萨尔茨堡、亚得里亚海沿岸和西加利西亚。1810年，弗朗茨一世把女儿玛丽·路易丝嫁给了拿破仑。

en:
According to Thucydides, Pericles told the Athenians that the forty talents of gold on the statue of Athena inside the Parthenon were all removable, to be used in an emergency and replaced afterwards. The temple was begun in 447 BC, when the Delian League was at the peak of its power. Ictinus and Callicrates were its architects, and it has hardly a straight line: the platform bulges upward at the centre, and the columns swell and lean slightly inward. Phidias' Athena Parthenos, about thirteen metres high, probably built on a cypress frame under plates of ivory and gold, was lost at an unknown date. The temple became a Christian church, and for about 250 years under Latin rule a Catholic church of Our Lady, with a bell tower at its southwest corner. In 1436 Cyriacus of Ancona was the first since antiquity to describe it and call it by name, 'a divine work of Phidias'.

After the Ottomans took the Acropolis in 1458 the church became a mosque: the tower was raised into a minaret, the apse became a mihrab, and the saints on the walls were whitewashed, but the structure stayed intact. Evliya Celebi called it an impregnable fortress not made by human agency and prayed it might stand forever. The French artist Jacques Carrey drew its sculptures for the Marquis de Nointel's embassy, and his drawings are sometimes the only record of them. On 26 September 1687, during Morosini's siege, a Venetian mortar round fired from the Hill of Philopappos blew up the gunpowder the Ottomans kept in the Parthenon, where families of the local Turkish community had also taken shelter. Three of the four cella walls nearly collapsed, three-fifths of the frieze fell, and about three hundred people were killed. Morosini then tried to loot the figure of Poseidon and Athena's horses from the west pediment; they fell and smashed as his soldiers tried to detach them. From 1801 agents of Lord Elgin removed about half the surviving sculptures, saying they had Ottoman permission, though that was later disputed. The British government bought the marbles in 1816 and passed them to the British Museum, and Lord Byron likened the removal to looting.
zh:
据修昔底德记载，伯里克利曾向雅典人说明，帕特农神庙里雅典娜像上的四十塔兰同黄金全部可以拆下，危急时取用，事后再补。神庙始建于公元前447年，当时提洛同盟势力正强。建筑师是伊克蒂诺斯和卡利克拉特，整座神庙几乎没有一条直线：台基中央微微上拱，柱身鼓胀并稍向内倾。菲狄亚斯所作的雅典娜·帕特农巨像高约十三米，大概以柏木为骨架、外包象牙和金片，在第一个千年的某个时候失落，年代不详。神庙后来成了基督教堂，在拉丁人统治的约250年间是天主教的圣母堂，西南角建有钟楼。1436年，安科纳的齐里亚科是古代以后第一个描述它并称呼它本名的人，说它是「菲狄亚斯的神圣作品」。

奥斯曼人1458年占领卫城后，教堂改成清真寺：钟楼加高为宣礼塔，后殿改为米哈拉布，墙上圣像被白灰覆盖，但结构仍然完整。埃夫利亚·切莱比称它是非人力所造的坚不可摧的堡垒，祈愿它永世长存。法国画家雅克·卡雷随诺安特尔侯爵的使团画下它的雕刻，这些画有时是雕刻仅存的记录。1687年9月26日，莫罗西尼率威尼斯军队攻城，一发迫击炮弹从菲洛帕波斯山射出，炸了奥斯曼人存在帕特农里的火药；当地土耳其人家的妇孺也躲在里面。内殿四面墙有三面几乎倒塌，五分之三的浮雕带坠落，约三百人丧命。莫罗西尼随后想把西三角墙上的波塞冬像和雅典娜的马群劫走，兵士动手拆卸时雕像坠地摔碎。1801年起，埃尔金伯爵的代理人拆走约一半幸存雕刻，称已得奥斯曼当局许可，其合法性有争议。1816年英国政府买下这批石雕，交给大英博物馆；拜伦勋爵则把这种做法比作劫掠。

en:
Hagia Sophia is famous for the light that reflects everywhere in the nave and makes the dome look as if it hovered; forty windows circle its base. Justinian I began the church in 532 after the Nika riots destroyed its predecessor. The architects were Anthemius of Tralles and Isidore of Miletus, and more than ten thousand people worked on it. It was consecrated on 27 December 537, five years and ten months after building began, under a dome about 31 metres across that rests on pendentives. Western visitors before 1453 found it dilapidated, with several doors fallen from their hinges. On 12 December 1452 Isidore of Kiev proclaimed there the union of the Catholic and Orthodox churches decided at Florence, and Doukas says the anti-union Orthodox avoided the cathedral as tainted.

In the last days of the siege, on 21 May 1453, Nestor Iskander's tale records a flame that circled the whole neck of the church before rising to heaven, an omen read as the Holy Spirit leaving the city. Doukas says that when the walls fell, people crowded into the church because of a prophecy: the Turks would slaughter the Romans as far as the Column of Constantine, where an angel would give a sword to a poor man and the Turks would be driven back to Persia. They closed the gates. Ottoman troops battered the doors down and divided the people inside as spoils. When Mehmed II entered, a scholar climbed the ambo and recited the shahada, and Mehmed is reported to have taken a sword to a soldier who tried to pry up a paving slab of Proconnesian marble. The first Friday prayer was held on 1 June 1453, and Aya Sofya became Istanbul's first imperial mosque.

Later sultans changed it to suit the new rite. Bayezid II built a minaret at the northeast corner. Suleiman brought two colossal candlesticks from his conquest of Hungary and set them on either side of the mihrab. Under Selim II, Mimar Sinan, who was also an earthquake engineer, braced the tired Byzantine walls with exterior supports, built two minarets at the west end and the tomb of Selim II.
zh:
圣索菲亚大教堂以中厅里四处映照的光线闻名，穹顶看上去像悬在半空，穹座一圈开着四十扇窗。532年尼卡暴动烧毁前代教堂后，查士丁尼一世动工兴建这座教堂，设计者是特拉勒斯的安提莫斯和米利都的伊西多尔，参与施工的有一万多人。537年12月27日献堂，距动工五年十个月，直径约31米的穹顶架在三角帆拱上。1453年以前，西方访客见到的教堂已经破败，好几扇门从铰链上脱落。1452年12月12日，基辅的伊西多尔在此宣布佛罗伦萨会议决定的天主教与东正教合一，杜卡斯说，反对合一的东正教徒把这座大堂当作受了玷污的地方，不再来。

围城最后几天，即1453年5月21日，内斯托尔·伊斯坎德尔的《夺取沙皇城记》记载，一团火焰绕着教堂的颈部转了很久，然后升入天空，人们把它解读成圣灵离城而去的预兆。杜卡斯说，城墙被攻破后，人们涌进这座教堂，是因为一则预言：土耳其人会屠杀罗马人，一直杀到君士坦丁圆柱，那时一位天使会把剑交给一个穷人，土耳其人就会被赶回波斯。他们关上了门。奥斯曼军队撞开大门，里面的人被胜利者当作战利品分掉。穆罕默德二世入内后，一位宗教学者登上读经台念诵清真言；据说穆罕默德还拔剑制止一名士兵撬起普罗孔尼索斯大理石地砖。6月1日举行了第一次主麻礼拜，圣索菲亚成为伊斯坦布尔第一座帝国清真寺。

此后的苏丹按新的礼仪改建它。巴耶济德二世在东北角增建一座宣礼塔。苏莱曼一世把匈牙利战事中带回的两座巨型烛台放在米哈拉布两侧。塞利姆二世在位时，兼任抗震工程师的米马尔·锡南用外加支撑加固了疲惫的拜占庭墙体，在西端增建两座宣礼塔，并建了塞利姆二世陵。

en:
Some Ottoman jurists forbade Muslims to pray in the Sultan Ahmed Mosque. The ulema held that a sultan should pay for an imperial mosque from the spoils of conquest, and Ahmed I had won no major victory; he took the money from a strained treasury. The treaty of Zsitvatorok in 1606, which for the first time had the sultan address the Holy Roman Emperor as padishah, was seen as a blow to Ottoman prestige, and Ahmed hoped a great mosque would win God's favour. Work began in 1609 on the southeast side of the old Hippodrome, across from Hagia Sophia. The ground held the Hippodrome's bleachers and imperial box and the palaces of viziers including Sokollu Mehmed Pasha, so the state had to carry out a costly expropriation.

Sedefkar Mehmed Agha built the mosque, a pupil of Sinan. Its prayer hall covers 64 by 72 metres under a central dome 43 metres high and 23.5 metres across, carried on four semi-domes, and a broad courtyard lies in front. Six minarets rise around it, four at the corners of the prayer hall and two at the outer corners of the courtyard. Folklore says the architect misheard the sultan's order for 'altin minareler', gold minarets, as 'alti minare', six minarets; the story is probably an invention. The walls carry more than twenty thousand Iznik tiles in blue, green and white, and the tile works were so burdened that in 1613 the sultan forbade the making of tiles for anyone else. Over two hundred coloured-glass windows light the hall, and the calligraphy was by Seyyid Kasim Gubari of Diyarbakir. Europeans call it the Blue Mosque for its blue tones.

Around it stood madrasas, a hospital, a soup kitchen, a bath, shops and Ahmed's tomb. The mosque opened in 1617, the year the sultan died, and the last construction accounts were signed by his successor, Mustafa I.
zh:
苏丹艾哈迈德清真寺落成前后，一些奥斯曼法学家甚至禁止穆斯林到这里礼拜。教法学者认为，苏丹建帝国清真寺应当用征战的战利品支付，而艾哈迈德一世没有取得重大胜利，只能动用吃紧的国库。1606年的日特瓦托罗克和约第一次让苏丹称神圣罗马皇帝为帕迪沙，被视为奥斯曼声望受挫，艾哈迈德希望靠一座大清真寺求得真主的恩惠。1609年，工程在旧赛马场东南侧动工，正对圣索菲亚大教堂。这里原有赛马场看台和皇家包厢，还有索科卢·穆罕默德帕夏等维齐尔的宅邸，国家必须花大价钱征购土地。

建筑师是锡南的弟子塞德夫卡尔·穆罕默德阿迦。礼拜殿占地64米乘72米，中央穹顶高43米、直径23.5米，由四座半穹顶承接，殿前是宽阔庭院。六座宣礼塔环立四周，四座在礼拜殿四角，两座在庭院外角。相传建筑师把苏丹要的「金宣礼塔」听成了「六座宣礼塔」，这个故事多半出于附会。殿内墙面用了两万多块蓝、绿、白色调的伊兹尼克瓷砖，烧瓷作坊忙不过来，1613年苏丹下令禁止为他人烧制瓷砖；二百多扇彩色玻璃窗给大殿采光，经文由迪亚巴克尔人赛义德·卡西姆·古巴里书写；偏蓝的色调让欧洲人称它为蓝色清真寺。

寺周建有经学院、医院、施粥场、浴场、店铺，以及艾哈迈德的陵墓。清真寺1617年举行开幕礼，艾哈迈德一世也在同年去世；最后一批工程账目由继任者穆斯塔法一世签署。

en:
The Bibliotheca Corviniana took its name from the raven on the arms of Matthias Corvinus, and a bookbinding workshop in Buda developed a distinctive leather binding for his books. In 1444 none of this existed: the library was still only a possibility inside Buda's old Gothic palace. Matthias became king in 1458 and began collecting in the 1460s, with copyists, translators and an international network of buyers, and had volumes made to order in Florentine workshops. After he married Beatrice of Naples in 1476, Italian humanists, painters and craftsmen came to Buda, and the king rebuilt the palace in an early Renaissance style, adding an Italian loggia and two rooms with golden ceilings: one was the library, the other a passage painted with the twelve signs of the zodiac.

The shelves held Greek and Latin classics beside theology, law, history, geography, medicine, architecture and natural science. Hungarian estimates put about 2,500 codices in the collection when Matthias died in 1490, some finished in Florence and never delivered. A Florentine humanist, Bartolomeo della Fonte, wrote that Lorenzo de' Medici's own Greek and Latin library was encouraged by the Hungarian king's example. That patronage ended with Matthias. After the defeat at Mohács in 1526, Suleiman spared the royal palace but carried off its bronze statues, among them the Hercules whom the king's humanists compared with Matthias, and many volumes went to Istanbul; others were given away, dispersed or lost. About 216 Corvinae can still be traced, and some lost volumes held the only copies of ancient works, including the full works of Hypereides.
zh:
科尔文纳图书馆（Bibliotheca Corviniana）得名于马加什·科尔温纹章上的渡鸦，布达的装订作坊还专为他的藏书发展出一种独特的皮面装帧。1444年这一切还不存在，图书馆只是布达旧哥特王宫里的一处空位。马加什1458年即位，1460年代起开始藏书，靠抄写员、译者和遍布各国的采购网络，还向佛罗伦萨的作坊订制抄本。1476年他迎娶那不勒斯的贝亚特丽切后，意大利人文主义者、画家和工匠来到布达，国王把王宫改建成早期文艺复兴风格，添了意大利式敞廊，还有两间金色天花板的厅廊：一间是图书馆，另一间是绘有黄道十二宫的走廊。

书架上，希腊语和拉丁语古典著作与神学、法律、历史、地理、医学、建筑、自然科学书籍并列。据匈牙利学者估算，马加什1490年去世时馆藏约有2500部抄本，其中有些已在佛罗伦萨完成，却没有运到布达。佛罗伦萨人文主义者巴尔托洛梅奥·德拉·丰特写道，洛伦佐·德·美第奇建立自己的希腊语、拉丁语图书馆，就受到这位匈牙利国王的启发。马加什一死，这种扶持也随之中断。1526年匈牙利在摩哈赤战败后，苏莱曼放过了王宫，却运走了宫中的青铜雕像，其中有宫廷人文主义者拿来比附马加什的赫拉克勒斯像；大量抄本也运往伊斯坦布尔，另一些被赠送、流散或遗失。可考的科尔文纳抄本约216部；已散佚的抄本中，有几部保存着古代著作的唯一文本，包括许佩里德斯的全部作品。

en:
Kremnica ducats were rated the hardest currency in Central Europe because their gold stayed consistently pure, and records report 21.5 million of them struck at the town's mint over its history. The Golden City is the whole mining town: gold veins, shafts, the mint, a double ring of walls and the castle on the hill above the square. On 17 November 1328 King Charles Robert of Anjou granted the settlement of Cremnychbana the privileges of a free royal mining and minting town and founded a mint there; it struck gold florins from 1335. The Chamber Count, head of the mining and minting chamber, sat in Kremnica and supervised the mines and mints of twelve counties for the crown. Settlers came from Italy, Bavaria, Austria, Silesia and Bohemia, among them minters from Kutná Hora. On the castle hill a Romanesque church with its graveyard and ossuary was ringed with fortifications, which by the late fourteenth century enclosed the Chamber Count's palace and a store for the gold dug out and the coins struck. By the fifteenth century Kremnica ranked second among the towns of the Kingdom of Hungary, and its deputies took the place after Buda's in the Diet.

After the middle of the fifteenth century the castle was rebuilt so that its defenders could stand against firearms. The Miner's Bastion began as a small chapel of the Nativity of the Virgin, built for a burgher named Langsfelder; apparently in the sixteenth century, under the Turkish threat, its nave was pulled down and the presbytery became an open bastion. The tower of St Catherine's church was badly damaged by fire in 1560 and finished afterwards in Renaissance style, and in 1588 Peter Gräf cast the great Renaissance bell Urban for the Clock Tower. Kremnica became a stronghold of the Reformation and a centre of medal making, above all the mostly religious medals of Joachim Deschler. Meanwhile the miners had to dig deeper, groundwater filled the shafts, and mining grew less profitable. Between 1765 and 1772 the town put up a plague column, one of the last such monuments in the Habsburg lands.
zh:
克雷姆尼察杜卡特被视为中欧最硬的通货，因为它的金子成色始终如一；记录称克雷姆尼察造币厂历来共铸出2150万枚。黄金城克雷姆尼察指的是整座矿城：金脉、竖井、造币厂、双重城墙，以及高踞广场上方山丘的城堡。1328年11月17日，匈牙利国王安茹的查理·罗贝尔授予克雷姆尼察班亚（Cremnychbana）村镇自由王家矿业和造币城镇的特权，并在此设立造币厂；造币厂自1335年起铸造金弗罗林。矿务总管是矿业与造币总署的首脑，驻在克雷姆尼察，替王室监管十二个州的矿山和造币厂。移民来自意大利、巴伐利亚、奥地利、西里西亚和波希米亚，其中有来自库特纳霍拉的造币工匠。城堡山上原有一座带墓地和藏骨堂的罗马式教堂，外围筑起工事，14世纪末，工事里已有矿务总管的宫邸，以及存放开采出的黄金和新铸钱币的库房。到15世纪，克雷姆尼察在匈牙利王国各城中位居第二，议会里其代表的席次仅次于布达。

15世纪中叶以后，城堡经过改建，使守军能够抵御火器。矿工棱堡最初是市民朗斯费尔德出资建的圣母降生小堂；大概在16世纪，因奥斯曼人的威胁，小堂中殿被拆，圣所改成开放的棱堡。圣凯瑟琳教堂的塔楼1560年毁于火灾，后来按文艺复兴样式续建完成；1588年，彼得·格雷夫为钟楼铸造了文艺复兴风格的大钟「乌尔班」。克雷姆尼察成为宗教改革的据点，也是奖章制作中心，尤其是约阿希姆·德施勒刻制的宗教题材奖章。同时，矿工不得不越挖越深，竖井里积满地下水，采矿越来越不划算。1765年至1772年，城里立起一座瘟疫柱，是哈布斯堡领地上最晚建成的此类纪念碑之一。

en:
Notre-Dame rises on the Ile de la Cite, an island in the Seine. Bishop Maurice de Sully had the earlier cathedral there pulled down and the cornerstone laid in 1163 before Louis VII and Pope Alexander III, and the work ran on for nearly two centuries. In the fourteenth century the choir was given flying buttresses with a span of fifteen metres, and the two transept roses are among the largest in Europe. In 1239 Saint Louis deposited the Crown of Thorns, which he had bought from the Latin emperor Baldwin II, in the cathedral until the Sainte-Chapelle was ready to receive it. By 1444 the great church had stood finished for about a century.

In December 1431 the ten-year-old Henry VI of England was crowned king of France in Notre-Dame, because Reims, the traditional coronation church, was in French hands. In 1572 Marguerite de Valois married the Protestant Henry of Navarre; the bride walked to the church on a raised platform from the bishop's palace, and the bridegroom, a Huguenot, had to stay outside during the mass. The St Bartholomew's Day massacre began six days later. In 1756 the canons, finding the church too dark, had the medieval stained glass removed except for the rose windows. In the Revolution the cathedral became a Temple of Reason: the twenty-eight statues of the kings of Judah on the west front were beheaded because they were taken for kings of France, most of the bells were melted down, and the building served as a warehouse. Napoleon had it formally returned to Catholic worship on 18 April 1802.
zh:
巴黎圣母院立在塞纳河中的老城岛西岱岛上。1163年，主教莫里斯·德·叙利命人平掉岛上的旧教堂，在路易七世和教宗亚历山大三世面前放下第一块基石，工程持续了近两百年。14世纪，唱诗班席加上了跨度15米的飞扶壁；耳堂两面玫瑰窗属于欧洲最大的一批。1239年，圣王路易把从拉丁皇帝鲍德温二世手中买来的荆冠先存放在圣母院，待圣礼拜堂建成后再行安放。到1444年，这座大教堂已经落成约一百年了。

1431年12月，十岁的英格兰国王亨利六世在圣母院加冕为法兰西国王，因为传统的加冕教堂兰斯掌握在法国人手里。1572年，玛格丽特·德·瓦卢瓦嫁给新教徒纳瓦拉的亨利，新娘沿着从主教府搭到教堂的高台走来，新郎是胡格诺教徒，弥撒期间只能留在教堂外面。六天后，圣巴托洛缪之夜的屠杀开始。1756年，司铎们嫌堂内太暗，把除玫瑰窗外的中世纪彩窗尽数拆去。大革命中教堂被改成理性庙：西立面上二十八尊犹大列王像被当成法兰西国王，全部砍头；多数大钟被拆下熔毁，教堂则当了仓库。1802年4月18日，拿破仑正式把它交还天主教礼拜。

en:
In 1444 the Versailles area was small villages, farmland and woodland, with marshes around the hill where Louis XIII built a modest brick-and-stone hunting lodge in 1623. Courtiers scorned the place, and one wrote that the lodge would not inspire vanity in the simplest gentleman. After it was enlarged into a chateau, Louis XIII still forbade his queen to sleep there. His son thought very differently. In August 1661 Louis XIV was a guest at a festival given by his finance minister Nicolas Fouquet at Vaux-le-Vicomte, and the house and gardens by Louis Le Vau, Andre Le Notre and Charles Le Brun impressed him, and the scale of Fouquet's display led him to imprison the minister that September and the same three men went on to shape Versailles. Louis XIV personally directed and inspected the plans. Jules Hardouin-Mansart took over in 1678 and built the 73-metre Hall of Mirrors. Its 17 mirrors, each made of many small panes, came from the royal glassworks founded to break the Venetian monopoly. According to a contemporary anecdote, the mirrors were Mansart's ploy to stop Le Brun from finding still more room to impress the king with his paintings.

The court moved in on 6 May 1682 and stayed, under a strict etiquette, until 1789 apart from the years of the regency. Louis XIV received the Doge of Genoa, an embassy from Ayutthaya and one from Safavid Iran. He died there on 1 September 1715, and the regent took the five-year-old Louis XV to Vincennes and then Paris. At Christmas 1763 the seven-year-old Mozart played several works during his stay at the palace. On 5 October 1789 a crowd of several thousand marched from the markets of Paris to the palace over the price of bread and forced the royal family back to Paris the next day. The furnishings were sold in seventeen thousand lots and the fleurs-de-lys were chiselled off the walls. Napoleon, as emperor, considered making Versailles his residence and gave up because of the cost.
zh:
1444年，凡尔赛宫日后矗立之处是几个小村庄、农田和林地，山丘四周是沼泽；1623年，路易十三在这座山丘上盖了一座朴素的砖石猎舍。廷臣们看不起这个地方，其中一人写道，这座猎舍连最普通的绅士也引不起虚荣。猎舍扩建成城堡之后，路易十三仍不许王后在此过夜。他的儿子想法大不相同。1661年8月，路易十四赴财政大臣尼古拉·富凯在沃勒维孔特宫举办的宴会，路易·勒沃、安德烈·勒诺特尔和夏尔·勒布伦所造的宫殿与花园给他留下深刻印象，富凯排场之大也让他在当年9月把这位大臣下狱；这三个人后来都参与了凡尔赛的营造。路易十四亲自过问和审阅图样。1678年，于勒·阿杜安-芒萨尔接手，修起73米长的镜厅。厅里的17面镜子，每面由许多小镜片拼成，由为打破威尼斯垄断而设立的王家制镜厂供货。据当时的一则轶事，满墙镜子是芒萨尔的一招，为的是不让勒布伦有更多地方用画作去打动国王。

1682年5月6日宫廷迁入，在严格的礼仪之下一直住到1789年，只在摄政期间中断。路易十四在此接见过热那亚总督、阿瑜陀耶使团和萨法维伊朗使团。1715年9月1日他在凡尔赛去世，摄政把五岁的路易十五先带到万塞讷，再带回巴黎。1763年圣诞节，七岁的莫扎特在宫中小住，演奏了几首作品。1789年10月5日，数千人为面包的价钱从巴黎的市场一路走到宫前，第二天迫使王室一家回到巴黎。宫中陈设分一万七千批拍卖，墙上的百合花徽被凿掉。拿破仑称帝后考虑过以凡尔赛为居所，因花费太大作罢。

en:
The Palais des Papes stands on the Rocher des Doms above the Rhone, with 15,000 square metres of floor space, the largest Gothic palace in Europe. Benedict XII, an austere Cistercian, had the old bishop's palace pulled down and from 1335 built the fortified Palais Vieux around a cloister. His successors, above all the extravagant Clement VI, added the Palais Neuf, with a Grand Chapel 52 metres long. Simone Martini's pupil Matteo Giovanetti led the painters of the chapels, and the papal library held some two thousand volumes, the largest in Europe at the time. The building ate up much of the papacy's income while it went up.

The popes went back to Rome in 1377, and Avignon kept two antipopes. In 1398 Geoffrey Boucicaut's troops besieged Benedict XIII in the palace. He held out for five years before he escaped. A fire in 1413 destroyed the painted blue vault, spangled with gold stars, that decorated the Great Tinel. In 1433 Cardinal Pierre de Foix retook the palace as papal legate, and he lived there until his death. He was a capable administrator and a grand seigneur who spent without counting, and in 1444 the court in the palace was his.

Cardinal Clermont-Lodeve restored the chapels in 1516 and received Francis I there six times. In the night of 16 October 1791, during the quarrels over Avignon's annexation by France, some sixty prisoners were massacred in the old prisons of the palace and thrown into the ice-pit at the foot of the Tour de la Glaciere. After the Revolution the palace became a barracks and a prison. Under the Third Republic the remaining woodwork was cleared away and the frescoes were covered over. Soldiers stayed in it into the twentieth century.
zh:
教宗宫坐落在罗讷河畔的多姆岩上，楼面面积约一万五千平方米，是欧洲最大的哥特式宫殿。本笃十二世是个克己的西多会修士，他命人拆毁旧主教宫，1335年起围绕回廊筑起设防的旧宫。继任的教宗们，尤其是最讲排场的克雷芒六世，又加建了新宫和长52米的大礼拜堂。西蒙内·马蒂尼的学生马泰奥·焦万内蒂主持了礼拜堂的绘画，教宗藏书室收有约两千卷书，是当时欧洲最大的一批。营建期间，工程耗去了教廷的大部分收入。

1377年教宗迁回罗马，阿维尼翁留下了两位对立教宗。1398年，若弗鲁瓦·布西科的军队在宫中围困本笃十三世。他守了五年才逃脱。1413年一场大火烧毁了大提内尔厅的装饰，那是一片镶着金星的蓝色天幕和壁画。1433年，枢机皮埃尔·德·福瓦以教宗使节身份收复了宫殿，住到去世。他既是干练的行政官，又是挥金如土的大贵族，1444年时宫里的宫廷就是他的。

1516年，枢机克莱蒙-洛德夫修复了礼拜堂，并在宫中六次接待弗朗索瓦一世。1791年10月16日夜里，在阿维尼翁并入法国的纷争中，约六十名囚犯在宫内旧监狱遇害，尸体被扔进格拉西耶尔塔底的冰窖。大革命之后，宫殿改作兵营和监狱。第三共和国时期，残余的木构被清走，壁画被盖住。军队一直驻扎到20世纪。

en:
The Aljafería was raised on the plain outside the Roman walls of Saraqusta, the Muslim Zaragoza, where Muslim troops held their military displays. From 1065 Abu Ja'far Ahmad al-Muqtadir, second king of the Banu Hud, built it as a pleasure palace: in his own verses he called it the Palace of Joy and named its throne room the Golden Hall. The name it kept comes from Abu Ya'far, as he was called. A fortified rectangle with sixteen semicircular towers enclosed a courtyard with pools, rooms of mixtilinear arches and carved stucco painted red, blue and gold, and a small private mosque whose mihrab arch recalls the Great Mosque of Córdoba. Ceilings and carved wood reproduced the sky, to show the king of Zaragoza as heir to the caliphs. It is the only large Hispano-Muslim building of the taifa era that survives.

Alfonso I the Battler took Zaragoza in 1118, and from then on the palace belonged to the Christian kings of Aragon. Peter IV the Ceremonious extended it in the fourteenth century, adding a chapel and new Mudéjar halls beside the old rooms, and Spanish sources record rooms set aside for his wild beasts. In 1486 the old Troubadour Tower became a dungeon of the Inquisition, and prisoners later scratched graffiti on its walls. Ferdinand and Isabella then had a new palace built over the northern wing, by Mudéjar craftsmen. Its throne room has a gilded ceiling of thirty coffers, carved with their emblems of yoke and arrows and a Gordian knot with the motto 'Tanto monta' (cutting the knot or untying it, it is the same), and a frieze dated 1492 says they drove out the old enemy after freeing Andalusia from the Moors. In 1593 the palace was turned into a Renaissance fortress with a new moat, and later into barracks. The sieges of Zaragoza in the Peninsular War damaged it badly.
zh:
阿尔哈费里亚宫建在穆斯林的萨拉戈萨（阿拉伯语称萨拉库斯塔）罗马城墙外的平原上，那里是穆斯林军队举行阅兵演练的地方。1065年起，巴努·胡德王朝第二任君主阿布·雅法尔·艾哈迈德·穆克塔迪尔在此修建游乐宫殿：他在自己的诗里称它为「喜悦之宫」，把御座殿叫做「金厅」。宫名阿尔哈费里亚，来自他的称号阿布·雅法尔。十六座半圆形塔楼环着长方形的设防围墙，墙内有带水池的庭院、用混合线脚拱券和雕花灰泥装饰的殿堂，灰泥上涂着红、蓝和金色，还有一间私人小礼拜寺，米哈拉布的拱券仿自科尔多瓦大清真寺。天花板和木雕再现天穹，让萨拉戈萨的国王显得像哈里发的继承人。它是泰法时代仅存的大型伊斯兰宫殿。

1118年阿方索一世「战士」攻下萨拉戈萨，此后这里成为阿拉贡基督教国王的王宫。14世纪，礼仪者佩德罗四世扩建宫殿，在旧殿旁增建了礼拜堂和穆德哈尔风格的新厅，西班牙文资料还记有给他的猛兽预备的房间。1486年，宫里的旧塔（吟游诗人塔）成了宗教裁判所的监狱，囚犯后来在墙上留下大量涂鸦。随后天主教双王请穆德哈尔工匠在北翼之上另建一座新宫。其御座厅的镀金顶棚分三十格，雕着双王的轭与箭，还有戈耳狄俄斯之结，配着格言「割断与解开，一样」，檐口的铭文题为1492年，称二人收复安达卢斯、驱逐了老敌人。1593年，宫殿被改造成带新壕沟的文艺复兴式要塞，后来又充作兵营。半岛战争中的萨拉戈萨围城使它受到严重破坏。

en:
Tradition reads the plan of El Escorial as a gridiron. On 10 August 1557, the feast of Saint Lawrence, Philip II's army beat the French at Saint-Quentin, and the foundation charter dedicated the new monastery to that saint, who was martyred in Rome by roasting on a grill; with four corner towers and the royal palace as the 'handle', the finished plan is said to recall it. The grill shape only emerged when Juan de Herrera closed the main facade and removed six towers, and the better-supported model is Josephus's description of the Temple of Solomon, with statues of David and Solomon flanking the basilica entrance. The building stands on the slope of Mount Abantos in the Sierra de Guadarrama, about forty-five kilometres northwest of Madrid, built of local grey granite. Philip meant it as a pantheon for his father and the new dynasty under Charles V's last will, apart from the old Trastamara burial places, and as a centre of study for the Counter-Reformation. The first stone was laid on 23 April 1563. Juan Bautista de Toledo, who had worked on Saint Peter's in Rome, designed it; after his death in 1567 Giovanni Battista Castello and then Herrera took over, and the works were declared finished in 1584. 'The work of El Escorial' became a Spanish byword for a job that never ends.

Monastery, palace, basilica, school and library shared one building. Hieronymite monks kept the offices while Philip's ambassadors travelled his empire and neighbouring kingdoms buying manuscripts; over four hundred books prohibited by the Inquisition were kept there for experts only, and about 7,500 relics were housed in 507 reliquaries. As his health failed Philip worked from his rooms beside the high altar, where a window let him watch mass from his bed when gout confined him, and he died there on 13 September 1598. Most kings of Spain from Charles V onward lie in the Royal Pantheon. A fire in 1671 destroyed 5,280 manuscript codices, though the hall of printed books was saved. In the Peninsular War the monastery was sacked and the monks expelled.
zh:
相传埃斯科里亚尔修道院的平面是一只烤架。1557年8月10日圣洛伦索瞻礼日，腓力二世的军队在圣康坦击败法军，建院特许状把新修道院奉献给圣洛伦索；这位圣徒在罗马被放在烤架上炙烤殉道，而成形的平面有四角塔楼，王宫部分突出如柄，据说就是在模仿烤架。不过烤架的形状要到胡安·德·埃雷拉封闭正立面、去掉六座塔楼后才出现，更有依据的原型是约瑟夫斯笔下的所罗门圣殿，大殿入口两侧立着大卫和所罗门的雕像。修道院坐落在瓜达拉马山的阿万托斯山坡上，马德里西北约45公里，用当地的灰色花岗岩砌成。腓力要按卡洛斯五世的遗嘱把它建成父亲和新王朝的陵寝，与特拉斯塔马拉家族的旧墓地分开，并使它成为反宗教改革的学术中心。1563年4月23日奠基，曾参与罗马圣彼得大教堂工程的胡安·包蒂斯塔·德·托莱多负责设计；他1567年去世后，先后由乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·卡斯泰洛和他的弟子埃雷拉接手，1584年宣告完工。西班牙语后来有句俗话：「埃斯科里亚尔的工程」，指一件做不完的事。

修道院、王宫、大殿、学校和图书馆共处一座建筑：赫罗尼莫会修士主持宗教事务，腓力派使节走遍帝国和邻国搜购抄本；四百多册被宗教裁判所查禁的书存放在馆中，只许专家翻阅，全院还藏有约7500件圣物，分装在507具圣物箱里。腓力晚年体弱，在大祭坛旁的寝室里理政，那里有一扇窗，痛风发作卧床时也能望见弥撒；1598年9月13日他死在这里。自卡洛斯五世起的西班牙国王大多葬于院中王家陵寝。1671年大火烧毁5280册手抄本，印刷本大厅幸而保住。半岛战争期间修道院遭洗劫，修士被驱逐。

en:
The Alhambra takes its name from al-Hamra, the red one, after the reddish rammed earth of its walls on the Sabika hill above Granada. In 1444 it was a palace-city apart from the town below, with at least six major palaces, a Friday mosque, baths, workshops and a tannery. The Sultan's Canal brought water from the Darro some six kilometres east, partly through tunnels in the bedrock. The sultan received embassies in the Hall of Ambassadors, a chamber 18 metres high inside the Comares Tower, under a wooden ceiling of 8,017 interlocking pieces laid out as the seven heavens.

In the Court of the Lions twelve marble lions ring a fountain whose basin carries a poem by the vizier-poet Ibn Zamrak. The hall on the south side is called the Hall of the Abencerrajes. Legend says that the father of Boabdil, the last sultan, invited the chiefs of that family to a banquet there and had them massacred, though the name has no historical link to the family. The Nasrid motto is carved across the walls again and again: 'No victor but God.'

After the surrender of Granada in January 1492, Ferdinand and Isabella took up residence in the Alhambra and stayed in Granada until 25 May. On 31 March they signed the edict expelling the Jews who would not convert, known as the Alhambra Decree. Columbus laid his plan before them in the Hall of Ambassadors, and they signed his contract on 17 April. In 1590 a gunpowder magazine exploded beside the Palace of the Lions and destroyed one of its muqarnas ceilings, replaced with a Baroque vault in 1714 for a visit by Philip V. The Tendilla family, whose second count was the first Spanish governor, held the post until Philip V dismissed the Marquis of Mondéjar in 1717 or 1718 for opposing him in the War of the Spanish Succession. Little state money followed, and by the early nineteenth century prisoners, disabled soldiers and other outcasts lived in the palaces.
zh:
阿尔罕布拉宫的名字来自阿拉伯语「哈姆拉」，意思是红色，因为萨比卡丘上的围墙用发红的夯土筑成，高踞格拉纳达之上。1444年，这里是一座自成一体的宫城，有至少六座大型王宫、一座聚礼清真寺、浴室、作坊和鞣皮作坊。苏丹渠从东面约六公里外的达罗河引水，部分水道凿在基岩隧洞里。苏丹在使节厅接见来使，这座18米高的方厅位于科马斯塔中，顶上8017块木件相扣，拼成象征七重天的藻井。

狮子庭院里，十二尊大理石狮子环着喷泉，泉沿刻着维齐尔诗人伊本·扎姆拉克的诗句。南面的一厅叫阿本塞拉赫斯厅。相传末代苏丹博阿布迪尔的父亲邀该家族的首领赴宴，在席间将他们尽数诛杀，不过这个厅名与这个家族并无史实上的联系。墙上反复刻着纳斯里德王朝的格言：「除真主外，绝无战胜者」。

1492年1月格拉纳达投降后，斐迪南和伊莎贝拉住进宫中，在格拉纳达待到5月25日。3月31日，他们在这里签署敕令，驱逐不肯改宗的犹太人，后世称《阿尔罕布拉宫敕令》。哥伦布在使节厅向他们陈述远航计划，4月17日双方签了合约。1590年，狮子宫旁一座火药库爆炸，毁了一厅的钟乳石顶棚，1714年为迎接费利佩五世来访，换成巴洛克拱顶。滕迪利亚家族的第二任伯爵是宫中第一任西班牙总督，该家族此后世代掌管宫务，到1717或1718年，费利佩五世因侯爵在西班牙王位继承战争中反对自己，撤了蒙德哈尔侯爵的职。此后国家很少拨款，到19世纪初，宫室里住着囚犯、伤残士兵和其他无依无靠的人。

en:
Beneath the turrets of the Belém Tower are carved beasts, among them a rhinoceros, and it probably shows the animal that reached Lisbon on 20 May 1515. The Sultan of Cambay had given it to Afonso de Albuquerque, who forwarded it to Manuel I, and it was unloaded near the site where the tower was being built. Dürer, who never saw it, made his Nuremberg woodcut from a letter and a sketch. In December Manuel sent the rhinoceros on to Pope Leo X, but the ship was wrecked off Liguria and the animal, chained to the deck, drowned.

King John II had ordered a strong fort for the mouth of the Tagus but died before any plans were drawn, and Manuel I took up the proposal some twenty years later. Francisco de Arruda, a military architect who had worked on Portuguese fortresses in Morocco, began the tower about 1514, on a basalt outcrop a short way from the shore, in place of an armed ship that had guarded the estuary. It was finished in 1519 or 1520. Raised of pale lioz limestone, it combines a bastion with a thirty-metre tower, carved with twisted ropes and knots, armillary spheres and the cross of the Order of Christ, while the domed turrets show Moorish influence. It celebrated the voyage to India and received the fleets arriving at the mouth of the river, the ceremonial sea entrance to Lisbon.

Its own guns decided little. In 1580 the garrison surrendered to the Duke of Alba's Spanish forces after a few hours of battle, and under Spanish rule the powder stores became dungeons for political prisoners. In 1589 Philip I of Portugal (Philip II of Spain) ordered the Italian engineer João Vicenzio Casale to build a better fort in place of the 'useless castle of São Vicente'; his three designs were never carried out. A plaque dated 1655 records the tower's role as a customs post, where vessels entering the harbour had to pay a tax. French troops were quartered in it from 1808, and afterwards Lord Beresford advised stronger batteries beside the bastion, because its walls were very low.
zh:
贝伦塔的角楼底座下雕着一些野兽，其中有一头犀牛，大概刻的就是1515年5月20日抵达里斯本的那头。它是坎贝苏丹送给阿方索·德·阿尔布克尔克的礼物，由后者转送曼努埃尔一世，卸船的地点就在贝伦塔的工地附近。丢勒从没见过这头犀牛，他根据寄到纽伦堡的一封信和一幅草图刻成了那幅著名的木刻。同年12月，曼努埃尔把犀牛转赠教皇利奥十世，船在利古里亚外海失事，被锁链拴在甲板上的犀牛溺水而死。

若昂二世曾下令在塔霍河口修一座坚固的堡垒，却在计划绘成之前去世，二十年左右之后曼努埃尔一世重提此议。军事建筑师弗朗西斯科·德·阿鲁达在摩洛哥参与过葡萄牙要塞的建造，约1514年在离岸不远的一处玄武岩礁石上动工，取代原先守卫河口的一艘武装大船。塔于1519或1520年建成，用浅色的利奥兹石灰岩砌成，由炮垒和三十米高的塔楼组成，雕着绞绳纹和绳结、浑天仪和基督骑士团的十字，带穹顶的角楼有摩尔建筑的影响。它纪念远航印度的壮举，迎接驶抵河口的船队，是里斯本的礼仪海门。

它自己的火炮没有起过多少作用。1580年，守军与阿尔瓦公爵的西班牙军队交战几个小时后投降，西班牙统治时期，火药库改成了关押政治犯的地牢。1589年，腓力一世（即西班牙的腓力二世）命意大利工程师若昂·文森齐奥·卡萨莱在「无用的圣文森特城堡」的位置上另建一座更坚固的要塞，他的三份设计都没有实施。一块1655年的牌匾记录了塔的海关职能：进入港口的船只都要缴税。1808年起法国部队驻进塔中，此后贝雷斯福德勋爵建议在炮垒两侧加设更坚固的炮台，因为炮垒的墙很低。

en:
On the chalk of Salisbury Plain stands a ring of about thirty upright sarsens, each some four metres high and twenty-five tons heavy, once capped by lintels held in place with mortise-and-tenon joints. Inside, five free-standing trilithons make a horseshoe open towards the midsummer sunrise, and among them stand smaller bluestones from the Preseli Hills of Wales, some 230 kilometres away. The monument was raised in stages between about 3100 and 1600 BC. The Middle Ages explained it with stories. In 1136 Geoffrey of Monmouth wrote that the stones were healing stones, raised by giants in a ring on an Irish mountain, and that Merlin brought them to Salisbury Plain as a memorial to British nobles killed by the Saxons. A folk tale says the Devil bought the stones from a woman in Ireland and carried them to the plain. When he boasted that no one would ever learn how they came there, a friar answered, 'That's what you think!', and the Devil hurled a stone that struck the friar's heel. It stuck in the ground, and that stone is called the Friar's Heel.

No one answered the riddle much better in the centuries that followed. In the 1620s the Duke of Buckingham had excavations dug, hoping for gold; they turned up a deer antler and some coal. From 1633 the architect Inigo Jones studied the stones and decided that the Romans had built them. In 1666 John Aubrey made the first accurate plan, noted the ring of 56 pits that now bears his name, and thought the monument a Druid temple. From 1719 William Stukeley surveyed the stones every summer, found that the midsummer sun rose over the Heel Stone, introduced the word trilithon, and was as sure as Aubrey that the Druids had built it. On 3 January 1797 one of the great trilithons fell.
zh:
索尔兹伯里平原的白垩地上立着一圈约三十根萨尔森巨石，每根高约4米、重约25吨，顶上原横架石楣，以榫头卯眼相接。圈内有五座独立的三石牌坊，排成马蹄形，开口正对夏至日出；其间立着较小的青石，产自约二百三十公里外威尔士的普雷塞利山。巨石阵从约公元前3100年起分几个阶段修成，至约公元前1600年停工。中世纪的人用故事解释它。1136年，蒙茅斯的杰弗里写道，这些是疗伤的石头，巨人把它们立成一圈在爱尔兰的一座山上，梅林将它们运到索尔兹伯里平原，作为被撒克逊人杀害的不列颠贵族的纪念碑。民间还有个故事：魔鬼从爱尔兰一个女人手里买下石头，运到平原上；它夸口说没人会知道石头是怎么来的，一名托钵修士回答「你想得美！」，魔鬼便掷出一块石头，砸中修士的脚跟。石头扎进地里，那块石头就叫「修士的脚跟」。

此后几百年里，没有人把这个谜解得更明白。1620年代，白金汉公爵主持发掘，指望找到黄金，只挖出一根鹿角和一些煤。从1633年起，建筑师伊尼戈·琼斯研究这些石头，断定是罗马人所建。1666年，约翰·奥布里画出第一张精确的平面图，记下后来以他命名的那圈五十六个坑，认为这是德鲁伊的神庙。1719年起，威廉·斯蒂克利每年夏天测绘石阵，发现夏至的太阳从踵石上方升起，还创用「trilithon」（三石牌坊）一词，同奥布里一样笃信是德鲁伊所建。1797年1月3日，一座大三石牌坊倒塌。

en:
In 1252 Haakon IV of Norway sent Henry III a polar bear, and it went fishing in the Thames from the Tower of London, tied to the bank by a chain; Louis IX of France sent an elephant two or three years later. The Tower began as the White Tower, begun in 1078 for William the Conqueror under Gundulf, bishop of Rochester, the first stone keep in England, raised against the Roman city wall beside the river. Later kings wrapped it in two concentric rings of walls and a moat and added St Thomas's Tower with the water gate later called Traitors' Gate. By the fifteenth century it was armoury, treasury, mint, record office, royal residence and zoo at once, and from the early fourteenth century kings lodged in it for several nights before their coronation and rode in procession to Westminster.

It was a prison too. In 1483 the young Edward V and his younger brother were lodged here and were last seen in public that June. Anne Boleyn, Margaret Pole, Catherine Howard and Lady Jane Grey were beheaded on Tower Green, a privilege of rank that spared them the jeering crowd on Tower Hill, where 112 people were beheaded over four centuries. The future Elizabeth I spent two months under arrest here in 1554. Walter Raleigh had his rooms altered to house his family, and wrote his History of the World there; released for a last voyage to Guiana, he went back to the block in 1618. The boldest attempt on the Crown Jewels came in 1671, when an Irish adventurer named Thomas Blood, disguised as a parson, bound the keeper, flattened the crown with a mallet and nearly carried it out. Charles II pardoned him and granted him Irish lands worth 500 pounds a year. Simon Fraser, Lord Lovat, executed on Tower Hill in 1747 after the Jacobite rising, was the last man beheaded in Britain.
zh:
1252年，挪威国王哈康四世送给亨利三世一头北极熊，它被链子拴在岸边，在泰晤士河里捉鱼；两三年后，法兰西的路易九世又送来一头大象。伦敦塔的起点是白塔，1078年征服者威廉下令动工，由罗切斯特主教贡杜夫监造，是英格兰第一座石砌主楼，借泰晤士河畔的罗马城墙而起。后来的国王又在白塔外围加上两圈同心城墙和一道护城河，并建起圣托马斯塔，即后来所称的「叛徒门」水门。到15世纪，伦敦塔同时是军械库、国库、造币厂、档案馆、王宫和兽苑；从14世纪初起，历代国王加冕前都在塔里住上几夜，再列队前往威斯敏斯特。
