它也是监狱。1483年，年幼的爱德华五世和弟弟被安置进塔，当年6月之后再没有人在公开场合见过他们。安妮·博林、玛格丽特·波尔、凯瑟琳·霍华德和简·格雷郡主在塔内绿地被斩首，这是身份高贵者才有的待遇，免得受塔山上围观人群的辱骂；四百年间另有112人在塔山被斩首。1554年，后来的伊丽莎白一世曾在此被关押两个月。沃尔特·雷利被关在塔中时，住处经过改造，好让家人同住，他的《世界史》就写于狱中；他为最后一次圭亚那远航获释，回来后仍在1618年被处决。1671年，爱尔兰冒险家托马斯·布拉德扮成牧师前来，捆住看守，用锤子把王冠砸扁，差点带走；查理二世赦免了他，还赐给他每年值五百英镑的爱尔兰土地。詹姆斯党起事之后，洛瓦特勋爵西蒙·弗雷瑟于1747年在塔山被斩首，他是不列颠最后一个被斩首的人。

en:
Edinburgh Castle sits on the plug of an extinct volcano, a dolerite crag 130 metres above sea level with cliffs on three sides and one gentler slope up from the east. The garrison's worry was water, for basalt is almost impermeable; a thirty-four-metre well still ran dry in drought or siege. A royal castle has stood on the rock since the eleventh century, and St Margaret's Chapel, built under David I, is the oldest building in Edinburgh. In the fifteenth century the castle was increasingly an arsenal, and by 1511 Robert Borthwick was casting bronze guns here, among them the Seven Sisters. The English captured them at Flodden, and Thomas Howard, the Lord Admiral, admired their graceful shape.

Mary, Queen of Scots, gave birth to James VI in a small room of the palace on 19 June 1566. Five years later William Kirkcaldy of Grange held the castle for her against the regent, and the Lang Siege of 1571 to 1573 began. He had forty cannon and only seven gunners, and bombarded the town below. In May 1573 about a thousand English troops with twenty-seven cannon from Berwick breached the walls, and David's Tower and the Constable's Tower fell into the entrance. The garrison threatened to mutiny, and Grange surrendered to the English; he was hanged at the Cross in August. Most of the medieval castle was lost in that bombardment, and the Half Moon Battery went up over David's Tower.

The Honours of Scotland, the crown, sceptre and sword, were found in a chest in a vault when the castle surrendered in 1573. After Cromwell took the castle in 1650, following a three-month siege, the Privy Council sent them in June 1651 to Dunnottar Castle hidden in sacks of wool. When Cromwell's troops blockaded Dunnottar, Christian Fletcher, wife of the Kinneff minister, took them out, and she and her husband buried them under the floor of Kinneff church until the Restoration. After the Union of 1707 they were locked in an oak chest and the Crown Room was walled up. In 1818 commissioners, Walter Scott among them, broke in and found all three wrapped in linen, as they had been left 111 years before.
zh:
爱丁堡城堡坐落在一座死火山的岩颈上：辉绿岩崖顶海拔130米，三面悬崖，只有东面一条较缓的坡可上。守军常年的难题是水：玄武岩几乎不透水，井凿到34米深，遇到干旱或围城仍会干涸。11世纪起岩上就有王室城堡，大卫一世时期所建的圣玛格丽特礼拜堂是爱丁堡最古老的建筑。15世纪这里越来越多地用作军械库，1511年时罗伯特·博思韦克已在此铸造青铜炮，其中有一组名为「七姊妹」。英军在弗洛登战役中缴获了它们，英国海军大臣托马斯·霍华德称赞它们形制优美、做工精良。

1566年6月19日，苏格兰女王玛丽在宫中的一间小屋里生下詹姆士六世。五年后，威廉·柯卡尔迪·格兰奇为她据守城堡，反对摄政，「长围」自1571年延续到1573年。他有四十门炮，却只有七个炮手，还向山下城区开炮。1573年5月，约一千名英军带着从贝里克调来的二十七门炮轰塌城墙，大卫塔和康斯特布尔塔倒塌，堵住了入口。守军威胁哗变，格兰奇向英军投降，8月在爱丁堡市集十字被处以绞刑。中世纪城堡大半毁于这场炮战，半月炮台就建在大卫塔的残基之上。

苏格兰王权仪仗，即王冠、权杖和宝剑，1573年城堡投降时是在拱顶里的一只箱子中找到的。1650年克伦威尔围城三个月攻下城堡之后，枢密院于1651年6月把仪仗藏在羊毛袋里送往邓诺塔。克伦威尔的军队封锁邓诺塔时，金内夫牧师的妻子克里斯蒂安·弗莱彻把仪仗取了出来，她和丈夫把它们埋在金内夫教堂的地板下，直到王政复辟。1707年联合之后，仪仗被锁进一只橡木柜，王冠室的门也被砌死。1818年，以司各特为成员之一的委员会破门而入，发现三件仪仗用亚麻布包着，和111年前封存时一样。

en:
The Kraków Cloth Hall began as two rows of cloth stalls facing each other in the middle of the Main Market, with a lane between them that was closed off at both ends at night. Bolesław V promised stone stalls in the 1257 town charter, and around 1300 the passage received its roof. Before 1358 Casimir III replaced it with a Gothic hall 108 metres long and ten metres wide. Two rows of stalls, each 7.5 metres deep, ran along the central hall, and eighteen vaulted booths opened onto it through pointed or round-arched doorways. In the fifteenth century, its golden age, eastern merchants brought spices, silk, leather and wax into this passage, while Kraków sent out textiles, lead and salt from Wieliczka.

Fire destroyed the Gothic hall in 1555, and the rebuilding of 1556-1559 gave it its Renaissance form. Master Pankracy covered the long hall with a barrel vault, Santi Gucci designed the attic, arcaded and crowned with a row of carved mascarons, and Jan Maria Padovano added columned loggias. In 1601 a passage was cut across the building. After Prince Józef Poniatowski briefly liberated Kraków from the Austrians in 1809, a ball was held in the Cloth Hall.
zh:
克拉科夫纺织会馆最初只是主市场中央两排相对的布摊，中间一条小巷，入夜后两端关闭。1257年博莱斯瓦夫五世颁发设城特许状，承诺修建石质布摊；约1300年，通道加上了屋顶。1358年以前，卡齐米日三世把它改建成一座长108米、宽10米的哥特大殿。中央大厅两侧各有深7.5米的摊位带，18个带拱顶的铺位经尖拱或半圆拱门洞朝向大厅。15世纪是它的黄金时代，东方商人把香料、丝绸、皮革和蜂蜡带进这条通道，克拉科夫则向外运出纺织品、铅和维利奇卡盐。

1555年大火烧毁哥特会馆，1556至1559年的重建使它有了文艺复兴的面貌。匠师潘克拉齐为长厅加上筒形拱顶，圣蒂·古奇设计了阿提卡墙，墙上有拱券分格，顶端排着一列怪面雕饰，扬·马里亚·帕多瓦诺则增建柱廊。1601年，工匠又横向凿穿会馆，开出一条通道。1809年约泽夫·波尼亚托夫斯基亲王暂时从奥地利人手中解放克拉科夫后，纺织会馆里举行了一场舞会。

en:
Prague Castle runs for some 570 metres along the hilltop above the Vltava, and its centre is St Vitus Cathedral, where the kings of Bohemia were crowned and buried. When Prague became an archbishopric in 1344, King John laid the foundation stone of a new Gothic minster. Matthias of Arras, summoned from Avignon, planned a French-style cathedral on the model of Rodez and Narbonne and died with only the east end of the choir built. Peter Parler, twenty-three years old, took over the lodge and worked the stone like sculpture: the busts on the triforium show the royal family, the bishops and the two master builders, Parler among them. His St Wenceslas Chapel is sheathed below in more than 1,300 semi-precious stones around paintings of the Passion, and a door with seven locks leads to the crown jewels. The Hussite wars stopped the work, and a great fire in 1541 destroyed large parts of the castle. The minster stayed half-finished for centuries, closed by a provisional wall, with a timber-roofed structure where the nave should have been.

Below the castle, the Charles Bridge carries the old coronation road across the river. Legend says that Charles IV, a believer in numerology, laid the first stone himself at 5.31 on the morning of 9 July 1357: written out as digits, 135797531 reads the same in both directions, and the emperor held that such a number would make the bridge strong. It was finished in 1402, runs 516 metres on sixteen arches between three bridge towers, and for more than four centuries was the only fixed crossing of the Vltava at Prague. In 1621, after the White Mountain, the severed heads of the executed rebel leaders were fixed to the Old Town bridge tower as a warning. In 1648 the Swedes, who held the Lesser Town bank, tried to push into the Old Town and the heaviest fighting took place on the bridge itself. From the 1680s an avenue of thirty statues, mostly baroque, went up along the parapet.
zh:
布拉格历史中心以城堡为冠。布拉格城堡沿伏尔塔瓦河畔的山脊绵延约五百七十米，核心是圣维特大教堂，波希米亚国王在这里加冕，也葬在这里。1344年布拉格升为大主教区，国王约翰为新建的哥特式大教堂奠基。从阿维尼翁召来的阿拉斯的马提亚斯（Matthias of Arras）按罗德兹和纳博讷两座南法大教堂的样式设计法式教堂，去世时只建起唱诗班席的东端。二十三岁的彼得·帕尔莱日（Peter Parler）接掌石匠作坊，把石料当雕塑来做：楼廊上的半身像刻着王室成员、主教和两位总建筑师，帕尔莱日本人也在其中。他建的圣瓦茨拉夫礼拜堂，下半部墙面镶嵌一千三百多块半宝石，环绕着耶稣受难组画，一扇配七把锁的小门通往王冠珍宝。胡斯战争使工程中断，1541年一场大火又烧毁城堡的大片建筑。此后许多世纪里大教堂一直没有建完：横厅用临时墙封堵，本该建中殿的地方盖着木屋顶。

城堡脚下，查理大桥载着旧日的加冕大道跨过伏尔塔瓦河。相传笃信数字术的查理四世亲手放下第一块基石，时间是1357年7月9日清晨5时31分：把数字连起来是135797531，正读反读都一样，皇帝认为这样的数字能让大桥坚固。桥1402年完工，长五百一十六米，十六个桥拱，三座桥头塔拱卫，此后四个多世纪里是布拉格唯一的固定过河通道。1621年白山战败后，被处死的叛乱首领的头颅悬挂在老城桥塔上示众。1648年，占据小城河岸的瑞典军队想攻入老城，最激烈的战斗就发生在桥上。从1680年代起，三十尊雕像沿栏杆立起，多数是巴洛克风格。

en:
Trakai Castle stands on an island in Lake Galvė, west of Vilnius, built of red Gothic brick with stone kept for the foundations and the upper walls. Kęstutis began the stone fortress in the second half of the fourteenth century and moved his residence and treasury there; Teutonic troops badly damaged it in 1377. After Jogaila and Vytautas reconciled and Vytautas recovered Trakai in 1392, a second building campaign lasted until about 1409, and the Order's own stonemason Radike apparently supervised the work during a truce, four years before Grunwald. On the southern side a six-storey keep 35 metres high, with movable gates, held a chapel and living quarters. It was linked to the multi-storey Ducal Palace around an inner yard, its Ducal Hall, about 10 by 21 metres, surpassed in size only by the hall of the Upper Palace in Vilnius Castle. Later work added corner towers and a gatehouse, and in the lake's high water of the time a moat just wide enough for small boats separated palace from castle, crossed by gates that could be raised.

After Grunwald removed the Teutonic threat, the island became less a frontier fort than a decorated residence, with frescoes in the palace and foreign envoys received in its hall. A visitor who saw it in 1414, Guillebert de Lannoy, described a castle 'completely new, built from bricks following French pattern'. Jogaila visited thirteen times between 1413 and 1430. Vytautas died there on 27 October 1430, while the envoys carrying the papers for his coronation as king of Lithuania were stopped at the Polish border. The archive of the grand duchy, the Lithuanian Metrica, was kept in the castle until 1511. Later the castle served as a prison, and under Sigismund Augustus it was redecorated in Renaissance style and briefly served as a royal summer residence. The Muscovite war of 1655 to 1660 damaged it, and it was not rebuilt but gradually fell into disrepair.
zh:
特拉凯城堡立在维尔纽斯以西加尔瓦湖的一座岛上，用红色哥特砖砌成，只在地基和墙体上部使用石块。14世纪后半叶，科斯图提斯在岛上动工修建石砌要塞，并把住所和财库迁到这里；1377年条顿骑士团的进攻使它严重受损。约盖拉与维陶塔斯和解、维陶塔斯1392年收复特拉凯之后，第二轮工程持续到约1409年，据称休战期间监工的是骑士团自己的石匠拉德克，时间在格伦瓦尔德战役前四年。南侧立起一座35米高的六层主楼，设有可升降闸门，内有小堂和住所。主楼连着有内院的多层公爵宫，宫中的公爵厅约10米宽、21米长，只有维尔纽斯城堡群的上宫比它大。后来又添了角楼和门楼；当时加尔瓦湖水位较高，宫殿与城堡之间隔着一道只容小船通过的窄壕，两边以可吊起的闸门相连。

格伦瓦尔德战役解除条顿威胁后，这座湖心岛更多成了装饰一新的王公住所，宫中绘有湿壁画，外国使节在大厅受接见。1414年，吉勒贝尔·德·拉努瓦见到一座「全新的砖筑城堡，依照法式样式建造」。约盖拉在1413至1430年间来过十三次。1430年10月27日，维陶塔斯在堡中去世，为他运送立陶宛国王加冕文书的使者当时被拦在波兰边境。立陶宛大公国的档案「立陶宛登记簿」在堡中存放到1511年。后来这里一度用作监狱，齐格蒙特·奥古斯特时期按文艺复兴风格重新装饰，短期充作王室夏宫。1655至1660年的莫斯科战争使城堡受损，此后没有再修，逐渐荒废。

en:
The Kiev Pechersk Lavra began as a cave. Tradition dates it to 1051, when the monk Anthony, back from Mount Athos, settled in the hillside cave above the Dnieper that the priest Hilarion had dug for himself. Disciples gathered, Theodosius of Kursk among them, and when they numbered twelve they built a church and cells; Anthony moved to a neighbouring hill and dug a new cave. The brothers lived by the communal rule of Theodore the Studite. Theodosius ran a hospice for beggars, the blind and the lame on a tenth of the house's income, and every Saturday a cart of bread went out to the prisoners. The stone Dormition Cathedral was consecrated in 1089, its frescoes and mosaics painted by artists from Constantinople. Once the monks had moved into the main monastery, the caves became their burial place, the bodies laid in niches along the corridor walls, and princes of the Lithuanian era, among them Konstanty Ostrogski, victor of Orsha, were buried in the lavra.

Raiders sacked the lavra again and again; the Mongols in 1240 were the worst, and in 1482 Crimean Tatars burned and plundered it. After the Union of Brest the monastery became a prize between the Orthodox and Catholic communities, and the Orthodox kept it with the support of the Ostrogski princes. The preacher Joannicius Galiatovsky published a legend: when a Polish army besieged the monastery in 1630, the Mother of God turned a 'fiery rain' against the invaders and saved the monks. At the turn of the eighteenth century Hetman Ivan Mazepa paid for a large rebuilding and for new fortifications; in 1718 a fire destroyed the great church, the archive, the library and the printing house. Above the ensemble rises the Great Bell Tower, four tiers and 96.5 metres high, built in 1731-1745 to the design of Johann Gottfried Schadel, the tallest free-standing bell tower of its time. Its main bell, the Uspensky, was cast in 1732 by Ivan Motorin, who also cast the Tsar Bell in Moscow. Some Orthodox believers held a pilgrimage to Kiev to be better than the journey to Jerusalem.
zh:
基辅洞窟大修道院起初只是一个洞。传统上把创建定在1051年：从阿索斯山修行归来的修士安东尼，住进了第聂伯河高岸山坡上神父伊拉里翁早先为自己挖的那个洞。门徒渐聚，库尔斯克的费奥多西也在其中，人数到十二人时，大家建起一座教堂和几间修室；安东尼后来迁到邻近的山冈，另挖了一个新洞。修士们依斯图狄乌斯的费奥多尔所立的共居会规生活。费奥多西办了一所收容乞丐、盲人和跛者的济贫院，经费取自修道院收入的十分之一，每周六还有一车面包送给囚犯。石造安息大教堂1089年祝圣，壁画和马赛克出自君士坦丁堡的画师。修士迁入大修道院以后，洞穴成了他们的墓地，遗体安放在洞道两侧墙壁的壁龛里；立陶宛时代的王公也葬在修道院里，其中包括奥尔沙之战的胜者康斯坦丁·奥斯特罗格斯基。

修道院一次次遭劫，1240年蒙古人的洗劫最为惨重，1482年克里米亚鞑靼人又纵火劫掠。布列斯特联合之后，修道院成了东正教和天主教两边争夺的对象，东正教一方靠奥斯特罗格斯基王公家族的支持保住了它。传教士约阿尼基·加利亚托夫斯基发表过一则传说：1630年波兰军队围攻修道院，圣母降下「火雨」打向围攻者，修士得救。18世纪之交，盖特曼伊万·马泽帕出资大规模重建并修筑防御工事；1718年一场大火烧毁了大教堂、档案、藏书和印刷所。大钟楼凌驾于整个修道院之上，四层、高96.5米，约翰·戈特弗里德·谢德尔设计，1731至1745年建成，是当时最高的独立钟楼；主钟乌斯片斯基钟1732年由伊凡·莫托林铸成，他也铸造了莫斯科的沙皇钟。一些东正教信徒认为，赴基辅朝圣比远赴耶路撒冷更好。

en:
From the early eighteenth century the Kremlin walls were painted white, so that the citadel looked white rather than brick-red. It stands on Borovitsky Hill, where the Neglinnaya stream ran into the Moskva, and its walls enclose 27.5 hectares, five palaces and four cathedrals. In 1444 the hill still held the white-limestone fortress of the grand princes; within half a century Ivan III had rebuilt it. Pietro Antonio Solari, one of the Italians he invited, designed the new wall and towers, and the Spassky Gate bears a Latin inscription praising him. Fioravanti's Dormition Cathedral was where the tsars were crowned, with Ivan IV the first in 1547. The Ivan the Great Bell Tower, on the same square, was long the tallest building in Muscovite Russia.

Two giant curiosities stand in the grounds. The Tsar Cannon was cast in bronze in 1586 by Andrei Chokhov, billed as the largest bombard in the world by calibre, and it was never used in war. Voltaire is said to have joked that the Kremlin's two greatest items were a bell that was never rung and a cannon that was never fired. The Tsar Bell was the third of its line. The first, completed in 1600, needed 24 men to ring its clapper, and the second burned in 1701. Ivan Motorin and his son Mikhail cast the two-hundred-ton successor in the 1730s, and when fire reached the Kremlin in 1737 it was still hanging in a temporary wooden frame above its pit. The guards threw cold water on it, eleven cracks opened, a slab of over ten tons broke off, and the burning frame dropped the bell back into the pit, where it lay for almost a century.

Catherine II engaged Vasily Bazhenov to build a new residence there, a design that meant demolishing several churches and palaces and a stretch of the wall, but it was delayed for lack of funds. French forces held the Kremlin from 2 September to 11 October 1812, and Napoleon, retreating, ordered the whole of it blown up. The Arsenal, parts of the wall and several towers were destroyed, but rain had damaged the fuses and the damage was less severe than intended.
zh:
18世纪初起，莫斯科克里姆林宫的城墙刷成白色，那时的城塞看上去是白的，而不是砖红色。它建在博罗维茨山上，涅格林纳亚河曾在此汇入莫斯科河，城墙围出二十七公顷半的地方，里面有五座宫殿和四座大教堂。1444年，山上还是大公们的白色石灰岩堡垒；不到半个世纪，伊凡三世把它重建了一遍。他请来的意大利人之一皮埃特罗·安东尼奥·索拉里设计了新的城墙和塔楼，斯帕斯卡亚塔门上刻有称颂他的拉丁文铭文。菲奥拉万蒂所建的圣母升天大堂是沙皇加冕之处，1547年伊凡四世第一个在此加冕。同一广场上的伊凡大帝钟楼，长期是全俄最高的建筑。

城圈之内还有两件庞然大物。沙皇炮1586年由安德烈·乔霍夫以青铜铸成，号称口径世界第一的臼炮，却从未用于战争。据说伏尔泰打趣过，克里姆林宫有两样最了不起的东西，一口从没响过的钟和一门从没开过火的炮。沙皇钟是同一系列的第三口：1600年完工的头一口要二十四人才拉得动钟舌，第二口1701年毁于火灾；伊凡·莫托林和儿子米哈伊尔18世纪30年代铸出两百吨重的新钟，1737年克里姆林宫失火时，它还吊在铸坑上方的临时木架里。守卫往钟上泼冷水，钟体裂开十一道缝，一块十多吨重的裂片脱落，燃烧的木架断裂，钟落回坑中，躺了将近一个世纪。

叶卡捷琳娜二世请瓦西里·巴热诺夫在这里为她设计新宫，方案要拆掉几座教堂、几座宫殿和一段城墙，后来因经费不足搁置。1812年9月2日至10月11日，法军占据克里姆林宫，拿破仑撤退时下令把整座克里姆林宫炸毁。军火库、部分城墙和几座塔楼被毁，但雨水浸湿了引信，损失比预想的轻。

en:
The tale is told that Ivan IV had the builder of this cathedral blinded so that he could never raise its equal. The chronicle names the builder only as 'Barma with company', and later tradition adds a second master, Postnik; historians doubt the blinding, because Postnik Yakovlev went on to build the walls and towers of the Kazan Kremlin. The cathedral stands on Red Square, and was built in 1555-1561 to mark Ivan's conquest of Kazan. Its proper name is the Cathedral of the Intercession of the Most Holy Theotokos on the Moat, and it replaced a white-stone Trinity church in the middle of the market place. During the Kazan war Ivan had put up a wooden memorial church beside Trinity for each victory, until seven of them stood there. The stone cathedral set eight chapels around a tall central church of the Intercession on a single platform, and several were dedicated to saints on whose feast days the decisive battles for Kazan fell. Kazan itself was taken on 2 October 1552, the feast of Saints Cyprian and Justina, who have a chapel here.

The popular name came in 1588, when Tsar Fyodor had a tenth chapel built over the grave of Vasily the Blessed, a Muscovite fool-for-Christ who went naked through the streets in chains and rebuked even Ivan. Miracles were reported at his tomb that year and he was canonised; Ivan is said to have helped carry his bier. On Palm Sunday the patriarch and the tsar held their procession here, and the church stood for the Temple of Jerusalem. In 1680-1683 the open arcades were walled in, brick galleries replaced the wooden ones, and a new tent-roofed belfry joined the churches into one building; altars from thirteen wooden churches built at the execution sites on Red Square were moved into the lower level. The great fire of 1737 burned the church out almost completely, and Ivan Michurin restored it. In 1812 the French stabled horses in the lower churches and plundered what they could carry. Legend says Napoleon ordered the cathedral blown up and rain put out the fuses, but no document confirms it.
zh:
相传伊凡四世弄瞎了圣瓦西里大教堂的建造者，免得他再造出能与之媲美的建筑。编年史只把建造者记作「巴尔马及其同伴」，后来的说法又添了一位匠师波斯特尼克；史家多不信刺目之说，因为波斯特尼克·雅科夫列夫此后还参与修筑喀山克里姆林宫的城墙和塔楼。教堂立在红场上，1555至1561年建成，纪念伊凡攻取喀山。它的正式名称是护城河边圣母帡幪大堂，取代了市集中央一座白石三一教堂。喀山战事期间，伊凡每打赢一仗，就在三一教堂旁添一座木制纪念教堂，最后攒下七座；石造大堂把八座圣堂围在高耸的中央帡幪堂四周，立在同一个台基上，其中几座奉祀的圣徒，纪念日恰是喀山决战之日。喀山本身于1552年10月2日陷落，这一天是圣济普里安和圣尤斯蒂娜的纪念日，堂里有一座圣堂就奉祀他们。

教堂的俗名得于1588年，这年沙皇费奥多尔在圣愚瓦西里的墓上添建了第十座小堂。瓦西里是莫斯科的「为基督装疯」的圣愚，赤身戴链行走街头，连伊凡也敢当面责备。这一年他的墓前传出神迹，他被封为圣徒；据说伊凡当年亲自扶过他的灵床。每年棕枝主日，牧首和沙皇的游行行列到此，这座教堂象征耶路撒冷圣殿。1680至1683年，敞开的拱廊被砌上砖墙，木制回廊改成砖砌，新建的帐篷顶钟楼把各座教堂连成一体；红场上处决地点旁十三座木教堂的圣坛也迁进了底层。1737年的大火几乎把教堂内部烧空，伊万·米丘林负责修复。1812年法军在下层教堂里养马，掠走可搬动的器物。传说拿破仑下令炸毁这座教堂，一场雨浇灭了引线，但没有文献可以证实。

en:
Mausolus, satrap of Caria under the Persian king, decided to build a new capital at Halicarnassus, and he died in 353 BC with a grand tomb already planned. His sister and wife Artemisia II carried on the work and outlived him by only two years. She is said to have mixed his ashes into her daily drink, and painters from the Renaissance on, Rembrandt among them, liked to show her doing it. The tomb rose about 45 metres: a stone platform, a marble block, thirty-six Ionic columns and a stepped pyramid roof, with a four-horse chariot carrying figures of Mausolus and Artemisia on the summit. Four Greek sculptors, Scopas, Leochares, Bryaxis and Timotheus, took one side each, and the tomb held some 400 freestanding sculptures. Antipater of Sidon counted it among the Seven Wonders, and the Romans afterwards called every grand tomb a mausoleum.

It stood above the harbour for sixteen centuries; Alexander spared it in 334 BC, and in the twelfth century the scholar Eustathius could still write that it 'was and is a wonder'. Earthquakes brought it down, though exactly when is uncertain. When the Knights Hospitaller arrived in 1402 to build the Castle of Saint Peter, they found ruins and used the site as a quarry. In 1494 they took its stones again to thicken the castle walls against cannon, burned much of the marble into lime, and set the best relief slabs into the walls.

In 1522, with Sultan Suleiman about to attack, the knights stripped almost every block that was left. One of them, de La Touret, wrote that his party found a stair of twelve steps and a corridor lined with statues and reliefs; they admired the sculpture and then smashed it. The work-end horn sounded before they reached the burial chamber, and when they returned next morning the door stood open and gold ornaments lay broken on the floor. Later research showed that robbers had tunnelled in long before them.
name_zh: 哈利卡那索斯的摩索拉斯陵墓
zh:
哈利卡那索斯的摩索拉斯陵墓，是为卡里亚总督摩索拉斯修的。他隶属波斯国王，决定在哈利卡那索斯建新都，公元前353年去世时，宏伟的陵墓已有规划。他的姊妹兼妻子阿尔特米西亚二世接手工程，只比他多活了两年。据说她把他的骨灰调进每日的饮料里喝下，文艺复兴以来的画家，包括伦勃朗在内，都爱画这个场面。陵墓高约45米：石砌台基、大理石方块、三十六根爱奥尼亚式柱子和阶梯形的金字塔顶，顶上是一辆驷马战车，车里立着摩索拉斯与阿尔特米西亚的雕像。斯科帕斯、莱奥卡雷斯、布里亚西斯和提摩修斯四位希腊雕刻家各负责一面，陵墓里共有约四百尊圆雕。西顿的安提帕特把它列入七大奇迹，罗马人此后以他的名字称呼一切宏伟的陵墓。

巨墓在海港上方矗立了十六个世纪；亚历山大在公元前334年放过了它，12世纪时，学者尤斯塔提乌斯仍能写下它「过去是奇迹，现在还是」。后来地震把它震塌，具体时间并不清楚。1402年医院骑士团到来修建圣彼得城堡时，看到的已是废墟，便把遗址当成采石场。1494年他们再次取走陵墓的石料，加厚城堡的城墙以抵挡火炮，把大量大理石烧成石灰，又把最好的浮雕板嵌进墙里。

1522年，苏莱曼苏丹即将来攻，骑士团把剩下的石块拆得几乎一块不剩。其中一位骑士德拉图雷特写道，他们发现一道十二级台阶和一条两侧排满雕像与浮雕的甬道，先对雕刻赞叹一番，随后动手砸碎。收工号在他们进入墓室前吹响，次日清晨再来时，墓门已开，金器碎了一地。后来的研究表明，盗墓者早在他们之前就从地道进去过。

en:
Al-Azhar was the first mosque built in Cairo, the new Fatimid capital. The general Jawhar al-Siqilli began it in 970, out of limestone from the Mokattam hills. Its name is usually derived from az-Zahra, 'the shining one', a title of Fatima, the Prophet's daughter. In the late 980s the vizier Ya'qub ibn Killis made it a centre of higher learning, with a permanent staff of 35 scholars teaching law, grammar, logic and astronomy. When Saladin overthrew the Fatimids in 1171, the qadi he appointed banned congregational prayer there, the silver band bearing the Fatimid caliphs' names was torn from the mihrab, and student stipends stopped. The Fatimid palace's books were sold off over ten years; in one account soldiers soled their shoes with the bindings of a 'hill of books'. Legend says Maimonides lectured at the mosque in Saladin's day, though no proof survives. The Mamluk sultan Baibars restored Friday prayers in 1266, and Ibn Khaldun taught there. In 1444 students lodged in riwaqs grouped by nationality and school of law.

Selim I, who took Egypt for the Ottomans in 1517, attended Friday prayers at al-Azhar in his last week there but gave nothing to its upkeep. In the eighteenth century Abd al-Rahman Katkhuda, head of the Janissaries, added the Gate of the Barbers, where students had their heads shaved, and the Soup Gate, where rice soup was served to them,. In 1776 he was buried in the mausoleum he built inside the mosque, the first burial there since a woman mystic died around 1588. In 1798 Napoleon set up a diwan of nine Azhar sheikhs to govern Cairo; three months later a revolt against the French began at the mosque. The Citadel's guns fired straight at it, French troops tied horses to the mihrab and threw Qur'ans on the floor, and six of the ulema were killed. After the Azhar student Suleiman al-Halabi assassinated General Kléber, the mosque was shut, and its doors stayed bolted until Ottoman and British help arrived in 1801.
zh:
爱资哈尔大学的前身是法蒂玛王朝新都开罗建起的第一座清真寺。大将昭海尔于970年动工，用的是穆盖塔姆山的石灰岩。寺名通常认为取自「宰赫拉」，意为「光辉的女子」，是先知之女法蒂玛的称号。980年代末，维齐尔叶尔孤白·伊本·基利斯把它办成高等学府，聘了三十五名学者常年任教，讲授教法、语法、逻辑、天文等科目。1171年萨拉丁推翻法蒂玛王朝后，他任命的法官禁止在寺内举行聚礼，米哈拉布上刻着法蒂玛哈里发名字的银带被拆走，学生的津贴也停了。法蒂玛王宫的藏书被变卖了十年，据一份记述，士兵用精美的封皮垫鞋底，书堆成了「书丘」。传说麦蒙尼德在萨拉丁时代曾在寺里讲授医学和天文学，但没有任何史料佐证。马穆鲁克苏丹拜巴尔斯1266年恢复了这里的聚礼，伊本·赫勒敦在此讲学。1444年，学生住在按民族和教法学派划分的学舍里。

1517年夺取埃及的奥斯曼苏丹塞利姆一世，在离开前的最后一周到爱资哈尔参加主麻聚礼，却没有为它的维护捐过一文。18世纪，禁卫军首领阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼·卡特胡达添建了「理发师门」，学生进寺前在门外剃头，又修了「汤门」，向学生施散米汤。1776年，他葬在自己在寺内修的陵寝里，这是约1588年一位女神秘主义者去世后寺内的头一次安葬。1798年，拿破仑成立由九名爱资哈尔谢赫组成的政务会治理开罗，三个月后，反抗法军的起义就从这座清真寺发起。城堡上的炮火直接轰向寺里，法军把马拴在米哈拉布上，将《古兰经》掷在地上，六名乌莱玛被处死。爱资哈尔学生苏莱曼·哈拉比刺杀克莱贝尔将军后，寺被封闭，寺门一直紧闭到1801年奥斯曼与英国军队赶到。

en:
Herodotus, who visited around 450 BC, was told that an inscription on the outside recorded the radishes, garlic and onions eaten by the work gangs, and that 100,000 men had laboured in three-month shifts for twenty years. His interpreters may have misread the signs. The Pyramid of Cheops is the tomb of Khufu, the Fourth Dynasty pharaoh the Greeks called Cheops, whose vizier Hemiunu some scholars credit as the architect. About 2.3 million blocks went into it, with granite for the King's Chamber brought from Aswan, more than 900 kilometres up the Nile, and white Tura limestone sheathing its faces. At 146.6 metres it was the tallest structure raised by human hands for more than 3,700 years; with the casing stripped it measures 138.5.

In the Middle Ages other builders were named: Christians read the pyramids as Joseph's granaries, and a Coptic legend, told by the Arab writer al-Mas'udi, made them the work of Surid, the antediluvian king who dreamed of the Flood and ordered Egypt's knowledge stored in them. Caliph al-Ma'mun's workmen are said to have tunnelled into the pyramid in the ninth century; al-Mas'udi records that they found an emerald jar holding a thousand coins, just enough to cover the cost of the digging. In 1196 Saladin's son al-Aziz Uthman set workmen to demolish the pyramids, starting with Menkaure's; by one account they kept at it for eight months, by another one, and only Menkaure's was damaged. Stripped casing is said to have been carted into Cairo, and by the late Middle Ages people feared to enter the pyramid because of its bats and hauntings.

In 1435 Cyriacus of Ancona reached the Giza plateau, compared the monument with Herodotus and refuted the story of Joseph's granaries. The Oxford scholar John Greaves made a survey of the pyramids more accurate than any traveller's before him, and in his Pyramidographia of 1646 put the start of Khufu's reign at 1266 BC, some thirteen centuries too late. In the 1760s Nathaniel Davison, then secretary to Wortley Montagu, crawled along a passage deep in bat dung above the Grand Gallery and found the low chamber over the King's Chamber that now bears his name.
zh:
公元前450年左右到访的希罗多德听说，塔外刻有铭文，记着工匠吃掉的萝卜、大蒜和洋葱，又说十万人以三个月一班轮换，修了二十年。给他当翻译的人可能把那些文字读错了。胡夫金字塔是第四王朝法老胡夫（希腊人叫他齐奥普斯）的陵墓，一些学者认为设计者是他的维齐尔赫米乌努。整座塔用去约二百三十万块巨石，国王墓室用的花岗岩从九百多公里外的阿斯旺顺尼罗河运来，四面坡铺着图拉出产的白色石灰岩。塔原高146.6米，保持人类最高建筑的纪录超过三千七百年；外层石被拆走后，高138.5米。

中世纪的人把它归到别人名下：基督徒把这些塔当作「约瑟的粮仓」，一则科普特传说经阿拉伯作者马斯欧迪转述，说洪水之前的国王苏利德梦见灭世，便下令把埃及的学问封进金字塔。据说9世纪哈里发马蒙的工匠从塔身一侧凿入隧道；马斯欧迪记载，他们找到一只祖母绿罐，里面有一千枚钱币，恰好抵偿凿塔的花费。1196年，萨拉丁之子阿齐兹·奥斯曼派工匠拆金字塔，先从孟卡拉金字塔下手；一说他们干了八个月，另一说只干了一个月，最后只有孟卡拉金字塔受损。剥落的外层石据说被运进开罗；到中世纪晚期，人们因为里面的蝙蝠和闹鬼的传闻而不敢进塔。

1435年，安科纳的奇里亚科来到吉萨高原，拿希罗多德的记载同眼前的建筑对照，推翻了「约瑟的粮仓」的说法。牛津学者约翰·格里夫斯对金字塔的测量比此前任何旅行者都准确；他1646年出版的《金字塔志》把胡夫即位定在公元前1266年，比实际晚了约一千三百年。18世纪60年代，纳撒尼尔·戴维森当时是沃特利·蒙塔古的秘书，他沿大甬道上方一条积满蝙蝠粪的窄道爬行，发现了国王墓室上方的那间低矮石室，后来这间石室便以他的名字命名。

en:
The Citadel of Aleppo crowns a fifty-metre mound in the middle of the city, an oval 450 metres long and 325 wide at its base, and the hill has been in use since the middle of the third millennium BC. Local tradition says the prophet Ibrahim once milked his flocks on the hill, and the storm-god Hadad had a temple there when Aleppo was the capital of Yamhad. The mound was once faced throughout with large limestone blocks and is girdled by a moat twenty-two metres deep and thirty wide, crossed by a single tall viaduct of arches. The two mosques on the crown, the Great Mosque and the Mosque of Abraham, began as Byzantine churches.

The citadel held prisoners in the wars with the Franks. Baldwin II of Jerusalem was held there for two years, Joscelin II of Edessa died in its cells, and Raynald of Chatillon was kept there before his release. Most of what crowns the mound is the work of Saladin's son al-Zahir Ghazi, who between 1193 and 1215 deepened the moat, threw the arched bridge across it and built the bent entrance, a vaulted ramp that turns six times under machicolations, its passages carved with figurative reliefs and threaded with secret stairs. His 'palace of glory' burned down on his wedding night and was rebuilt. Wells on the crown went down 125 metres, and tunnels ran out to the advance towers and, it was said, under the moat into the city.

Timur's invasion of 1400 destroyed the citadel, and some fifteen years later the Mamluk governor Sayf al-Din Jakam was authorised to rebuild: he added two advance towers and a new palace above the higher entrance tower, and the Ayyubid palace was almost entirely abandoned. Qansuh al-Ghawri, one of the last Mamluk sultans, replaced the flat ceiling of the Throne Hall with nine domes. Under the Ottomans the citadel served as a barracks, and Suleiman ordered it restored in 1521. An anonymous Venetian traveller counted some 2,000 people living inside in 1556, and in 1679 the French consul d'Arvieux reported 1,400, of them 350 janissaries.
zh:
阿勒颇城堡坐落在城中心一座五十米高的土丘上，丘基为椭圆形，底部长四百五十米、宽三百二十五米，这座土丘自公元前第三千年中期起就有人使用。当地相传先知易卜拉欣曾在这座山丘上放牧羊群、挤取羊乳；阿勒颇做亚姆哈德国都城时，风暴神哈达德的神庙也立在丘顶。山坡曾整体包着大块的石灰岩，丘下环绕着深二十二米、宽三十米的壕沟，只有一座高耸的多拱引桥可以通过。丘顶的大清真寺和易卜拉欣清真寺，最初都是拜占庭人的教堂。

十字军战争中，这里关押过不少俘虏：耶路撒冷国王鲍德温二世被囚两年，埃德萨伯爵乔斯林二世死在堡中，沙蒂永的雷纳德获释前也关押于此。丘顶现存的建筑大半出自萨拉丁之子扎希尔·加齐之手：1193至1215年间，他加深壕沟、架起拱桥，又修出折角式大门，攻门者要在拱顶坡道上连转六道弯，头顶全是倾倒沸液的堞口，通道里刻着人物浮雕，还岔出暗藏的阶梯。他那座「荣耀宫」在新婚之夜失火焚毁，后来又重建。丘顶的水井深达一百二十五米，地道通向前方塔楼，据说还穿过壕沟通到城里。

1400年帖木儿的入侵毁坏了城堡，约十五年后马穆鲁克总督赛义夫丁·贾克姆获准重建：他加了两座前沿塔楼，又在较高的入口塔楼上新建一座宫殿，艾尤布时代的宫殿几乎被完全弃用。马穆鲁克晚期的素丹坎苏·戈里把觐见大殿的平顶换成了九座穹顶。奥斯曼时代城堡作兵营，苏莱曼1521年下令修缮。1556年一位不知名的威尼斯旅行者数出城堡里住着约两千人，1679年法国领事达尔维厄报告有一千四百人，其中三百五十名是耶尼切里。

en:
Above the door of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre a wooden ladder rests on the cornice beneath an upper window. The Franciscan Elzear Horn engraved it in 1728, and it stayed where it was because the six Christian rites that share the church must all agree before anything in it is moved. The Ottoman firman of 1757 became the first documentary basis for how the church is divided. The Holy City of Jerusalem is not a single building but a set of shrines within one walled city. Every Holy Saturday the Greek Orthodox patriarch goes into the tomb chapel and comes out with lit candles, the Holy Fire. Muslim writers described the rite long before. Al-Biruni, who has the imam and the emir of the city waiting outside the tomb, adds that one sultan replaced the lamp's cloth wick with a copper one, and the lamp lit anyway.

On the Haram al-Sharif the Dome of the Rock stands beside the small open-pillared Dome of the Chain. The fifteenth-century historian Mujir al-Din tells the legend of a chain that Solomon hung there, which only an honest man could grasp. A debtor who had hidden the gold in a walking-stick took hold of it to swear he had repaid; when the creditor swore the opposite, the chain withdrew to heaven. In the platform's eastern wall is the Golden Gate. Jews expect the Messiah to enter by it, and Christians hold that Jesus rode through it on Palm Sunday; in 1541 Suleiman walled it up, most likely for defence. The Via Dolorosa runs about 600 metres from the old Antonia Fortress to the Sepulchre. Franciscan friars led pilgrims along it from about 1350, at first from the Sepulchre towards Pilate's house, the reverse of Jesus's path; the route as now walked dates from the eighteenth century.

In the winter of 1700 Judah HeHasid arrived from Poland with some 500 Ashkenazim and died within days. His followers built a synagogue on borrowed money, and around 1720 their Arab creditors burned it down and the Ashkenazim were banished from the city. The empty plot was known ever after as the Hurva, the Ruin.
zh:
耶路撒冷圣墓教堂的门上方，一扇窗下的檐台上靠着一把木梯。方济各会士埃尔泽尔·霍恩1728年刻印的版画里已经画着它；共用这座教堂的六派基督徒必须一致同意才能挪动堂内任何东西，所以它一直留在原处。奥斯曼1757年的敕令成为教堂分配办法的第一份文献依据。耶路撒冷圣城没有哪一座建筑可指，而是一座围城里的一组圣迹。每年圣周六，希腊正教牧首走进墓亭，手持点燃的蜡烛走出，称为圣火。穆斯林作家很早就记下了这一仪式：比鲁尼写到伊玛目和城中的埃米尔在墓外等候，还说有一位苏丹把灯的布灯芯换成铜芯，灯仍然自己亮了。

圣殿山（尊贵禁地）上，圆顶清真寺旁立着以柱环绕、四面敞开的链圆顶。15世纪的历史学家穆吉尔丁讲过一个传说：所罗门在此悬了一条锁链，只有诚实的人才抓得住。有个欠债人把金子藏进手杖，握住锁链发誓已经还清；债主也握着它发誓没有收到，锁链便缩回了天上。禁地东墙里封着金门：犹太人相信弥赛亚将经由此门入城，基督徒则说耶稣棕枝主日骑驴经过此门；1541年，苏莱曼把它砌死，多半出于防御。苦路（维亚多勒罗沙）从旧安东尼亚堡到圣墓教堂约600米。方济各会修士约自1350年起带朝圣者沿此路行进，起初是从圣墓走向彼拉多的官邸，与耶稣所走的方向相反；现行的路线则是18世纪定下来的。

1700年冬，犹大·赫哈西德率约五百名阿什肯纳兹人从波兰抵达，几天后便去世。门徒借债建起一座会堂，1720年前后阿拉伯债主放火烧堂，阿什肯纳兹人也被逐出城。那块空地此后称作胡瓦，意思是废墟。

en:
The Kaaba is the cuboid stone building at the centre of the Masjid al-Haram in Mecca, about fifteen metres high. Muslims believe that Ibrahim and his son Ismail raised it at God's command, and that an angel brought the Black Stone, which he set in the eastern corner. Pilgrims circle the Kaaba seven times anti-clockwise, the tawaf, starting from the Black Stone, and kiss or touch it if the crowd allows.

Around 600, after fire and flood, the Quraysh rebuilt the house and quarrelled over which clan should set the Black Stone in place. Muhammad had the clan elders raise the stone on a cloak, then set it in its place with his own hands. When he took Mecca in 630 he struck down the 360 idols around the Kaaba and spared a painting of Maryam and her son Isa. Fire during the Umayyad siege of Mecca in 683 badly damaged the building, and in 693 Caliph Abd al-Malik razed what was left and rebuilt it on the Quraysh foundations. The Kaaba returned to its cube shape, and its basic structure has not changed since.

In 930, during the Hajj, the Qarmatians under Abu Tahir al-Jannabi attacked Mecca, defiled the Zamzam well with the bodies of pilgrims and carried the Black Stone off to al-Ahsa. The Abbasids ransomed it in 952.

From Ayyubid times the kiswa, the cloth that covers the Kaaba, was made in Egypt, and under the Mamluks and Ottomans the commander of the Hajj caravan carried it to Mecca every year. The old cloth was cut into pieces and sold to pilgrims. The mahmal, a processional covering that went with the kiswa, became an accepted tradition only in the fifteenth century. In 1626 heavy rains and flooding brought the walls of the Kaaba down, and the Ottoman sultan Murad IV had it rebuilt with granite from Mecca.
zh:
天房是麦加禁寺中央的长方体石殿，高约十五米。穆斯林相信，易卜拉欣和儿子易司马仪奉真主之命筑起了这座殿堂，天使送来黑石，他把黑石嵌在东角。朝觐者绕天房逆时针走七圈，称为绕行（塔瓦夫），从黑石开始，人群允许时便上前亲吻或触摸它。

约600年，天房遭火灾和洪水之后由古莱什人重建，各部落为该由哪个家族安放黑石争执不下。穆罕默德让众族长把黑石托在斗篷上抬起，再亲手把它安放就位。630年他进入麦加，击倒天房周围的三百六十尊偶像，唯独留下一幅麦尔彦和她儿子尔撒的画像。683年倭马亚军围攻麦加时，天房失火，严重受损。693年，哈里发阿卜杜勒·马利克把残余部分拆平，在古莱什人的旧基上重建。天房恢复成立方体，基本结构此后再没有改变。

930年朝觐期间，盖尔迈特派在阿布·塔希尔·贾纳比率领下进攻麦加，把朝觐者的尸体抛入渗渗泉，又将黑石劫往哈萨。阿拔斯王朝952年才将它赎回。

从阿尤布王朝起，覆盖天房的罩幕（基斯沃）在埃及制作，马穆鲁克和奥斯曼时期由朝觐驼队的首领每年押运到麦加。旧幕被剪成小块卖给朝觐者。迈哈米勒是随罩幕同行的仪仗，15世纪起才被普遍接受。1626年暴雨和洪水冲垮了天房的墙，奥斯曼苏丹穆拉德四世用麦加的花岗岩重建了它。

en:
The City of Sana'a is a wonder made of a whole walled town: 6,500 houses packed inside clay ramparts nine to fourteen metres high, entered through the Bab al-Yaman, a southern gate more than a thousand years old. The old city was divided into quarters, each centred on an endowed complex of mosque, bathhouse and garden. Household waste went down chutes and dried quickly in the mountain air, and the dried matter was burned to heat the bathhouse, while the garden was watered with grey water from the mosque's ablution pool.

The houses are towers of stone and fired brick, up to eight storeys high, with friezes, carved frames and stained-glass windows. One extended family lived in a single tower, and a new floor went up when a son married. Grain and animals stayed on the ground floor, and the top room, the mafraj, was a second reception room where men chewed qat of an afternoon. The Suq al-Milh, the Salt Market, sold salt, bread, spices, raisins, cotton, copper and silverware.

The Ottomans took Sana'a in 1547 and the Zaydi imams drove them out in 1629. West of the walls lay Bi'r al-Azab, first mentioned in 1627, then called the Turkish Quarter and noted for its gardens. In 1679 Imam al-Mahdi Ahmad banished the Jews of nearly all Yemeni towns to the Tihama coast in the Mawza Exile. Those who came back in 1680 were given a plot outside the walls, where they built the Qa' quarter. In 1763 Carsten Niebuhr, the only member of a Danish expedition to survive the journey, was received in Sana'a by Imam al-Mahdi Abbas, though the climate made the party ill and drove them back to Mokha.
zh:
萨那城的奇观就是这座有城墙的城本身：六千五百栋房屋挤在九至十四米高的土墙之内，南门「也门门」已有上千年历史。老城分成若干街区，每个街区都围绕一组宗教捐赠建筑，即清真寺、澡堂和菜园。各家的污物顺槽而下，在山间空气里很快晒干，晒干的东西用来烧澡堂；菜园则用清真寺净身池的废水浇灌。

民宅就是塔楼：石头和烧砖砌成，最高八层，有饰带、雕花窗框和彩色玻璃窗。一座塔楼住一个大家庭，儿子娶妻便往上添一层。底层囤粮、圈牲口，顶层的「迈夫拉杰」是第二间客厅，男人们下午在这里嚼卡特。盐市出售食盐、面包、香料、葡萄干、棉花、铜器和银器。

1547年奥斯曼人攻占萨那，1629年栽德派伊玛目把他们赶了出去。城墙以西是比尔阿扎布，最早见于1627年的记载，当时叫「土耳其区」，以花园著称。1679年，伊玛目迈赫迪·艾哈迈德下令把也门几乎各城镇的犹太人驱往提哈马沿海，史称「穆瓦扎流徙」；1680年回来的人在城墙外分到一块地，在那里建起盖阿街区。1763年，丹麦考察队中唯一活着走完全程的卡斯滕·尼布尔在萨那受到伊玛目迈赫迪·阿拔斯接见，但当地气候使考察队成员病倒，他们退回了摩卡。

en:
Nizwa Fort is a stone drum twenty-four metres high and forty-three across. It stands in Nizwa, which between the eighth and twelfth centuries was, off and on, the capital of Oman's imams. Beside it stood an older fort, Hisn al-Aqr, said to have been built by Imam al-Salt bin Malik in the ninth century, and in 1625 Imam Nasir bin Murshid had it rebuilt on its ruins. The great round fort came a generation later, in the 1650s, built for the second Ya'rubi imam, Sultan bin Saif, remembered as the imam who drove the Portuguese out of Oman. The main body took twelve years and rises above an underground stream. It was the seat of the imams and walis, and held prisons.

Everything about it was made to withstand artillery. The foundations go thirty metres into the ground, part of the tower is filled with rock and rubble, and the walls are rounded and thick. There are 480 gun-ports and twenty-four openings for heavy guns, and four cannon sit on the summit, one of them engraved with Sultan bin Saif's name.

The only way up is a single twisting stair, barred by a heavy wooden door studded with spikes. An attacker who forced it risked boiling oil or water poured through shafts above every set of doors, and date syrup oozing from the fort's date cellars could serve instead. The dark passage hides around six pitfalls, covered by planks that can be pulled away. Seven wells, cisterns and underground cellars for food and munitions made a long siege survivable, and the wall-walk at the top had room for 120 guards with muskets.
zh:
尼兹瓦城堡的主楼是一只石砌的巨鼓，高二十四米、直径四十三米。尼兹瓦在八至十二世纪之间时断时续地做过阿曼伊玛目的都城。城堡旁原有一座更老的要塞阿格尔堡，据说是伊玛目萨勒特·本·马利克在9世纪所建，1625年，伊玛目纳绥尔·本·穆尔希德命人在它的废墟上重建。这座圆形大堡晚一代人才出现，建于17世纪50年代，主人是叶阿里卜朝第二任伊玛目苏丹·本·赛义夫，人们记得他是把葡萄牙人逐出阿曼的伊玛目。主体工程用了十二年，立在一条地下溪流之上。这里是伊玛目和地方长官的驻地，设有监狱。

它处处是为抵挡火炮设计的。地基深入地下三十米，塔身一部分填满碎石和泥土，塔墙圆而厚实。四百八十个枪眼和二十四个重炮射孔，塔顶架着四门炮，其中一门刻有苏丹·本·赛义夫的名字。

登塔只有一条盘旋窄梯，隔着一扇钉满尖刺的厚重木门。破门而入者，会遭遇每组门上方孔洞里倾倒的滚油和开水，枣窖里渗出的枣浆也可以拿来代用。幽暗的通道里约有六处陷阱，盖着可以抽走的木板。七口水井、蓄水池和存放粮食军火的地下窖足以撑过长期围困，塔顶巡道可容一百二十名火枪手守望。

en:
Agathangelos records the vision behind the foundation: Gregory the Illuminator saw a figure come down from heaven and strike the ground with a golden hammer to show where the cathedral should stand. Later tradition took the figure to be Christ, and the name Etchmiadzin means the descent of the Only-Begotten, though the name is not found before the fifteenth century. The cathedral is the mother church of the Armenian Apostolic Church, at Vagharshapat. Tradition places its foundation between 301 and 303, when Gregory built it near the royal palace over a pagan temple, after King Tiridates III made Armenia the first country to adopt Christianity as a state religion. The core of the present building dates from the fifth century, when Vahan Mamikonian rebuilt the dilapidated church on a cross-shaped plan with four free-standing piers.

In 1441 a council of several hundred clergy met at Etchmiadzin and voted to move the catholicosate there from Sis, and Catholicos Kirakos restored the cathedral. The Kara Koyunlu then ruled the place; in 1502 Safavid Persia took it and granted the Armenian Church some privileges. In 1604, as Shah Abbas I deported Armenians to Persia in his war with the Ottomans, Etchmiadzin was plundered. The shah wanted to pull the cathedral down and rebuild it in Persia; in the end only the notable stones were taken to New Julfa near Isfahan. They were the altar, the stone where Christ was said to have descended, and the Right Arm of Gregory the Illuminator, and in 1611 they were built into the church of St George there.

From 1627 Catholicos Movses had the dome, roof, foundations and paving repaired and a wall built around the cathedral, turning it into a fort-like complex. A belfry over the west wing was begun in 1654 and finished in 1658. Catholicos Simeon set up Armenia's first printing house nearby in 1771. In June 1804, in the Russo-Persian War, General Tsitsianov's troops entered Etchmiadzin; according to a French military envoy to Persia, they looted it and badly damaged the Armenian buildings, in contrast to the shah's respectful treatment of his Christian subjects. The Russians withdrew soon afterwards, when the Persians held Erivan.
zh:
史家阿加坦格洛斯记下了建堂的异象：启蒙者格列高利看见一位使者自天而降，以金锤敲击地面，标出教堂该建的地方。后来的传统认为这位使者就是基督，埃奇米阿津因此意为「独生子降临」，不过这个名字15世纪以前还看不到。埃奇米阿津主教座堂在瓦加尔沙帕特，是亚美尼亚使徒教会的母堂。相传它始建于301至303年之间：梯里达底三世把基督教立为国教，亚美尼亚成为世上第一个以基督教为国教的国家，格列高利便在王宫近旁一座异教神庙的旧址上建起这座教堂。现存建筑的核心来自5世纪，瓦汉·马米科尼扬重建了已经破败的教堂，采用十字形平面，四根立柱独立承重。

1441年，数百名教士在埃奇米阿津开会，决议把大主教座从西斯迁到这里，基拉科斯大主教重修了教堂。当时此地归黑羊王朝统治；1502年萨法维波斯夺取这里，给了亚美尼亚教会一些特权。1604年，沙阿·阿拔斯一世在对奥斯曼的战争中把亚美尼亚人迁往波斯，埃奇米阿津随之遭到洗劫。沙阿原想把教堂拆掉，到波斯重建；最后只有著名的石块被运到伊斯法罕附近的新朱尔法，包括祭坛、相传基督降临处的那块石头和启蒙者格列高利的右臂，1611年被砌入当地的圣乔治教堂。

从1627年起，莫夫塞斯大主教修缮了穹顶、屋顶、地基和铺地，并在教堂四周筑墙，使之成为一座堡垒式的建筑群。西翼上的钟楼1654年动工，1658年建成。西缅大主教1771年在近旁办起亚美尼亚第一家印刷所。1804年6月，在俄波战争中，齐齐安诺夫将军的部队进入埃奇米阿津；据一位驻波斯宫廷的法国军事使节记载，俄军劫掠此地，严重损坏了亚美尼亚人的宗教建筑，沙阿对基督徒臣民却以礼相待。不久之后，波斯守住埃里温，俄军撤走。

en:
On the Absheron peninsula, at Surakhany near Baku, natural gas seeps from the rock through seven vents and burns on its own; the Persian name Ateshgah means house of fire. In the tenth century al-Istakhri wrote that fire-worshippers lived near Baku. The pentagonal complex standing there now, a courtyard ringed by monks' cells with a four-pillared altar in the middle and a trident above, was built in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, most likely by Indian merchants: Multani traders from Punjab, together with the Armenians, controlled much of the commercial economy around the Caspian. Of its seventeen inscriptions fourteen are Hindu, two Sikh and one Persian, and the dates on them run from 1668 to 1816. They dedicate the shrine to Jwala Ji, the fire goddess, and the building resembles her shrine at Jawalamukhi in the Himalayas; some devotees called the Baku shrine the greater Jwala Ji and the Kangra one the lesser. Whether Zoroastrians worshipped on the site earlier cannot be ruled out, but nothing proves it.

The people who kept the fire were a mixed company. Engelbert Kaempfer counted seven fires here in 1683 and met two worshippers descended from Persians who had gone to India, and the Jesuit Villotte found Hindus, Sikhs and Zoroastrians together. The German traveller Johannes Lerch recorded twelve Guebres living at the temple in 1733. In 1770 Samuel Gottlieb Gmelin saw devotees performing yogi austerities, and in 1784 George Forster found small jets of sulphurous fire in the cells, each coming from a funnel shaped like a Hindu altar and used for worship, cooking and warmth. In 1820 the French consul Gamba still found Hindus, Sikhs and Zoroastrians there.
zh:
巴库圣火庙在阿布歇隆半岛上巴库近旁的苏拉哈尼，天然气从岩缝的七处气孔渗出，自行燃烧；阿特什加这个波斯语名字意为「火的居所」。10世纪，伊斯塔赫里写到巴库附近住着拜火之人。现存的五边形建筑群建于17至18世纪，多半出自印度商人之手：来自旁遮普木尔坦的商人与亚美尼亚人一道，掌握着里海一带的大部分商业。院落四周排着僧房，中央是四柱祭坛，屋顶立着三叉戟。庙里共有十七处题记，十四处印度教、两处锡克教、一处波斯语，标明的年代从1668年到1816年。题记把此庙奉献给火焰女神久瓦拉吉，建筑也与喜马拉雅山麓贾瓦拉穆基的久瓦拉吉神庙相似；有的信徒把巴库这座称作大久瓦拉吉，坎格拉那座称作小久瓦拉吉。这里更早是否有琐罗亚斯德教徒礼拜，不能排除，但没有证据。

守着火的人成分混杂。1683年恩格尔贝特·肯普弗在这里数到七处火口，还遇到两名祖上从波斯迁往印度的礼拜者；耶稣会士维洛特见到印度教徒、锡克教徒和琐罗亚斯德教徒共处一庙。1733年，德国旅行家勒尔希记下庙里住着十二名古波斯拜火教徒。1770年，萨穆埃尔·格梅林看到信徒在行瑜伽苦修；1784年，乔治·福斯特看到各间僧房里都有小股带硫磺味的火焰，从一个做成印度祭坛形状的漏斗里喷出，用来礼拜、做饭和取暖。1820年，法国领事冈巴仍在这里见到印度教徒、锡克教徒和琐罗亚斯德教徒。

en:
Narikala is a citadel of two walled courts strung along a steep rocky ridge above the sulfur baths of Tbilisi, its walls stepping down towards the Kura, where Metekhi fortress faces it across the river. Georgian sources call it Shuris-tsikhe, the Rival Fortress, and legend credits its building to Vakhtang I Gorgasali. A fortress stood here by the fourth century, and the Georgian chronicles say a Persian governor built it to keep watch on the Iberian king at Mtskheta. David the Builder, who stormed Tbilisi in 1122, expanded it. The name Narikala first appears in the seventeenth century, from the Persian narin qala, 'citadel'; every major Georgian fortress had one, and in time only Tbilisi's kept the name.

Most of the works date from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, including the square Stambolis Tower and the Shahtakhti gun platform. In the reign of Rostom, the Safavid-appointed king of Kartli, a wall was run from the city to the fortress to divide the two, and he handed the fortress itself to the Iranians. The Turkish traveller Evliya Celebi was in Tbilisi at about this time. He counted six hundred flat-roofed houses inside the walls, with a mosque, a caravanserai, a bath and the khan's palace, and described a tower over the Kura with a water-hole so that the garrison could drink during a siege; Georgian scholars call his account somewhat exaggerated. A domed church of St Nicholas stood inside, which Vakhushti Batonishvili described in 1735. The Ottomans took Tbilisi in 1578 and held it for about forty years. In September 1795 Agha Mohammad Khan's Qajar army beat Heraclius II at Krtsanisi, and the fortress was badly damaged in the fighting; its walls were rebuilt the next year.
zh:
纳里卡拉堡由两座围墙院落连成，沿第比利斯硫磺浴场上方的陡峭石脊铺开，城墙顺山势向库拉河层层下降，与对岸的梅特希堡隔河相望。格鲁吉亚文献称它为舒里斯齐赫，意为「匹敌之堡」，相传它的修建者是瓦赫坦格一世·戈尔加萨利。4世纪这里已经有要塞，格鲁吉亚史书说是一名波斯总督所建，用来监视姆茨赫塔的伊比利亚国王。1122年攻克第比利斯的大卫四世扩建了它。纳里卡拉这个名字17世纪才见于记载，来自波斯语 narin qala，意为「城堡」；当时每座大要塞都有一个，后来只有第比利斯的保住了这个名字。

多数工事修建于16至17世纪，包括方形的伊斯坦布尔塔和沙赫塔赫提炮台。萨法维册封的卡特利国王罗斯托姆在位期间，一道墙从城区一直修到要塞，把城和堡隔开，他还把要塞本身交给了伊朗人。土耳其旅行家埃夫利亚·切莱比差不多同一时期到过第比利斯，他数出墙内有六百座平顶房屋，还有清真寺、商队客栈、浴场和汗的宫殿，又写到库拉河上的一座塔里有取水孔，守军被围时靠它解渴；格鲁吉亚学者认为他的描述有些夸张。堡内有一座圆顶的圣尼古拉堂，瓦赫什特·巴托尼什维利在1735年描述过它。奥斯曼人1578年夺取第比利斯，占据约四十年。1795年9月，卡扎尔的阿迦·穆罕默德汗在克尔察尼西击败伊拉克略二世，要塞在战斗中严重受损，次年城墙得到重修。

en:
The Marble Throne of the Golestan Palace stands on supports carved in the shapes of men, women, fairies and demons. Fath-Ali Shah commissioned it in 1805: 65 pieces of marble from a mine in Yazd, designed by the painter Mirza Baba Shirazi and carved by the royal stonecutter Mohammad Ebrahim Esfahani. It was modelled on the throne of the prophet Solomon, said to have been carried through the sky by genies and fairies and to have come down wherever Solomon wished. The palace is the royal complex inside the arg, Tehran's citadel, built under Shah Tahmasp I. Abbas I made a large garden in the north part of the enclosure, and Suleiman I built a palace there with an audience hall, where Shah Soltan Hoseyn received the Ottoman ambassador Ahmad Dari Effendi in the last year of his reign.

Karim Khan Zand took the throne in Tehran's old audience hall, putting on Nader Shah's armbands and other jewels that had been in the hands of the Qajar chief Mohammad Hasan Khan, and then held open court. He built a large new hall with an iwan, a garden and private quarters. He then went back to Shiraz. In 1786 Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar, who had spent sixteen years as a hostage at Karim Khan's court in Shiraz, made Tehran his capital. He was crowned King of Kings in 1796, and the Kiani Crown designed under him was made of red velvet set with about 1,800 pearls, 300 emeralds and 1,800 rubies, copied from Sasanian crowns and those of the mythical Kiyani shahs. His nephew Fath-Ali Shah was crowned in Tehran in 1797 and took his seat in the iwan, and expanded the complex.
zh:
戈勒斯坦宫（古列斯坦宫）的大理石御座，座脚刻成男人、女人、仙女和恶魔的形状。1805年法塔赫·阿里沙下令制作：六十五块采自亚兹德矿场的大理石，由画师米尔扎·巴巴·设拉子设计，王室石匠穆罕默德·易卜拉欣·伊斯法罕尼雕成。它仿照先知所罗门的王座，传说那座王座由精灵和仙女驮着在空中飞行，所罗门想落在哪里就落在哪里。宫殿是德黑兰城堡阿尔格里的王室建筑群，阿尔格建于沙阿·塔赫玛斯普一世时。阿拔斯一世在城堡北部辟了一座大花园，苏莱曼一世在那里建了带议事厅的宫殿，萨法维末代君主苏丹·侯赛因在位最后一年，就在这里接见奥斯曼大使艾哈迈德·达里·埃芬迪。

卡里姆汗·赞德在德黑兰的旧议事厅登基，身上戴着原先落在卡扎尔首领穆罕默德·哈桑汗手里的纳迪尔沙的臂环和其他珠宝，随后开放朝见。他在此新建了一座有敞厅的大议事厅、一座花园和后宫，之后回到设拉子。1786年，曾在设拉子卡里姆汗宫中做了十六年人质的阿迦·穆罕默德汗·卡扎尔定都德黑兰。1796年他加冕为众王之王；在他治下设计的基扬王冠以红丝绒制成，缀有约一千八百颗珍珠、三百颗祖母绿和一千八百颗红宝石，形制仿照萨珊王朝和神话中基扬诸沙的王冠。其侄法塔赫·阿里沙1797年在德黑兰加冕，在敞厅里登基，并扩建了这组宫殿。

en:
Local legend says that Shem, son of Noah, began the building of Khorezm and dug the sacred Xeyvak canal of Khiva with a miraculous spade, and that clay from here was used for buildings in Medina in the Prophet's lifetime. Itchan Kala is the walled inner city of Khiva, a rectangle of 650 by 400 metres. Its mud-brick walls are 8 to 10 metres high and 5 to 6 thick, 6,250 metres round, with a watchtower jutting out every 30 metres. Four gates, Ota on the west, Bogcha on the north, Tosh on the south and Polvon on the east, have towers on both sides of the passage. In 1598 the Amu Darya changed course and left the old capital, Gurganj, without water, and the state moved its capital to Khiva.

The Juma Mosque was founded in the tenth century and rebuilt in 1788 as a dimly lit hall of carved wooden columns, among them old ones taken from ancient buildings. Next to the west gate stands the Kunya-Ark, the citadel of the khans, whose western wall is among the oldest parts of the city. In the second half of the seventeenth century it gained Anusha Khan's baths, the Ak Mosque and the khan's reception hall. In the first half of the eighteenth century the war between Bukhara and Iran for the khanate damaged the city, and the broken walls were restored only near the century's end.

Pahlavon Mahmud (1247-1326) was a local poet from a family of humble craftsmen, an unbeatable wrestler and a healer, and the city has revered him as its patron. By his will he was buried in his own leather workshop, and the grave became a pilgrimage place for Uzbeks, Turkmens and Karakalpaks. A small mausoleum went up over it in 1664. In 1810, after a successful campaign against Kungrad, Muhammad Rahim Khan I decided to rebuild the whole complex with a richly decorated mausoleum, a pilgrims' room and a khanaqah. Several khans of Khiva were buried there, among them Abulgazi, Anusha and Muhammad Rahim himself.
zh:
当地相传，诺亚之子闪开创了花剌子模的营建，用一把神铲挖出希瓦神圣的海瓦克渠；又说这里的黏土在先知在世时被用来修建麦地那的建筑。希瓦内城是希瓦城墙围起的内城，是一个650米乘400米的长方形。土坯城墙高8至10米，厚5至6米，周长6250米，每隔30米外突一座敌楼。四座城门，西为阿塔门，北为巴赫恰门，南为托什门，东为波尔冯门，门道两侧有墩台。1598年阿姆河改道，旧都古尔甘吉断水，国家便把都城迁到了希瓦。

聚礼清真寺始创于10世纪，1788年重建，成为一座光线昏暗、立着雕花木柱的大厅，其中有取自古建筑的旧柱。西门旁是汗王的城堡库尼亚-阿尔克，它的西墙是城中最古老的部分之一。17世纪后半叶，这里添了阿努沙汗的浴室、阿克清真寺和汗的觐见厅。18世纪上半叶，布哈拉与伊朗为争夺汗国而交战，城市遭到重创，残破的城墙直到世纪末才修复。

帕赫拉万·马哈茂德（1247至1326）是当地诗人，出身卑微的匠人家庭，又是所向无敌的摔跤手和治病的人，城里人奉他为守护者。他留下遗嘱葬在自己的皮匠作坊里，墓地成了乌兹别克人、土库曼人和卡拉卡尔帕克人朝圣的地方。1664年墓上起了一座小陵。1810年，穆罕默德·拉希姆汗一世远征昆格勒得胜后，决定改建整个建筑群，修了装饰华丽的陵墓、供朝圣者用的房间和苏菲道堂。好几位希瓦汗葬在这里，其中有阿布勒加齐、阿努沙和拉希姆汗本人。

en:
The Registan is the great sandy square of Samarkand; its name means the place covered in sand. Crowds gathered on it to hear royal proclamations announced by blasts on enormous copper pipes, and to watch public executions. Between 1417 and 1420 Ulugh Beg built his madrasa on the west side: a high pointed-arch portal facing the square, four minarets at the corners, four domed lecture halls and two tiers of student cells around the courtyard. A Kufic inscription on the portal reads that the facade is twice the height of the sky and weighs so much that the Earth's spin is delayed. Ulugh Beg lectured there himself, and the poet Jami studied there. In 1444 it was one of the foremost schools of the Muslim east.

Opposite, on the east side, Ulugh Beg founded a khanaka in 1424, and a caravanserai of his stood on the north side. In 1500 Muhammad Shaybani took Samarkand from the last Timurid rulers. By the early seventeenth century the khanaka and the caravanserai had decayed, and Yalangtush Bahadur, the Uzbek ruler of Samarkand, ordered two new madrasas. The Sherdar Madrasa rose on the khanaka's site from 1619, built by the architect Abdul Jabbar with Muhammad Abbas as master of decoration. It nearly mirrors the older madrasa across the square, but its portal shows animals with the sun on their backs, tigers by its name though Russian accounts call them leopards, a motif found on Seljuk coins. Its oversized dome may have caused the building to deteriorate within a few decades.

From 1646 the Tilya-Kori, the Gilded Madrasa, went up on the site of Ulugh Beg's old caravanserai, partly reusing its foundations and walls. Its mosque on the west side of the courtyard, with gilded mihrab and minbar, served as the city's congregational mosque. Behind the Sherdar, where the roads to Tashkent, Bukhara and Shahrisabz meet, the Chorsu bazaar was rebuilt as a domed hat market in the later eighteenth century.
zh:
雷吉斯坦广场是撒马尔罕的大沙广场，「雷吉斯坦」的意思就是「铺沙之地」。人们聚在这里，听巨型铜管吹响后宣布的君王诏令，也围观公开处决。1417至1420年，兀鲁伯在广场西侧建起他的经学院：朝向广场的高大尖拱门楼，四角四座宣礼塔，四座穹顶讲堂，学生的僧房沿院落分两层排开。门楼上的库法体铭文写着，这面墙的高度是天的两倍，重得让大地的自转都变慢了。兀鲁伯亲自在这里讲学，诗人贾米也曾在这里求学。1444年，它是穆斯林东方最出色的学府之一。

对面的东侧，兀鲁伯在1424年建了一座罕卡修行所，北侧是他的商队客栈。1500年，昔班尼攻占撒马尔罕，从最后的帖木儿后裔手中夺走了这座城。17世纪初，罕卡和客栈都已破败，撒马尔罕的乌兹别克统治者雅兰图什·巴哈杜尔下令新建两座经学院。希尔·多尔经学院从1619年起在罕卡旧址上兴建，建筑师是阿卜杜勒·贾巴尔，穆罕默德·阿巴斯主持装饰。它几乎是对面老经学院的镜像，门楼上却是背负太阳的猛兽，名字里是虎，俄文资料则称之为雪豹，这种图案见于塞尔柱钱币。它过大的穹顶可能是建筑几十年后损坏的原因。

1646年起，季里·牙·卡尔里经学院（意为「贴金经学院」）在兀鲁伯旧商队客栈的旧址上兴建，部分沿用了原有的地基和墙体。院落西侧的清真寺里，米哈拉布和敏拜尔都贴了金，这座经学院兼作全城的聚礼清真寺。希尔·多尔身后，在通往塔什干、布哈拉和沙赫里萨布兹的几条路会合之处，乔尔苏巴扎在18世纪后期被重建成一座穹顶帽市。

en:
The Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta rode out to make a circuit of Sarai. He set off in the early morning and it was past midday when he reached the other end of the city. He counted thirteen mosques for Friday prayer and found each people living in its own quarter with its own bazaars, while visiting merchants had a walled quarter to protect their goods. The sultan's palace was called Altun Tash, 'golden head'. Al-Umari, writing a little later, said the city stood on salty ground and had no wall. Even at its height the khan did not stay in Sarai all year but moved with the Horde. It is unclear which Sarai either man described, since medieval writers may have known two successive towns of that name.

The brick ruins at Selitrennoye run for several kilometres along an Akhtuba branch. One estimate gives the built area about ten by two kilometres, with excavated estates, a mosque, a large necropolis and craft workshops. Most scholars now identify it with the newer Sarai of the 1330s, and where Batu's older town stood is still unsettled. Timur's army destroyed the newer capital in 1395. In 1444 the Great Horde was centred on Sarai, though the surviving court may have used another site or a much reduced town. Afanasy Nikitin passed through on his way to India, and in 1502 the Crimean khan Mengli I Giray sacked and burned the city.

In 1623-1624 the Russian merchant Fedot Kotov reported that the khan's court, palaces and mosques here were all of stone, and that the buildings were being pulled down and the stone carried to Astrakhan. When Samuel Gmelin travelled the lower Volga in 1769-1770, the Kalmyks told him that their fathers had found the city still in full splendour. Gmelin did not believe it and wrote that the old capital of Great Tatary had been ruined long before.
zh:
摩洛哥旅行家伊本·白图泰骑马绕萨莱城走了一圈：清晨出发，过了正午才到城的另一头。他数出十三座可以举行聚礼的清真寺，各族人各住各的街区，各有自己的集市，外来商人则住在一个有围墙的街区，墙是为了保护他们的货物。苏丹的宫殿叫「阿尔通塔什」，意思是「金头」。稍晚的阿尔-奥马里写到，这座城建在盐碱地上，没有城墙。即使在汗国最强盛的时候，可汗也不全年驻在萨莱，而是随汗廷迁徙。这两位作者写的是哪一座萨莱已不清楚，中世纪作者笔下可能先后有两座同名城镇。

谢利特连诺耶遗址的砖构残迹沿阿赫图巴一条支汊延伸数公里；有估算认为城区约长10公里、宽2公里，已发掘出宅院、清真寺、大型墓地和手工业作坊。多数学者现在认为这里是14世纪30年代建立的新萨莱，拔都时代的旧城在哪里仍无定论。1395年，帖木儿的军队摧毁了新都。1444年，大帐汗国以萨莱为中心，但残存的汗廷可能用的是另一处遗址，也可能是一座大幅缩小的城镇。阿法纳西·尼基京前往印度时经过此地；1502年，克里米亚可汗明里一世·格莱洗劫并焚毁了这座城。

1623至1624年，俄国商人费多特·科托夫记载，这里的汗廷、宫殿和清真寺都是石头建的，当时这些建筑正被拆掉，石料运往阿斯特拉罕。1769至1770年，萨穆埃尔·格梅林走过伏尔加河下游，卡尔梅克人告诉他，自己的祖辈来到这里时，城还完好壮丽。格梅林不信，他写道，大鞑靼的这座旧都早已被毁。

en:
Tortuga is a steep island that Columbus thought looked like a turtle's shell, a few kilometres off the north-west coast of Hispaniola. On its south side lies a sheltered harbour, and above it a steep rock stands on a plateau. In 1640 the French engineer Jean Le Vasseur built Fort de Rocher around that rock, with 24 guns trained on the harbour and a keep on top that he called the Dovecote. It could be entered only by a stair cut into the rock and then a ladder let down from above. A Spanish force from Santo Domingo lost a ship to the fort's guns, and the men who landed marched into an ambush. Le Vasseur opened the port to outlaws of every nation in exchange for a share of their takings, and Tortuga became the first great pirate outpost of the Caribbean. He did not last: in 1653 two of his lieutenants killed him. As the story goes, he had taken one man's mistress, and the two lured him out of the fort to inspect a warehouse, where a musket shot and then daggers finished him.

The men who gathered there were the boucaniers, named for the Arawak word buccan, the wooden frame on which meat was smoked. They began as landless hunters of wild cattle and boar on Hispaniola and Tortuga, selling smoked meat to passing corsairs; Spanish efforts to wipe out both the hunters and their cattle pushed them toward piracy. In 1663 the two buccaneer stations, Tortuga and Jamaica, were estimated to hold about fifteen ships and nearly a thousand men.

Alexandre Exquemelin reached Tortuga in 1666 as an indentured servant of the French West India Company, served three years, then joined the buccaneers, probably as a barber-surgeon, in the band of Henry Morgan. His account of them appeared in Dutch in Amsterdam in 1678 and in English in 1684. Morgan sued the English publishers for libel over its claim that he had set monks and nuns to carry scaling ladders at Portobello as human shields; the court found for him, the book was retracted, and he was paid 200 pounds.
zh:
托尔图加岛地势陡峻，哥伦布觉得它的轮廓像龟壳，在伊斯帕尼奥拉岛西北岸外数公里。南岸有一处避风的港湾，港湾上方的高地上耸着一块陡峭的巨岩。1640年，法国工程师让·勒瓦瑟尔绕着这块岩石修起罗谢堡，架着24门炮对准港口，岩顶上有他称作「鸽舍」的主楼；要进去，只能先走岩石中凿出的石阶，再登上从上面放下的梯子。不久，一支从圣多明各来的西班牙舰队被炮台击沉一艘船，登陆的人踩进了伏击圈。勒瓦瑟尔向各国亡命徒开放港口，只从每份战利品里抽成，托尔图加成了加勒比头一个大海盗据点。他自己没能坐稳：1653年，两名部下杀了他。据说他夺了其中一人的情妇，两人便把他骗出要塞去查看仓库，先开一枪，再用匕首结果了他。

聚在这里的人叫布坎尼尔，名字来自阿拉瓦克语的 buccan，指熏肉用的木架。他们原是伊斯帕尼奥拉和托尔图加没有土地的猎人，猎野牛和野猪，把熏好的肉卖给过路的海盗船；西班牙人想把猎人和牛群一起消灭，反而把他们推向了海盗这条路。1663年，据估计托尔图加和牙买加两个据点共有约十五条船、近一千人。

亚历山大·埃克斯克默兰1666年作为法国西印度公司的契约佣工来到托尔图加，服役三年后加入布坎尼尔，大概是以外科理发师的身份，跟随亨利·摩根的人马出海。他的记述1678年用荷兰文在阿姆斯特丹出版，1684年出了英译本。书里说摩根在波托贝洛攻城时逼修士和修女扛云梯当人肉盾牌，摩根为此告英文出版商诽谤，法庭判他胜诉，书被收回，他还拿到200英镑赔偿。

en:
Puerto Rico was the easternmost of Spain's Caribbean islands and a port of call for the treasure fleets, and the entrance to San Juan Bay was watched from a rocky headland the Spaniards called El Morro. In 1539 King Charles I authorised the first harbour defences. On the advice of Gonzalo Fernandez de Oviedo, who judged the site of La Fortaleza unsuitable, a battery went up on the headland: a tower with four embrasures and, at the foot of the slope, a water battery for three guns. In 1587 the military engineers Juan de Tejada and Bautista Antonelli drew up the design of the fort proper, and work began in 1589. The finished castle rises through six levels to 43 metres above the Atlantic.

In 1593 the first garrison arrived: Portuguese soldiers sent from Lisbon by Philip II, some bringing wives and some marrying Puerto Rican women. Two years later Francis Drake forced his way towards the bay, hoping to seize a cargo of gold and silver kept at La Fortaleza. A chain was drawn across the harbour entrance, and El Morro's gunners put a cannonball through the cabin of his flagship; Drake fell back with heavy losses. In June 1598 the Earl of Cumberland landed on the east side, where the defences were weak, and took El Morro from the land side, the only time it was taken in battle. Dysentery, which killed about 400 of his men, forced the English out by November. In 1625 a Dutch fleet under Boudewijn Hendricksz passed the castle into the harbour and burned the city, but El Morro held.

After the British took Havana in 1762, Charles III sent Field Marshal Alejandro O'Reilly and the engineer Tomas O'Daly to make San Juan a 'Defence of the First Order'. They began in 1765, and by the late 1780s O'Daly's engineers had finished El Morro in its present form.
zh:
波多黎各是西班牙加勒比岛屿中最东边的一座，也是运宝船队的停靠港，海角要塞（埃尔莫罗）所在的岩石岬角，西班牙人称作「莫罗」，守着圣胡安港湾的入口。1539年，国王卡洛斯一世批准修建最初的港口工事。贡萨洛·费尔南德斯·德·奥维耶多认为拉福塔莱萨的选址不合适，于是岬角上建起一座炮台：一座开四个炮眼的塔，山坡脚下另有一个能架三门炮的水边炮台。1587年，军事工程师胡安·德·特哈达和包蒂斯塔·安东内利画出要塞本体的设计，1589年开工。建成的城堡共六层，高出大西洋海面43米。

1593年，第一支守军抵达，是腓力二世从里斯本派来的葡萄牙士兵，有人带着妻子，有人娶了波多黎各女子。两年后，德雷克强行闯向港湾，想夺取存放在拉福塔莱萨的一批金银。港口入口拉起一条铁链，海角要塞的炮手一炮打穿了他旗舰的船舱，德雷克退了回去，损失惨重。1598年6月，坎伯兰伯爵在防御薄弱的东侧登陆，从陆地一侧拿下海角要塞，这是它唯一一次战败失守。痢疾夺去他约400名部下的性命，英军11月被迫撤走。1625年，鲍德温·亨德里克斯率领的荷兰舰队越过城堡驶入港湾，烧了城，海角要塞却守住了。

1762年英军攻陷哈瓦那后，卡洛斯三世派陆军元帅亚历杭德罗·奥赖利和工程师托马斯·奥戴利，要把圣胡安建成「一等防御」。他们1765年动工，到18世纪80年代末，奥戴利的工程师完成了海角要塞的改建，定下了最终的形制。

en:
A white dome stands on a hilltop at the edge of the Multan Fort, visible from miles away. The tomb was built between 1320 and 1324, and is believed to have been commissioned by Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq, who ruled Delhi from 1320 to 1325, probably as a tomb for himself. It is the earliest example of Tughluq architecture and older than the Tughluq monuments of Delhi. His son Muhammad bin Tughluq gave the building to the descendants of Sheikh Rukn-ud-Din Abul Fateh (1251-1335), the Suhrawardiyya Sufi of Multan and grandson of Bahauddin Zakariya, who is known as Shah Rukn-e-Alam, 'Pillar of the World'. By his own wish the sheikh had been buried in his grandfather's mausoleum, and his coffin was moved into this tomb later.

The tomb is an octagon of three tiers, thirty-five metres high, with sloping turrets at the corners and a battlemented roof, a mark of how far Tughluq military architecture shaped even buildings that were not military. Red brick is bound with shisham beams that have blackened over the centuries, and dark blue, azure and white tilework contrasts with the polished red brick. The dome is fifteen metres across and is reputed to be the second largest in South Asia after the Gol Gumbaz at Bijapur; the interior has no internal buttresses or supports. The sarcophagus lies a little off the centre, surrounded by the graves of seventy-two of the saint's relatives, which allude to the seventy-two companions of Imam Hussein killed at Karbala. The annual urs, the festival commemorating the saint's death, draws more than 100,000 pilgrims.
zh:
沙·鲁克内·阿拉姆陵的白色穹顶立在木尔坦堡边缘的高地上，几里外就能望见。陵墓建于1320至1324年，据信由统治德里的吉亚斯—乌德—丁·图格鲁克（1320至1325年在位）下令修建，很可能是给自己预备的墓。它是图格鲁克风格最早的建筑，比德里的图格鲁克诸建筑还早。他的儿子穆罕默德·本·图格鲁克把这座陵墓赠给了谢赫·鲁克努丁·阿布勒·法塔赫（1251—1335年）的后人。这位谢赫是木尔坦苏赫拉瓦迪耶教团的苏非圣徒、巴哈乌丁·扎卡里亚的孙子，封号沙·鲁克内·阿拉姆，意为「世界之柱」。他依照自己的遗愿葬在祖父的陵墓里，灵柩后来才迁入这座陵。

陵体八角三层，高35米，角上立着内倾的角塔，顶部环列雉堞，可见图格鲁克王朝的军事建筑风格连非军事建筑也受影响。墙身全用红砖，束以印度黄檀木梁，木梁历经数百年已经发黑，深蓝、天蓝与白色的瓷砖与打磨过的红砖形成对比。穹顶直径15米，据说是南亚第二大穹顶，仅次于比贾布尔的果尔·古姆巴斯；内部没有支撑结构。圣徒的石椁略偏中央安放，周围是他七十二名亲属的墓，这个数目暗指在卡尔巴拉殉难的伊玛目侯赛因的七十二名同伴。每年纪念圣徒忌辰的「乌尔斯」法会，吸引十万多名朝圣者。

en:
Mehrangarh crowns a rocky hill 122 metres above the Jodhpur plain, and the way in leads through seven gates. Rao Jodha, chief of the Rathores, moved his capital from Mandore, whose thousand-year-old fort no longer seemed safe, and fixed the foundation of the new fort on 12 May 1459. The hill was called Bhakurcheeria, the mountain of birds. According to legend its only human occupant was the hermit Cheeria Nathji, 'lord of birds', who refused again and again to leave. Jodha asked Karni Mata of Deshnoke, a warrior-sage of the Charan caste, for help, and at her word the hermit left at once, cursing the citadel with a lasting scarcity of water. Jodha built him a house and a temple to appease him, and Karni Mata laid the foundation stone herself.

Another account says a man of the Meghwal caste called Raja Ram offered to be buried alive in the foundations to bring the fort good fortune, in return for a promise that the Rathores would look after his family. His family was given land. Most of the existing fort dates from the reign of Maharaja Jaswant Singh, from 1638 to 1678, and its walls rise up to 36 metres high and 21 metres wide.

The gates record Marwar's wars. Jai Pol, the main gate, was built by Maharaja Man Singh in 1806 to celebrate his victories over the armies of Jaipur and Bikaner. Fateh Pol celebrates a victory over the Mughals in 1707. Dedh Kangra Pol still bears the scars of cannonballs fired by Jaipur's armies, and in the north-east a small memorial pavilion marks the spot where the soldier Kirat Singh Sodha fell defending the fort. Inside stand the Pearl Palace, the Flower Palace and the Mirror Palace. Beside Loha Pol, the last gate into the main part of the fort, are the handprints of ranis and princesses who committed sati after their husbands died.
zh:
梅兰加尔城堡踞在焦特布尔平原上方122米的岩山上，进堡要过七道门。拉索尔氏族的首领拉奥·乔达把都城从曼多尔迁出，那里的千年古堡在他看来已经不够安全；1459年5月12日，新堡奠基。岩山本叫巴库尔切里亚，即「鸟山」。相传山上唯一的住户是人称「鸟主」的隐士切里亚·纳特吉，他一再拒绝搬走。乔达请来德斯赫诺凯的查兰族武圣克勒妮·玛塔，隐士见她出面便立刻离去，临走诅咒这座城堡永远缺水。乔达在堡内为他建屋修庙以平息诅咒，奠基石由克勒妮·玛塔亲手安放。

另一种说法是，梅格瓦尔种姓的拉贾·拉姆自愿被活埋进地基，为城堡求吉，条件是拉索尔人照顾他的家族，他的家人得到了土地。现存的城堡大部分建于摩诃罗阇贾斯万特·辛格在位的1638至1678年；城墙最高36米，最厚21米。

一道道城门，记着马尔瓦尔的战事。主门贾伊门是摩诃罗阇曼·辛格1806年为庆祝战胜斋普尔和比卡内尔的军队而修建的。法塔赫门庆祝1707年战胜莫卧儿人。代德坎格拉门上留着斋普尔军队炮弹的痕迹；东北角有一座小亭，纪念守城时倒在那里的士兵基拉特·辛格·索达。堡内有珍珠宫、花宫和镜宫。进入堡内主区的最后一道门洛哈门旁边，留着王后和公主们的手印，她们在丈夫去世后殉夫自焚。

en:
The Taj Mahal stands on the right bank of the Yamuna at Agra, a white marble tomb that Shah Jahan commissioned for his wife Mumtaz Mahal. She died giving birth to their fourteenth child, in the camp where she had followed him on a campaign in the Deccan. Court historians recorded that he avoided affairs of state for a week. Tradition says that among her last wishes was a tomb more beautiful than any in the world.

Work began in 1632 on a site south of Agra where Raja Jai Singh had a mansion; he gave it up in exchange for a large palace in the middle of the city. More than twenty thousand workers and artisans were employed under a board of architects led by Ustad Ahmad Lahori; Ismail Afandi, from the Ottoman lands, designed the dome. Marble from Makrana came up a fifteen-kilometre earthen ramp on wagons drawn by oxen and elephants, and the builders raised a brick scaffold that mirrored the tomb instead of timber ones. Twenty-eight kinds of stone were inlaid in the marble, among them lapis from Afghanistan, turquoise from Tibet and jade from China. The tomb was finished in 1648; the complex is believed to have been completed in 1653.

The four minarets, each more than forty metres tall, were built leaning slightly outward so that, if they fell, they would fall away from the tomb. Below, Mumtaz's cenotaph lies at the exact centre of the chamber; Shah Jahan's stands to the west on a larger base, off the axis. In 1658 Aurangzeb deposed his father and held him in Agra Fort, from where he could see the Taj. Shah Jahan died in 1666 and was buried beside his wife. The gem merchant Tavernier, who visited Agra in 1665, wrote of a twin tomb of black marble planned across the river; the story is a myth. In the eighteenth century the Jats of Bharatpur, invading Agra, carried off two chandeliers, one of agate and one of silver, and the gold shield on the main finial.
zh:
泰姬陵在阿格拉的亚穆纳河右岸，是沙贾汗为妻子慕塔芝·玛哈修建的白色大理石陵墓。她随他在德干作战，在军营里生下第十四个孩子时去世。宫廷史家记载，皇帝一周不理朝政。相传她的遗愿之一，是要一座世上最美的陵墓。

工程1632年动工，基址在阿格拉城南，原是杰伊·辛格王公的府邸，他把它让出来，换得城中的一座大宫殿。两万多名工匠和民夫在乌斯塔德·艾哈迈德·拉合里为首的建筑师班子下做工，来自奥斯曼的伊斯梅尔·阿凡提设计穹顶。马克拉纳的大理石用牛和象拉的大车，沿十五公里长的夯土坡道运来；工匠没有搭木脚手架，而是砌起一座与陵墓同形的砖脚手架。大理石上镶嵌了二十八种宝石和美石，有阿富汗的青金石、西藏的绿松石和中国的玉。陵墓1648年建成，整个建筑群据信在1653年完工。

四座宣礼塔都高四十多米，微微向外倾斜，万一倒塌，会倒向远离陵墓的一侧。下层墓室里，慕塔芝的衣冠冢位于正中，沙贾汗的在西侧较大的基座上，偏离中轴。1658年奥朗则布废黜了父亲，把他软禁在阿格拉堡，隔河能望见泰姬陵。沙贾汗1666年去世，葬在妻子身旁。宝石商人塔韦尼耶1665年到过阿格拉，他写到河对岸原计划再建一座黑色大理石的孪生陵墓，这个说法只是传闻。18世纪，珀勒德布尔的贾特人入侵阿格拉，劫走一盏玛瑙吊灯、一盏银吊灯，以及主宝顶上的金罩。

en:
According to the Sthala Purana, Hampi began with a goddess: Parvati, as Pampa, practised austerities on Hemakuta Hill to win the ascetic Shiva, and the name Hampi descends from hers. Pilgrims came to the Virupaksha temple long before the Vijayanagara emperors made the place their capital in 1336, and local tradition holds that it alone kept drawing worshippers after 1565. Its painted gopuram is 50 metres high and opens onto a 750-metre stone bazaar; inside are a hundred-column hall and a community kitchen fed by a channel cut into the rock. Some 1,600 monuments lie among the granite boulders, mostly Dravidian in style, with Hoysala touches in some pillars and ceilings and Indo-Islamic arches and domes in a few buildings such as the elephant stables.

A Krishna temple dated 1515 fronts a long bazaar street wide enough for chariots, and south of it sits a 6.7-metre Narasimha, the man-lion form of Vishnu, in yoga; its floor is stained with carbon from an attempt to burn the shrine. At the Vitthala complex a stone chariot shrine holds Garuda, and a hall of 56 stone beams gives musical notes when struck. In the royal centre the Mahanavami platform rises in three stages carved with marching elephants, horses and camels, female stick-dancers, and townspeople throwing water at one another at Holi; visitors called it the House of Victory. Near the river stands the King's Balance, of the kind used for the tulabharam rite, in which a person gave gifts equal to his body weight. The elephant stables are eleven chambers, ten of them domed.

In 1520 the Portuguese Domingo Paes found the city as large as Rome and the best provided in the world. After the battle of Talikota on 23 January 1565 the sultanates' armies plundered it; older accounts say they camped there six months and burned the country far around, though historians now see little evidence of damage beyond the royal centre. The wooden pavilion that probably stood on the platform burned, and a hundred stone stubs mark the audience hall beside it. A few decades later the Italian Cesare Federici reported the houses still standing but empty, inhabited, he was told, only by tigers and other wild beasts.
zh:
据《斯塔拉往世书》，亨比的缘起是一位女神：帕尔瓦蒂化身潘帕，在赫马库塔山上苦修，要赢得苦行的湿婆，亨比这个名字就由她的名字演变而来。早在毗奢耶那伽罗的皇帝们于1336年在此建都之前，香客就已来到维鲁帕克沙神庙，当地传说称，1565年之后只有这座庙仍有信众聚集。庙前的彩绘瞿布罗门楼高50米，朝向一条750米长的石砌市集；门内有百柱厅，还有一座公共厨房，水由凿在岩石上的水渠引来。约一千六百处古迹散布在花岗岩巨石之间，多为达罗毗荼式，部分柱子和天花带有曷萨拉风格，象厩等少数建筑则用了印度伊斯兰式的拱券与穹顶。

1515年的克里希纳神庙前是一条宽得能走战车的长市集街，神庙以南是6.7米高、结跏趺坐的人狮毗湿奴（那罗辛哈），神龛的地面被烟熏得发黑，那是有人想烧毁这座神龛留下的炭痕。维塔拉神庙群里有供奉迦楼罗的石战车，还有一座由56根石梁组成的大厅，敲击时能发出乐音。王城区的大平台（玛哈纳瓦米平台）分三层，壁上刻着列队的象、马、骆驼，持棍的女舞者，还有在洒红节上互相泼水的市民；来访的外国人称它为「胜利之家」。河边立着国王天平，这类天平用于「称身布施」仪式，施主按自己的体重施舍财物。象厩是一排十一间屋子，其中十间带穹顶。

1520年，葡萄牙人多明戈·派斯觉得这座城和罗马一样大，是世上供应最周全的城市。1565年1月23日塔利科塔之战后，诸苏丹国的军队洗劫了它；较早的记述说他们在此驻扎了六个月，把周围大片地方烧得干干净净，不过也有学者认为，王城区以外几乎没有受损的证据。平台上很可能有过的木构楼阁被焚，旁边的觐见厅只剩一百根石柱残桩。几十年后，意大利人切萨雷·费德里奇说，城里的房子仍然立着，却空无一人，据说里面住的只有老虎和别的野兽。

en:
A medieval Marathi legend says a queen vowed to fast until she could see the spire of a temple, and the architect Kokasa began at the top of a rock and carved downward, finishing the shikhara within a week; the temple was named Manikeshwar after her. The story seems to refer to Kailasa, Cave 16 at Ellora, usually attributed to the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I and carved, archaeologists believe, out of a single rock from the top down. Its courtyard measures 82 by 46 metres at the base, the top of the sanctuary stands 32.6 metres above the court, the base is carved so that elephants seem to hold the temple aloft, and one panel shows Ravana shaking Mount Kailasa. A copper-plate inscription of about 812 says that Krishnaraja built a temple at Ellora so wondrous that even the gods and its architect were astonished.

Kailasa is the largest of thirty-four temples and monasteries, Buddhist, Hindu and Jain, cut side by side along two kilometres of basalt cliff in the Charanandri hills, 29 kilometres northwest of Aurangabad. Excavation began in the sixth or seventh century. The Rashtrakutas carved part of the Hindu and Buddhist caves, and the Yadavas the last of the Jain ones. Jain worship here ended after the region fell under Islamic rule in the late thirteenth century.

Khilji's troops, who desecrated a Yadava temple at nearby Devagiri, left the Ellora temple alone and came to look at it, and Sufi orders later camped in the caves, which took the name Rauza. The Bijapur historian Rafi al-Din Shirazi called Kailasa a wonder and a rarity, comparable to Persepolis. Under the Mughals Aurangzeb used to picnic there with his family; he is recorded as calling Kailasa one of the wonders of the transcendent Artisan, and there is no record that he tried to destroy it, whatever later tradition says. Niccolao Manucci judged from the workmanship that the caves were the work of the ancient Chinese. The art historian Hermann Goetz thought the last layer of paint in Kailasa was commissioned by the Maratha queen Ahilyabai Holkar.
zh:
一则中世纪马拉地传说讲，一位王后立誓不见神庙塔尖便不进食，建筑师科卡萨就从岩石顶部开始向下雕凿，一周之内完成了塔尖；神庙因这位王后得名马尼格什瓦尔。故事似乎指的是埃洛拉的第16窟凯拉萨神庙，通常归于罗湿陀罗拘陀国王克里希纳一世，考古学家认为它是从整块岩石由上往下凿成的。庭院底部长82米、宽46米，圣所顶端高出庭院32.6米，基座雕成象群托举神庙的样子，还有一幅浮雕刻着罗波那撼动凯拉萨山。约812年的一块铜版铭文说，克里希纳罗阇在埃洛拉造了一座神庙，奇妙得连神祇和建筑师本人都为之惊叹。

凯拉萨是埃洛拉石窟三十四座寺院和僧院中最大的一座，佛教、印度教和耆那教的石窟沿恰拉南德里山两公里长的玄武岩崖壁并排开凿，在奥兰加巴德西北29公里。开凿始于六七世纪。罗湿陀罗拘陀王朝开凿了一部分印度教窟和佛教窟，亚达瓦王朝开凿了最后几座耆那教窟。13世纪晚期这一带落入伊斯兰统治后，耆那教在此的礼拜随之中止。

基尔吉的军队亵渎了附近德瓦吉里的一座亚达瓦神庙，却没有动埃洛拉的神庙，反而把它当作景点来看；后来苏非教团在石窟里扎营，这里得名「劳扎」。比贾布尔史家拉菲丁·设拉子称凯拉萨是奇观和稀世之物，足以与波斯波利斯相比。莫卧儿时期，奥朗则布常带家人来此野餐；据记载，他称凯拉萨是大匠（真主）的奇迹之一，也没有记录说他试图毁坏它，尽管后来的传说另有讲法。尼科劳·马努齐根据工艺断定石窟出自「古代中国人」之手。艺术史家赫尔曼·戈茨认为，凯拉萨最后一层彩绘是马拉塔女王阿希莉娅拜·霍尔卡委托绘制的。

en:
The Sun Temple at Konark was built as the stone chariot of the sun god Surya. It is attributed to King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty and dated to about 1250, on the coast some thirty-five kilometres north-east of Puri. Twelve pairs of carved wheels line its base, each nearly 3.7 metres across, with seven horses pulling. The wheels are sundials: eight spokes mark the eight watches of the day, and the shadows give the time to the minute. Seen from inland at dawn, the khondalite chariot seems to rise out of the sea carrying the sun. The tower over the sanctuary is estimated to have stood about seventy metres high; the assembly hall that survives is about thirty-nine.

Odia folklore tells of Dharmapada, the twelve-year-old son of the master builder Bishu Maharana. The king had threatened to execute all 1,200 craftsmen unless the crown was finished by morning; the boy completed it alone in a single night, and when the masons feared they would be doomed if the truth came out, he jumped to his death. No source mentions him before the nineteenth century.

Worship was still going on in 1384, when a copper-plate inscription records it, and Abul Fazl, writing at Akbar's court, described a prosperous site whose temple astonished visitors. Kalapahar, the Bengal general who invaded Odisha in 1568, is believed to have attacked the temple, and one study dates its ruin to between the late sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries. Sailors in the Bay of Bengal used the dark mass as a landmark and called it the Black Pagoda, against the White Pagoda of Jagannatha at Puri; the name appears in European accounts by 1676. In the eighteenth century a Maratha holy man found it abandoned and overgrown. Under Maratha rule Konark's stone went into the wall around the Puri temple, and around 1779 the brahmachari Goswain had the ten-metre chlorite Aruna pillar moved from the entrance to the Lion Gate at Puri. In 1803 the East India Marine Board asked that the ruin be protected; the only step taken was a ban on removing more stone.
zh:
戈纳勒格太阳神庙（科纳克太阳神庙）被建成太阳神苏利耶的石战车。相传为东恒伽王朝的那罗辛诃·提婆一世所建，约在1250年，位于普里东北约三十五公里的海岸。底座两侧共有十二对雕花石轮，每只直径近3.7米，前方有七匹马牵引。这些轮子同时是日晷：八根轮辐标出一天的八个时辰，日影能把时间读到分。黎明从陆上望去，这座孔兹岩战车仿佛载着朝阳从海中升起。神龛上方的主塔估计原高约七十米，残存的集会殿约三十九米。

奥里亚民间传说里有个十二岁的少年达摩帕德，是工匠头比苏·莫赫拉纳的儿子。国王下令，塔顶若不能在天亮前完工，一千二百名工匠都要处死；少年独自一夜把塔顶装好，工匠们却怕真相泄露后自己难逃一死，他便跳下身亡。19世纪以前的资料都没有提到过他。

1384年的铜版铭文记载这里仍有祭祀，阿克巴宫廷里的阿布勒·法兹勒也写到一座兴盛的神庙，令来访者惊叹。1568年入侵奥里萨的孟加拉将领卡拉帕哈德，据信攻击过这座神庙；有研究把它的毁坏定在16世纪末至17世纪初。孟加拉湾的水手把这座黑色巨物当作航标，称它「黑塔」，与普里贾格纳特神庙的「白塔」相对，1676年的欧洲人记载里已有此名。18世纪，一位马拉塔苦行僧人发现这里荒废无人，被草木覆盖。马拉塔统治时期，戈纳勒格的石料被拿去修普里神庙的围墙；1779年前后，梵行者戈萨因把庙前十米高的绿泥石阿噜那石柱迁走，立到普里神庙的狮门前。1803年，东印度海事局请求保护遗址，实际只做了一件事：禁止再从这里运走石料。

en:
Swayambhunath stands on a hill west of Kathmandu, in a valley that was once a lake. The name means 'self-arising'. According to the Swayambhu Purana the lake was home to nagas, until the Buddha Vipassi, of an age long past, sowed a lotus seed in it. The seed grew into a flower of a thousand petals that gave out an eternal light. Manjushri came to worship, drained the lake by cutting through the mountains with his indestructible sword, and later Prachandadev, king of Gaud, raised a great stupa to protect the light, which hid it from view.

A long stairway on the eastern side of the hill, built in the seventeenth century by Pratap Malla of Kathmandu, leads up to a white dome. On it stands a cube painted on all four faces with the eyes of the Buddha looking in every direction, the nose between them shaped as the Nepali numeral one. Above the cube rise thirteen gold-plated bronze rings, the thirteen stages before nirvana. Monkeys live on the hill and have given the shrine the name Monkey Temple; they are said to be lice from the hair of Manjushri.

A damaged inscription records work ordered here by a Licchavi king in 640. Nagarjuna is said to have stayed on the hill for twelve years, and Shantarakshita and Padmasambhava to have performed rites here on their way to Tibet. In the fifteenth century the Indian monk Shariputra, the last known abbot of Bodh Gaya, found the stupa in bad condition and had it restored with the help of a Malla king, probably by 1412; he went on to Tibet and China and died in Beijing in 1426. In 1504 King Ratna Malla of Kantipur invited the Kagyu yogin Tsangnyon Heruka, the Madman of Tsang, who completed a renovation within three months.
zh:
斯瓦扬布纳特寺（斯瓦扬布，又称四眼天神庙）坐落在加德满都以西的山丘上，这片谷地从前是一个湖。寺名意为「自体升起」。《斯瓦扬布往世书》说，湖里住着龙众，直到久远年代的毗婆尸佛在湖中播下一粒莲子，长出千瓣莲花，放出永恒的光芒。文殊菩萨前来朝拜，用斩不断的宝剑劈开群山、排干湖水；后来高达国王普罗昌达德瓦为保护这道光建起大佛塔，光芒便被塔身遮住。

山东侧有一道长长的石阶，是17世纪加德满都国王普拉塔普·马拉修筑的，沿阶而上是白色的穹顶。穹顶上立着方台，四面各绘一双佛眼注视四方，两眼之间的鼻形是尼泊尔数字的「一」。方台之上是十三层鎏金铜相轮，对应涅槃之前的十三层境界。山上栖居着猴子，因此又叫「猴庙」；相传这些猴子是文殊菩萨头发里的虱子所化。

一块损坏的碑文记载，640年一位李查维国王曾下令在此施工。相传龙树曾在山上驻锡十二年，寂护和莲花生入藏途中也在此作过法事。15世纪，印度高僧室利沙（菩提伽耶已知的末代住持）见佛塔破败，在一位马拉国王协助下主持重修，约在1412年前完工；他随后前往西藏和中国，1426年在北京圆寂。1504年，甘提布尔国王拉特纳·马拉请来噶举派瑜伽士藏宁·赫如迦，人称「藏地疯圣」，他三个月内完成了一次修缮。

en:
Over the gate of the Bara Katra, the Great Caravanserai, a Persian inscription by Shaduddin Muhammad Siraji said that Prince Shah Shuja was always absorbed in charity, and that Abul Qasim had built the house in hope of God's mercy. Twenty-two shops were attached to it, their rents to pay for repairs and to lodge travellers free; whoever undid the arrangement would be punished on the Day of Judgment. The building stands on the north bank of the Buriganga at Dhaka, south of the Chawk Bazaar. Mir Abul Qasim, diwan and chief revenue officer of Shah Shuja, built it between 1644 and 1646. It was meant as the residence of the prince, who governed Bengal and Orissa for his father Shah Jahan, but it served as a hostelry for travellers. The plan followed the caravanserais of Central Asia: four wings enclosed a square courtyard, with shops and living quarters on all four sides. The river-facing south wing ran almost sixty-eight metres, its centre thrust forward in a three-storey gateway beside tall octagonal towers, and the way in led through a guardroom and an octagonal domed hall into the court.

Shah Shuja did not stay in Bengal. When Shah Jahan fell ill in 1657 he proclaimed himself emperor, but Aurangzeb's army beat him at Khajwa in January 1659. Pursued back through Bengal, he reached Dhaka on 12 April 1660 and a month later boarded ships for Arakan. The half dozen camel-loads of gold and jewels he brought were beyond anything seen before in Arakan, but its king Sanda Thudhamma never provided the ships to Mecca that he had promised. When Shuja plotted to overthrow him the plot was betrayed; he set fire to Mrauk U, was captured and was put to death, and his treasure was melted down.

In Mughal times Dhaka was a river port where large merchant ships could enter the Buriganga, with an important trade link to Indonesia, and the katra was used mainly for customs clearance and as a resting place for merchants and travellers. Shaista Khan, a later governor, built the slightly smaller Chhota Katra 185 metres to the east in 1663 for his officials and growing family.
zh:
巴拉卡特拉商队驿站（意为「大驿站」）的门上嵌着一块波斯语石匾，由沙德丁·穆罕默德·西拉吉撰文，写道沙舒贾亲王一向热心施舍，阿布·卡西姆为求神恩建了这座房屋。附带的二十二间店铺，租金用来修缮房屋并供旅人免费投宿；谁若撤销这一安排，末日审判时必将受罚。驿站在达卡布里甘加河北岸、乔克巴扎尔以南，1644年至1646年由沙舒贾的迪万、首席税务官米尔·阿布·卡西姆修建。它本是为亲王准备的居所，亲王代父沙贾汗治理孟加拉和奥里萨，但驿站实际用作旅舍。它仿照中亚商队客栈的形制：四座翼楼围成方形庭院，四面都是店铺和住房。临河的南翼长近六十八米，中央突出三层门楼，旁边是高耸的八角塔楼；进门先过卫兵室，再经一座八角形穹顶大厅才到庭院。

沙舒贾没有在孟加拉久留。1657年沙贾汗病重，他自立为帝，却在1659年1月的卡朱瓦之战中败给奥朗则布的军队。他被一路追击退回孟加拉，1660年4月12日到达卡，一个月后登船前往若开。他带去的六驮金银珠宝，是若开从未见过的财富，可若开国王僧陀都昙摩（Sanda Thudhamma）始终没有按许诺提供去麦加的船。沙舒贾图谋推翻国王，事情败露，他放火烧了妙乌城，被捕后处死，财宝被熔化。

莫卧儿时代的达卡是河港，大型商船可以驶入布里甘加河，同印度尼西亚之间有重要的贸易往来，驿站主要用于清关，也供商人和旅客歇脚。后来的总督沙伊斯塔汗在东面一百八十五米处建起稍小的「小卡特拉」（Chhota Katra），1663年落成，供官员和他日益庞大的家族居住。

en:
Many of the teak pillars of the Kanbawzathadi Palace carried Mon inscriptions naming the towns, regions and people who had donated them.
