Bayinnaung, founder-king of the Toungoo empire, commissioned the palace in his capital Pegu on 17 November 1553, and by 1556 it had seventy-six halls and apartments on a seventy-acre plot at the centre of the city. European visitors wrote of its richly gilded buildings. The Great Audience Hall was the largest, roofed with gold plates and painted gold inside, and the king received his ministers there beside the Lion Throne, carved with lions. The palace had nine royal thrones, each with its own motif and used on different occasions. The Bee Throne Hall held the king's private quarters and was topped by a seven-tiered pyatthat roof.

In 1565 Shans who had been resettled in Pegu rose in rebellion and burned down much of the capital, the whole palace complex included. Bayinnaung had it rebuilt, and on 16 March 1568 the new palace was opened with every vassal ruler present. He raised the titles of four former kings living in Pegu, among them Mekuti of Lan Na and Maha Chakkraphat of Siam. When Bayinnaung died in 1581, his son Nanda Bayin cremated him in front of the palace as a universal ruler. Nanda's empire fell apart, and in 1599 Toungoo and Arakanese forces besieged Pegu for months until the city fell. The victors divided its gold, silver and jewels, and the Arakanese burned the city down, the palace with it. Eight of the nine thrones were lost in the fire.
zh:
勃固王宫（甘菩遮塔迪宫）的许多柚木殿柱刻着孟文铭文，记下献柱的城镇、地区和人的名字。东吁帝国的开创者勃印曩，于1553年11月17日下令在都城勃固兴建这座王宫，到1556年，宫中已有七十六座厅堂和寝宫，坐落在城市正中七十英亩的地块上。到访的欧洲人写道，殿宇满饰金箔，富丽堂皇。大觐见厅最大，殿顶铺金板，内壁漆金，国王在这里接见大臣，身旁是雕满狮子的狮子座。宫中有九座王座，纹饰各不相同，用于不同的场合。蜂王座殿是国王的私人起居处，顶上立着七层重檐的塔尖。

1565年，重新安置在勃固的掸人起事，烧毁了大片都城，整个宫城都在其中。勃印曩下令重建，1568年3月16日新宫启用，各属国君主齐聚。他还给住在勃固的四位前国王晋封，其中有兰那的缅古底和暹罗的玛哈·扎克拉帕特。1581年勃印曩去世，儿子南达勃因在宫前按转轮圣王之礼将他火化。南达的帝国随后分崩离析，1599年东吁和若开的军队围攻勃固数月，终于破城。胜利者瓜分了城里的金银珠宝，若开人又把全城烧毁，王宫也在其中。九座王座中有八座毁于这场大火。

en:
Angkor Wat faces west, unlike most Khmer temples, and its reliefs run counter-clockwise, the reverse of the usual order and the one used in Brahmin funeral rites; some scholars take this to mean that Suryavarman II intended it as his tomb. At the equinox the rising sun stands over the central tower when seen from the western causeway. Suryavarman began the temple about 1122 on the advice of the brahmin Divakarapandita as his state temple to Vishnu, and work ceased at his death about 1150 with some of the reliefs unfinished. Between five and ten million sandstone blocks, the heaviest 1.5 tons, were quarried at Mount Kulen about forty kilometres away.

The temple fills 162 hectares of the old capital inside a moat 190 metres wide and more than five kilometres around. Three galleries climb to a quincunx of towers, the central one 65 metres above the ground: the five peaks of Mount Meru, with the wall and moat for the surrounding mountains and ocean. Almost a thousand square metres of bas-relief line the outer gallery, among them the churning of the sea of milk, a procession of Suryavarman himself, and the 32 hells and 37 heavens. More than 1,796 devatas have been documented on the walls, and their hair, headdresses and jewellery vary from figure to figure.

When the temple passed to Theravada Buddhism, the central shrine was walled in and the new walls were carved with standing Buddhas. Unlike most Angkor monuments, it was never wholly abandoned. Pilgrims left Buddha images in the cruciform cloister called the Hall of a Thousand Buddhas and cut merit inscriptions there in Khmer, Burmese and Japanese. Japanese visitors of the early 1600s took the temple for the Jetavana, the Buddha's monastery in India. A relief of Vishnu defeating the asuras was added in the sixteenth century, and several towers were pulled down in the mid-seventeenth. The oldest surviving plan of the temple carries the Jetavana label. It is an illustrated plan, not a survey, copied in Nagasaki in 1715 by Fujiwara Tadayoshi from an undated drawing credited to the interpreter Shimano Kenryo, a name the Japanese scholar Yoshiaki Ishizawa suspects was an alias.
zh:
和大多数高棉寺庙不同，吴哥窟坐东朝西，浮雕按逆时针排列，与通常的次序相反，正是婆罗门葬仪的次序；一些学者因此认为苏利耶跋摩二世是想把它造成自己的陵庙。春秋分之日从西边引道望去，初升的太阳正挂在中塔之上。苏利耶跋摩二世约在1122年采纳婆罗门国师（Divakarapandita）的建议动工，作为供奉毗湿奴的国庙，约1150年他去世时工程中止，部分浮雕未完工。建庙用了五百万到一千万块砂岩石料，最重的一块达一吨半，采自约四十公里外的库楞山。

庙占地162公顷，坐落在旧都之内，四周围着190米宽、周长逾五公里的护城河。三层回廊逐层升高，通向五塔组成的塔林，中塔高出地面65米：五塔象征须弥山五峰，城墙与护城河就是环绕的群山与大海。外围回廊有近一千平方米的浮雕，其中有搅乳海、苏利耶跋摩二世本人的行列，以及三十二层地狱和三十七重天。墙上已记录的女神像超过1796尊，发式、头冠和首饰各不相同。

吴哥窟转入上座部佛教后，中央神殿被封入墙中，新墙面刻上立身佛像。与吴哥大多数古迹不同，它从未被彻底废弃。朝圣者把一尊尊佛像供进十字形的千佛廊，又在廊中刻下做功德的铭文，文字有高棉文、缅文和日文。17世纪初的日本来客，把这座庙当成了佛陀在印度的祇园精舍。16世纪，回廊上增刻了毗湿奴战胜阿修罗的浮雕；17世纪中叶，几座塔被拆除。现存最早的吴哥窟平面图就题作祇园精舍图：这是一幅示意图，不是实测图，1715年藤原忠义在长崎摹绘，所据原图没有年份，传为通词岛野兼了所作，日本学者石泽良昭怀疑这个名字是化名。

en:
The royal mosque of the Aceh sultans, the original Baiturrahman, had a multi-tiered thatched roof, a typical feature of Acehnese architecture. Tradition gives it two founding dates: 1612, under Sultan Iskandar Muda, or 1292, under Sultan Alaidin Mahmudsyah. The earlier date would put the mosque more than two centuries before Ali Mughayat Syah founded the sultanate and began his conquests of northern Sumatra in 1520. It stood in Kutaraja, the capital, later called Banda Aceh.

Aceh was called the 'porch of Mecca'. Its court became a noted centre of Islamic scholarship and trade, where the Qur'an and other Islamic texts were translated into Malay, and scholars such as Hamzah Fansuri, Abdurrauf of Singkil and Nuruddin ar-Raniri worked. Iskandar Muda extended the sultanate's control over most of Sumatra. After his son-in-law Iskandar Thani a series of queens ruled, until a man took the throne in 1699 for the first time in almost sixty years. Regional rulers gained the real power, and by the 1680s a Persian visitor could describe a northern Sumatra where 'every corner shelters a separate king or governor'. In 1727 a Bugis dynasty took power.

At the turn of the nineteenth century the court was that of Sultan Jauhar al-Alam, who spoke English and French. He allowed the Chinese captain of Penang, Koh Lay Huan, to gather pepper plants in Aceh to start pepper cultivation on Penang.
zh:
亚齐苏丹的王家清真寺，也就是最初的拜图拉赫曼大清真寺，屋顶是多层叠起的茅草顶，这是亚齐建筑的典型特征。传统上它有两个始建年代：一说是1612年伊斯坎达尔·穆达苏丹在位时，一说是1292年阿拉丁·马哈茂德沙苏丹所建。若是后一说，这座清真寺比阿里·穆加亚特沙建立苏丹国、在1520年开始征服苏门答腊北部还早两百多年。它位于都城哥打拉贾，后来称班达亚齐。

亚齐被称为「麦加走廊」。宫廷成为著名的伊斯兰学术和贸易中心，《古兰经》等伊斯兰典籍在这里译成马来文，哈姆扎·凡苏里、辛基尔的阿卜杜拉乌夫和努鲁丁·拉尼里等学者在此活动。伊斯坎达尔·穆达把苏丹国的控制扩展到苏门答腊大部分地区。他的女婿伊斯坎达尔·萨尼之后，历代女王相继执政，直到1699年才有男性登位，距上一位男性统治者近六十年。实权落到地方首领手里，1680年代，一位波斯旅人写到，苏门答腊北部「每个角落都有各自的国王或总督」。1727年，一个布吉人王朝取得王位。

19世纪之交，在位的是会说英语和法语的佐胡尔·阿拉姆苏丹。他准许槟城的华人甲必丹辜礼欢（Koh Lay Huan）在亚齐采集胡椒苗，在槟城开始种植胡椒。

en:
Pura Besakih climbs nearly 1,000 metres up the slopes of Mount Agung, the highest mountain on Bali, in six terraced levels. Indonesian accounts count twenty-six related temples, led by Pura Penataran Agung; the English account counts twenty-three. A split gateway marks the entrance, and the Kori Agung gate opens into the second courtyard. The stone bases of Penataran Agung and several other temples resemble megalithic stepped pyramids at least 2,000 years old, and the site was almost certainly holy in prehistoric times. Balinese tradition says the sage Rsi Markendya received his divine revelation at Pura Basukian, here in the complex. Hindu worship is certain from 1284, when the first Javanese conquerors settled in Bali.

By the fifteenth century it was a state temple of the Gelgel dynasty, which had an origin story of its own. The Babad Dalem, an eighteenth-century chronicle, says that Majapahit planted a vassal dynasty on Bali and that its second ruler, Dalem Samprangan, was vain and incompetent. His youngest brother Dalem Ketut founded a new royal seat at Gelgel and visited Majapahit, where Hayam Wuruk gave him powerful heirlooms. Majapahit then fell into chaos and vanished. The chronology does not hold, since Hayam Wuruk died in 1389 and Majapahit fell in the early sixteenth century.

Gelgel dominated Bali from the early sixteenth century to 1686. About the middle of that century the Brahmin sage Nirartha, who had fled chaotic conditions in Java, was received at the court of Dalem Baturenggong. In Gelgel village the dynasty's ancestral shrine was Pura Jero Agung, beside Pura Dasar, a lowland counterpart of Besakih. The Dutch first appeared in 1597 and entered friendly relations with the king. They found a densely populated island of more than 300,000 people, whose cotton cloth traders from Java's north coast exchanged for pepper. Fighting broke out at court after a king died in 1651. In 1686 the usurping minister Anglurah Agung fell in battle, and Dewa Agung Jambe, a scion of the old line, set up a new seat at Klungkung.
zh:
布撒基寺沿巴厘最高峰阿贡火山的山坡向上，分六层台地，海拔近一千米。印尼语资料记有26座彼此相连的寺庙，以佩纳塔兰阿贡主庙为首，英文资料则作23座。入口是一座中劈山门，科里阿贡宫门通向第二进院落。佩纳塔兰阿贡和其他几座寺庙的石基形似巨石阶梯金字塔，至少已有两千年，这片土地在史前几乎可以肯定就是圣地。巴厘人相传，圣贤摩根德耶在寺内的巴苏基安寺领受了神的启示。可以确定的是，自1284年第一批爪哇征服者定居巴厘起，这里就是印度教的礼拜地。

到15世纪，它已是格尔格尔王朝的一座国家神庙，这个王朝有自己的来历。18世纪的《巴巴德·达仑》记载，满者伯夷在巴厘扶植了一个藩属王朝，第二代国王达仑·桑普朗岸自负又无能。他的幼弟达仑·克图在格尔格尔另立王庭，还去满者伯夷朝见，哈雅姆·乌鲁克赐给他有法力的传家宝。满者伯夷随后陷入混乱，就此消失。这套说法的年代对不上：哈雅姆·乌鲁克死于1389年，满者伯夷灭亡在16世纪初。

格尔格尔从16世纪初到1686年称雄巴厘。16世纪中叶前后，逃离爪哇乱局的婆罗门贤者尼拉尔塔受到达仑·巴图伦贡宫廷的接待。格尔格尔村里，王室祖庙是耶罗阿贡寺，旁边的达萨寺是布撒基母庙的低地对应庙。荷兰人1597年首次到达，与国王建立了友好关系。他们看到的是一座三十多万人口的稠密岛屿，岛上产的棉布由爪哇北岸的商人换取胡椒。1651年一位国王去世后，王廷爆发内斗。1686年，篡权的大臣安格鲁拉·阿贡战死，旧王室的后裔德瓦·阿贡·詹贝在克隆孔另立新王庭。

en:
Tradition says the Jokhang stands on a lake. King Songtsen Gampo tossed his hat (a ring in another version) ahead of him and promised to build a temple where it landed; it fell into a lake, where a white stupa rose. Goats carried earth to fill the lake, so the town was first called Rasa, 'Goats', and only later Lhasa. Around the middle of the seventh century the king built the temple to house the Jowo Mikyo Dorje, the statue of the Buddha at eight years old that his Nepalese queen Bhrikuti had brought. The statue in the main hall is the other Jowo, Shakyamuni at twelve: a gilded bronze 1.5 metres tall, with a jewelled crown and a diamond on its forehead. Tibetan legend says the Buddha himself had the divine craftsman make it. It came with the Tang princess Wencheng, and when the Tang were feared to be planning an invasion she is said to have hidden it in a secret chamber of the temple. Later it was set in the central chapel, and the Nepalese image went to the Ramoche temple. Pilgrims walk the Barkhor circuit, prostrate themselves, and press forward to touch the Jowo's knee.

Tsongkhapa founded the Great Prayer Festival here in 1409, and thousands of monks from Drepung, Sera and Ganden gathered at the Jokhang to chant; Gedun Gyatso, abbot of Drepung, revived it in 1518. In the seventeenth century the Fifth Dalai Lama enlarged the temple and had gilded copper plates nailed over its roofs; the golden roofs became its mark. After the Gorkha war of 1792 the Qianlong Emperor barred Nepalese from the temple, which became an exclusive place of worship for Tibetans. Outside stand two stone monuments. One is a 5.5-metre pillar inscribed in Tibetan and Chinese with the treaty that fixed the border between the Tibetan king Ralpacan and the Tang emperor Muzong. The other is a tablet of 1794 with advice on hygiene against smallpox; Tibetans chiselled pieces out of it, believing the stone itself could cure.
zh:
相传大昭寺建在一片湖上。松赞干布向前抛出帽子（另一说是戒指），说帽子落在何处就在何处建寺；帽子落进湖里，湖中忽然升起一座白塔。人们用山羊驮土把湖填平，所以这座城起初叫「惹萨」，意为羊，后来才叫拉萨。七世纪中叶，赞普建寺，供奉尼泊尔尺尊公主带来的觉卧米居多杰，也就是释迦牟尼八岁时的塑像。主殿里供的却是另一尊觉卧：十二岁的释迦牟尼，鎏金铜像，高1.5米，头戴宝冠，额前镶着钻石。藏地传说，释迦牟尼本人请天匠造了这尊像。它随唐朝文成公主入藏；据说唐朝要出兵的风声传来时，公主把它藏进寺里的一间暗室。后来它被安置在中央殿，尼泊尔的那尊像则移往小昭寺。香客沿八廓街绕寺转经，全身伏地叩拜，挤上前去摸一摸觉卧的佛膝。

1409年，宗喀巴在这里创办默朗钦波祈愿大法会，哲蚌、色拉、甘丹三寺的数千名僧人聚在大昭寺诵经、举行法事；1518年，哲蚌寺堪布根敦嘉措使大法会得以复兴。17世纪，第五世达赖喇嘛扩建大昭寺，把鎏金铜板钉在木石结构的屋顶上，金顶成了大昭寺的标志。1792年廓尔喀战争后，乾隆皇帝不许尼泊尔人入寺，这里成了藏人专有的礼拜之地。寺外立着两座石碑。一座是高5.5米的石柱，用藏汉两种文字刻着藏王热巴巾和唐穆宗之间划定边界的盟约。另一座是1794年的石碑，刻着预防天花的卫生劝告；藏人把碑石凿下碎片，相信石头本身能治病。

en:
Around 256 BC Li Bing, Qin governor of Shu, built the Dujiangyan with his son at the foot of Mount Yulei, where the Min River spills onto the Chengdu Plain. Local legend gives the son, Erlang, the part of the hero: at the River God Temple he ambushed the dragon that took a human sacrifice every year, and chained it under the Lidui bluff. Li Bing put no dam across the river. He built a levee to split it. Its pointed Fish Mouth divides the water into an inner and an outer stream, sending roughly six tenths into the irrigation canals in the dry season and four in flood. Below it the Flying Sand Weir throws floodwater and silt back into the outer stream, and the twenty-metre Bottle-Neck Channel carries the controlled flow through the mountain cut. The levee was piled from long bamboo baskets of river stones held by wooden tripods. With no gunpowder yet, the channel was cut by heating the rock and cooling it until it split, eight years' work.

The works only keep working by being rebuilt. Every winter crews dredge the shoals and replace the baskets, following the six words carved at the Two Kings Temple: dredge the shoals deep, keep the weirs low. In 228 Zhuge Liang posted twelve hundred soldiers to the weirs and set a full-time weir officer over them. Late in the Yuan dynasty the official Jidangpu rebuilt the headworks in mortared stone clamped with iron, the first time iron and stone replaced bamboo, and cast a sixteen-thousand-jin iron turtle for the Fish Mouth. In 1550 the water commissioner Shi Qianxiang poured molten iron into his stonework and cast an iron-ox fish mouth of seventy thousand jin. When the rebel Zhang Xianzhong took Chengdu in 1644, the turmoil of the Ming-Qing transition emptied the plain of people, and the works decayed until rice cultivation was set back for decades. In 1803 a local man, He Xiande, and his wife raised a plank-and-bamboo suspension bridge across both streams, and villagers called it the Couple's Bridge.
zh:
约公元前256年，秦国蜀郡守李冰和他儿子在玉垒山下、岷江出山口处修起都江堰，治住岷江年年泛滥。当地传说里立功的是李冰之子二郎：他在河神庙设伏，擒住每年索要人祭的孽龙，把它锁在离堆下的深潭里。李冰没有横江筑坝，而是修了一道分水堤。堤头形如鱼嘴，把岷江分成内外两江，枯水时约六成水入内江灌溉，洪水时只放四成。下游的飞沙堰把多余的洪水和泥沙翻回外江，宽二十米的宝瓶口把受控的江水穿过山体送向成都平原。筑堤用的是塞满卵石的长竹笼，以木桩三角架固定；凿山时没有火药，工匠堆柴烧红岩石、再用水激冷使之崩裂，前后用了八年。

这套工程全靠年年重修。每年冬天枯水期，民夫淘挖河底淤沙、更换竹笼，依的是二王庙石壁上刻的六字诀：深淘滩，低作堰。228年，诸葛亮派出一千二百名兵丁护堰，并设了专职堰官。元代后期，四川肃政廉访使吉当普首次以铁锚加固的浆砌条石取代竹笼重修堰首，又铸了一头一万六千斤重的铁龟代替鱼嘴。1550年，水利佥事施千祥以浆砌条石灌注铁水固堤，用七万斤生铁铸铁牛鱼嘴。1644年张献忠攻占成都，明清易代的动乱使平原人口流散、堰务荒废，水稻种植倒退了几十年。1803年，本地何氏夫妇倡议重修索桥，以木板为面、竹索为栏，横跨内外两江，民间称作夫妻桥。

en:
The Grand Canal runs about 1,800 kilometres, the longest artificial waterway in the world, and its southern end is at Hangzhou, where it meets the Qiantang River. Emperor Yang of the Sui joined older channels into one system, and the histories say more than three million people were called up to dig its sections. He was said to have sailed down it with a flotilla of boats 105 kilometres long. In 610 he ordered the Jiangnan Canal cut from Jingkou to Yuhang, now Hangzhou, 'more than eight hundred li long and over ten zhang wide' in the words of the Zizhi Tongjian, wide enough for dragon boats, with posting palaces set up along it for a planned tour east to Kuaiji. Rebels killed him at Jiangdu in 618. The Yuan cut a new summit section across the Shandong hills and cut hundreds of kilometres from the route. After 1411 the Ming renovated almost the whole canal, with 165,000 labourers in Shandong alone.

Hangzhou's customs station stood on Beixin Bridge, where the canal meets the Xitang and Yuhangtang rivers, and by 1429 at the latest it was taxing canal boats. It was one of seven great canal customs houses, called chaoguan because duty was paid in paper notes. In 1496 the official Liu Jingyin built a stone bank and a platform reaching three zhang out over the water, with steps on both sides, because boats could hardly land to declare their cargo at the fallen bank. In 1561 the governor-general Hu Zongxian heaped more than a thousand pirate heads into a mound outside the customs house and set up a stele naming it Fengjing Guan. A little north, the Gongchen Bridge was built in 1631 with three stone arches; its name means to salute the emperor, and it is counted as the canal's end. The customs wharf was the imperial landing for the southern tours of the Kangxi and Qianlong emperors. Qianlong made six, beginning in 1751, and each usually took in Yangzhou, Suzhou, Hangzhou and Jiangning.
zh:
大运河杭州段是大运河的南端，运河全长约1800公里，是世界上最长的人工水道，在杭州与钱塘江相接。隋炀帝把各段旧河连成一个整体，史书说，为开凿各段运河征发了三百多万人。相传他曾率一支长达105公里的船队沿运河南下。610年，他又下令疏凿江南河，《资治通鉴》记这段工程「自京口至余杭，八百余里，广十余丈」，宽得能走龙舟，沿途修起驿宫，准备东巡会稽。618年，他在江都被叛军所杀。元代在山东丘陵间新凿一段河道，把航程缩短了数百公里；1411年以后，明朝几乎把整条运河重修一遍，仅山东一段就用了十六万五千名民夫。

杭州的钞关设在北新桥上，运河在这里与西塘河、余杭塘河汇合，至迟到1429年已经向运河上的船只收税。它是运河七大钞关之一，称「钞关」，是因为过关税费只收纸钞。1496年，南京户部主事刘景寅在关前筑起石岸，又修了一座伸入运河三丈的高台，两侧有台阶，因为原先岸石倾倒，船只上岸报关很不方便。1561年，浙直总督胡宗宪在关外把千余颗倭寇首级堆成京观，立碑题名「封鲸观」。再往北，拱宸桥在1631年建成，三孔石拱，桥名取迎敬帝王之意，被视为大运河的终点。北新关的码头是康熙、乾隆南巡的御码头。乾隆帝从1751年起六次南巡，每次一般都要到扬州、苏州、杭州和江宁。

en:
Tradition says Meng Jiangnu walked a thousand li to bring winter clothes to her husband, taken to build the wall, found that he had died there, and wept until a stretch of it fell down. The story is set under the Qin first emperor, who sent Meng Tian with 300,000 men against the steppe peoples and joined the older walls into one line. The Ming did not call theirs the Great Wall but 'border barriers', since the old name recalled the tyranny of Qin Shi Huang. In 1444 their defences were still patchy, with garrisons at the passes near Beijing and an earthen wall in Liaodong.

The Tumu disaster of 1449 put the Ming on the defensive, and raids into the Ordos grew. After years of court quarrels over attack or defence, a wall was the compromise: Yu Zijun proposed it over the objections of the Minister of War Bai Gui, who feared the cost. In 1474 forty thousand men raised more than two thousand li of wall with 800 strong points and posts in a few months, from Hengcheng on the Yellow River past Huamachi to Qingshuiying in Shaanxi. Ningxia's own Hedong wall, 387 li from Huangshazui to Huamachi, was built the same year under Xu Tingzhang and Fan Jin. In 1482 a large band of Mongol raiders was trapped between the double lines and beaten, and the border people took it as proof that the wall worked.

From 1567 Qi Jiguang took charge of the defences near Beijing, faced sections of the rammed-earth wall with brick, and built more than a thousand hollow watchtowers between Shanhai and Changping. Europeans heard of the wall from the sixteenth century, but the Jesuit Bento de Gois, travelling overland from India, only passed through it at the Jiayu Pass at the end of 1605. In May 1644 Wu Sangui, the Ming general holding the Shanhai Pass, opened its gates to the Manchu army while the rebel Shun army approached from the south. Under the Qing, whose empire included Mongolia, work on the wall as a defence stopped.
zh:
万里长城的传说里，孟姜女千里为被征去修长城的丈夫送寒衣，到了才知道丈夫已死在那里，她放声痛哭，哭倒了一段城墙。这个故事被安在秦朝，秦始皇派蒙恬率三十万人北击草原部族，并把旧墙连成一线。明朝人不叫它长城，而叫「边墙」，因为长城这个名字让人想起秦始皇的暴政。1444年，明朝的防线还零零散散，北京附近各关口驻有军队，辽东筑有一道土墙。

1449年土木之变使明朝转入守势，蒙古人对河套的袭扰日益频繁。朝廷为该攻还是该守争论多年，筑墙是折中的办法。余子俊力主筑墙，兵部尚书白圭则担心耗费太大而反对。1474年，四万人几个月内筑成两千多里边墙和八百处据点墩台，自黄河边的横城经花马池延伸到陕西清水营。宁夏本省自黄沙咀到花马池长三百八十七里的河东墙，同年由徐廷璋、范瑾督造。1482年，一大股蒙古入寇骑兵被夹在两道边墙之间击败，边民这才认定筑墙有用。

1567年起，戚继光主持北京一带的防务，把部分夯土墙外包青砖，并在山海关至昌平之间修起上千座空心敌台。欧洲人从16世纪起就听说过长城，但直到1605年底，从印度陆路东来的耶稣会士鄂本笃才在嘉峪关穿过它。1644年5月，镇守山海关的明将吴三桂向满洲大军打开关门，当时李自成的大顺军正从南面逼近。清朝的疆域包括了蒙古，长城作为边防的修筑也就停了。

en:
The banquet hall of Gyeongbokgung was said to have stood three storeys high on forty-eight stone pillars, each carved with a climbing dragon; a Ryukyuan envoy, the Yongjae chonghwa records, counted these pillars among the three finest sights in Joseon. The hall belonged to the first and principal palace of the dynasty, built after King Taejo moved his capital to Hanyang in 1394. Taejo asked the scholar-official Jeong Do-jeon to name the palace and its main halls, and Jeong took gyeongbok, 'great blessing', from the Book of Songs, from the line wishing that the lord may enjoy great blessing for ten thousand years. The throne hall Geunjeongjeon was finished in 1395, and five kings were crowned there, Sejong among them. Sejong made Gyeongbokgung his main palace in 1421, and in his reign it held the Hall of Worthies, a water clock, an astronomical observatory and a facility for casting movable type.

The banquet hall, Gyeonghoeru, stood on an island in a square pond, and in 1412 it was rebuilt on a much larger scale; envoys and officials feasted there. In 1506 a hill called Mansesan was heaped up on the west side of the pond, and it is said to have been planted with flowers from across the country and set with miniature palaces, while the king crossed the water in a boat called the Yellow Dragon and lanterns floated on the pond at night. A fire in 1553 destroyed the quarters around the king's bedchamber but spared the throne hall and the banquet hall, and rebuilding began in the spring of 1554 with 3,700 workers, conscripted labourers and hired men together, and finished by September. In 1592, during the Imjin War, the palace was completely burned down. Korean texts report a rumour that commoners set the fire to destroy the palace records, but the palace was still standing when the Japanese entered the city. Of Gyeonghoeru only the stone pillars survived, and the palace was not rebuilt.
zh:
据说景福宫的宴厅庆会楼曾是三层楼阁，立在四十八根石柱上，每根都雕着一条攀升的龙；据记载，一位琉球使者把这些石柱列为朝鲜三大壮观之一。宴厅所属的景福宫是朝鲜王朝第一座正宫，1394年太祖迁都汉阳后兴建。太祖命文臣郑道传为宫殿和各主要殿阁命名，郑道传从《诗经》取「景福」二字，出自祝愿君子万年、享大福的诗句。正殿勤政殿1395年落成，先后有五位国王在此即位，世宗便是其中之一。世宗1421年起以景福宫为主要宫殿，他在位期间，宫中设有集贤殿、水钟、天文观测台和铸造活字的设施。

庆会楼立在方形池塘中的岛上，1412年大规模重建，官员和使节在这里赴宴。1506年，池西堆起万岁山，据说山上种满各地名花，布置了小型仙宫模型，国王乘一条叫「黄龙舟」的船往来，夜里池面漂着灯笼。1553年一场大火烧毁了国王寝殿一带，勤政殿和庆会楼幸存；1554年春开始重建，征役民夫和雇工合计三千七百人，到9月落成。1592年壬辰倭乱期间，景福宫被烧成白地。朝鲜的文献记有传闻，说是平民为销毁宫中记录而放火，但日军进城时宫殿仍然完好。庆会楼只剩下石柱，宫殿此后没有重建。

en:
Two stories about a woman named Iparhan are told in Kashgar. In the Kashgarian telling she was a daughter or consort of Khoja Jahan, taken to Beijing by the Qianlong Emperor, where she kept daggers in her sleeves against his advances until she was poisoned. Qing tellings made her Afaq Khoja's granddaughter with a natural scent, the Fragrant Concubine, whose body was carried home by 120 bearers on a journey of more than three years. The historical Consort Rong entered the harem in 1760 and was buried at the Eastern Qing Tombs after her death in 1788. A casket in the tomb hall is said to have carried Iparhan back.

The Afaq Khoja Mausoleum stands five kilometres northeast of Kashgar, at Ayziret, and is the holiest Muslim site in Xinjiang. It was built about 1640 as the tomb of Muhammad Yusuf, a Naqshbandi master from Andijan who had come to the region early in the century; his son Afaq Khoja buried him there. A tiled dome about sixteen metres across rises over the tomb chamber, with four corner minarets banded with arabesques, and the graves inside are glazed blue and draped in coloured silks. Around it lie four prayer halls on wooden beams, a lecture hall and a cemetery.

Afaq Khoja led the White Mountain Khojas. Expelled from Yarkand, he travelled to Tibet, where the fifth Dalai Lama wrote him a letter of introduction to the Dzungar leader Galdan, and about 1680 he came back with Galdan's army. He became the real ruler of Kashgar and Yarkand and paid the Dzungars 100,000 silver tangas a year. When he died in the mid-1690s he was laid beside his father, and the mazar is said to hold five generations of the family, 72 graves in all. His great-grandsons Burhan-ud-din and Khoja Jahan, freed by the Qing from Dzungar captivity at Ili, killed a Qing officer and revolted; the Qing crushed them in 1759. Even so, in 1760 the Qianlong Emperor ordered the old khoja tombs at Kashgar guarded and repaired at official expense.
zh:
喀什流传着关于伊帕尔罕的两种说法。喀什噶尔的说法里，她是霍集占的女儿或妃子，被乾隆帝带到北京，袖里藏着匕首抵拒他，最后被毒死。清代的传说则把她写成阿帕克和卓的孙女、天生异香的香妃，遗体由一百二十人抬回，路上走了三年多。历史上的容妃1760年入宫，1788年去世，葬在清东陵。墓室里有一口棺，据说就是把伊帕尔罕运回来的那口。

阿帕克和卓麻札（阿巴和加麻札）在喀什噶尔东北五公里的艾孜热特村，是新疆最受尊崇的穆斯林圣迹。此墓约在1640年始建，最初是玛木特·玉素布的墓；他是来自安集延的纳合昔班底教长，17世纪初来到回疆，由儿子伊达雅图勒拉，即阿帕克和卓，安葬在这里。墓室上盖着直径约16米的琉璃瓦穹顶，四角立着缠有阿拉伯式花纹色带的宣礼塔，室内墓座覆着蓝釉、披着彩色丝绸。周围另有四座木梁礼拜殿、一座讲经堂和一片公墓。

阿帕克和卓是白山派的首领。他被逐出叶尔羌后一路去了西藏，五世达赖喇嘛给他写了一封致准噶尔首领噶尔丹的引荐信，约1680年他随噶尔丹的军队返回，成为喀什噶尔和叶尔羌的实际统治者，每年向准噶尔缴纳十万腾格白银。他死于17世纪90年代中叶，葬在父亲身旁，据说麻札先后葬了家族五代七十二人。他的曾孙波罗尼都、霍集占兄弟，由清军从伊犁的准噶尔囚禁中救出，却杀了清朝将领起兵，1759年被清军平定。尽管如此，乾隆帝在1760年颁旨，命人看守喀什噶尔旧和卓的坟墓，修葺也由官府出资。

en:
Salvador was founded in 1549 by Tomé de Sousa, Brazil's first governor-general, as a fortress on a cliff above the Bay of All Saints. The Jesuits came with him under Manuel da Nóbrega. The chronicler Simão de Vasconcelos wrote that when Tomé de Sousa objected that the college site lay outside the city, Nóbrega answered that the city would come to gather around the house. The college for boys and its chapel were built of mud, which soon decayed, and Governor Mem de Sá had a masonry church raised. In 1585 Fernão Cardim found it hung with damask and velvet, with a silver cross and three heads of the Eleven Thousand Virgins among its relics. The present cathedral is the fourth church on the Terreiro de Jesus ground and was consecrated in 1672. Its facade and interior are clad in lioz stone shipped from Portugal, and the high altar, carved by the lay brother João Correia, is one of the few Mannerist altars in Brazil.

A West India Company fleet captured and sacked the city in 1624, and a Luso-Spanish fleet retook it a year later. Pillories stood in open places such as the Terreiro de Jesus, symbols of authority and justice, and of lashings; the one later moved to the Praça da Piedade gave its name to the Pelourinho district. The Franciscans, whose house had outgrown its buildings, laid the foundation stone of a new convent in 1686. Their church was finished in 1720 and its twin towers only in the 1790s, and every surface inside is carved and gilded. Italian Capuchins who visited in the eighteenth century were indignant at such show.

On Easter Sunday 1745 the captain Theodózio Rodrigues de Faria landed the image of Nosso Senhor do Bonfim, a replica of the one at Setúbal, his hometown, which he had vowed to bring to Brazil during a storm. It waited in the Penha church until the Bonfim church was finished inside and was then carried over in procession. In 1809 the church's treasurer began the custom of the fitinhas, ribbons cut to the length of the image's right arm to its chest, to raise money for the devotion.
zh:
巴伊亚的萨尔瓦多城由巴西首任总督托梅·德·索萨在1549年建成，当时是万圣湾上方高崖上的一座要塞。耶稣会士在曼努埃尔·达·诺布雷加带领下随他同来。编年史家西芒·德·瓦斯孔塞洛斯写道，托梅·德·索萨反对学院选址在城外，诺布雷加回答说，城会聚拢到这座房子周围来。耶稣会的男童学院及其礼拜堂都是泥墙，不久就破败了，总督曼·德·萨后来建起一座砖石教堂。1585年，费尔南·卡尔丁见到堂内挂着锦缎和天鹅绒，有银十字架，圣骨中有一万一千贞女中的三颗头颅。这座主教座堂是耶稣广场这块地上的第四座教堂，1672年祝圣；立面和内部用从葡萄牙船运来的莱奥兹石包砌，主祭坛由世俗修士若昂·科雷亚雕成，是巴西少有的风格主义祭坛之一。

1624年，西印度公司舰队攻陷并洗劫了这座城，一年后，西班牙与葡萄牙联合舰队把它夺回。耶稣广场等露天场所立着刑柱佩洛里尼奥，象征权威和司法，也是施鞭刑的地方；后来迁到皮耶达德广场的那一根，成了佩洛里尼奥街区名称的由来。方济各会的修道院已容不下修士，1686年为新修道院奠基；教堂1720年完工，双塔直到18世纪90年代才建成，内部每一处表面都是雕刻和金饰。18世纪到访的意大利嘉布遣会士对这种排场十分愤慨。

1745年复活节，船长特奥多济奥·罗德里格斯·德·法里亚把邦芬耶稣像运到萨尔瓦多。他在风暴中曾许愿要把这尊像带到巴西，圣像是他家乡塞图巴尔那尊的复制品。圣像先安放在佩尼亚教堂，等邦芬教堂内部完工，才举行游行迁入。1809年，教堂司库开创了许愿丝带的习俗：丝带按圣像右臂到胸口的长度剪裁，为这项供奉筹款。

en:
The Cerro Rico de Potosi is a bare red cone of almost 4,800 metres above the Villa Imperial, and the friar Diego de Ocana, describing it in 1606, called it the eighth wonder of the world. He measured the mountain's base with a cord, 11,033 varas around, and counted 8,000 Indians working its galleries by tallow candle. In the first years after 1545 the hill yielded native silver rich enough to need only smelting, done in guayras, the small clay wind furnaces the Incas had used; some six thousand of them stood on pedestals across the slopes to catch the wind, burning wood, charcoal and llama dung. By 1565 the high-grade ore was gone. Mercury amalgamation let the miners work poorer rock, the mercury coming from Huancavelica, and in 1609 a better pan process was invented at Potosi itself. The workings reached 1,150 metres down from the summit, the mountaintop was removed in the course of mining, and the hill took its present shape in the seventeenth century.

The Crown took a fifth of the silver as the quinto, and the mountain drew every kind of man. From 1622 to 1625 the Basques fought an open war with the Vicunas, a mix of Andeans and non-Basque Spanish and Portuguese colonists, for control of the ore and its management; the Crown intervened, and the two sides settled with a wedding between the children of their leaders. A few years before, in 1617-19, Catalina de Erauso, the nun who escaped her convent and dressed as a man, had lived in the city as a llama driver and soldier. The miners called the hill the mountain that eats men. The Inca Garcilaso, writing in 1609, tells that when Huayna Capac sent his vassals to work it, a roar and a voice told them the silver was kept for others who would come after; Arzans later derived the name Potosi from that thunder. Historians see in the story a Spanish invention to justify the mining.
zh:
波托西富饶山是波托西皇家城上方一座近4800米高的红色秃峰，修士迭戈·德·奥卡尼亚在1606年描述它时，称之为「世界第八奇迹」。他用绳索量过山脚，一周长11033巴拉，并记下有8000名印第安人就着牛油烛火在坑道里劳作。1545年后的头几年，山里的天然银高品位到只需熔炼；炼银用的是印加人旧有的瓦伊拉风炉，那是花盆般大小的黏土炉，约有六千座立在墩座上、布满山坡，借着山风燃烧木材、木炭和骆马粪。到1565年，高品位矿已经采尽。水银混汞法让低品位矿石也能取银，水银来自万卡韦利卡；1609年，波托西本地又发明了更合用的槽碾混汞法。矿洞从山顶向下深达1150米，开采中山顶被整个削去，这座山在17世纪定型为最终的模样。

王室把银产的五分之一作为五一税收走，银山也引来了各色人等。1622至1625年，巴斯克人同「小羊驼」派为争夺矿石和矿务管理权在城里公开交战，后者由本地人和非巴斯克的西班牙人、葡萄牙殖民者混成；王室出面干预，双方以两派首领的子女联姻和解。几年前的1617至1619年，逃出修道院、女扮男装的修女卡塔利娜·德·埃劳索曾在这座城里当过赶骆马的人和士兵。矿工把这座山叫作「吃人的山」。印加·加西拉索在1609年记下一则传说：瓦伊纳·卡帕克派人来开山，忽有一声巨响和一个声音说，这里的银子留给以后到来的人；后来阿尔桑斯据此把「波托西」解释为雷鸣。史家认为这是西班牙人为开矿正名而编的说法。

en:
Spanish officials knew of Machu Picchu, though they seem to have gone there rarely. Colonial papers list a village called Picchu, usually taken to be this place, as a tribute-payer of the Ollantaytambo encomienda, and its tribute was carried down to Ollantaytambo once a year instead of being collected on the spot. A curaca named Juan Mácora, perhaps the last, is recorded in 1568. Spaniards of the late sixteenth century also noted that local people spoke of returning to 'Huayna Picchu', which may have been the Inca name of the site. It sits 80 kilometres north-west of Cuzco at 2,430 metres, on a granite saddle between two peaks, with the Urubamba curling around it on three sides below cliffs that drop 450 metres.

Pachacuti is thought to have ordered the royal estate built after he conquered the middle and lower Urubamba valley. Building was once dated to about 1450, but radiocarbon dates from burials show people living here from about 1420. Roughly two hundred buildings stand on parallel terraces around a central square, among them the Temple of the Three Windows with its white granite wall and the Intihuatana, 'the place where the sun is tied', which may have been aligned with the sacred peaks around it. The granite was quarried on site and fitted without mortar, which two fault lines running through the ridge would have made nearly useless; doors and windows are trapezoidal and corners are rounded.

About 750 people lived here, most of them yanacona retainers whose ancestry ran from the Andes to the coast and the Amazon; in the harsh season the staff fell to a few hundred. Llamas and alpacas were brought up from the high puna, some 4,000 metres above the sea, for meat and wool, guinea pigs were buried in tomb caves, and six dogs were laid among the human dead, thought to be companions of the dead. The estate was not passed down to the next Sapa Inca. It was used for about eighty years and then abandoned, seemingly because of the Spanish conquests elsewhere in the empire, and smallpox carried ahead of the conquistadors may have killed most of its people. The latest radiocarbon dates stop around 1530.
zh:
西班牙官员知道马丘比丘，却似乎很少上去。殖民时期的文书里有个叫皮丘（Picchu）的村子，通常认为就是这里，它是奥扬泰坦博监护地的纳贡村，贡赋每年送到奥扬泰坦博交纳，不在当地征收。1568年的文书记下了一位叫胡安·马科拉的酋长，或许是最后一任。16世纪末的西班牙人还记下，当地人说要回「瓦伊纳比丘」，这可能就是此地的印加旧名。马丘比丘在库斯科西北80公里、海拔2430米处，坐落在两座山峰之间的花岗岩鞍部，乌鲁班巴河从三面环绕，崖壁直落450米才到河面。

帕查库特在征服乌鲁班巴河中下游谷地之后，据认为下令修建这座王家别业。动工时间过去定在1450年前后，但墓葬的碳十四测年显示，1420年前后这里已有人居住。约200座建筑沿平行台地、围着中央广场排开，其中有白花岗岩砌墙的三窗庙，以及因蒂瓦塔纳石，克丘亚语意为「拴住太阳之处」，它可能与四周的圣山对齐。花岗岩就地开采，干砌咬合、不用灰浆；山脊上有两条断层穿过，灰浆几乎派不上用场。门窗呈梯形，墙角磨圆。

这里住着约750人，多数是亚纳科纳侍从，血统上有安第斯高地、沿海和亚马孙的来源；严酷的冬季只留几百人看守。美洲驼和羊驼从4000米左右的高原草地赶上山来，供肉食和取毛；豚鼠葬在墓洞里，还有六条狗葬在人骨之间，被认为是死者的伴侣。这座别业不传给继位的萨帕·印卡，使用了约80年便遭废弃，似乎与西班牙在帝国别处的征服有关；先于征服者传来的天花，也可能夺走了多数居民的性命。最晚的碳十四年代止于1530年前后。

en:
The Chimu held that the Sun made three eggs, gold for the ruler and the elite, silver for the rulers' spouses and copper for everyone else, and panels of gold are said to have covered the city's walls. At the centre of Chan Chan the Chimu raised ten rectangular ciudadelas, one walled royal compound for each king. Each had a single entrance on its north side. At Nik An the adobe walls reach twelve metres, five metres thick at the foot and one at the crown, a taper made in anticipation of earthquakes on this coast. Inside, the compounds share one layout: a northern plaza with low benches along its edge, U-shaped audiencias that probably housed officials, a central block of storehouses and a southern living quarter with its own well. Among the storehouses stood a low truncated pyramid, the burial platform of the compound's lord, and most of these platforms were looted in the first years of the Spanish conquest. In Nik An, formerly called Tschudi, moulded reliefs cover the walls: waves, nets, pelicans, and fish pointed north and south, which can be read as the cold Humboldt current and the warm El Nino current. A pond at its centre was probably used for ceremonies.

After the Inca conquest around 1470 the compounds lost their court and their kings, and the Spanish town of Trujillo soon rose beside them. Throughout the Viceroyalty the compounds were looted again and again, because people believed a great treasure of gold and silver lay hidden between their walls and pyramids. A list of goods taken from one burial tomb at Chan Chan in the sixteenth century came to the equivalent of 80,000 pesos of gold. The adobe was made for an almost rainless coast, and the heavy rains of El Nino years soak the base of the walls and damage them. The name of the deserted city first entered Spanish paper in the Trujillo town council's act of 1536, written as Cauchan.
zh:
奇穆人相信太阳生下三颗蛋：金蛋归统治者和贵族，银蛋归统治者的配偶，铜蛋归其余的人；据说城中的墙壁还覆有金板。昌昌城塞的中心，奇穆人建起十座长方形城寨，每一位国王拥有一座带围墙的王宫。每座城寨只在北面开一个出入口。尼基·安城寨的土坯墙高达12米，墙基厚5米，墙顶仅1米，这样收分是为了防备这条海岸上的地震。各城寨的格局相同：北面是边缘砌有矮台座的广场，接着是可能供官员办公的U形听政所，中部是成排的库房，南部是带水井的居住区；库房之间立着一座低矮的截顶金字塔，即城寨主人的陵台，大多数陵台在西班牙人征服最初的几年里就被盗掘一空。尼基·安城寨旧称楚迪，墙面覆满模压浮雕：海浪、渔网、鹈鹕，还有分别朝南朝北游的鱼，可以解读为寒冷的洪堡洋流与温暖的厄尔尼诺洋流。城寨中央的水塘可能用于仪式。

约1470年印加征服后，城寨失去了宫廷和国王，西班牙人的特鲁希略很快在它们旁边建起。整个总督区时期，昌昌一再遭到洗劫，因为人们相信墙垣和金字塔之间藏着大批金银。16世纪的一份清单记下了从昌昌一座墓中掠走的财物，价值相当于八万比索黄金。土坯墙本是为几乎无雨的海岸而造，厄尔尼诺年的大雨会浸坏墙基。这座废城的名字第一次落进西班牙文书，是1536年特鲁希略市政会的文件，写作「考昌」。

en:
The Qhapaq Nan, the royal road of the Incas, ran more than 30,000 kilometres without the use of a wheel; estimates go up to 40,000. Roads left Cuzco for the four quarters of the Tawantinsuyu, and two main routes ran north to south. The coastal road hugged the foothills where the plain turned to desert. The high road, the one the Incas called the Qhapaq Nan, held the puna grasslands above 4,000 metres from Quito through Tumebamba, Huanuco and Cuzco to the Mendoza River, more than 5,000 kilometres. Much of it was older than the Incas, taken over from Wari and Tiwanaku routes. The empire's expansion began around 1438, and each conquest was tied to Cuzco by road; Tupac Yupanqui, the successor of Pachacuti, reached the Quito region around 1463.

On steep slopes the road was cut into stone steps. Rivers were crossed on log and slab bridges, on rows of tied totora reeds, in oroya baskets over gaps wider than 50 metres, and on suspension bridges of ichu-grass rope. The Apurimac bridge spanned 45 metres; every two years mita labour built a new one and the old bridge was cut into the river. Chasqui runners waited at relay stations to carry messages on, and word from Quito could reach Cuzco, 2,000 kilometres away, in under ten days. Tambos a day's walk apart sheltered travellers, and qullqa warehouses held goods for redistribution, 497 of them at Huanuco Pampa alone.

Pedro Cieza de Leon wrote in 1553 that the road ran 'everywhere clean, swept, clear of debris', but by then the Spanish conquerors had used it. Diego de Almagro's expedition to Chile went south largely along the road from Cuzco to Paria and Tupiza. Disease and war cut the native population from more than 12 million to about 1.1 million in fifty years, and the labour that kept the road up was gone. Horses and mules replaced llamas, and the Spaniards kept only the routes that served their mines and ports; Cieza saw the road already broken in many places, yet it 'shows the great thing that it was'.
zh:
印加路网（Qhapaq Nan，克丘亚语意为「王家大道」）全长三万多公里，据估计最长可达四万公里，路上没有用过轮子。道路从库斯科通向塔万廷苏尤的四方，南北向有两条主干道。沿海大道在平原变为沙漠的地方贴着山麓前行。高原大道才是印加人所说的「王家大道」，行在海拔4000米以上的普纳草原上，从基多经图梅班巴、瓦努科和库斯科，通到门多萨河，全长五千多公里。道路大半比印加更古老，是接收了瓦里和蒂亚瓦纳科的旧路。帝国的扩张约从1438年开始，每征服一地，就修路与库斯科相连；帕查库提的继任者图帕克·尤潘基约在1463年到达基多一带。

陡坡上的路面凿成石阶。过河有木桥、石板桥，有把托托拉芦苇捆扎成排的浮桥，有用吊篮跨越50多米宽峡谷的奥罗亚，还有伊楚草绳编成的悬索桥。阿普里马克河上的索桥跨度45米，每隔两年由米塔役工重建一座，旧桥被斩断，落入河中。查斯基信使在驿站等候，把消息接力传下去，基多的消息不到十天就能送到2000公里外的库斯科。相隔一天脚程的坦博驿馆供旅人住宿，科尔卡仓库存放待分配的物资，仅瓦努科潘帕就有497座。

佩德罗·谢萨·德·莱昂在1553年写道，这条路「处处整洁，清扫干净，没有杂物」，可那时西班牙征服者已经走过它。迭戈·德·阿尔马格罗远征智利，大体就是顺着库斯科到帕里亚、图皮萨的这段大道南下。疾病和战争在五十年里把原住民人口从一千二百多万减到约一百一十万，养护道路的劳力也没有了。马和骡取代骆马驮运，西班牙人只保留通向矿山和港口的路线；谢萨看到许多地方的路面已经崩坏，却仍「显出它当年的宏伟」。

en:
For its first decades Cartagena had no walls, and raiders knew it. The French sacked the open town in 1544; John Hawkins bombarded it for eight days in 1568 and Martin Cote ransacked it the next year. After Francis Drake burned the city in 1586, Philip II put the engineer Bautista Antonelli in charge of the Caribbean defences, and the walled Cartagena he planned took two centuries to finish. Bastions and curtain walls girdled the old city, and Governor Francisco de Murga later enclosed Getsemaní too, its one gate and causeway covered by the Media Luna, the Half Moon battery. Inside the bay, forts commanded each shipping passage, and between Manzanillo and Castillo Grande a floating chain could close the water.

The landward core of the system was the Castillo San Felipe de Barajas on San Lázaro hill, a triangle of eight batteries built by enslaved Africans under Spanish supervision, begun in 1639 and extended until 1657. The seaward gate was the Bocachica narrows: in 1640 three Portuguese ships ran aground in the old Bocagrande passage and the wrecks helped build up a sandbar, and the defence of the bay shifted to Bocachica, where San José and San Luis stood on either side. The sea works had their failures. Pointis overran San Luis in 1697 when it held only thirty men, breached the Half Moon Gate and sacked the city for a month. In 1741 Edward Vernon took San Luis with a vastly larger force, but his assault on San Felipe failed. Blas de Lezo, who shared command of the defence with Sebastián de Eslava, had lost an eye, the use of an arm and a leg in earlier wars, and refused to wear an eyepatch. Afterwards the engineer Antonio de Arévalo completed San Fernando and San José at Bocachica and, from 1771 to 1778, laid a 3,400-yard underwater jetty, the Escollera, across Bocagrande. San Felipe's tunnels ran beneath the hill, and chambers in its main gallery could be blown up against attackers overhead.
zh:
建城后的头几十年，卡塔赫纳一道城墙也没有，袭掠者对此一清二楚。1544年法国人洗劫了不设防的城镇；约翰·霍金斯1568年连续炮击八天，次年马丁·科特又来劫掠。1586年弗朗西斯·德雷克纵火焚城，腓力二世才把加勒比诸港的防务交给军事工程师巴蒂斯塔·安东内利，他设计的环城城防此后施工了两百年。老城用棱堡和幕墙一圈圈围起，总督弗朗西斯科·德·穆尔加后来又把赫塞马尼区圈进墙内，该区唯一的城门与堤道由半月炮台封锁。内湾里，要塞逐一把各条通航水道置于炮火之下，曼萨尼约与卡斯蒂约格兰德两处堡垒之间，还能拉起一道横过水面的漂浮铁链。

卡塔赫纳要塞体系在陆地一侧的核心，是圣拉萨罗山上的圣费利佩·德·巴拉哈斯城堡：三角形堡体上布有八座炮台，由被奴役的非洲人在西班牙人监督下修筑，1639年动工，1657年前后仍在扩建。海上大门是博卡奇卡窄口：1640年，三艘葡萄牙船在旧的博卡格兰德航道搁浅，沉船促使沙洲加速淤积，海湾的防守转到博卡奇卡，圣何塞堡和圣路易斯堡分立两岸。这些海上工事并非无懈可击。1697年，普安蒂男爵趁圣路易斯堡只有三十名守军，一举将其攻破，又轰开半月门，洗劫城市一个月。1741年，爱德华·弗农以悬殊的兵力攻占了圣路易斯堡，进攻圣费利佩堡却失败了。与总督塞巴斯蒂安·德·埃斯拉瓦共同指挥守城的布拉斯·德·莱索，早年的战争中已丢了一只眼睛、一条腿，一只胳膊也不能动，却不肯戴眼罩遮掩。战后工程师安东尼奥·德·阿雷瓦洛在博卡奇卡建成圣费尔南多堡和圣何塞堡，又在1771至1778年间于博卡格兰德铺出一条3400码长的水下石堤，称作埃斯科列拉。圣费利佩堡的坑道穿行在山体之下，主廊道中的几间暗室可以引爆，对付头顶上的进攻者。

en:
The isthmus of Panama is the narrowest point between the Caribbean and the Pacific, and in the sixteenth century the Spanish crown wondered whether a ship could be sent through it. Vasco Nunez de Balboa crossed it in 1513 and was the first European to see the Pacific. A paved royal road, the Camino Real, was soon carrying goods from Panama City to Nombre de Dios, later to Portobelo. In 1524 Charles I suggested digging a canal, and a first project followed in 1529, but the politics of Europe and the technology of the day made it unworkable. In 1590 the Jesuit Jose de Acosta wrote that a cut would flood the land because one sea lies lower than the other, and it was also feared that other maritime powers would profit from the canal.

The one real attempt was Scotland's. The Company of Scotland raised 400,000 pounds in a few weeks, from every level of society, about a fifth of the wealth of Scotland. In July 1698 five ships sailed from Leith with some 1,200 people and founded New Edinburgh on the Gulf of Darien, calling the colony Caledonia. The promoter William Paterson meant it to hold an overland route between the two oceans. Yellow fever, malaria and hunger killed so many that the settlement was abandoned after eight months, and the relief ships that arrived in August 1699 found ruined huts and 400 overgrown graves. A second expedition rebuilt the huts, but Spanish forces besieged the fort and the Scots left for good in March 1700. The failure ruined the Scottish Lowlands financially and has been cited as one motive for the Act of Union of 1707.

In 1811 Alexander von Humboldt weighed five possible routes for a canal across Central America and judged the one through Nicaragua and its great lake the most promising. The canal at Panama was finally opened on 15 August 1914.
zh:
巴拿马地峡是加勒比海和太平洋之间最窄的地方，16世纪，西班牙王室就在想能不能让船从这里穿过去。1513年，巴斯科·努涅斯·德·巴尔沃亚越过地峡，成为第一个望见太平洋的欧洲人。不久，一条铺石的王家大道开始把货物从巴拿马城运往农布雷-德迪奥斯，后来改运往波托韦洛。1524年，卡洛斯一世提出开凿运河，1529年有了第一个方案，但欧洲的政局和当时的技术都让它行不通。1590年，耶稣会士何塞·德·阿科斯塔写道，凿通地峡会淹没陆地，因为两个海一高一低；人们还担心运河会让别的海上强国得利。

真正动过手的只有苏格兰。苏格兰公司几周之内从社会各阶层筹到40万英镑，约占苏格兰财富的五分之一。1698年7月，五艘船载着约一千二百人从利斯启航，在达连湾建起新爱丁堡，把殖民地叫作喀里多尼亚。发起人威廉·佩特森想让它控制两洋之间的陆路通道。黄热病、疟疾和饥饿夺走了太多人命，定居点八个月后就被放弃；1699年8月赶到的补给船只见到破败的棚屋和四百座荒草丛生的坟墓。第二批移民重建了棚屋，但西班牙军队围攻堡垒，苏格兰人在1700年3月彻底撤走。这次失败使苏格兰低地陷入财政困境，有人认为它是1707年《联合法案》的动因之一。

1811年，亚历山大·冯·洪堡比较了穿越中美洲的五条可能线路，认为经尼加拉瓜及其大湖的一条最有希望。巴拿马运河最终于1914年8月15日通航。

en:
Tikal, which its inscriptions name Yax Mutal, lies in the rainforest of the Peten Basin, on parallel limestone ridges above swampy lowland, and it had no water but rain. Ten reservoirs held it, and raised causeways ran between the plazas and temple groups. The mapped centre covers more than 16 square kilometres and holds about 3,000 structures; its long list of rulers is known from inscriptions and tombs.

The stones record the city's wars. On 14 January 378 the ruler Chak Tok Ich'aak was killed, on the same day a westerner called Siyah K'ak', probably a general serving Teotihuacan, arrived at Tikal. The next year a boy, Yax Nuun Ayiin, the son of a Teotihuacan lord known as Spearthrower Owl, was enthroned as king. After Calakmul and Caracol defeated Tikal in 562, no stela was raised for over a century and public sculpture was deliberately mutilated. Then Jasaw Chan K'awiil I captured an enemy noble of Calakmul in 695 and cast the rival into decline. He lies deep under Temple I, the Temple of the Great Jaguar, which rises in nine stepped levels, perhaps for the nine levels of the underworld, and carries a roof comb with the seated king. His tomb held jaguar skins, jade, spondylus shells and a jade necklace of 114 large beads weighing 3.9 kilograms. His son Yik'in Chan K'awiil raised Temple IV, one of the tallest pyramids of pre-Columbian America.

By the end of the ninth century most of the people had gone. Squatters lived in the palaces, put thatched houses on the ceremonial plazas, and by the tenth century the rainforest was taking the ruins. In 1525 Cortes crossed the Itza kingdom of the Peten on his march to Honduras, and in 1697 the Itza capital Nojpeten fell to a Spanish assault. The name Tikal, 'at the waterhole', was given to one of the old reservoirs by hunters and travellers much later.
zh:
蒂卡尔，铭文里写作亚什·穆塔尔，坐落在佩滕盆地的雨林中，建在数道平行的石灰岩高脊上，四周是沼泽低地，除了雨水再没有别的水源。十座水库蓄着雨水，抬高的堤道连接各广场和神庙群。已测绘的中心区超过16平方公里，分布着约三千座建筑；它长长的统治者名单，靠铭文和陵墓才为后人所知。

石头上记着这座城的战事。公元378年1月14日，国王查克·托克·伊查克被杀，同一天，一个叫西亚赫·卡克的外来者入城，他多半是为特奥蒂瓦坎效力的将领。第二年，一个男孩，特奥蒂瓦坎一位名叫掷矛枭的首领之子亚什·农·阿因，被立为国王。562年卡拉克穆尔联合卡拉科尔打败蒂卡尔，此后一个多世纪没有再立石碑，公共雕塑也被有意砸毁。695年，贾索·钱·卡维尔一世俘获卡拉克穆尔的一名贵族，把宿敌推入衰落。他安葬在一号神庙深处，也就是大美洲豹神庙：神庙分九层台阶，或许对应冥界的九层，顶冠雕着端坐的国王。墓里有美洲豹皮、玉石、海菊蛤贝，还有一条114颗大珠串成的玉项链，重3.9公斤。他的儿子伊金·钱·卡维尔建了四号神庙，是前哥伦布时代美洲最高的金字塔之一。

到9世纪末，大部分居民已经离开。占住者住进宫殿，在祭祀广场上搭起茅屋，到10世纪，雨林开始吞没遗迹。1525年科尔特斯进军洪都拉斯，横穿佩滕的伊察王国；1697年伊察都城诺赫佩滕被西班牙人攻陷。蒂卡尔这个名字，意思是「水塘边」，是后来的猎人和旅人给了其中一座古水库的。

en:
The name means 'at the mouth of the well of the Itza', and water made the city: northern Yucatan has no surface rivers, and four cenotes, the sink-wells of the limestone plain, could give Chichen water all year. The largest, the Sacred Cenote, is 60 metres across, and post-conquest Maya and Spanish sources describe offerings and human victims cast into it to the rain god Chaac. The Temple of Kukulkan, called El Castillo by the first Spaniards, rises about 30 metres in nine terraces with feathered-serpent heads at the foot of its balustrades; around the equinoxes, in the late afternoon, a shadow like a serpent wriggles down the north stair. Nearby is the Great Ball Court, 168 by 70 metres, the largest in ancient Mesoamerica, with a panel showing a decapitated player whose wound streams blood in the form of snakes.

The Itza, whose name the locals glossed as 'those who speak our language brokenly', arrived in the region around 800. In the tenth century Chichen grew into the regional capital of northern and central Yucatan, trading through its port of Isla Cerritos for central Mexican obsidian and Central American gold. Excavation shows the city had declined by 1100. The Book of Chilam Balam of Chumayel nonetheless tells of Hunac Ceel, ruler of Mayapan: when no one survived a ceremony in the Sacred Cenote, he leaped in himself, and when he was pulled out he prophesied his own rise to power. Colonial sources make him the conqueror of Chichen in the thirteenth century.

Francisco de Montejo the Younger was sent inland in late 1532 with the aim, from the start, of founding a capital at Chichen Itza, and he renamed it Ciudad Real. At first he met no resistance and divided the land among his soldiers, but the Maya grew hostile and besieged the Spanish among the ruins. An all-out assault cost him 150 men, and in 1534 he abandoned the place under cover of darkness. In 1536, while the Spanish were away, Nachi Cocom of Sotuta had Xiu ambassadors massacred at his estate of Otzmal, a feud with roots in 1441, when the Xiu killed the Cocom of Mayapan. By 1588 Chichen Itza was a working cattle ranch.
zh:
奇琴伊察的名字意为「伊察人的井口」，这座城因水而兴：尤卡坦北部没有地表河，四口天然井（石灰岩平原上塌陷形成的溶井）可以为奇琴提供全年不断的淡水。最大的圣井直径60米，征服后的马雅和西班牙资料都记载，人们把祭品甚至活人投进井中，献给雨神查克。库库尔坎金字塔被最早的西班牙人叫作「城堡」，高约30米，九层台基，栏杆底端雕着羽蛇头；春分、秋分前后的傍晚，北面台阶上会出现一条蛇形的影子蜿蜒而下。旁边的大球场长168米、宽70米，是古代中美洲最大的球场，墙上一幅浮雕刻着被斩首的球员，伤口喷出的血化成一条条蛇。

伊察人的名字，当地人解释为「说我们的话结结巴巴的人」，他们约在800年前后来到这一带。10世纪，奇琴成了尤卡坦北部和中部的区域首府，借北岸港口塞里托斯岛做贸易，换来中墨西哥的黑曜石和中美洲的黄金。发掘表明，它在1100年前已经衰落。不过《楚玛耶尔的奇兰·巴兰之书》仍讲述了马雅潘统治者胡纳克·塞尔的故事：一次圣井仪式中无人生还，他便自己跳了下去，被拉上来后预言自己将要掌权。殖民时期的资料把他写成13世纪征服奇琴的人。

小弗朗西斯科·德·蒙特霍1532年底受命深入内陆，目的从一开始就是在奇琴伊察建都，他把这里改名「王家城」。起初没有遇到抵抗，他把周围的土地分给士兵。马雅人渐渐敌对，把西班牙人围困在废墟之中；一次全力进攻折了150人，1534年他趁夜色撤走。1536年西班牙人离开期间，索图塔的纳奇·科科姆在自己的奥特斯马尔庄园杀害了休氏使节，两家的仇怨要追到1441年休氏屠杀马雅潘科科姆家族。到1588年，奇琴伊察已经是一座经营中的养牛牧场。

en:
At the centre of Tenochtitlan stood the Hueyi Teocalli, the Great Temple, which the Mexica understood to be the centre of the universe. Its platform measured about 100 by 80 metres and carried two shrines with separate staircases, one to the war god Huitzilopochtli and one to the rain god Tlaloc. Work on the first temple began after the city's founding in 1325, and it was rebuilt six times. It stood inside a walled square 500 metres to a side with about 45 public buildings, among them the ball court and its tzompantli, the rack of skulls. Outside the wall was Moctezuma's palace, with 100 rooms, each with its own bath.

The sixth temple was Ahuitzotl's, dedicated in the year 8 Reed, 1487. Post-conquest accounts claim that 80,400 captives were sacrificed over four days, on four tables set at the top; the Codex Telleriano-Remensis puts the figure at about 4,000, and the historian Ross Hassig gives a range of 10,000 to 80,400. In June 1520 Cortes attacked the temple and his men reached the top of its 114 steps, but at a cost of nearly a hundred dead, and were driven back. During the 1521 siege Spanish soldiers again reached the summit, set the temple on fire and planted their banners, while below the Aztecs cut out the hearts of 70 Spanish prisoners at Huitzilopochtli's altar. The victors dismantled the pyramid and used its stone to build the Spanish city.

One stone survived by going underground. The sun stone, a basalt disc 3.6 metres across and weighing nearly 25 tonnes, lay uncovered beside the ruined temple for years, until Archbishop Alonso de Montufar ordered it buried so that the memory of the old sacrifices would be lost. On 17 December 1790 workmen levelling the Plaza Mayor found it half a yard down. Antonio de Leon y Gama persuaded the cathedral canon not to bury it again and wrote one of the first studies of its carving, and in 1791 it was set into the outer wall of the cathedral's west tower, facing the Spanish square.
zh:
特诺奇蒂特兰的中心矗立着韦伊特奥卡利，即大神庙，墨西卡人认为它是宇宙的中心。台基约100米长、80米宽，上面两座神殿各有独立的石阶，一座奉战神威齐洛波契特里，一座奉雨神特拉洛克。第一座神庙在1325年建城之后动工，先后重建六次。神庙围在边长500米的方墙之内，墙里约有45座公共建筑，包括球场和陈列头骨的头骨架；墙外是蒙特苏马的宫殿，有100个房间，每间都带浴室。

第六期神庙由阿维措特尔主持，1487年芦苇八年落成。征服后的记载称，四天之内有80400名俘虏在塔顶四张祭桌上被杀；《特列里亚诺-雷曼西斯手抄本》记的数字约为四千人，历史学家霍斯·哈西格给出的范围是一万到80400。1520年6月，科尔特斯进攻大神庙，西班牙人打上114级台阶的顶端，但死了近一百人，被逼退下来。1521年围城期间，西班牙士兵再次登上塔顶，放火烧神庙，插上自己的旗帜；就在脚下，阿兹特克人在威齐洛波契特里的祭坛前挖出70名西班牙俘虏的心脏。胜利者拆了金字塔，用石料修建西班牙人的城市。

有一块石头靠埋入地下躲过了这一切。太阳石是玄武岩圆盘，直径3.6米，重近25吨，在破败的神庙旁露天放了多年，直到大主教阿隆索·德·蒙图法尔下令把它埋掉，好让旧日献祭的记忆随之消失。1790年12月17日，工人铲平马约尔广场时，在半码深的地方发现了它。安东尼奥·德·莱昂-加马说服大教堂的议事司铎不要再埋，并写下最早研究其雕刻的论著之一；1791年，它被嵌进大教堂西塔的外墙，面朝西班牙人的广场。

en:
The silver of Zacatecas was won with quicksilver. Ore was ground to powder in mule-driven stone mills, then spread in a yard with salt, copper pyrites, lime and quicksilver and turned now and then for anything from two weeks to two months, until the silver bound itself to the mercury in an amalgam. The mixture was washed in a stream, which is why the refining haciendas stood beside running water. The quicksilver came under the Crown's monopoly from Almadén in Spain and Huancavelica in Peru. The success of the mines drew indigenous workers to the camp, and black slaves were imported to work in them.

Zacatecas began in 1548 as a military mining camp, the year the first major vein was struck at the San Bernabé mine. The town ran south along the Arroyo de la Plata, built on rough ground at the foot of the Cerro de la Bufa with no orderly plan: narrow streets and alleys followed the old Indian neighbourhoods down a ravine, and with no flat ground the houses were built tall. Philip II granted the title of city in 1585. The El Edén mine began work in 1586 in the Cerro de la Bufa and produced mostly gold and silver, with its peak in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Local legend puts the devil in its tunnels, because of the sound of wind whistling around the rocks.

The mine owners' money paid for churches and mansions, with the building boom at its height in the eighteenth century; the cathedral, finished in 1752, has a Churrigueresque front of carved pink stone. The Palacio de la Mala Noche takes its name from a story about its owner, the miner José Manuel de Rétegui: ruined, he had resolved on suicide one night when word came that a rich vein had been found in one of his mines. By about 1797 the Vetagrande company had sunk a general shaft 360 varas deep, roughly 300 metres.
zh:
萨卡特卡斯的白银是靠水银炼出来的。矿石先在骡子拉动的石碾里磨成粉，再摊在院子里，拌上盐、铜黄铁矿、石灰和水银，隔些时候翻动一次，短则两周，长则两个月，直到银与汞结成汞膏。混料要拿到溪水里冲洗，所以选矿庄园总是建在流水旁边。水银受王室专卖，来自西班牙的阿尔马登和秘鲁的万卡韦利卡。矿山兴旺，吸引土著来到矿营，也有黑奴被运来矿上做工。

萨卡特卡斯矿城1548年起于一座军事矿营，这一年圣贝尔纳贝矿坑挖到第一条大银脉。城镇沿「银溪」向南延伸，坐落在布法山脚的崎岖地面上，没有规整的规划：窄街小巷顺着旧时印第安人的聚居区排进一道峡谷，没有平地，房子就盖得很高。1585年，腓力二世授予它城市的称号。埃登矿1586年在布法山里开工，主要出金和银，盛产期在17、18世纪。当地传说魔鬼就住在矿道里，因为风吹过岩石会发出呼啸声。

矿主们的钱花在教堂和宅邸上，建造热潮在18世纪达到顶点；1752年建成的主教座堂，正面是丘里格拉风格的粉色石雕。「恶夜宫」得名于它的主人、矿主何塞·曼努埃尔·雷特吉的一段传说：他破产后一晚已决意自尽，恰在这时有人报来，他的一座矿里发现了富矿脉。1797年前后，贝塔格兰德公司凿成了一条深360巴拉（约300米）的总竖井。

en:
The last roof beam at Mesa Verde was felled in 1281, and within a few years the people who cut it had left for good. Mesa Verde is a forested tableland in the Four Corners country of south-west Colorado, its canyons cut into sandstone that holds whole villages in its alcoves. For about six hundred years the Ancestral Puebloans farmed corn, beans and squash on the mesa tops. From the late twelfth century, under pressure from drought and competition, they began building in the cliffs. Cliff Palace, the largest cliff dwelling in North America, fills one alcove with 21 kivas, two kiva-like rooms and some twenty-five living rooms, home to perhaps 100 to 120 people. Its walls were plastered in yellow, white and red, and a tunnel joins the two southernmost kivas, perhaps so that performers could appear and vanish during ceremonies. About 600 cliff dwellings are known on the mesa.

A drought from 1276 to 1299 ended the building, and the last inhabitants left about 1285 for Arizona and New Mexico, where the pueblos of Acoma, Zuni, Jemez and Laguna count their descendants. In 1444 the stone villages had been empty for some 160 years. The Utes, who long wintered on the high plateaus here, held the cliff dwellings to be sacred ancestral sites and did not live in them.

In 1776 the Franciscans Atanasio Dominguez and Silvestre Velez de Escalante left Santa Fe with ten men and the cartographer Bernardo de Miera y Pacheco, hoping to find an overland road to Monterey, and followed the route Juan Rivera had taken eleven years earlier into Ute country. They camped near the mesa in August and named the region Mesa Verde, the green table, for its high, tree-covered plateaus, but never got close enough, or at the right angle, to see the villages in the cliffs. Near the town of Dolores they did record other Ancestral Puebloan ruins, the first Europeans to do so.
zh:
梅萨维德悬崖村的最后一根房梁砍伐于1281年，几年之后，砍下它的人就离开了，再没回来。梅萨维德是科罗拉多州西南部四角地带的一片林木覆盖的台地，峡谷切进砂岩，崖龛里藏着整座整座的石头村落。古普韦布洛人在台顶种了大约六百年的玉米、豆子和南瓜；从12世纪晚期起，在旱灾和部族竞争的压力下，他们开始在崖壁间营造村落。其中的悬崖宫是北美最大的崖居，一处岩龛里有21座基瓦、2间类似基瓦的房间和约25间居室，可能住过100到120人。墙面抹着黄、白、红三色的灰泥，最南端的两座基瓦之间有一条地下通道，或许是供仪式上的表演者忽隐忽现用的。台地上已知的崖居约有600处。

1276至1299年的大旱终止了营造，最后的居民约在1285年前后南迁到亚利桑那和新墨西哥，阿科马、祖尼、赫梅斯和拉古纳等普韦布洛人都是他们的后裔。1444年，这些石头村落已空了约160年。乌特人长期在这里的高地上过冬，把崖居视为神圣的祖先遗址，从不住进去。

1776年，方济各会士阿塔纳西奥·多明格斯和西尔韦斯特雷·贝莱斯·德·埃斯卡兰特带着十名随从和制图师贝尔纳多·德·米耶拉·伊·帕切科从圣菲出发，想找一条通往蒙特雷的陆路，起初沿着十一年前胡安·里韦拉走过的路线进入乌特人的地界。八月，他们在台地附近扎营，见这里的高地林木葱郁，便把这一带取名梅萨维德，意为「绿色的桌子」，却始终没能走到看得见崖中村落的位置和角度。不过在多洛雷斯一带，他们确实记录了另外一些古普韦布洛人的遗迹，是最早记录这类遗迹的欧洲人。

en:
Monks Mound rises a hundred feet from the Mississippi bottomlands, and every basket-load of its soil and clay was carried by hand. Around 1100 the Mississippian city at Cahokia covered about six square miles and held some 120 earthworks and perhaps fifteen to twenty thousand people; its trade reached the Great Lakes and the Gulf Coast, in copper, shark teeth and whelk shells. The great mound holds some 22 million cubic feet of earth. It measures about 955 feet long, counting the access ramp at its southern end, by 775 wide, a base roughly the size of the Great Pyramid's, and climbs in four terraces to a flat summit. There stood a building about 105 feet long, probably a temple or the chief's residence. A two-mile palisade with bastions enclosed the central precinct and was rebuilt several times. By 1400 the city stood empty, and no substantial settlement returned to the area for two centuries.

The mound outlived its builders. In 1735 French missionaries built a chapel on the west end of its south terrace. In 1809 a small group of Trappist monks, given land by Nicholas Jarrot, settled on one of the smaller mounds; they grew wheat on the upper levels of the great mound and garden produce on the south terrace, above the floods. During their stay the lawyer Henry Marie Brackenridge came over from St. Louis and wrote the first detailed description of the mound. The sight, he wrote, struck him with an astonishment not unlike what he felt contemplating the Egyptian pyramids; heaping up such a mass must have taken years and the labour of thousands. He complained to Thomas Jefferson in a letter that his discovery was being ignored. The mound took the name it carries now from the monks.
zh:
僧侣墩从密西西比河泛滥平原上拔起约30米，每一筐泥土和黏土都靠人手搬来。约1100年，密西西比文化的卡霍基亚城方圆约六平方英里，有大小土丘约一百二十座，人口可能有一万五千到两万；贸易远及五大湖和墨西哥湾沿岸，铜、鲨鱼牙和海螺壳都在其中。大土墩用土约2200万立方英尺，长约955英尺（含南端的引坡）、宽775英尺，底面积与胡夫金字塔相去不远，分四层台地收束到平顶，顶上有一座长约105英尺的大建筑，很可能是神庙，或首领的居所。中央祭祀区围着一道长两英里、带棱堡的木栅栏，几度重修。到1400年前后，这座城已经荒空，此后约两百年里，附近没有再出现像样的聚落。

土墩比建造者活得更久。1735年，法国传教士在南层台地的西端盖了一座小礼拜堂。1809年，一小群特拉普会修士得到尼古拉·雅罗赠予的土地，在一座较小的土丘上住下，又把大土墩当作菜地：上层台地种小麦，南层台地种蔬菜，高出洪水之上。修士们还在的时候，律师亨利·马里·布雷肯里奇从圣路易斯过来，写下关于这座土墩的第一份详细记述：他说，眼前景象令他惊愕，与凝望埃及金字塔时的感受相去不远；堆起这样一座土山，必耗费多年光阴和数千人的劳作。他后来在给托马斯·杰斐逊的信里抱怨，自己的发现无人理会。这座土墩也因此得名僧侣墩。

en:
The story that white paint was first applied to hide the fire stains of 1814 is a myth. The porous sandstone walls were whitewashed when the house was finished, with a mixture of lime, rice glue, casein and lead, and the public was calling it the White House by 1811. In 1444 this stretch of the Potomac lay in the country of the Algonquian-speaking Piscataway. The Residence Act of July 1790 put the new republic's capital on the river, and in July 1792 George Washington looked over the entries for the President's House and quickly chose that of James Hoban, an Irish-born architect trained at the Dublin Society of Arts. The upper floors drew on Dublin's Leinster House. Enslaved African Americans quarried the stone, Scottish masons raised the sandstone walls, and shortages of material and labour cut the planned three main floors to two. John Adams, the first president to live in it, arrived on 1 November 1800 and wrote to his wife Abigail the next day: 'May none but honest and wise men ever rule under this roof.'

Thomas Jefferson, who thought the house 'big enough for two emperors, one pope, and the grand lama in the bargain', worked with Benjamin Latrobe on low colonnades to hide the laundry, stable and storage. On 24 August 1814, after the American defeat at Bladensburg, British troops under Robert Ross and George Cockburn burned the house in retaliation for American destruction in the Canadas. Paul Jennings, Madison's enslaved attendant, recalled in his memoir that Dolley Madison carried off only the silver, while the doorkeeper and the gardener took down the portrait of Washington and sent it away by wagon with other valuables. The British officers ate the dinner that had been prepared for the President's party. Only the scorched outer walls remained, and most were torn down and rebuilt, except for parts of the south wall. Hoban and Latrobe both contributed to the rebuilding, which lasted from 1815 until 1817.
zh:
说白漆最初是为掩盖1814年的火烧痕迹才刷上的，这是个误传。房子竣工时，多孔的砂岩墙面就用石灰、米胶、酪蛋白和铅调成的涂料刷白，民间至迟在1811年已经管它叫白宫。1444年，波托马克河的这一段属于说阿尔冈昆语的皮斯卡塔韦人的地界。1790年7月的《首都选址法》把新生共和国的首都定在这条河边；1792年7月，乔治·华盛顿审阅总统府的应征方案，很快选中了詹姆斯·霍本的设计。霍本生于爱尔兰，曾在都柏林艺术协会受训，宅邸的上层参照了都柏林的伦斯特府。被奴役的黑人采石，苏格兰石匠砌起砂岩墙体，材料和人手短缺，使原计划的三个主楼层缩成两层。约翰·亚当斯是第一位入住的总统，1800年11月1日搬进来，次日写信给妻子阿比盖尔：愿此后在这屋顶下主政的人，个个诚实而明智。

托马斯·杰斐逊嫌这房子「两个皇帝、一个教皇再加上大喇嘛都住得下」，和建筑师本杰明·拉特罗布在两侧加了低矮的柱廊，遮住洗衣房、马厩和库房。1814年8月24日，美军在布拉登斯堡战败后，罗伯特·罗斯和乔治·科伯恩率英军入城，为报复美军在加拿大的破坏，烧了总统府。麦迪逊的黑人侍从保罗·詹宁斯在回忆录里说，多莉·麦迪逊只带走了银器，把华盛顿画像摘下来、连同其他贵重物品装车运走的是看门人和园丁。英军军官吃掉了为总统一行备好的晚餐。最后只剩熏黑的外墙，这些墙大多拆毁重建，只有南墙的几段保留下来。霍本和拉特罗布都参与了重建的设计和监督，工程从1815年持续到1817年。

en:
The Arctic tundra has few natural landmarks, and in a caribou drive a line of stone cairns could stand in for a line of people. On southern Victoria Island the Iqaluktuuq drive runs for more than three kilometres, with over 1,500 inuksuit and 70 hunting blinds, put up and rebuilt over many generations. The lines steered the herd towards set entry points, into water where kayakers waited, or towards bowmen in the blinds. Cairns were often dressed with turf, feathers or bird wings, which added colour, movement in the wind and noise. Several Inuit could raise a drive of dozens of cairns, with a few blinds, in under an hour.

The word inuksuk joins inuk, 'person', and -suk, 'substitute': 'that which acts in the capacity of a human'. The simplest is a single stone set upright; the size of larger ones suggests that building was often a communal effort. Inuksuit served as reference points, route markers, fishing places, camp and hunting-ground markers, places of veneration and food caches. At Enukso Point on Baffin Island about a hundred cairns stand in two groups, from single upright stones to carefully piled monuments up to seven feet high, and the grouping may be as much as two thousand years old. Drives of this type on Victoria Island are linked to Inuit occupation from about 1350, so by 1444 the craft was old and in use.

At the water crossings used by the Caribou Inuit, hunters waited in kayaks that might be painted with bands of red ochre to look like boulders along the shore. When the caribou were halfway across, the kayaks shot out after them.
zh:
北极苔原上天然地标很少，驯鹿围猎时，一排石堆可以充当一排人。维多利亚岛南部的伊卡卢图克（Iqaluktuuq）围猎场绵延三公里以上，有一千五百多座石堆和70个猎手掩体，是历代人不断修建、重建而成。石堆排成的线把鹿群引向预定的入口：赶进水里，皮艇手在那里等着，或者引向掩体里的弓箭手。石堆上常缀着草皮、羽毛或鸟翅，增添颜色，在风中摆动，也会发出声响。几个因纽特人不到一小时，就能堆起几十座石堆和几个掩体。

因努伊特石堆（inuksuk）一词由 inuk（「人」）和 -suk（「替代」）拼成，意思是「充当人的东西」。最简单的石堆只是一块竖立的石头；较大的石堆规模可观，说明常常是众人合力所建。它们用作参照点、路标、捕鱼处、营地和猎场的标记、敬拜之处和藏肉的窖穴。巴芬岛的伊努克索角有约一百座石堆，分成两群，从单块竖石到精心垒起、高达七英尺的石堆都有，这片石阵可能早至两千年前就已存在。维多利亚岛上这类围猎场与约1350年起的因纽特人居住有关，所以到1444年，这门手艺已经古老，仍在使用。

卡里布因纽特人（驯鹿因纽特人）在鹿群渡水的地点，猎手坐在皮艇里等候，艇身有时涂着一道道红赭石，看上去像岸边的巨石。鹿群游到一半时，皮艇便冲出去追赶。

en:
Sakurai Genbei, master carpenter to Ikeda Terumasa, is said to have been dissatisfied with the finished keep, feeling that it leaned a little to the southeast. He climbed to the top and jumped to his death with a chisel in his mouth.

The keep stands on Himeyama, a hill 45.6 metres above sea level, at a key point on the San'yo road. After Sekigahara in 1600 Tokugawa Ieyasu gave Himeji to his son-in-law Ikeda Terumasa, who pulled down Toyotomi Hideyoshi's three-storey keep and rebuilt the castle from 1601 to 1609. The main keep is 46.4 metres high and looks five storeys tall from outside, though it has six floors and a basement. The first floor, with more than 330 tatami mats, is called the thousand-mat room, and its walls carry racks for matchlocks and spears. Small rooms called warrior hiding places let defenders wait to kill intruders by surprise.

The approach was built to confuse. Gates, baileys and walls send an attacker round the complex in a spiral, and the paths often double back, so that the 130 metres from the Hishi Gate to the keep become a steep, narrow walk of 325 metres. About a thousand loopholes let defenders shoot arrows and matchlocks, and thirty-three wells lay inside the inner moat in case of a siege. The castle was never attacked in this way, so the maze was never tested.

Himeji is also said to have its ghosts. A variant of the Dish Mansion ghost story, Banshu Sarayashiki, is set here: the maidservant Okiku was falsely accused of losing valuable family dishes, killed and thrown into a well, and her ghost haunts the well at night, counting the dishes. The yokai Osakabehime is said to live in the keep, shunning the humans she hates and reading their minds. In another tale Hideyoshi ran out of stone while building his keep until an old woman gave him her millstone; others followed her example, and the supposed Old Widow's Stone is set in a castle wall.
zh:
据说，池田辉政手下的大木匠樱井源兵卫对落成的天守不满意，觉得它略微向东南倾斜，便爬上天守顶，口衔凿子跳了下去。

天守立在海拔45.6米的姬山上，位于山阳道的交通要冲。1600年关原之战后，德川家康把姬路城赐给女婿池田辉政，辉政拆掉丰臣秀吉的三层天守，在1601至1609年间重建了整座城。大天守高46.4米，从外面看是五层，实际是六层加一层地下室。底层铺三百多张榻榻米，号称千叠敷，墙上设有挂铁炮和长枪的武具架。叫武者隐的小间，让守军可以埋伏着，等闯入者进来时出其不意地杀出。

攻城之路被设计得让人迷路。门、曲轮和城墙把进攻者引得绕着城区盘旋，路又常常折回，从菱之门到天守直线只有130米，实际却是一条又陡又窄的325米山路。墙上开着约一千个狭间，供守军射箭和放铁炮，内壕之内挖了三十三口水井，以备围城。城从未遭到这样的进攻，这座迷宫也就一直没有经受过检验。

姬路城还传说有鬼怪。《皿屋敷》鬼故事有一种叫《播州皿屋敷》，故事就发生在这里：侍女阿菊被诬弄丢了家传的贵重盘子，被杀后投入井中，她的鬼魂夜里留在井边数盘子。妖怪长壁姬据说住在天守里，躲着她憎恨的人类，能读出人心。另有一则传说：秀吉修天守时石头不够，一位老妇献出了自己的石磨，旁人也纷纷效仿，这块相传的「姥石」就嵌在一道城墙里。

en:
In 1443, rebels loyal to the old Southern Court attacked the palace at night and set it on fire. Emperor Go-Hanazono got away, and tradition says he slipped out through the Kara Gate dressed as a lady-in-waiting. The raiders took the sacred jewel, one of the three imperial regalia, and it did not come back to the court until 1458. The palace was the Kyoto Imperial Palace in the Kamigyo district, and by 1444 it had been the emperor's seat for over a century.

The Heian palace had stood 1.7 kilometres to the west, but it burned so often that emperors took to living in mansions lent by noble families, and it was finally abandoned in the late twelfth century. The present grounds were once the Tsuchimikado Higashinotoin, a Fujiwara mansion that became the palace of the Northern Court in the fourteenth century. After a fire in 1401 Ashikaga Yoshimitsu rebuilt it on the model of the Heian palace. Here stood the Shishinden, where emperors were enthroned, and the Seiryoden. The Onin War of 1467 scattered the court nobles and impoverished the court. Go-Kashiwabara succeeded in 1500 and was enthroned only in 1521, twenty-one years later. The court had cancelled its own ceremonies to save money, and he finally took the throne in the Shishinden with gifts from the Hongan-ji abbot Jitsunyo and the shogunate.

Oda Nobunaga and Toyotomi Hideyoshi put the palace in order after taking Kyoto. The Tokugawa shoguns kept tight control over the court. In the Purple Robe Incident of 1627 the shogunate voided Emperor Go-Mizunoo's grants of purple robes to eminent monks, and two years later he abdicated without telling it. In 1788 the Tenmei fire, the worst in the city's history, burned the palace, Nijo Castle, the shoshidai residence and more than four-fifths of Kyoto. Shogun Tokugawa Ienari ordered the rebuilding, which the shogunate paid for over the objection of Matsudaira Sadanobu that such splendour was unaffordable. In 1790 the halls were raised on the plan of the Heian palace as reconstructed in Uramatsu Kozen's study of the old palace, the Daidairi zukosho.
zh:
1443年，效忠旧南朝的叛军夜袭皇居并放火。后花园天皇逃了出去，相传他扮作女官，从唐门溜走。三种神器之一的神玺被叛军夺走，直到1458年才回到朝廷。这座皇居就是京都上京的京都皇居，到1444年，已是天皇居所百余年。

平安时代的大内里原在其西1.7公里，因频频失火，天皇常寄住公家借出的宅邸，12世纪后期大内里被彻底废弃。现在这片皇居的基址原为藤原氏的土御门东洞院殿，14世纪成为北朝的皇居。1401年火灾之后，足利义满仿照平安宫把它重建。境内有举行即位礼的紫宸殿和清凉殿。1467年应仁之乱使公家四散、朝廷困窘。后柏原天皇1500年继位，直到二十一年后的1521年才举行即位礼：朝廷为省钱曾自行中止各项仪式，最后靠本愿寺法主实如和幕府的献金，在紫宸殿办成了仪式。

织田信长、丰臣秀吉入主京都后整修皇居，德川幕府则牢牢管着朝廷。1627年紫衣事件中，幕府宣布后水尾天皇准许高僧穿紫衣的敕令无效，天皇两年后未告知幕府就退位了。1788年，京都史上最大的火灾天明大火烧毁皇居、二条城、京都所司代和八成以上的街市。将军德川家齐下令重建，费用由幕府承担，松平定信曾以耗费过大反对。1790年，殿舍依照里松固禅《大内里图考证》复原的平安宫形制建成。

en:
In 1776 the small Kishiwada domain spent 84 percent of its whole budget in Edo. That was the price of alternate attendance, under which daimyo spent every other year in the shogun's capital and left their wives and heirs there when they went home. Lords had begun attending the ruler voluntarily under Hideyoshi, and in 1635 Shogun Iemitsu wrote the yearly attendance into the Laws for the Military Houses. Every domain therefore kept houses in Edo, mostly on land granted by the shogunate. A large domain kept three: the upper residence, where the lord lodged and his wife and heir lived; the middle residence for the heir or a retired lord; and the lower residence, a suburban villa with gardens, rice warehouses and a drill ground. In 1684 the Tosa domain's houses held 3,195 people, 1,683 of them in the upper residence alone. Inside a yashiki's gates the shogunate did not use its powers of search, even when a fugitive criminal slipped in.

Getting there was an operation of its own. The Kaga house of Kanazawa brought between 2,500 and 4,000 men, and the Kaga steward Yokoyama Masahiro kept a diary of each journey. Leaving the castle town, a lord hired extra men to make the train look larger, and let them go at the edge of town, which cut the numbers by about half. Commoners along the road had to give way, and riders had to dismount; only the lord's own people and the Tokugawa cadet houses were owed a kneeling bow. The march alone cost a domain 5 to 20 percent of its revenue, and the Edo houses together took 50 to 75 percent. A visit from the shogun could beggar a great house: in the Genroku years the Kaga domain spent 360,000 ryo on a single one.

The Mito Tokugawa were lords who lived permanently in Edo. In the grounds of their upper residence at Koishikawa, Tokugawa Yorifusa laid out a garden in 1629, and his son Mitsukuni named it Korakuen with advice from the Ming scholar Zhu Zhiyu. After the Meireki fire of 1657 burned much of Edo, the shogunate granted daimyo outlying lower residences to ease the crowding.
zh:
1776年，小小的岸和田藩把全部支出的百分之八十四花在了江户。这是参勤交代的代价：大名每隔一年要在将军的都城居住，回国时妻子和嫡子留在江户。大名最早是丰臣秀吉时期自愿去拜见当权者，1635年三代将军家光把每年参勤写进了《武家诸法度》。各藩因此都有江户藩邸，宅地多由幕府拨给。大藩通常有三处：上屋敷是藩主的住处，正室和嫡子也住在这里；中屋敷给嗣子或隐居的前藩主居住；下屋敷在郊外，带园林、藏米的仓廪和练兵场。1684年，土佐藩各处府邸共住三千一百九十五人，仅上屋敷就有一千六百八十三人。幕府不在藩邸大门之内行使搜查权，逃进去的罪犯也一样。

赶路本身就是一项大工程。加贺前田家从金泽出发的行列有两千五百到四千人，加贺藩家老横山政宽还留下了每次旅程的日记。离开城下町时，藩主会雇来人手撑场面，到町外便遣散，人数随之减半。沿途的平民要让路，骑马的要下马，只有本藩藩主和御三家的行列才须跪伏。仅路上花费就占藩收入的百分之五到二十，连同江户府邸的开销则达百分之五十到七十五。将军一次驾临就能让大藩伤筋动骨：元禄年间，加贺藩为一次接待花了三十六万两。

水户德川家是常驻江户的藩主。1629年，德川赖房在小石川上屋敷里营建庭园，其子光圀在明朝遗臣朱舜水指点下命名为后乐园。1657年明历大火烧毁江户大半之后，幕府给大名拨出郊外的下屋敷，以缓解市区拥挤。

en:
In the Tale of the Bamboo Cutter, a ninth-century text, the emperor has the elixir of immortality left by Kaguya-hime burned on the summit nearest heaven, and the tale derives the name Fuji both from the many soldiers (shi) who climbed there and from fushi, 'undying'. The mountain is a lone cone 3,776 metres high, snow-capped for about five months of the year. The early court feared its fire. Ash fell in 781, the oldest dated eruption record, and the Fujinomiya shrine is thought to have been founded to quiet the mountain's kami, identified with Konohanasakuya-hime. At first only Shugendo ascetics were allowed on the mountain, and women were forbidden to climb it. By the Edo period pilgrims purified themselves at that shrine before the ascent. Fuji had last erupted on a large scale in the Heian age, and in 1444 it had been quiet for centuries.

In the Sengoku age the ascetic Kakugyo practised austerities in a cave at Hitoana near Fujinomiya, and the faith later called Fuji-ko descends from him. A later teacher of his line, Jikigyo Miroku, won over the poor townspeople of Edo and in 1733 fasted for thirty-five days on the mountain until he died. After his death the confraternities multiplied until Edo was said to hold eight hundred and eight of them, with eighty thousand members, and the oshi guides of the Yoshida approach lodged their climbing parties. People unable to climb through age, infirmity or gender climbed fujizuka instead: mounds about ten feet high, built in and around Edo, with ten stations like the mountain itself.

In 1707 a huge earthquake struck along the Nankai Trough, and 49 days later Fuji split open on its southeast flank. For about a fortnight scoria and ash fell on the lands to the east. The scholar Arai Hakuseki, living in Edo a hundred kilometres away, wrote that the ash came down like falling snow. Fields and villages near the mountain were buried, and the Odawara domain's records counted more than two thousand dead in the disaster. The new crater hill was named Hoei-zan. There was no lava flow, and Fuji stayed quiet for the rest of the Edo age.
zh:
9世纪的《竹取物语》里，天皇命人把辉夜姬留下的不死之药拿到离天最近的山顶焚烧，故事把「富士」之名既解作登山的众多武士（士），也解作「不死」。富士山是一座海拔3776米的孤峰，山顶积雪约五个月。古代朝廷畏惧它的火：781年降灰，是有确切年代的最早喷发记录，富士宫的神社据信是为安抚山神而建，山神被视作木花之佐久夜毗卖。起初只有修验道的修行者可以入山，女性则禁止登山。到江户时代，登山的信众先在这座神社净身。富士山上一次大规模喷发还在平安时代，到1444年已经平静了好几百年。

战国年间，修行者角行在富士宫附近的人穴苦修，后来所称的富士讲即出自他的法脉。其后一位传人食行身禄把信仰传给江户的贫苦町人，1733年在山中绝食三十五天后入定。他死后，讲社越办越多，江户号称有八百零八个讲社、八万讲众，吉田口的御师接待登山的信众。因年老、体弱或性别而不能登山的人，就爬富士冢：一丈来高的土丘，筑在江户及周边，也按十站仿造富士山。

1707年，南海海槽发生特大地震，49天后富士山东南斜面炸开。此后约两周，火山渣和火山灰倾落在东侧。身在百公里外江户的学者新井白石写道，灰落下来像下雪一样。山下的田野和村庄被埋，小田原藩记录的死者超过两千人。新喷出的火山丘得名宝永山。这次喷发没有熔岩流出，此后整个江户时代富士山再未喷发。

en:
The Kazan Kremlin is the citadel on the high hill above the Kazanka, the old fortress of the Kazan khans. In the fifteenth century the khan's Ark was girdled by oak walls, perhaps partly of stone, up to nine metres thick, with four gated towers; the muddy Bulak channel protected it on the west. Inside stood the khan's palace and the congregational mosque with the mausoleums of the khans. Prince Andrey Kurbsky wrote of 'exceedingly tall' stone mosques where the dead kings were laid, and tradition gave the cathedral mosque eight minarets. When the city was stormed in 1552 the imam Kul Sharif, a poet who had gone on diplomatic missions to Moscow for the khans, organised his students to defend the khan's palace and was killed in the fighting.

The leaning Söyembikä Tower is the hardest part of the Kremlin to date. Scholars date it to the turn of the eighteenth century, to about 1645-1650, or even to the khans. Legend says Ivan the Terrible's artisans raised it in a week and the Kazan queen Söyembikä threw herself from its top tier, which gave the tower her name. After the siege Ivan IV called in the Pskov masters Postnik Yakovlev and Ivan Shiryay, said to be the builders of Saint Basil's in Moscow, with 200 Pskov stonemasons to rebuild the citadel. The Annunciation Cathedral went up from pale local sandstone, the only sixteenth-century Russian church with six piers and five apses; yet in that century only a third of the 1,800 metres of oak wall was replaced in stone. Five stone buildings of khan date, among them the mosque, the palace and the mausoleums, served for more than a century and a half as stores for arms and ammunition before they were pulled down as dilapidated. The English envoy Giles Fletcher named Kazan among four Russian fortresses that could withstand any siege. In July 1774 Pugachev's rebels shelled the Kremlin for two days before he was forced to retreat; after his capture he was held in one of its casemates on his way to execution in Moscow.
zh:
喀山克里姆林宫是卡赞卡河高冈上的城塞，喀山汗国旧日的堡垒。15世纪时，汗的城堡围以厚达九米的橡木城墙，局部可能为石砌，开四座城门塔楼；泥泞的布拉克河汊护着西侧。城内有汗的宫殿和聚礼清真寺，寺旁是历代汗的陵墓。安德烈·库尔布斯基公爵写到山上有「极高的」石砌清真寺，故去的汗就葬在那里；相传主清真寺有八座宣礼塔。1552年城破之际，伊玛目库尔·谢里夫率学生保卫汗宫，战死在宫中；他是诗人，曾代表汗国出使莫斯科。

倾斜的苏尤姆别卡塔是整座城塞里最难断代的部分。学者有的把它定在18世纪初，有的定在1645至1650年前后，也有人认为可追溯到汗国时期。传说讲伊凡雷帝的工匠七天将它建成，喀山王后苏尤姆别卡从最高一层纵身跳下，塔也因此得名。围城之后，伊凡四世召来普斯科夫匠师波斯特尼克·雅科夫列夫和伊凡·希里亚伊，据说两人也建造了莫斯科的圣瓦西里大教堂，并征集200名普斯科夫石匠重建城塞。圣母领报大堂用当地浅色砂岩砌成，六柱五后殿的形制在16世纪俄罗斯教堂中仅此一例；但整个16世纪，一千八百米橡木城墙只换了约三分之一的石墙。汗时代留下的五座石建筑，包括清真寺、宫殿和陵墓，被充作军械和弹药库一百五十多年，终因破败拆除。英国使节贾尔斯·弗莱切把喀山列为俄国四座经得起任何围攻的要塞之一。1774年7月，普加乔夫的起义军炮轰克里姆林宫两天，被迫撤退；他被俘后曾关在这座城堡的一间囚室里，再被押往莫斯科处决。

en:
Unlike the universities of Europe, Sankore had no central administration, student registers or set course of study. It was a web of private masters: a student attached himself to one sheikh for up to ten years, studied in the master's house or at the mosque, paid in coin or goods and often earned his keep by copying manuscripts. Sankore is the mosque of the quarter of that name in Timbuktu, a word that means 'white masters' in Songhai, a reference to the light-skinned Sanhaja Berbers. The French account has a mosque built here under Mansa Musa in the 1320s, while the English one credits a wealthy Tuareg woman of the Aghlal tribe with paying for it in the fourteenth or early fifteenth century. It was built of clay and wood beams in the Sahelian manner, and classes met in its open courtyard. Between 1578 and 1582 the chief qadi of Timbuktu, al-Aqib ibn Mahmud ibn Umar, pulled down the sanctuary and rebuilt it to the dimensions of the Kaaba in Mecca.

Books were the dearest goods in Timbuktu, brought across the desert from North Africa. Leo Africanus, who reached the city around 1510 and published his account in 1526, wrote that manuscripts sold for more than any other merchandise and that the learned were maintained at the king's expense. In the sixteenth century the city held 150 to 180 Qur'anic schools for four to nine thousand pupils, and some two or three hundred students from wealthy families went on to higher study. At each of four levels the student was given a turban. Ahmad Baba, the foremost Sankore scholar, wrote more than forty books, including a biographical dictionary of Maliki scholars read across the Maghreb. After the Moroccan conquest of 1591 many Sankore scholars were arrested on charges of sedition and deported to Morocco with their manuscripts. Ahmad Baba alone lost a library of 1,600 volumes, and he came back to Timbuktu only in 1608.
zh:
和欧洲的大学不同，桑科雷没有中央管理、学籍册和固定课程，它是一张私人师徒织成的网：学生跟定一位谢赫，长则十年，在老师家中或清真寺里读书，学费以钱或货物支付，还常靠抄书糊口。桑科雷大学是廷巴克图桑科雷区的清真寺；「桑科雷」在桑海语中意为「白主人」，指的是浅肤色的桑哈贾柏柏尔人。法文资料说曼萨·穆萨在位时的1320年代这里首建了清真寺，英文资料则把14世纪或15世纪初的营建归于阿格拉勒部落一位富有的图阿雷格妇人，说是她出资修成。寺体用黏土和木梁砌成，是萨赫勒做法，课就在露天庭院里上。1578至1582年间，廷巴克图首席卡迪阿基卜·伊本·马哈茂德·伊本·欧麦尔拆毁旧礼拜殿，照麦加天房的尺寸重建。

书是廷巴克图最贵重的货物，从北非随商队越沙漠而来。利奥·阿非利加努斯约1510年到过这座城市，1526年出版了他的记述，书中说手写本卖得比任何其他货物都贵，学者由国王出钱供养。16世纪，城中有150到180所古兰经学校，学童四千到九千人，另有两三百名富家子弟升入高阶学习。学业分四级，每升一级授一种头巾。桑科雷众学者之首艾哈迈德·巴巴著书四十余种，其中一部马立克派学者传记辞典风行整个马格里布。1591年摩洛哥征服之后，许多桑科雷学者以煽乱罪名被捕，连同手稿一起押往摩洛哥。仅艾哈迈德·巴巴一人就失去一千六百卷藏书，直到1608年才回到廷巴克图。

en:
The Tarikh al-Sudan, written down in the seventeenth century from oral tradition, says that Sultan Kunburu became a Muslim, had his own palace pulled down and turned the site into a mosque. He built himself another palace beside it, on the east side. His immediate successor built the towers of the mosque, and the sultan after him built the surrounding wall. The Great Mosque of Djenné stood in the river town of Djenné on the flood plain of the Bani River. Nobody knows when the first mosque was built, and dates between about 1200 and 1330 have been suggested.

The building was rebuilt more than once. The architectural historian Labelle Prussin gives a reading in which the first mosque was razed by Kunburu's successor, who built a new one, and the Songhay ruler Askia Mohammed rebuilt the original at the end of the fifteenth century. When the Moroccans invaded at the end of the sixteenth century, the Songhay mosque was destroyed and another was rebuilt, and this is the mosque the Tarikh describes. Around it stood one of the most important Islamic learning centres in Africa in the Middle Ages, where thousands of students came to study the Quran in Djenné's madrasas.

Around 1818 the Fulani leader Seku Amadu launched his jihad and conquered the town. He appears to have disapproved of the mosque, and Prussin calls the Moroccan building far too sumptuous for the puritanical tastes of the Fulbe ruler of Massina. He let it fall into disrepair, and he closed all the small neighbourhood mosques of the town.
zh:
据17世纪根据口述传统写成的《苏丹史》记载，昆布鲁苏丹皈依伊斯兰教后，下令拆掉自己的王宫，把那块地改作清真寺，又在清真寺东侧为自己另建了一座宫殿。他的直接继任者给清真寺建了塔楼，再下一位苏丹建了四周的围墙。杰内大清真寺立在河畔小城杰内，坐落于巴尼河的泛滥平原上。第一座清真寺究竟何时建成，没人知道，有人提出的年份在1200年到1330年之间。

这座建筑不止一次重建。建筑史家拉贝尔·普鲁辛的解读是：第一座清真寺被昆布鲁的继任者拆除、另建了新寺，15世纪末，桑海统治者阿斯基亚·穆罕默德重建了原来的那一座。16世纪末摩洛哥人入侵时，桑海时期的清真寺被毁，另一座又被重建，《苏丹史》所述的就是这一座。清真寺周围是中世纪非洲最重要的伊斯兰教学府之一，成千上万的学生来杰内的经学院里学习《古兰经》。

1818年前后，富拉尼首领塞库·阿马杜发动圣战，攻占了杰内。他似乎不赞成这座清真寺；普鲁辛称，这座摩洛哥式的寺对富拉尼人的马西纳统治者而言太过奢华，不合他们清教徒式的口味。他任由它失修，还封闭了城里各坊的小清真寺。

en:
The Walls of Benin were never walls of stone. Around Edo, the Oba's capital, workmen dug a ditch and piled the earth from it into a rampart on the city side; from the bottom of the ditch to the top of the bank was as much as 17 metres in places. Oba Oguola, who reigned around 1280, and Oba Ewuare are both remembered for re-digging and deepening the moats, which already existed before them. The inner ring, about 12 kilometres long, was finished around 1460. Smaller ditches and banks ran around villages and towns beyond it, and all the earthworks together have been estimated at roughly 16,000 kilometres across 6,500 square kilometres.
