The inner ring was cut by hand: one estimate holds that 5,000 men working ten hours a day could have finished it in 97 days, within a single dry season. Nine guarded gates let people through, traders paid a toll to enter, and invaders on the steep bank risked burial in sand avalanches, with the Oba's soldiers above them armed with spears and poisoned arrows.

European visitors kept measuring the earthwork against the walls they knew. The Portuguese Duarte Pacheco Pereira, who wrote in 1508 that he had been to Benin four times, found a city with no wall, only a moat so wide and deep that it needed no other defence. Around 1600 the Dutch captain Dierick Ruiters rode through a gate and saw a very high earthen bulwark and a broad dry ditch full of tall trees. Olfert Dapper, who never saw Africa and compiled his book from the reports of Dutch travellers, described gates eight or nine feet high made of one whole piece of wood that turned on a pin in the middle. In 1778 the French captain Landolphe found a ditch more than twenty feet wide and a bank planted with a thorn hedge so thick that not even an animal could get through. In 1787 another Frenchman, Legroing, saw the vestiges of an old earthen wall and noted that he had not seen a single stone on the whole way up from the coast.
zh:
贝宁城墙从来不是石墙。在奥巴的都城埃多四周，工匠挖出壕沟，再把挖出的泥土在靠城一侧堆成堤垒；从壕底到垒顶，有些地段高达17米。约在1280年在位的奥巴·奥古拉和奥巴·埃瓦雷都以重挖、加深壕沟闻名，而壕沟在他们之前就已存在。长约12公里的内圈约在1460年完工。内圈之外，许多较小的壕垒环绕着村镇，所有土工合计估计约有一万六千公里，分布在六千五百平方公里的土地上。内圈全靠人力挖成：有一种估算认为，5000人每天干十小时，97天就能完工，赶在一个旱季之内。内圈有九座有人看守的城门，商人入城要交税；来攻者在陡峭的堤坡上有被沙崩埋住的危险，上面还有手持长矛和毒箭的奥巴士兵。

欧洲来客总忍不住拿这座土工和他们熟悉的城墙比较。葡萄牙人杜阿尔特·帕切科·佩雷拉在1508年写道，他到过贝宁四次，那里没有墙，只有一条又宽又深的壕沟，凭它便足以自守。约1600年，荷兰船长迪里克·勒伊特斯骑马过门，见到一道极高的土垒和一条又阔又深的旱壕，壕中长满高树。奥尔弗特·达珀从未到过非洲，他据荷兰旅行者的报告写道，城门八九英尺高，用整根木料做成，绕中央一根枢轴转动。1778年，法国船长朗多尔夫看到一条二十多英尺宽的壕沟，堤上种着荆棘篱笆，密得连牲畜也钻不过去。1787年，另一位法国人勒格鲁万看到旧土墙的残迹，还补了一句：他从海岸一路上来，连一块石头都没见到。

en:
In 1648 the visitor Giovanni Francesco da Roma wrote that the manikongo's two-storey palace was the only building of its kind in all Kongo. It stood in M'banza-Kongo, a town on the flat-topped mountain of Mongo dia Kongo where major trade routes met; the first Portuguese to reach it in 1491 needed ten days to get there from the mouth of the Congo. A letter from the Portuguese ambassador to Lisbon compared the area inside the inner walls to Évora, and it was perhaps the largest town in sub-equatorial Africa. Kongo tradition remembered that the mountain had been won: the Mwene Kabunga, whose lands lay to the west around a shrine, had been one of Lukeni's wary allies, and two centuries later his descendants were still challenging the conquest symbolically in an annual celebration.

Stone came with the Portuguese. The first stone-and-mortar building in the capital was a church raised in 1491 by Portuguese craftsmen with Kongo labourers. Later kings added a wall of stone, 5 to 6 metres high, around the royal quarter, a stone palace and more churches; the city's important buildings came to include some twelve churches and many private chapels. A count of the 1620s recorded 4,500 baptisms a year in the city and its valleys, which points to some 130,000 people in the parish and 30,000 to 45,000 on the mountaintop. Portuguese traders and Jesuits lived in the city from the 1550s and once conspired together to unseat the manikongo Diogo I.

The Jagas sacked the city in 1568 and the church was burned, then rebuilt; in 1596, under Álvaro II, it became the cathedral of the new diocese of Angola and Congo. The name São Salvador first appears in the letters of Álvaro I. In 1678 the troops of the pretender Pedro III destroyed the city, which was abandoned, and the cathedral beside the kings' cemetery was left in ruins. In the eighteenth century people told of this ruined church, which Kongo people called Nkulumbimbi, that angels had built it overnight.
zh:
1648年来访的乔瓦尼·弗朗切斯科·达·罗马写道，马尼刚果的两层王宫是全刚果唯一的两层建筑。王宫所在的姆班扎刚果城是一座建在平顶山蒙戈·迪亚·刚果上的城，几条主要商路在这里交会；1491年最早抵达的葡萄牙人从刚果河口赶来，走了十天。葡萄牙大使写给里斯本的信里，把内城墙以内的范围比作埃武拉，这里可能是赤道以南非洲最大的城市。刚果人记得这座山是夺来的：卡本加酋长的领地在西边，有一处圣所，他是卢肯尼的盟友，却让人放心不下；两个世纪之后，他的后裔仍在每年的庆典上象征性地向这场征服发起挑战。

石造建筑随葡萄牙人而来。城里第一座石灰砌的建筑，是1491年由葡萄牙工匠带着刚果劳工盖起的一座教堂。后来的国王又在王家街区和葡萄牙人街区四周筑起五六米高的石墙，建起石造王宫和更多教堂；城里的重要建筑包括约十二座教堂和许多私人祈祷堂。1620年代的教会统计记载，城中及周围谷地每年施洗四千五百人，按这个数字推算，教区总人口约13万，山顶住着三万到四万五千人。葡萄牙商人和耶稣会士自1550年代起住在城中，还曾合谋推翻马尼刚果迪奥戈一世。

1568年雅加人攻破并洗劫了这座城，教堂被烧，后来重建；1596年在阿尔瓦罗二世任内，它成为新设的安哥拉与刚果教区的主座教堂。「圣萨尔瓦多」这个名字最早出现在阿尔瓦罗一世的书信里。1678年，僭位者佩德罗三世的军队摧毁了这座城市，城市被废弃，王陵旁边的主座教堂只剩残垣。18世纪有人说，这座废墟教堂刚果人称作库伦比姆比，是天使一夜之间建起来的。

en:
Kalanga oral tradition compresses the whole Torwa dynasty into one man, Chibundule, whose power was bound up in a braid worn like a horn on the crown of his head. The story goes that Changamire Dombo could only beat him by giving him a daughter or sister in marriage, who cut the braid. Chibundule is the praise name of Madabhale, the first ruler of Butua, and means the sounding of the war horn.

Khami grew up in the granite country west of the Zimbabwe Plateau, on the Khami River, as Great Zimbabwe declined. In the early fifteenth century traders opened a route along the Zambezi to the goldfields west of Great Zimbabwe, bypassing it, and a Leopard's Kopje chiefdom near the gold made Khami its seat: the Kingdom of Butua, ruled by the Torwa dynasty under its mambo, or king. The Portuguese called the country the Mother of Gold; the navigator Ahmad ibn Majid wrote of the 'King of Butua' in 1502, and in 1493 the mambo had sent the Mwenemutapa 4,000 cattle and copious gold.

Seven built-up areas housed the royal family along the ridge, commoners the open valley. The platforms were circular, sometimes terraced, rising two to seven metres, and encased in dry-stone walls laid without mortar. The great retaining wall of the Precipice Platform runs sixty-eight metres and stands six metres high, decorated along its whole length with a checkerboard pattern, and the walls of the Hill Complex are worked in chequer, herringbone and cord patterns.

Torwa power ended in a family quarrel. In the 1640s the mambo's brother, who had married into a powerful family of Shona-speaking Muslim traders called the Mwenye, forced the king into exile; a Portuguese prazo-holder and his army restored him in 1644, and the prazo-holder left soldiers in the capital but was killed on the road, after which they withdrew. The Hill Complex was probably destroyed in the conflict, its palace showing signs of fire. Dombo's Rozvi army conquered Butua around 1683 and did not occupy Khami, building Danamombe as their capital instead.
zh:
卡兰加口传把整个托尔瓦王朝压缩成奇本杜莱一个人，他的力量系于头顶那条像犄角一样的发辫。故事说，昌加米尔·多姆博奈何他不得，最后把一个女儿或姐妹嫁给他，由她剪去了发辫。奇本杜莱是布图阿开国君主马达巴莱的赞美名，意为战号吹响。

卡米城在津巴布韦高原以西的花岗岩地带、卡米河畔，大津巴布韦衰落之际兴起。15世纪初，商人开辟了一条沿赞比西河、绕过大津巴布韦直达其西面金矿的商路，靠近金矿的一个豹地文化酋长国以卡米为都：这就是托尔瓦王朝的曼博（国王）统治的布图阿王国。葡萄牙人把这个国家称作「黄金之母」；航海家艾哈迈德·伊本·马吉德在1502年记下了「布图阿之王」，1493年曼博曾送给穆韦内穆塔帕四千头牛和大量黄金。

山脊上七片建筑区住着王族，平民住在开阔的谷地里。台地呈圆形，有的垒成阶梯，高出地面二至七米，外面用不施灰浆的干砌石墙包边。峭壁台地的大挡土墙长六十八米、高六米，整面墙饰有棋盘格纹；山丘建筑群的墙上饰有棋盘纹、鱼骨纹和绳纹。

托尔瓦的统治结束于一场家族争端。1640年代，曼博之弟娶进说绍纳语的穆斯林商人望族姆文耶，靠岳家把国王赶出国土；一名葡萄牙普拉佐领主带兵送他复位，时在1644年，领主留在都城的士兵，在他途中被杀后撤走。山丘建筑群多半毁于这场冲突，宫殿留有火烧的痕迹。约1683年，多姆博的罗兹维军队征服了布图阿，没有占用卡米，而是另建达纳莫姆贝为都。

en:
The elite of Kilwa kept imported pots from Arabia and China as marks of status, and set them in niches built into their walls to be seen. The town covered the coral island of Kilwa Kisiwani. Settlers had lived there since the ninth century, in houses of wattle and daub; stone buildings appear around the thirteenth century, about when Kilwa took control of the gold trade at Sofala, and at its peak the town held more than 10,000 people. Local oral tradition says the island was sold to Ali bin Hasan, son of the king of Shiraz; coins bearing the name Ali bin al-Hasan have been found at Kilwa. When Ibn Battuta came in 1331 he called Kilwa one of the most beautiful cities in the world.

The Friday mosque anchored the town. Its northern prayer hall held sixteen bays and was one of the first mosques on the coast built without a courtyard; an inscription records 1269 as the start of work on its minaret. In the early fourteenth century Sultan al-Hasan ibn Sulaiman added the southern extension with its great dome. Ibn Battuta described the mosque as made entirely of wood, though excavation has since shown its stone walls predate the fourteenth century. Pots of coins bearing the name of Ali bin al-Hasan were found inside its walls.

On a bluff outside the town stood Husuni Kubwa, the sultan's palace and emporium, about 8,000 square metres of coral stone: a south court used for commerce, over a hundred rooms, an octagonal swimming pool, and a broad stairway leading down to a mosque on the beach. Most of the imported glazed pottery found there was Chinese celadon, including a Yuan flask dated to about 1300. Yet the palace was inhabited only briefly and abandoned before it was finished, and neither the Kilwa Chronicle nor the Portuguese accounts describe a comparable building. The Gereza fort, possibly Portuguese in origin, has the form of an Omani fort. In July 1505 the Portuguese under Francisco de Almeida besieged and burned the town, and many questions about its layout remain unanswered.
zh:
基尔瓦城的精英阶层把阿拉伯半岛和中国进口的陶瓷当作身份的标志，摆在墙上专门开出的壁龛里供人观看。城建在基尔瓦基西瓦尼这座珊瑚岛上。9世纪起岛上就有人定居，房屋都是枝条灰泥墙；石造建筑约在13世纪出现，大致就在基尔瓦控制索法拉黄金贸易的时候，到最兴盛时全城有一万多人。当地口传说，这座岛是卖给设拉子国王之子阿里·本·哈桑的；基尔瓦出土过铸有阿里·本·哈桑之名的钱币。1331年伊本·白图泰来到这里，称基尔瓦是世界上最美的城市之一。

星期五清真寺是全城的中心。北段礼拜厅有十六个开间，是东非海岸最早不带庭院的清真寺之一，一条铭文记下1269年为它的宣礼塔动工之年。14世纪初，苏丹哈桑·伊本·苏莱曼增建了带大穹顶的南段。伊本·白图泰说整座寺是木构的，但发掘证明石墙早于14世纪。墙体内还发现成罐的钱币，铸着阿里·本·哈桑的名字。

城外悬崖上立着胡苏尼库布瓦宫，苏丹的宫殿兼货栈，约八千平方米的珊瑚石建筑：一座用于商贸的南院、百余间房屋、八角游泳池，以及一道宽大石阶直下海滩上的清真寺。这里出土的进口釉陶以中国青瓷为主，其中有一件约1300年的元代瓷瓶。这座宫殿却只被短暂居住，尚未完工便遭废弃，《基尔瓦编年史》和葡萄牙人的记载都没有提到与它相当的建筑。格雷扎堡可能最初由葡萄牙人所建，现状是阿曼风格的堡垒。1505年7月，葡萄牙人在弗朗西斯科·德·阿尔梅达率领下围攻并焚毁了基尔瓦，城里的布局有许多问题没有答案。

en:
Harar Jugol is the walled old town of the Muslim city on Ethiopia's eastern plateau. In 1559 Nur ibn Mujahid, who had married the widow of Ahmad Gragn, left on a jihad to Fatagar. While he was away the Ethiopians under Ras Hamalmal broke into Harar and killed the last Walashma sultan, Barakat ibn Umar Din. Nur defeated and killed the Emperor Gelawdewos at Fatagar and brought his head back to Harar in triumph. The years after were hard: Oromo riders defeated his army at Hazalo, and Nur built a large wall around Harar, with five gates: Assum Bari in the north, Argobba Bari in the east, Suqutat Bari in the southeast, Badro Bari in the south and Asmadin Bari in the west. The five quarters of the old town carry the same names. The wall held, and the Oromo devastated only the lands around the city. Refugees crowded inside, and in the famines one sa'a, a measure of four handfuls, of sorghum cost 12 ashrafis and a cow more than 300. A plague that followed the second famine killed Nur in 1568.

Within the wall Harar is called the City of Saints. UNESCO counts 82 mosques in the old town, three of them from the tenth century, and 102 shrines. A semi-legendary chronicle, the Fath Madinat Harar, says the saint Abadir Umar ar-Rida founded the city with 405 other saints who came from Arabia. The old town centres on the square of Ferez Magala, and the Jami mosque is a work of the sixteenth century. Harari houses, the gey gar, stand in walled compounds built of local stone, and the main room has raised platforms for sitting and sleeping and niches in the wall, two of them kept for books, above all the Qur'an. Their layout is dated to 1754, under Emir Yusuf. The dynasty founded by Ali ibn Da'ud ruled Harar for two centuries. His successor Abdullah married five of his sons to Oromo women and so made peace with the Oromo. In 1761 Ahmad I built the minaret of the grand mosque, sharifs from Mecca moved to the town, and by 1789 the emirs were certainly minting their own coins.
zh:
哈勒尔要塞古城是埃塞俄比亚东部高原上这座穆斯林城市的带城墙老城。1559年，娶了艾哈迈德·格兰遗孀的努尔·伊本·穆贾希德出征法塔加尔。他不在时，哈马尔梅尔将军率领的埃塞俄比亚军队攻进哈勒尔，杀了瓦拉什马末代苏丹巴拉卡特·伊本·欧麦尔丁。努尔在法塔加尔击败并杀死皇帝加拉德沃斯，把他的头颅带回哈勒尔。此后几年很艰难：奥罗莫骑兵在哈扎洛击败了他的军队，努尔于是环绕哈勒尔筑起一道大城墙，开五座城门：北为阿苏姆门，东为阿尔戈巴门，东南为苏库塔特门，南为巴德罗门，西为阿斯马丁门。老城的五个坊用的也是这些名字。城墙挡住了奥罗莫人，他们只能蹂躏城周的乡野。难民涌入城内，饥荒中一萨阿（四把之量）高粱卖到十二个阿什拉菲，一头牛要三百多。第二次饥荒之后瘟疫来袭，1568年夺去了努尔的性命。

城墙之内的哈勒尔号称「圣徒之城」。联合国教科文组织统计老城有82座清真寺，其中3座始建于10世纪，另有102座圣徒墓。半传说的《哈勒尔城的开启》说，圣徒阿巴迪尔·奥马尔·里达带着另外405位圣徒从阿拉伯来到这里建城。老城以费雷兹马加拉广场为中心，聚礼清真寺是16世纪的建筑。哈勒尔人的住宅叫盖伊加尔，建在围墙环绕的院落里，用本地石头砌成；正房里有供坐卧的高台，墙上有壁龛，其中两个专放书籍，首先是《古兰经》。这种格局定于1754年，埃米尔优素福在位时。阿里·伊本·达乌德建立的王朝统治哈勒尔两个世纪。继任的阿卜杜拉让五个儿子娶了奥罗莫女子，以此与奥罗莫人讲和。1761年，艾哈迈德一世修建了大清真寺的宣礼塔，麦加的圣裔也迁居此城，到1789年，埃米尔们确已铸造自己的钱币。

en:
Ships trading between the North Sea and the Baltic had to sail round Jutland and through the Sound, a slow and dangerous passage made dearer by the Sound Dues. Lübeck found a partial answer at the end of the fourteenth century. On 22 July 1398 thirty barges carrying the first load of Lüneburg salt reached the town along the new Stecknitz Canal. Its man-made stretch was only 11.5 kilometres long, joining the little Stecknitz and Delvenau rivers, and 85 centimetres deep, with thirteen wooden locks at first and seventeen later. Salt moved along it for five hundred years, but seagoing ships still had to take the northern passage. Each bargee was allowed only one barge, so none could grow rich, and they stayed dependent on the Lübeck salt merchants.

In 1571 Duke Adolf I of Holstein-Gottorp planned a canal to join the Eider with Kiel and compete with the Stecknitz Canal for merchant traffic. The split of Schleswig-Holstein between king, dukes and joint rule blocked it, and the plan came up again in the 1600s under Christian IV without result. Only after the Treaty of Tsarskoye Selo in 1773 brought Holstein under the Danish crown could Christian VII's canal commission, led by Heinrich Carl von Schimmelmann, begin work. From 1777 to 1784 diggers followed the small Levensau from Holtenau, and six locks lifted ships over a divide about seven metres high. The cut was 34 kilometres long, and with the canalised Eider and its lakes the route to Tönning on the North Sea ran 173 kilometres. It was 28.7 metres wide and 3.45 deep, and passed ships of up to 140 tonnes, three days or more from sea to sea. In a little over a century about 300,000 ships crossed it.

The Eider Canal could not take the later warships, and the present 98-kilometre Kiel Canal, opened in 1895, reused much of its watercourse.
zh:
往来北海与波罗的海的商船，从前必须绕过日德兰半岛、取道厄勒海峡，航程又慢又险，还要缴纳海峡通行税。14世纪末，吕贝克找到了半截办法：1398年7月22日，三十艘驳船载着吕讷堡的第一批盐，沿新开的施泰克尼茨运河驶进了城。这条运河的人工段只有11.5公里，连通施泰克尼茨河与德尔韦瑙河两条小河，水深85厘米，起初有十三座木闸，后来增到十七座。盐在上面运了五百年，海船却仍旧得绕行北方水路。每名船夫只许拥有一条船，没人发得了财，始终依赖吕贝克的盐商。

1571年，荷尔斯泰因-戈托普公爵阿道夫一世计划开一条把艾德河与基尔连起来的运河，与施泰克尼茨运河争夺商船。石勒苏益格-荷尔斯泰因分属国王、公爵和共同统治，工程因此受阻；17世纪克里斯蒂安四世重提此议，也没有结果。直到1773年《皇村条约》让荷尔斯泰因并入丹麦王室，由海因里希·卡尔·冯·席梅尔曼主持的克里斯蒂安七世运河委员会才得以动工。1777至1784年，挖掘者沿莱文绍小河从霍尔腾瑙向西推进，六座船闸把船只抬过约七米高的分水岭。人工段长34公里，加上渠化的艾德河及沿途湖泊，到北海边滕宁的全程有173公里。河面宽28.7米、水深3.45米，只通过140吨以内的船，从海到海要三天以上。一百多年里，约有三十万艘次船只通过。

艾德运河容不下后来的军舰，1895年通航的新基尔运河长98公里，沿用了它的大部分河道。

en:
The floors of the chief halls of the Forbidden City were paved with 'golden bricks', baked specially in Suzhou and nearby prefectures. The Yongle Emperor moved his capital from Nanjing to Beijing, and work began in 1406 on a palace modelled on the old one at Nanjing; it was finished in 1420. More than a million workers took fourteen years. Whole logs of nanmu came from the forests of the southwest and were floated down the rivers, a log from Sichuan taking three to five years to reach Beijing, and marble blocks were cut in quarries near the city. Craftsmen such as the carpenter Kuai Xiang and the mason Lu Xiang worked on it.

The palace is a rectangle 961 metres by 753, with a moat 52 metres wide. Beijingers said that its corner towers had nine beams, eighteen pillars and seventy-two ridges, and by one legend the artisans, after taking a tower apart for repairs in the early Qing, could not put it back together until the master carpenter Lu Ban stepped in. South of the Meridian Gate lay the outer court of three great halls for state ceremonies, and north of it the inner court where the emperor and his household lived. The name takes 'purple' from the Purple Subtle Enclosure, the heavenly dwelling of the supreme god, and 'forbidden' from the palace walls. Tradition gives it 9,999 rooms.

The halls burned within months of opening: lightning in 1421 destroyed the three main halls. Fires in 1557 and 1597 took them again, and the second rebuilding lasted three decades. When Li Zicheng withdrew from Beijing in 1644 he set the palace on fire; only the Wuying Hall, a few other halls, the corner towers and the Huangji Gate escaped. The Qing then proclaimed the boy Shunzhi emperor there that October, and the regent Dorgon worked from the Wuying Hall. They renamed principal buildings to stress harmony rather than supremacy and added shamanist shrines. Yongzheng moved to the smaller Hall of Mental Cultivation out of respect for Kangxi's memory, and Qianlong built the Palace of Tranquil Longevity as his retirement home.
zh:
紫禁城主要大殿的地面铺着「金砖」，是专门在苏州及附近各府烧造的。永乐帝把国都从南京迁到北京，1406年动工，以南京故宫为蓝本营建，1420年落成。一百多万人干了十四年。整根的楠木取自西南的山林，顺江河漂运北上，从四川运到北京的一根要三到五年；大块大理石在京城附近的采石场开凿。木工蒯祥、石工陆祥等名匠都参与了营建。

紫禁城是一座南北961米、东西753米的矩形之城，护城河宽52米。北京人说它的角楼有「九梁十八柱七十二条脊」；相传清初角楼拆下修缮后，工匠怎么也拼不回去，直到鲁班出面才重新装好。午门以内，南面是三大殿组成的外朝，用于国家大典；北面是内廷，皇帝与家人居住。城名里的「紫」取自紫微垣，那是上天至尊的居所，「禁」则指宫城。相传城里有房屋九千九百九十九间。

大殿启用后几个月就遭了火：1421年雷击，三大殿尽毁。1557年和1597年两场大火又把它们烧掉，后一次重建拖了三十年。1644年李自成撤出北京时放火焚宫，只有武英殿、另几座殿宇、四角角楼和皇极门幸免。同年十月，清朝在这里宣布幼帝顺治登基，摄政王多尔衮在幸存的武英殿办公。清朝改了主要殿宇的名字，突出「和」而不是至高无上，又添了萨满教神堂。雍正出于对康熙的缅怀，搬到较小的养心殿居住；乾隆建宁寿宫，作为自己退位后的居所。

en:
The Grand Canal's main line met the Yangtze at Zhenjiang, and Nanjing lay up the river from it, so the city's own canals were side cuts. The newest was the Rouge Canal, begun in 1393 on the order of Zhu Yuanzhang in the hills of what is now Lishui, some seven kilometres from Shijiu Lake to the Qinhuai, to link the Taihu water system with Nanjing. It had to pass a ridge about five kilometres long. An old record says the workmen left the great rock standing as a bridge and cut a passage more than ten zhang wide beneath it for boats, and so it was called the Heaven-Made Bridge. There were two such bridges, and the northern one collapsed in 1571.

The first canal of this kind was far older. In 245 Sun Quan, lord of Wu, had the Pogang Canal cut from Jurong to Danyang with twelve weirs along it, so that boats from Wu and Kuaiji could reach his capital at Jianye without going out into the Yangtze at Jingkou. These are the earliest weirs recorded in Chinese texts: ramps up which men or oxen hauled the boats on ropes, with every vessel paying a toll. A few years earlier a city canal, the Yundu, had been dug to carry supplies to the granary behind the Taichu Palace. In 1403 the Yongle Emperor moved the capital from Nanjing to Beijing, which cost Nanjing its place as China's chief political centre, and the reopened Grand Canal favoured Suzhou over it. When Matteo Ricci went from Nanjing to Beijing by the canal in 1600, he was on his way to win the Wanli Emperor's support.
zh:
大运河南京段所在的南京不在运河干线上：干线在镇江入长江，南京在江的上游，所以城里城外的河渠都是支河。最晚的一条是胭脂河，1393年由朱元璋下令开凿，在今溧水一带，从石臼湖到秦淮河长七公里多，把太湖水系和南京连起来。河道要穿过一道五公里长的山岗。记载说，工匠把巨石留作桥，从石中凿出十余丈宽的孔洞通船，所以叫「天生桥」。这样的桥共有两座，北桥在1571年崩塌。

这类河渠的先例要早得多。245年，吴主孙权下令开凿破岗渎，从句容到云阳（今丹阳），沿途设了十二道埭，吴郡、会稽的船可以不出京口入长江，直达都城建业。这是文献中最早的堰埭记录：人或牛用绳索把船拖过斜坡，过坝的船都要纳税。几年前，吴人还开了城内的运渎，把物资运到太初宫后的仓城。1403年，永乐帝把都城从南京迁到北京，南京失去了全国政治中心的地位，重新通航的大运河又让苏州占了先。1600年，利玛窦从南京沿运河去北京，为的是争取万历帝的支持。

en:
The pagoda of the Great Bao'en Temple was nine storeys of white glazed brick, 78.2 metres high, and could be seen from the Yangtze dozens of li away. It stood behind the temple halls outside Nanjing's southern gate, on ground said to have been holy since the third century, when the monk Kang Senghui brought relics and Sun Quan built the Jianchu Temple and an Ashoka pagoda, the first of their kind in Jiangnan. After a monk burned the old Tianxi Temple to the ground, the Yongle Emperor ordered it rebuilt in 1412 to palace standards, to repay his parents, the Hongwu Emperor and Empress Ma. The work took nineteen years, over a hundred thousand labourers and about 2.5 million taels. Piles were driven into the ground, charred in place, rammed down with iron-wheeled stones and sealed with cinnabar against damp and insects.

The pagoda was completed around 1428 and the whole temple by 1431, with Zheng He, the admiral then holding the Nanjing garrison, supervising. Its arch-frames were built of five-coloured glazed tiles moulded with lions, white elephants and flying sheep, and its finial was set with gold, silver and jewels. A hundred and fifty-two wind chimes hung at the eaves, and 140 lamps burned every night on 64 jin of oil. Tradition held that every glazed piece was fired in triplicate, one set for the tower and two buried underground as replacements. The playwright Tang Xianzu climbed it and wrote a poem about riding home and watching its lamps. Late in the Jiajing reign fire swept the temple and left only the pagoda, a meditation hall and the kitchen standing.

European merchants, travellers and missionaries called it the 'porcelain tower of Nanjing', set it beside the Colosseum, the Catacombs of Alexandria and the Leaning Tower of Pisa, and counted it among the wonders of the medieval world. Johan Nieuhof, steward of the Dutch East India Company embassy of 1655-1657, whose book carried about 150 illustrations drawn from life, was among the first Europeans to see it. In 1801 lightning knocked off the top four storeys, and they were soon restored.
zh:
大报恩寺琉璃塔九层，高78.2米，塔身贴白瓷色琉璃砖，数十里外的长江上也能望见。塔立在南京城南门外，殿宇之后，这块地方据说自3世纪起便是佛地：僧人康僧会带来舍利，孙权为他建起建初寺和阿育王塔，这是江南塔寺的开端。天禧寺被僧人放火烧得片木无存，1412年，永乐帝下令按皇宫的标准重建，为的是报答父亲朱元璋和母亲孝慈高皇后马氏的恩德。工程历时19年，征调工役十多万人，耗银约250万两。地基先钉入木桩，纵火焚成木炭，用铁轮滚石夯实，再铺一层朱砂防潮杀虫。

塔约在1428年竣工，全寺到1431年完工，由时任南京守备的郑和督造。塔的拱门门框用五色琉璃砖砌成，塑着狮子、白象和飞羊，塔刹镶嵌金银珠宝。檐角挂着152个风铃，140盏长明灯夜夜不熄，一夜耗油64斤。相传每块琉璃构件都一式烧三份，一份建塔，另两份埋入地下备换。剧作家汤显祖登过此塔，写下一首诗，说的是骑马归去时回望塔灯。嘉靖末年寺中再遭大火，只有塔、禅殿和香积厨存了下来。

欧洲的商人、游客和传教士称它为「南京瓷塔」，把它同罗马斗兽场、亚历山大地下墓室和比萨斜塔相提并论，列为中古世界奇观之一。约翰·纽霍夫随荷兰东印度公司1655至1657年的使团经行此地，他任使团管事，所著游记附有约150幅写生图，是最早见到此塔的欧洲人之一。1801年，雷火击毁塔顶四层，不久又修复了。

en:
Wu kings made Suzhou their capital and cut canals across the plain around it, and under the Ming, with the Grand Canal open to Beijing again, it became the greatest economic centre in China. The Korean official Choe Bu, shipwrecked and sent north along the canal in 1488, took Hangzhou for a feeder of Suzhou's market rather than a rival. A stone map of 1229, the Pingjiang Tu, shows the Song city with its main waterways mostly running beside its streets; it is the oldest surviving city plan in China. Outside the Fengmen Gate the canal passes the mouth of Lake Dantai under the Precious Belt Bridge, 53 arches and 318 metres of stone. Tradition says the prefect Wang Zhongshu gave his own belt to pay for it, and the bridge took its name from the gift. It carried the towpath, so it has no solid parapet and trackers hauled from the bridge itself. In 1793 John Barrow of the Macartney embassy saw it and noted that its central arches stand higher than the rest.

West of the old city, at Maple Bridge, Hanshan Temple faces the old canal. Tradition says the monks Hanshan and Shide came from Mount Tiantai to be abbots there in the Tang, and the temple took the name of Hanshan. Zhang Ji's poem on mooring at Maple Bridge and hearing the temple's midnight bell from the boat made it known across East Asia. In the Jiajing reign the monk Benji cast a great bronze bell and built a bell tower. In 825 the poet Bai Juyi, newly made prefect, cut the Shantang Canal from the Changmen Gate to Tiger Hill and built a road along its north bank, seven li in all. On his third southern tour, in 1762, the Qianlong Emperor walked the Seven-li Shantang and wrote 'Finding the view at Shantang'. He was so fond of the street that back in Beijing he had a Suzhou Street built along the back lake of the Summer Palace in its likeness.
zh:
大运河苏州段所在的苏州，原是吴王的都城，吴王在周围的平原上开凿了许多河道。到了明代，大运河重新通到北京，苏州成了中国最大的经济中心。1488年，遇风漂流的朝鲜官员崔溥沿运河北上，认为杭州是苏州市场的补给地，而不是对手。1229年刻成的《平江图》石碑画出了宋代平江府城，城里主要河道多与街道平行，它是中国现存最早的城市平面图。葑门外，运河经过澹台湖口，从宝带桥下流过，桥长318米，共53孔。相传刺史王仲舒捐出自己的宝带助成工费，桥因此得名。它是纤道桥，桥面不设挡板，纤夫就在桥上拉纤。1793年，马戛尔尼使团的巴罗见到此桥，记下它中间几孔比其余的高。

老城以西的枫桥，寒山寺的大门正对古运河。相传高僧寒山和拾得从天台山来此作住持，寺名取自寒山。张继写自己泊舟枫桥、在船上听到寒山寺夜半钟声，这首《枫桥夜泊》使寺名传遍东亚。嘉靖年间，僧人本寂铸了一口大铜钟，又建起钟楼。825年，诗人白居易新任苏州刺史，开凿山塘河，从阊门到虎丘，河北修路，合称山塘街，长约七里。1762年乾隆帝第三次南巡，游览七里山塘，亲笔写下「山塘寻胜」。他对这条街十分喜爱，回京后在颐和园后湖，仿照山塘的样子修了一条苏州街。

en:
In 1457 the Teutonic Order's own mercenaries sold Malbork Castle. The Bohemian commander held it in pledge for unpaid wages, and he gave it to Casimir IV of Poland for 190,000 florins, about 660 kilograms of gold. The castle covers nearly 21 hectares on the Nogat, the river link between the Vistula delta and the Baltic. The Order began the brick convent castle around 1280, and when Siegfried von Feuchtwangen moved its seat here from Venice in 1309 it became the capital of the monastic state and grew into three linked castles. The High Castle held the dormitories and St Mary's church, with St Anne's chapel beneath it as the burial place of the grand masters. The Middle Castle held the Grand Master's Palace, the infirmary and the Great Refectory, the largest secular room in the Order's state. The Lower Castle held the Karwan, an armoury and wagon house, and the farm buildings. Dry moats and towers separated the wards, and the castle once housed some three thousand brothers in arms.

Chronicles say that during the siege after Grunwald a traitor hung a red flag from a window of the Summer Refectory as a signal to the besiegers, who aimed an 80-kilogram cannonball at the single pillar that carried the vault while the Order's leaders sat inside. The ball missed it, by six centimetres according to later calculations.

In 1444 this was still the capital of a state weakened since Grunwald. Polish and Prussian forces besieged it from 27 February 1454, but an epidemic and the news of the defeat at Konitz broke the siege before the walls did; unpaid wages decided it three years later. Under the Polish crown the Great Refectory hosted royal feasts, and kings stayed in the Grand Master's Palace on their way to Gdansk. Swedish troops took the castle after a month's siege in 1656 and held it until 1660. After the First Partition the Prussians turned the High Castle into barracks and pulled down nearly all its Gothic vaults, made a riding hall of the Great Refectory and a cloth factory of the palace. In 1794 David Gilly surveyed the castle for possible demolition; his son Friedrich's engravings, published from 1799, helped turn opinion toward preservation.
zh:
1457年，条顿骑士团自己雇来的佣兵把马尔堡城堡卖掉了。波希米亚统领因骑士团欠饷而把城堡扣作抵押，最后以19万弗罗林、约合660千克黄金的价钱，把它交给波兰国王卡齐米日四世。城堡占地近21公顷，坐落在诺加特河畔，这条河把维斯瓦三角洲同波罗的海连在一起。约1280年，骑士团开始修建砖砌修道院城堡；1309年，齐格弗里德·冯·福希特旺根把骑士团驻地从威尼斯迁来，这里成为修道骑士国家的都城，并逐渐扩成三座相连的城堡。高堡里有宿舍和圣玛利亚教堂，教堂之下的圣安娜礼拜堂是历任大团长的安葬处。中堡有大团长宫、病坊和大餐厅，大餐厅是骑士团国家里最大的世俗厅堂。下堡有卡尔万（军械库兼车库）和农庄建筑。干壕和塔楼把各堡区隔开，城堡里曾住着约三千名兄弟战士。

编年史记载，格伦瓦尔德之战后的围城中，有个叛徒在夏餐厅的窗外挂出一面红旗，给围城者发信号；围城者朝撑着整座拱顶的那根独柱发射一枚80千克的炮弹，当时骑士团的首脑们就坐在厅里。炮弹没有击中，据后人推算只偏了六厘米。

1444年，这里仍是格伦瓦尔德战役后国力转弱的国家的都城。1454年2月27日起，波兰和普鲁士联军围攻城堡，但军中疫病流行，加上科尼茨战败的消息传来，攻城战在城墙未破时瓦解；三年后，真正决定归属的是欠饷。波兰王冠统治时期，大餐厅举办王家宴会，国王前往格但斯克时住在大团长宫。1656年，瑞典军队围城一个月后攻占，一直占到1660年。第一次瓜分之后，普鲁士人把高堡改成兵营，拆掉了几乎全部哥特式拱顶，把大餐厅改作马术场，把宫殿改成织布厂。1794年，大卫·吉里勘查结构，评估是否拆毁；他的儿子弗里德里希绘制的版画从1799年起陆续出版，使舆论转向保护。

en:
A city of barely 10,000 people began the church that was meant to carry the highest spire of any church. Ulm Minster was a citizens' church, paid for by the town rather than a bishop or an abbey. The old parish church stood outside the walls, and the burghers had been cut off from it during Emperor Charles IV's siege. On 30 June 1377 Mayor Ludwig Krafft laid the first stone of a new church inside the walls, and Heinrich Parler drew a hall church with three naves of roughly equal height. Ulrich von Ensingen, who had worked at Prague and Strasbourg, later took over and dreamed of a main tower more than 150 metres high. To balance it the nave had to rise well above the choir, which turned the hall church into a basilica. The minster was consecrated under a temporary roof in 1405.

The great tower nearly brought the church down. The vaults were of unequal height but equally wide, and in 1492 they threatened to bend the piers and bring the building down. Burkhard Engelberg of Augsburg saved it by strengthening the west tower's foundations, demolishing the heavy aisle vaults and setting slim piers under lighter ones, though the north wall of the nave was left out of true by up to 27 centimetres. In a named vote in 1530 seven eighths of Ulm's full burghers chose the Reformation, and in 1531 iconoclasts removed more than sixty altars. An old account says that, unable to lift the great organ, they tied ropes and chains round it and had horses drag it down. The minster was never a bishop's seat, so for all its size it is not a cathedral. Internal strife, the new faith and plain want of money stopped the works in 1543, with the main tower at roughly 100 metres and the choir towers at about 32. In 1817 the medieval frescoes were painted over in light grey, to show the minster in the plain, sublime dress that the old German building spirit was said to demand.
zh:
一座不到一万人的城市，动手建一座要配上全世界教堂中最高尖塔的教堂。乌尔姆大教堂是市民的教堂，出钱的是全城百姓，不是主教，也不是修道院。老教区教堂立在城墙之外，查理四世皇帝围城时，市民被切断了去教堂的路。1377年6月30日，市长路德维希·克拉夫特为城墙内的新教堂奠基，海因里希·帕勒设计了三座殿身大致等高的厅堂式教堂。后来接手主持工程的乌尔里希·冯·恩辛根曾在布拉格和斯特拉斯堡工作，他梦想着一座高逾150米的主塔。为与高塔相称，中殿必须远高于唱诗席，厅堂式教堂就此改成巴利卡式。1405年，教堂在临时屋顶下祝圣启用。

这座巨塔险些压垮整座教堂。拱顶高低不一，却同样宽阔，1492年眼看要把支柱压弯，使整座建筑倒塌。奥格斯堡的布克哈特·恩格尔贝格加固西塔地基，拆去沉重的侧廊拱顶，另立一排排细柱承托较轻的新拱顶，这才保住建筑，只是中殿北墙偏离垂直最多27厘米。1530年的记名投票中，八分之七的乌尔姆正式市民选择宗教改革，1531年毁像者搬走了六十多座祭坛。一份旧记载说，毁像者抬不动大管风琴，就用绳索和铁链缠住它，再套上马把它拖倒。这座教堂从来不是主教的驻地，所以尽管宏大，也不是主教座堂。内部纷争、改宗和纯粹的缺钱使工程在1543年停下，主塔只修到约100米，唱诗席双塔各约32米。1817年，中世纪壁画被整片涂成浅灰，据说这样才显出古德意志营造精神所要求的朴素崇高的样子。

en:
The moai are whole figures, not heads. Most were carved between 1250 and 1500 from the soft volcanic tuff of Rano Raraku, and nearly four hundred are still in and around the quarry, many buried to the shoulders by the slope, which is why people picture them as heads alone. A moai has no legs, heavy brows, long ears, thin pouting lips and a long nose whose nostrils curl like fish hooks. The head makes up three-eighths of the figure, in keeping with the Polynesian belief in the sanctity of a chief's head. Set on an ahu, a statue faced inland over the villages as the 'living face' of a deified ancestor, and its eye sockets are thought to have held white coral eyes with pupils of black obsidian or red scoria. The later figures wore a pukao, a cylinder of red scoria from the Puna Pau quarry that stands for a chief's topknot: the larger the statue, the more mana the chief who commissioned it was held to have. The tallest one raised, Paro, was nearly ten metres high and weighed some eighty tonnes. Island tradition says the leader Tu'u ko Iho brought the statues and made them walk to their platforms. The quarry looks abandoned in a hurry, with stone tools lying about and finished moai outside waiting to be moved.

When Jacob Roggeveen came ashore on Easter Sunday in 1722, the statues still gazed inland across the clan lands. The Spanish expedition of 1770 was amazed by the 'standing idols', all of them erect; four years later James Cook reported that some had been toppled. The toppling was an attempt by rival groups to destroy the mana in each other's statues, and they broke the figures in the fall to make sure they were dead. Oral histories tell of a clan pushing down a single moai in the night, and others speak of the earth shaking. Some statues fell forward with their faces hidden and their necks broken, others off the back of the platform. In the end none stood on an ahu; only the partly buried figures on the outer slopes of Rano Raraku were left.
zh:
摩艾石像是整尊的石像，不只是头。多数在1250年至1500年间用拉诺拉拉库松软的火山凝灰岩雕成，采石场内外还留着近四百尊，许多被坡上的土埋到肩膀，人们才以为它们只有头。摩艾没有腿，浓眉长耳，薄唇前噘，长长的鼻子，鼻孔弯成鱼钩状。头占整尊石像的八分之三，因为在波利尼西亚观念里，酋长的头是神圣的。立在阿胡上的石像脸朝内陆，望着村落，是神化祖先的「活的面孔」；据信它们深陷的眼眶里嵌着白珊瑚做的眼睛，瞳仁用黑曜石或红色火山渣。较晚的石像头顶戴着普卡奥，那是取自普纳保采石场的红色火山渣圆柱，象征酋长的发髻：石像越大，立像的酋长被认为拥有的神力越大。已立起的最高一尊叫帕罗，近十米高，约重八十吨。岛上的传统说，首领图乌·科·伊霍把石像带了来，让它们自己走到石台上。采石场像匆忙中停了工，石制工具散落在地上，雕好的摩艾立在场外，等着被运走。

1722年复活节那天，雅各布·罗赫芬登岛时，石像仍面朝内陆，望着各氏族的土地。1770年西班牙远征队惊叹于这些「站立的神像」，当时它们全都立着；四年后詹姆斯·库克报告说，有些已被推倒。推倒石像，是对立的集团想毁掉对方石像里的神力，推倒时还要摔断它们，确保它们「死透」。岛民的口述里，有氏族夜里推倒了一尊摩艾，也有人说是大地在摇晃。有的石像向前扑倒，脸被压住，脖子摔断，有的从石台后面掉下去。最后阿胡上再没有一尊立着，只剩拉诺拉拉库外坡上那些半埋的石像。

en:
Pohnpeian legend says that Nan Madol was raised by twin sorcerers, Olisihpa and Olosohpa, who came by canoe from a mythical western land looking for a place to build an altar to Nahnisohn Sahpw, the god of agriculture. After several false starts they built it off Temwen Island, and in the story they levitated the huge stones with the help of a flying dragon. Carbon dating puts the start of the great basalt building at about 1180, with the stone thought to come from a volcanic plug on the far side of Pohnpei; how it crossed the island is unknown, and rafts have been suggested without proof. The core, 1.5 by 0.5 kilometres, holds some ninety-two artificial islets of stone and coral fill, bordered by tidal canals, and the name Nan Madol means 'within the intervals'. Islet-building itself began in the eighth or ninth century.

The Saudeleur dynasty ruled Pohnpei from here. Tradition says its founders ruled kindly but their successors made ever heavier demands, and commoners owed the ruler frequent tributes of fruit and fish. The royal mortuary islet, Nandauwas, was built for the first Saudeleur, with walls 5.5 to 7.5 metres high around a central tomb, while the fifty-eight islets of Madol Powe in the northeast formed the mortuary sector, most of them holding priests' dwellings. Probably no more than a thousand people lived on the islets, and the Saudeleur required rival chiefs to live there rather than in their home districts, where they were harder to watch. Nan Madol had no fresh water or food of its own, so both came by boat, delivered first to Peiniot and later to the closer islet of Usennamw. Around 1628 Isokelekel, a semi-legendary invader, overthrew the Saudeleur and began the era of the nahnmwarki chiefs. They lived at Nan Madol but had to gather their own water and grow their own food, which is thought to have led them to move back to their home districts, though other explanations, such as a sharp fall in population, have been offered.
zh:
波纳佩传说，南马都尔是一对孪生巫师奥利西帕和奥洛索帕建起的。兄弟俩乘独木舟从传说中的西方之地而来，想找个地方为农业之神纳尼索恩·萨普筑一座祭坛，几经失败，最后在泰蒙岛外建成了祭坛。故事里，他们借一条飞龙之力，让巨石腾空而起。碳-14测定显示，大规模的玄武岩营建约始于1180年，石料据信取自波纳佩岛另一端的火山栓，怎样运过岛来不得而知，有人猜是木筏，但没有证据。1.5公里长、0.5公里宽的核心区里约有九十二座石块和珊瑚填筑的人工小岛，岛间是潮汐运河，「南马都尔」一名的意思是「在间隔之中」。人工小岛的修筑本身始于八、九世纪。

绍德雷尔王朝从这里统治全岛。传统说法是，开国的几代统治者宽厚，后继者的要求越来越重，平民须经常向统治者进献水果和鱼。王陵所在的南道瓦斯岛为第一代绍德雷尔而建，5.5至7.5米高的石墙围着中央墓室；东北部的马多尔波韦殡葬区有58座小岛，大多是祭司的住处。岛上住人大概不超过一千，绍德雷尔还要求各部落的对手首领住在这里，不得留在本土，以便监视。南马都尔自己没有淡水，也不出粮食，二者都靠船运来，先交到佩尼奥特岛，后来改在更近的乌森南姆岛交割。约1628年，半传说的入侵者伊索克勒克推翻绍德雷尔王朝，开启南姆瓦尔基首领的时代。这些首领住在南马都尔，却得自己取水、自己种地，据认为这使他们陆续搬回各自的本土地区，不过也有人提出别的解释，比如人口锐减。

en:
Rajendra I made the kings he had defeated send pots of Ganges water and pour them into the temple well at his new capital, named Cholagangam, and took the title Gangaikonda, the Chola who seized the Ganges. The temple he completed there, at Gangaikonda Cholapuram in 1035, is one of three granite Shiva temples called the Great Living Chola Temples, raised within eighty kilometres of one another in the Kaveri country.

The oldest, at Thanjavur, was built for his father Rajaraja I and finished around 1010. Its vimana climbs thirteen narrowing storeys, its finial was once sheathed in gold, and the passage wall carries 81 of the 108 dance postures of the Natya Shastra. The son's tower is smaller, but his is reckoned the finer work. The third, the Airavatesvara temple at Darasuram, was finished in 1166 under Rajaraja II. Its front hall is carved as a stone chariot on wheels, and the carved steps of its porch are the 'singing steps', which give out musical notes; a legend carved within says Airavata, Indra's white elephant, recovered his pure colour bathing in the temple tank, and the shrine takes its name from him.

The centuries after the Cholas were hard on all three. At Gangaikonda Cholapuram the palaces and the other temples of the capital were destroyed and only Rajendra's stands; at Darasuram the seven streets and seven courts named in the inscriptions shrank to a single court. The cause is unclear: one view blames the Pandyas in the late thirteenth century, another the armies of Malik Kafur, who raided the Tamil country for Delhi in 1311. After Vijayanagara defeated the Madurai sultanate in 1378 the temples returned to Hindu kings, and some twenty inscriptions record gifts from later Cholas, Pandyas and Vijayanagara. At Thanjavur the Nayaks of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries added the shrines of Murugan, Parvati and Nandi, and fortified walls were built around the temple after the sixteenth century. The Maratha rulers of Thanjavur, who held the city from the late seventeenth century, kept the Big Temple well maintained.
zh:
拉金德拉一世命被征服的各国送来一罐罐恒河水，倾入新都神庙中名叫「朱罗恒河」的圣井，自己取号「甘加贡达·朱兰」，意为夺得恒河的朱罗王。他在甘加贡达乔拉普兰建成的这座神庙，1035年落成，是朱罗王朝大神庙群三座花岗岩湿婆神庙之一；三庙在高韦里河流域，彼此相距不到八十公里。

最早的一座在坦焦尔，为他的父亲罗茶罗乍一世所建，约1010年落成：维马纳塔十三层逐层收分，宝顶原包金箔，回廊壁上刻着《舞论》一百零八种舞姿中的八十一种。儿子的塔身略小，雕工却被认为更精。第三座艾拉瓦特斯瓦拉神庙在达拉苏拉姆，1166年罗茶罗乍二世时建成，前殿雕成带轮的石战车，门廊上雕饰的台阶称作「音乐台阶」，踏上去会发出乐音；庙内刻着一则传说：因陀罗的白象艾拉瓦塔在圣池沐浴后恢复了洁白的肤色，神庙便以它为名。

朱罗王朝之后的几个世纪，三座神庙都很艰难。甘加贡达乔拉普兰都城里的宫殿和其他神庙都被毁，只剩拉金德拉所建的这一座；达拉苏拉姆铭文里记载的七街七进，也缩成仅存的一进院落。原因不明：一说是13世纪后期的潘地亚人所为，另一说是1311年为德里远征泰米尔之地的马利克·卡富尔的军队。1378年毗奢耶那伽罗攻灭马巴尔苏丹国后，各庙回到印度教君王手中，约二十条铭文记录了后来的朱罗、潘地亚和毗奢耶那伽罗君主的施舍。在坦焦尔，16、17世纪的纳亚克统治者添建了穆卢干、帕尔瓦蒂和南迪神殿，16世纪以后大庙四周又筑起设防的围墙。17世纪后期起统治坦焦尔的马拉塔君主，一直把这座大庙维护得很好。

en:
Before the Golden Temple there was a pool in what was probably jungle beside a caravan road, next to a tree called the Dukh Bhanjani Ber, 'the suffering remover'. Sikh tradition tells how Rajani brought her leper husband to the pool, and the water cured him. The third guru, Amar Das, chose the ground. Ram Das, the fourth, acquired it (by one account for 700 rupees from the village of Tung), and finished the pool as the centre of the new town of Ramdaspur. His son Arjan built the brick shrine, finished in 1589, lower than the ground around it so that worshippers go down to enter, with a single causeway to the sanctum. A later tradition says he invited the Sufi saint Mian Mir of Lahore to lay the foundation stone. In 1604 Arjan placed the Adi Granth in the shrine.

Arjan was arrested on Jahangir's order and tortured to death in 1606. His son Hargobind founded the Akal Takht, the eternal throne, in front of the causeway, as a seat for ceremonial, spiritual and worldly affairs. The police commissioner Masse Khan occupied it and turned it into an entertainment hall with dancing girls, until Sikhs killed him inside in 1740. In 1757 Ahmad Shah Durrani had waste and the entrails of slaughtered cows thrown into the pool. When he returned in 1762 he had the temple blown up with gunpowder, and the Sikhs came back and celebrated Diwali in the ruins. On 1 December 1764 Baba Gurbaksh Singh and 29 other Sikhs fought a last stand against the Afghan army and were killed, and Durrani destroyed the temple for the third time. Jassa Singh Ahluwalia collected donations, and a new gateway, causeway and sanctum were finished in 1776.

In 1802 Ranjit Singh took Amritsar from the Bhangi misl, paid homage at the temple and announced that he would rebuild it in marble and gold. He gave gilded copper panels for the roof, worth 500,000 rupees, and the first was set on the shrine in 1803. The temple was renovated in marble and copper in 1809.
zh:
金庙（哈曼迪尔寺）建起之前，这里是商队路旁一处多半是丛林的水塘，塘边长着一棵名叫杜赫·班贾尼·贝尔的枣树，意为「消除苦难者」。锡克传说，拉贾尼带着患麻风的丈夫来到水塘，丈夫洗浴后痊愈。第三代古鲁阿马尔·达斯选定了这块地。第四代古鲁拉姆·达斯取得了这块地（一说用七百卢比从通村买下），把圣池修成新城拉姆达斯布尔的中心。他的儿子阿尔琼用砖砌起谒师所，1589年竣工，寺基比四周地面低，信众要拾级而下才能入寺，只有一条长堤通向圣殿。后世传说，他邀请拉合尔的苏菲圣人米安·米尔为寺奠基。1604年，阿尔琼把《阿底·格兰特》供入寺中。

阿尔琼被贾汉吉尔下令逮捕，1606年遭酷刑处死。其子哈果滨在长堤前建起永恒王座（阿卡尔塔赫特），作为处理礼仪、宗教和世俗事务的所在。警察长官马斯·汗占据此寺，把它变成有舞女陪伴的娱乐场所，直到1740年被锡克人杀死在寺内。1757年，艾哈迈德沙·杜兰尼命人把污物和被宰牛只的内脏倒进圣池。1762年他重返，下令用火药炸毁神殿，锡克人回到废墟中，点灯庆祝排灯节。1764年12月1日，巴巴·古尔巴克什·辛格和另外29名锡克人与阿富汗大军死战到底，全部阵亡，杜兰尼第三次毁掉了这座寺。雅萨·辛格·阿卢瓦利亚募款，新的门楼、长堤和圣殿于1776年完工。

1802年，兰季德·辛格从邦吉米斯尔手中夺取阿姆利则，在寺前致敬，宣布要用大理石和黄金重修。他捐出镀金铜面板用作屋顶，价值五十万卢比，第一块于1803年装上殿身。1809年，寺庙用大理石和铜重修完毕。

en:
Tradition says that in the fifteenth century the Koli headman Ram Patil drove tall timber piles into a rock island off the fishing village of Rajapuri on the Konkan coast, making a medhekot, a wooden stockade where his people could sleep safe from pirates, with leave from the Nizam's officer. Once safe he stopped heeding that officer, who sent Piram Khan against him. Piram Khan anchored his boats in the creek as if he were a liquor merchant and sent casks of it to Ram Patil as gifts; that night, while the Kolis lay drunk, he landed his troops and cut them down.

The name Janjira comes from the Arabic jazira, an island, and the fort's older name was Jazire Mehrub. Piram Khan's successor Burhan Khan won the Nizam's leave to build a strong fort, and the present walls are said to be his work. They carry nineteen high bastions and more than five hundred cannon, among them the long-range Kalal Bangdi. The main gate faces east, with a second gate inside it. Beside it a carved tiger grips four elephants in its paws and a fifth in its tail: Burhan Khan's boast, the Marathi account says, that others might be elephants but he was a tiger too.

Its lords were the Siddis, seamen of Abyssinian origin whom the coast called Habshi. Two hundred sailors from Janjira were with the Ottoman fleet that reached Aceh in 1539, according to Fernao Mendes Pinto, and Ottoman records say Janjira mariners helped rout a Portuguese fleet off Yemen in 1587. Shivaji could not scale the walls, and his son Sambhaji tried to tunnel in until a Mughal attack on his capital pulled him away; the Marathas built Padmadurg a few kilometres off to watch the island. In April 1736 Chimaji Appa and Nanaji Surve fell on the Siddi camp near Rewas, and 1,500 Siddis died, among them their leader Siddi Sat. The peace that September left the Siddis Janjira, Gowalkot and Anjanvel; Tulaji Angre took the two mainland forts in 1745, and only the island stayed in Siddi hands.
zh:
相传15世纪，科利人头领拉姆·帕蒂尔在康坎海岸拉杰普里渔村外海的一座岩岛上打下高大木桩，围成木栅寨梅德科特，让族人能躲开海盗安睡，据点经尼扎姆沙王朝官员的许可而建。寨子一安稳，拉姆·帕蒂尔就不再听那名官员的话，官员便派皮拉姆汗去收拾他。皮拉姆汗把船泊进河口，佯装酒商，又送上几桶酒作礼物；当夜科利人醉倒，他派兵登岸，大肆砍杀。

穆鲁德-金吉拉要塞的「金吉拉」来自阿拉伯语jazira，意为岛屿；要塞旧称贾吉雷·梅赫鲁布。皮拉姆汗的继任者布尔汗汗得到尼扎姆沙的许可，修起坚固的要塞，现存的城墙据说出自他手。城墙列着十九座高墩台、五百多门火炮，远射程的「卡拉尔·班格迪」就在其中。正门朝东，门内还有第二道门；门边雕着一头老虎，四爪各按住一头象，尾巴卷起第五头。马拉地语资料说，这是布尔汗汗的夸口：别人尽可以做象，他也是虎。

岛上的主人是西迪人，来自阿比西尼亚的水手，海岸上称他们哈布舍。据葡萄牙作家费尔南·门德斯·平托记载，1539年抵达亚齐的奥斯曼舰队里有两百名金吉拉水手；奥斯曼的记录则称，1587年奥斯曼人与金吉拉的船队在也门外海击溃了一支葡萄牙舰队。希瓦吉攻不上城墙，他的儿子桑巴吉想挖地道潜入，被莫卧儿军进攻都城而调走。马拉塔人又在几公里外的岩礁上修起帕德马杜格堡，监视这座岛。1736年4月，奇马吉·阿帕与纳纳吉·苏尔韦突袭雷瓦斯附近的西迪营地，一千五百名西迪人丧命，首领西迪·萨特也在其中。当年9月议和，西迪人只剩金吉拉、高瓦尔科特和安詹韦尔三处；1745年图拉吉·安格雷夺占陆上两堡，最后留在西迪人手里的只有这座岛。

en:
The Kashi Vishwanath Temple houses Vishveshvara, the Shiva of Varanasi, and its lingam is believed to be the first of the twelve jyotirlingas to manifest itself, Shiva appearing as a column of light. According to the legend, Brahma and Vishnu were arguing over which of them was supreme when Shiva appeared as a column with neither beginning nor end. Vishnu, taking the form of a boar, tracked it beneath the ground and admitted he could not find its source; Brahma, a swan scouring the heavens, claimed falsely to have found the summit, and Shiva cut off his fifth head and cursed him to go without reverence. Hindu scripture makes Vishveshvara king over the other gods of Varanasi and its people. His lingam stands sixty centimetres high in a silver altar, and a visit to the temple and a bath in the Ganges are believed to set a pilgrim on the path to moksha.

North of the shrine lies the Gyan Vapi, the Well of Wisdom, which carries the temple's best-known story. In 1669 Aurangzeb ordered the temple demolished and had the Gyanvapi Mosque built in its place. It is said that the chief priest jumped into the well clasping the jyotirlinga, to save it from the invaders. Hindu pilgrims went on visiting the remnants of the temple.

Maratha rulers twice tried to rebuild on the old ground. In 1742 Malhar Rao Holkar planned to demolish the mosque and rebuild the temple, but the plan came to nothing, partly because the Nawab of Awadh intervened; in 1750 the maharaja of Jaipur had the land around the site surveyed, meaning to buy it, and also failed. The present temple went up in 1780, built by Malhar Rao's daughter-in-law Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore on a site adjacent to the mosque. A few years later the collector Mohammed Ibrahim built a naubatkhana, a drum house, in front of it at Warren Hastings' behest.
zh:
湿婆金庙（迦尸·毗湿瓦纳特神庙）供奉的是瓦拉纳西的湿婆「毗湿瓦纳特」，意为「宇宙之主」；相传这里的林伽是十二处究提林伽中最先显现的一处，湿婆以一根光柱的形象现身。传说梵天与毗湿奴正争论谁最伟大，湿婆便化作一根无始无终的光柱出现：毗湿奴化身野猪向地下追寻光柱之根，坦承找不到源头；梵天化作天鹅遍寻天空，谎称已找到柱顶，湿婆于是砍去他的第五颗头，诅咒他不再受人敬拜。印度教经典把毗湿瓦纳特说成瓦拉纳西全体神明和居民之王。庙中林伽高六十厘米，立在银质祭坛上，据信拜访此庙并在恒河沐浴，可走上通往解脱的道路。

庙北有一口吉扬瓦皮井，意为「智慧之井」，这座神庙最出名的故事就系在井上。1669年奥朗则布下令拆毁神庙，在原址建起吉扬瓦皮清真寺。据说大祭司抱着究提林伽跳进井里，不让圣物落入来犯者之手。印度教香客仍然前来朝拜旧庙的残迹。

马拉塔统治者两次想在原址重建神庙。1742年马尔哈尔·拉奥·霍尔卡计划拆毁清真寺、重建神庙，计划落空，部分原因是阿瓦德纳瓦布出面干预；1750年斋普尔摩诃罗阇命人勘测寺基周围的土地，打算买下来重建，也没有成功。现存的神庙1780年落成，营建者是马尔哈尔·拉奥的儿媳、印多尔的阿希莉娅芭伊·霍尔卡，选址在清真寺旁边。几年后，税务官穆罕默德·易卜拉欣奉沃伦·黑斯廷斯之命，在新庙门前修起一座鼓阁（那包特卡纳）。

en:
The ten front pillars of the Hall of Great Achievement are carved with coiled dragons, and it is said they were covered whenever the emperor visited, so as not to arouse his envy. The hall is the centre of the Temple of Confucius at Qufu in Yanzhou, which stands on the site of Confucius's own house. In 478 BC, the year after his death, the house of three rooms was made a shrine and kept his clothes, cap, lute, carriage and books; it became the model for thousands of Confucian temples. When Jin troops came south, the temple and its books were burned. In 1368 the Hongwu Emperor summoned Kong Kejian, the fifty-fifth-generation descendant; the duke pleaded illness, and came only after the emperor replied that illness would not do. By 1444 the Dukes Yansheng, his heirs, were the keepers of the shrine and offered the sacrifices on behalf of the state.

Nine courtyards run north along an axis more than a kilometre long. The Hall of Great Achievement, rebuilt in the Qing, is fifty-four by thirty-four metres and nearly thirty-two metres high, held up by twenty-eight pillars each carved from a single piece of stone. Yellow roof tiles, otherwise reserved for the emperor, cover the main halls.

In 1477 Confucius was granted the eight-row dance, an imperial honour. In 1530 it was decided that images of Confucius in official temples be replaced with spirit tablets, but temples kept by his family, Qufu among them, kept their statues. Lightning burned the main hall and over a hundred and twenty bays in 1499, and the rebuilding took five years. In 1511 rebels led by the brothers Liu Liu and Liu Qi took Qufu and fed their horses in the temple; the next year the court ordered the county town moved to surround the temple and the Kong mansion with a new wall. When lightning gutted the main hall again in 1724, the Yongzheng Emperor had drawings of every hall and ritual vessel submitted for his instruction. In the Thirteen Stele Pavilions, five imperial stelae set on stone tortoises were raised under the Kangxi, Yongzheng and Qianlong emperors, the heaviest weighing up to sixty-five tons.
zh:
大成殿正面的十根柱子刻满云中盘龙，据说皇帝驾临时要用绸子把柱子遮起来，免得惹他嫉妒。这座殿是孔庙（曲阜孔庙）的中心，孔庙在兖州曲阜，立在孔子故宅旧址上。孔子去世后第二年，即前478年，他的三间故宅被立为庙堂，收藏他的衣冠、琴、车和书，后来海内外数千座孔庙都以它为范本。金兵南侵时，庙宇和书籍都被烧成灰烬。1368年明太祖召见孔子五十五代孙孔克坚，孔克坚称病，只派儿子去南京，直到皇帝回敕「称疾则不可」才动身。1444年，衍圣公是孔子的嫡系后裔，世守祠庙，代表国家主持祭祀。

九进院落沿南北中轴排开，轴线长一公里多。清代重建的大成殿面阔五十四米、进深三十四米，高近三十二米，二十八根巨柱每根都用整块石头凿成。主要殿宇覆着本只有皇帝才能用的黄瓦。

1477年，孔子获准使用八佾之舞，这是帝王才有的礼数。1530年朝廷决定官办孔庙改用木牌位、撤去塑像，但孔氏后人守护的家庙，曲阜孔庙在内，仍留着塑像。1499年雷击烧毁大成殿和一百二十余楹房屋，重修历时五年。1511年刘六、刘七兄弟的叛军攻下曲阜，在庙内喂马驻军；次年朝廷下令移城就庙，绕着孔庙和孔府修筑新城墙。1724年雷火再次烧毁正殿，雍正帝命将各殿规制和祭器画图呈上，亲自指授。十三碑亭里有五座御碑亭，康熙、雍正、乾隆三朝先后立碑，碑下是石龟趺，最重的连碑带座达六十五吨。

en:
At Zhenjiang, the old Jingkou, the Jiangnan Canal runs into the Yangtze. Five canal mouths opened on this shore, and the most important was the Dajingkou, dug in the 490s. Boats carrying the grain and taxes of the southeast had to cross the open river to Guazhou on the far bank, where the 25-li Yilou Canal, cut in the Kaiyuan era of the Tang, led them on to the old canal. On the Jingkou side engineers dealt with the drop between river and canal one step at a time: in 734 a weir, over which oxen or trackers hauled boats on ropes; in 1067 a true lock; and in 1099 the transport official Zeng Xiaoyun built the Ao lock, five gates forming a four-chamber staircase that stored water, drew in the tide and sheltered boats from the wind. Gu Zuyu's Essentials of Historical Geography quotes the Nanxu Gazetteer: the gates open at high tide for the boats and close at the ebb to hold the water, and 'the million bushels of grain of the southeast take this road every year'.

The Xijin ferry on the south bank was called the Garlic Hill ferry in the Three Kingdoms and the Jinling ferry in the Tang, and poets waited there for a boat. One of them, Zhang Hu, wrote of the 'two or three lantern-lights' of Guazhou across the dark river at the ebb. In 1075 Wang Anshi, summoned back to court to carry on his reforms, moored for the night at Guazhou and wrote: 'Jingkou and Guazhou, one stretch of water between; Mount Zhong is only a few hills away.' In 1161 the Jin emperor Wanyan Liang, turned back at Caishi, moved his army to Yangzhou to cross at Guazhou instead; on the day set for the crossing his troops mutinied and killed him. Under the Qing the Kangxi and Qianlong emperors lodged in a travelling palace at Guazhou on their southern tours, and in 1758 the censor supervising the southern grain transport moved his office into the town.
zh:
大运河镇江段在京口（今镇江），江南运河在这里汇入长江。镇江沿江共有五个运河入江口，最重要的是南齐年间开凿的大京口。东南的漕粮和税赋北运，船要先横渡大江到对岸的瓜洲，唐代开元年间在那里开出25里的伊娄河，接上原有的运河。京口一侧，工匠一步一步对付运河与长江的水位差：734年建埭，牛或纤夫用绳索把船拖过坝；1067年改建真正的船闸；1099年两浙转运判官曾孝蕴又建起澳闸，五座闸门组成四级船闸，既能蓄水、引水，又能引潮、给船避风。顾祖禹《读史方舆纪要》引《南徐州志》说，潮涨就开闸放船，潮落便闭闸蓄水，「东南百万粟，每岁取途于此」。

南岸的西津渡三国时叫蒜山渡，唐代叫金陵渡，诗人常在这里候船。其中的张祜有一联「潮落夜江斜月里，两三星火是瓜洲」。1075年，奉召回京继续变法的王安石夜泊瓜洲，写下「京口瓜洲一水间，钟山只隔数重山」。1161年，金主完颜亮在采石矶被击退，移师扬州，打算改从瓜洲渡江；原定渡江的那天，军中哗变，他被部下杀死。清代，康熙、乾隆南巡时住在瓜洲的行宫，1758年，巡视南漕的御史也把衙署移进了瓜洲城。

en:
The Persian Wikipedia article on Bam guesses, from the similarity of two place names, that Bam may be the town of Haftvad in the Shahnameh, and the citadel the fortress he built on a mountaintop. In the story Haftvad fed a worm that had grown to the size of an elephant, until Ardashir I, twice beaten by Haftvad's army, entered the town with seven warriors disguised as rich merchants and poured molten lead down its throat. The Arg-e Bam is a fortress-city built entirely of unbaked clay brick, probably the largest adobe structure in the world. Its walls are 1,815 metres long and six to seven metres high, with a moat outside. The citadel stands at the centre, on the point with the widest view. The governor's quarters, on a rocky hill behind a double wall, held barracks, a stable for 200 horses and a well forty metres deep, and the houses and bazaar of the townspeople spread around them. No precise archaeological dating of the buildings exists, though one study concluded that the core of the city and the governor's section date from Parthian times. Under the Sassanids the castle was seized by Ardashir.

After the Arabs took Kerman in 645, one of their commanders founded the Al Rasoul mosque, one of the first in Iran. In 869 Ya'qub ibn al-Layth al-Saffar, at war with the Abbasids, defeated the Khawarij settled in the citadel and made it his permanent base. Writers of the tenth century knew Bam for its fine cotton cloth, busy bazaars, palm trees and its supposedly impregnable fortress. Under the Safavids (1502 to 1722) the citadel was considerably developed and the Four Seasons Palace was built.

In 1794 the last Zand ruler, Lotf Ali Khan, lost Kerman to Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar and fled by night to Bam. Its ruler betrayed him, fearing that his own brother had fallen into Qajar hands in Kerman. According to legend Lotf Ali Khan fought fourteen men alone for two hours before he was overcome and handed over to Agha Mohammad Khan. The Qajar ruler used the citadel as a strategic point against Afghan and Baluchi raids and turned it into a military complex.
zh:
波斯文维基的「巴姆」条凭两个地名的相似推测，巴姆可能就是《列王纪》里哈夫特瓦德的城，城堡则是他在山顶筑起的要塞。故事里哈夫特瓦德养着一条长到象那么大的虫，阿尔达希尔一世两度败于哈夫特瓦德的军队，最后带着七名勇士扮成富商进城，把熔化的铅灌进了虫的喉咙。巴姆城堡是一座整座以未烧的泥砖（土坯）筑成的要塞之城，很可能是世界上最大的土坯建筑。城墙周长1815米、高六七米，墙外有壕沟。城堡在城中央，占着视野最开阔的位置。长官区在岩丘上，由双层城墙护卫，内有兵营、可容200匹马的马厩和一口40米深的水井，平民的住宅和巴扎环绕在四周。城堡各处建筑没有确切的考古年代，不过有研究认为，城市的核心和长官区建于帕提亚时代。萨珊王朝时，这座要塞被阿尔达希尔攻占。

645年克尔曼被阿拉伯人征服后，一名阿拉伯将领建起拉苏尔清真寺，是伊朗最早的一批清真寺之一。869年，正与阿拔斯王朝作战的叶尔孤白·本·莱伊斯·萨法尔击败了栖身城堡的哈瓦利吉派，把这里定为常驻大本营。10世纪的穆斯林作者提到巴姆，称赞它的精美棉布、繁忙的巴扎、椰枣树，还有据说攻不破的要塞。萨法维王朝时期（1502至1722年），城堡大加扩建，四季宫也建于此时。

1794年，赞德王朝末代君主卢特夫·阿里汗在克尔曼败给阿迦·穆罕默德汗，连夜逃往巴姆。巴姆的统治者怕自己的兄弟已落入卡扎尔人手中，便出卖了他。相传卢特夫·阿里汗独自与十四人搏斗两个小时才被制服，随后被交给阿迦·穆罕默德汗。这位卡扎尔君主把城堡当作防备阿富汗人和俾路支人袭掠的据点，把它变成一座军事建筑群。

en:
In the eleventh century a Persian traveller described the two colossi of Bamyan as Surkh But and Khing But, the red idol and the white idol. The poet Unsuri sang of them as a pair of unhappy lovers, and a Persian legend made them King Salsal and his consort Shahmama. They stand cut into the red sandstone cliff above the cave monasteries of what had been a Buddhist centre on the silk road. The two figures are told apart by their hand gestures and identified as Vairocana and Sakyamuni, though the German Wikipedia names the larger one Dipamkara instead. Both were carved straight from the cliff around the sixth and early seventh centuries; their finer details were modelled in mud and straw and coated with painted stucco, the larger figure all in carmine red and the smaller in several colours, and the upper parts of the faces were probably huge wooden masks.

Around them the cliff is honeycombed with caves and painted chapels, estimated at some 900 dwelling caves by a Japanese team. Their walls were painted between the sixth and eighth centuries and blend Gupta Indian forms with Sasanian and Byzantine influences. Xuanzang, who came about 630, also described a reclining Buddha entering nirvana in a monastery east of the royal city, more than a thousand feet long, or about 300 metres.

The Islamic centuries did not erase the two idols. The Hudud al-Alam of 982 lists a red and a white Buddha, and in the twelfth century Muhammad ibn Mahmud al-Tusi praised the colourful wall paintings and the skill of the work. In 1221 Genghis Khan wiped out most of the valley's population but left the statues undamaged. In the seventeenth century the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb is said to have had artillery fired at the carvings; the shot did some damage, but the two Buddhas survived without major harm.
zh:
11世纪，一位波斯旅行者把巴米扬大佛的两尊立像称作苏尔赫·布特与欣格·布特，即红佛与白佛。诗人乌恩苏里把它们写成一对不幸的恋人，波斯传说又说它们是索尔索尔王和王后沙玛玛。两尊像凿在红色砂岩崖壁上，下方是曾经的佛教中心、丝绸之路上的洞窟寺院。两尊以手印区分，通常认作毗卢遮那佛与释迦牟尼佛，不过德文维基称较大的一尊是燃灯佛。它们都直接从崖壁凿出，约在6世纪至7世纪初完成；细部以草泥塑成，外抹彩绘灰泥，大佛通体涂成胭脂红，小佛饰以数种色彩，面部上半很可能是巨大的木质面具。

崖壁四周布满洞窟和画堂，日本考察队估计住人洞窟约900个。壁画作于6至8世纪，融合了印度笈多式造型和萨珊、拜占庭的影响。约630年到访的玄奘还记载，王城东面的一座寺院里有一尊入涅槃的卧佛，长千余尺，约合300米。

进入伊斯兰时代后，这两尊像并没有被抹去。982年的《世界境域志》记有一红一白两尊佛像，12世纪的穆罕默德·伊本·马哈茂德·图西赞美这里色彩鲜艳的壁画和工艺。1221年成吉思汗几乎杀光了山谷里的居民，却没有损伤佛像。17世纪，莫卧儿皇帝奥朗则布据说曾下令用火炮轰击雕像，造成一些损伤，两尊佛像没有受到大的破坏。

en:
The Spiral Minaret is all that stands of the Great Mosque of Samarra, begun in 848 by the Abbasid caliph al-Mutawakkil in the capital on the Tigris that al-Mu'tasim had founded a dozen years earlier. In its day the mosque was the largest in the world: a walled rectangle 240 by 158 metres, its walls eleven metres high and braced by 44 half-round towers, panelled with dark-blue glass mosaic, with room for over 80,000 worshippers. Tradition held that the fountain in its courtyard was cut from a single block of stone, the 'Pharaoh's Cup', and carried there by elephants. Mutawakkil was assassinated in 861, and ten years of unrest followed, with a civil war in 865 and 866.

The minaret stands 27 metres beyond the north wall on the axis of the mihrab, on a square base 33 metres across decorated with nine arched niches. Above it rises a cylinder of five tapering stages, 52 metres high in all, wrapped on the outside by a two-metre ramp of 399 steps winding anti-clockwise to the platform at the top, which the people of Samarra call al-jawn. A bridge once joined the tower to the mosque. It is visible from far around, and nothing like it had been seen in the Islamic world. Writers have compared its coiled mass to the ziggurats of ancient Mesopotamia, though some scholars reject the connection.

Samarra stayed the caliphs' residence until 892, when al-Mu'tadid moved the capital back to Baghdad. The city was looted around then and declined, though it kept its markets, and from the tenth century it drew pilgrims to the tombs of the imams Ali al-Hadi and Hasan al-Askari. In the twelfth and thirteenth centuries the Tigris shifted east, and the Baghdad-Mosul road moved to the west bank. The mosque was destroyed after Hulagu's invasion of 1258, and the Safavids are said to have wrecked more of the city later. Only the tower was left.
name_zh: 萨迈拉大清真寺宣礼塔
zh:
萨迈拉大清真寺宣礼塔（螺旋塔）是萨迈拉大清真寺仅存的地上建筑。清真寺由阿拔斯哈里发穆塔瓦基勒于848年动工，建在穆尔台绥姆十几年前于底格里斯河畔营建的都城里。当年这是世界上最大的清真寺：长方形围墙长二百四十米、宽一百五十八米，墙高十一米，外有44座半圆形扶塔，墙面镶着深蓝色玻璃马赛克，可容纳八万余人礼拜。相传院中的喷泉用一整块巨石凿成，叫「法老之杯」，是由大象运到这里的。861年穆塔瓦基勒遇刺，随后十年动荡，865至866年还爆发了内战。

宣礼塔立在北墙之外二十七米处，正对米哈拉布的轴线；方形塔基边长三十三米，开着九道拱龛。基上是五层逐层收分的圆柱，通高五十二米，塔外缠着一道两米宽的坡道，三百九十九级台阶逆时针盘旋而上，直通萨迈拉人称为「贾温」的塔顶平台。早年还有一座桥把塔和清真寺连在一起。它在远处就能望见，伊斯兰世界此前没有见过这样的塔。有人拿它盘旋的体量与美索不达米亚的吉古拉特神塔相比，但也有学者不承认这层渊源。

萨迈拉一直是哈里发的居所，直到892年穆阿台迪德把首都迁回巴格达。城市大约在那时遭劫掠，开始衰落，市集却保留下来；10世纪起，什叶派朝觐者来此拜谒伊玛目阿里·哈迪和哈桑·阿斯卡里的陵墓。12至13世纪，底格里斯河改道东移，巴格达至摩苏尔的大路挪到了西岸。1258年旭烈兀入侵后，清真寺被毁；据说后来萨法维人又毁坏了城中更多的建筑。最后只剩这座塔。

en:
The Bedouin called the great carved facade at the end of the Siq Khaznat el-Far'oun, the Treasury of the Pharaoh. They believed the stone urn, 3.5 metres high, on top of it held a hoard, and it is scarred with bullet marks from attempts to break it open, though the urn is solid rock like the rest of the facade. The Nabataeans, an Arab people, had cut their capital into the rose-red sandstone here: tombs with carved facades line the cliffs, and the way in is the Siq, a dark gorge in places only three or four metres wide. The Nabataeans controlled the flash floods with dams, cisterns and water conduits, and that water made the desert city possible. The Khazneh itself is thought to date from the beginning of the first century AD, in the reign of Aretas IV, possibly as a royal tomb.

By 1444 the Crusader castles of the valley had long been abandoned. The valley was Wadi Musa, where tradition says Moses struck the rock and brought forth water, and above it rose Jebel Harun, Mount Hor, where Aaron is said to be buried. The Muslims of Wadi Musa had long visited his tomb, and the Mamluk sultan Baibars came to it in 1276; the small domed shrine on the summit dates from the Mamluk period.

Europe had forgotten where Petra was when the Swiss traveller Johann Ludwig Burckhardt came this way in 1812. Dressed as an Arab and calling himself Sheikh Ibrahim ibn Abdallah, he heard of ruins near the supposed tomb of Aaron and told his guide he wished to sacrifice a goat there. On 22 August the guide led him through the narrow valley, and he became the first modern European to see Petra. He feared being taken for a treasure-seeking infidel, and when the guides grew suspicious he cut his visit short. He sacrificed the goat within sight of Aaron's tomb and left after sunset. His diary entry for that day runs to twelve pages, and he judged it very probable that the ruins were those of ancient Petra, though he left the decision to Greek scholars.
zh:
贝都因人把西克峡谷尽头那座雕凿的巨大立面叫作「法老的宝库」。他们相信立面顶上3.5米高的石罐里藏着财宝，石罐上弹痕累累，是有人开枪想打穿它留下的，其实石罐和整个立面一样是实心岩石。阿拉伯人的一支纳巴泰人把都城凿进了这里的玫瑰红砂岩：崖壁上排满雕饰立面的陵墓，入城的路是西克，一条幽暗的峡谷，窄处只有三四米。纳巴泰人用水坝、蓄水池和水渠控制山洪，沙漠中的城市因此能够存在。卡兹尼本身一般认为建于1世纪初哈里萨斯四世在位期间，可能是一座王陵。

到1444年，谷中的十字军城堡早已废弃。谷地名叫穆萨谷，相传摩西在这里以杖击石、引出泉水；谷后高耸哈伦山，即何珥山，据说亚伦葬在山上。穆萨谷的穆斯林早就来此朝拜亚伦的陵墓，马穆鲁克苏丹拜巴尔斯1276年也来过；山顶那座带圆顶的小圣祠建于马穆鲁克时期。

欧洲早已忘了佩特拉在何处，1812年瑞士旅行家约翰·路德维希·布尔克哈特经过这里。他扮作阿拉伯人，自称易卜拉欣·伊本·阿卜杜拉谢赫，听说传说中亚伦的陵墓附近有废墟，便对向导说，想到那里宰一只羊还愿。8月22日，向导引他穿过狭窄的山谷，他成为第一个见到佩特拉的近代欧洲人。他怕人把他当成寻宝的异教徒，向导起疑后，他便缩短了停留。他在亚伦陵墓的视线之内宰了羊，日落后离开。当天的日记长十二页，他判断这些废墟极可能就是古代的佩特拉，不过把定论留给希腊学者。

en:
The citadel of Hue is a Beijing-style palace inside a Vauban-style fortress. Phu Xuan had been the seat of the Nguyen lords, and in 1789 the Tay Son emperor Quang Trung chose it as his capital. In June 1802 Nguyen Phuc Anh defeated the Tay Son and took the throne of a united Vietnam as Gia Long. He kept the same ground for his capital, and, adopting Confucian models of statecraft, ordered a palace complex on the model of the Forbidden City in Beijing.

Geomancers were consulted. Gia Long himself chose the site on the north bank of the Perfume River and staked it out, with the flat-topped Ngu Binh hill, over a hundred metres high, standing before it like a natural screen, and two river islets serving as the Azure Dragon on the left and the White Tiger on the right. Surveys began in 1803, work on the Imperial City in 1804 and on the citadel in 1805. The citadel faces south, and its wall runs nearly ten kilometres round, 6.6 metres high and 21 thick, with forts at regular intervals and a moat of more than seven kilometres. It was built of earth at first, and brick came in only at the end of Gia Long's reign. Tens of thousands of labourers worked on it for some thirty years under two emperors, and his successor Minh Mang finished it.

Inside the citadel a second wall and moat enclosed the Imperial City, with gated courtyards leading to the throne hall, ancestral temples, offices and gardens, and within it the Purple Forbidden City, reserved for the emperor and his household. Gia Long also had every bronze weapon and bronze object collected after the Tay Son defeat and cast into nine great cannons to stand for his victory. Casting began in January 1803 and ended in December 1804. The cannons were named after the four seasons and the five elements, and in 1816 the emperor gave each the title 'Invincible General of the Gods', engraved on the barrel.
zh:
顺化皇城是一座北京式的宫城，外面套着沃邦式的要塞。富春原是阮氏诸侯的驻地，1789年西山朝的光中帝也选它作都城。1802年6月，阮福映击败西山朝，以嘉隆帝之名登上统一越南的王位。他仍以这块地方为都，采用儒家的治国模式，下令仿北京紫禁城的规制营建宫殿。

选址时请了堪舆家。嘉隆帝亲自在香江北岸选定地点并插标定界：前有顶部平坦、高过一百米的御屏山，像一面天然的屏风，江中两座沙洲分别当作左青龙、右白虎。1803年开始勘测，1804年修皇城，1805年修京城。京城朝南，城墙周长近十公里，高6.6米，厚21米，每隔一段设一座炮台，护城河长七公里多。城墙起初只用土筑，嘉隆末年才开始用砖。数万民夫前后干了近三十年，经历两位皇帝，由继位的明命帝完成。

京城之内，另有一道城墙和护城河环护皇城：一座座门禁院落通向正殿、太庙、官署和花园，再往里是紫禁城，只供皇帝和家眷使用。嘉隆帝还下令收缴西山朝覆灭后的全部铜兵器和铜器，铸成九门大炮，以纪念自己的胜利。1803年1月开铸，1804年12月完工。大炮以四季和五行命名，1816年皇帝又给每门炮敕封「神威无敌上将军」的封号，刻在炮身上。

en:
The widest temple among the Bagan Temples, the Dhammayangyi, was built under King Narathu (1167 to 1170), who came to the throne by killing his father Alaungsithu and his elder brother and presumably built on this scale to atone for it. The Burmese chronicles say some Indians assassinated him before the work was finished, while Sinhalese sources say Sinhalese invaders killed him. For unknown reasons the interior was bricked up, so that only the four porches and the outer corridors can be entered. It dates from the peak of monument building, about 1150 to 1200. The monuments on the plain are either solid stupas, which evolved from older Pyu designs, or hollow gu temples with pointed arches and vaulted chambers. The vaulting seems to have been developed at Bagan itself: the earliest vaulted temples there are eleventh-century, while in India vaulting became widespread only in the late twelfth.

At Myinkaba, just south of Bagan, stands the Gubyaukgyi, built in 1113 by Prince Yazakumar shortly after the death of his father Kyansittha. A popular retelling says Yazakumar was passed over as heir in favour of his nephew Alaungsithu and given land in compensation, which he sold to pay for the temple. Its walls hold 547 Jataka paintings, the oldest original paintings in Bagan, each captioned in ink in Old Mon. At the nearby Myazedi pagoda, two stone pillars carry the same text in Old Burmese, Pali, Old Mon and Pyu, and that inscription became the key to deciphering the Pyu language.

The Pagan Empire collapsed in 1287, and the vaulting techniques were lost in later periods; only much smaller gu temples were built afterwards. In 1790 King Bodawpaya began a huge pagoda at Mingun on the Irrawaddy. One account says it was meant to be a spacious vaulted temple and failed because later masons had lost the knowledge of vaulting and keystone arching. Another calls the work deliberately left unfinished, and says a prophecy was alleged to have foretold that the country would be gone once the pagoda was finished. It reached 50 metres, a third of the planned height.
zh:
蒲甘寺庙群里最宽的是达玛扬基寺，建于那腊都王在位时（1167至1170年）。他弑父阿朗悉都、杀死王兄夺得王位，据推测是为赎罪才兴建这座规模最大的寺庙。缅甸编年史说，工程未完他便被一些印度人刺杀；僧伽罗史料则说他死于僧伽罗入侵者之手。内殿因不明的原因被砖封死，只有四个门廊和外圈回廊可以进入。它建于蒲甘建寺最盛的时期，约1150至1200年。平原上的建筑分两类：实心的佛塔，由更早的骠人样式演变而来；和带尖拱、有拱顶内殿的窟式寺。拱顶技术看来是在蒲甘本地发展起来的：当地最早的拱顶寺庙属于11世纪，印度要到12世纪晚期才普遍使用拱顶。

城南敏卡巴村的古彪基寺建于1113年，是耶娑鸠摩王子在父亲江喜陀去世不久后所建。民间流传的说法是，耶娑鸠摩没能当上继承人，王位传给了他的外甥阿朗悉都，他得到一块土地作补偿，便卖地建了这座寺庙。寺内壁上有547幅本生故事画，是蒲甘现存最早的原作壁画，每幅都用孟文墨书题注。附近妙齐提塔的两根石柱上，同一篇碑文用古缅文、巴利文、古孟文和骠文刻成，后来成为解读骠文的钥匙。

蒲甘王朝1287年灭亡，拱顶技术在后世失传，此后只建得起小得多的窟式寺。1790年，波道帕耶王在伊洛瓦底江畔的敏贡动工兴建一座巨大佛塔。一种说法是它本想建成宽敞的拱顶寺庙，却因后世工匠已不懂拱顶和拱心石技术而失败；另一种说法是工程有意不再完成，据说有预言称塔一建成国家就会灭亡。塔身最后只到50米，是原定高度的三分之一。

en:
Tzintzuntzan means 'place of hummingbirds' in Purepecha, and five yacatas line a platform cut into the side of the Yahuarato hill, looking over Lake Patzcuaro. Each joins a rectangular stepped base to a rounded end, like a keyhole; the rubble core was faced with fitted stone slabs, and a wooden temple stood on top. The burials found among them hold rich grave goods and are probably those of kings and high priests. The Grand Platform beneath is a flat shelf about 450 metres by 250, dug into the hillside. When the king decided on war, huge bonfires were lit here and repeated by priests at the empire's other centres, a signal that the 91 settlements of the lake basin could all see.

According to the Relacion de Michoacan, the first king, Tariacuri, set out around 1300 to gather the lake communities into one state, and his lineage, the Vacuxecha, bore the name 'eagles'. By the mid-fifteenth century Tzintzuntzan was the capital of a tributary kingdom, and estimates of its population run from 25,000 to 40,000. In the 1470s an Aztec army under Axayacatl took a string of frontier towns and closed on the Purepecha heartland, but was in the end beaten back, and the Purepecha ruler fortified the frontier with military centres such as Cutzamala.

In 1522 King Tangaxuan II submitted to the Spaniards here without a fight, not wanting his city to suffer the fate of Tenochtitlan. In 1530 Nuno de Guzman had him executed. Bishop Vasco de Quiroga later moved his see to Patzcuaro, and the old capital emptied; the Franciscan monastery in Tzintzuntzan was built in part from the stones of the yacatas. About 1540 the Franciscan Jeronimo de Alcala wrote down the Relacion de Michoacan from Purepecha noblemen, preserving the ceremonies of the platform and the story of the conquest as the losers told it. In 1593 the Crown granted Tzintzuntzan the rank of a city, with its own native governor and council.
zh:
钦聪灿在普雷佩查语里意为「蜂鸟之地」，五座亚卡塔金字塔排列在雅瓦拉托山削出的平台上，俯临帕茨夸罗湖。每座亚卡塔都由长方形阶梯台身和圆形端头相接，形如钥匙孔，碎石内芯外面贴着严丝合缝的石板，顶上立着木构神庙。其间发掘出的墓葬随葬丰厚，墓主很可能是国王和高阶祭司。下方的大平台是一块约450米乘250米的平场，挖进山坡而成。国王决定开战时，这里会点起巨大的篝火，由祭司在王国其他中心重复点燃，帕茨夸罗湖盆的91个聚落都望得见。

据《米却肯纪事》，首位国王塔里亚库里约在1300年起要把环湖的村社合成一个国家，他的家族叫瓦库谢查，意思是「鹰」。15世纪中叶，钦聪灿是一个纳贡王国的都城，人口估计在两万五千到四万之间。1470年代，阿兹特克军队在阿萨亚卡特尔率领下夺了一串边境城镇，逼近普雷佩查腹地，最终还是被打退，国王随后在边境加筑库察马拉等军事据点。

1522年，国王坦加克森二世在这里向西班牙人投降，没有交战，为的是让自己的城免于特诺奇蒂特兰的下场。1530年，努尼奥·德·古斯曼把他处死。后来基罗加主教把主教座迁往帕茨夸罗，旧都随之空了下来；钦聪灿的方济各会修道院，部分就是用亚卡塔的石料建成的。约1540年，方济各会修士赫罗尼莫·德·阿尔卡拉据普雷佩查贵族的口述写成《米却肯纪事》，把台地上的仪式和败者口中的征服经过落于文字。1593年，王室封钦聪灿为城，准其设立自己的土著总督和议事会。

en:
Seventy-two Buddha statues sit inside perforated stupas on the upper terraces of Borobudur. The Babad Mataram tells that in 1757, despite a taboo on visiting the ruin, a crown prince of Yogyakarta went to see one of them, 'the knight captured in a cage', and pitied it. He fell ill on returning to his palace and died a day later.

By then the shrine was a ruin. No record of its building survives, but it went up on the Kedu Plain under the Sailendra dynasty and is thought to have been finished around 825, in the reign of Samaratungga. It is built of grey andesite: six square terraces below three circular ones and a central dome. Its walls and balustrades carry 2,672 relief panels, and it originally held 504 Buddha statues. Pilgrims entered from the east and circled clockwise past 1,460 narrative panels on their way up.

Between 928 and 1006 King Mpu Sindok moved the capital of Mataram to East Java after a series of volcanic eruptions, and it is uncertain how far this led to the abandonment of Borobudur. The terraces lay hidden under volcanic ash and jungle growth. The Old Javanese poem Nagarakretagama mentioned the vihara at Budur only vaguely in 1365, and later folk stories tied the monument to bad luck and misery. According to the Babad Tanah Jawi it was fatal to a rebel against the king of Mataram in 1709, when the hill was surrounded and the rebels were defeated and put to death.

In 1814 Thomas Stamford Raffles, the British administrator of Java, heard of a great monument in the jungle near Bumisegoro. He sent the engineer Hermann Cornelius, who spent two months there with 200 men felling trees, burning growth and digging away earth until the terraces emerged. Some galleries he left buried because of the danger of collapse.
zh:
婆罗浮屠寺上层的镂空佛塔里，坐着72尊佛像。《马打兰纪年》（Babad Mataram）记载，1757年，日惹的一位王储不顾禁忌来看其中一尊，称它是「被关在笼中的武士」，对它心生怜悯，回宫后患病，一天后便去世了。

那时这座精舍早已荒废。它的建造没有留下记录，只知道建在克杜平原，属夏连特拉王朝时期，据信约825年在位于萨马拉通加王时建成。塔身用灰色安山岩砌成：六层方形台基，上面是三层圆形平台和中央穹顶。墙面与栏杆上共有2672幅浮雕板，原供504尊佛像。朝圣者从东侧进入，顺时针绕行，一路经过1460幅叙事浮雕向上攀升。

928至1006年间，姆普·辛多克王在一连串火山喷发后把马打兰的都城迁往东爪哇，婆罗浮屠的废弃与此有多大关系并不确定。台基被火山灰和丛林掩盖起来。1365年的古爪哇诗《爪哇史颂》只含糊提到布杜尔的一处精舍，后来民间传说把这座建筑同厄运和苦难联系在一起。据《爪哇纪年》（Babad Tanah Jawi），1709年一名反叛马打兰国王的人因它而遭殃：山头被围，叛军兵败，被判处死。

1814年，英属爪哇官员托马斯·斯坦福德·莱佛士听说布米塞戈罗附近的丛林中有一座巨大建筑，派工程师赫尔曼·科内利乌斯前往。科内利乌斯带200人干了两个月，伐树、焚草、掘土，直到台基重新露出；有些廊道因有坍塌危险，他没有掘开。

en:
Javanese villagers explained Prambanan with a story about a princess and a thousand temples. Prince Bandung Bondowoso, it goes, killed the giant king Boko and wanted to marry his daughter Rara Jonggrang, 'the slender maiden'. She set him an impossible task, a thousand temples in a single night. With the help of spirits he finished 999. The princess lit fires in the east and had her maids pound rice, as at dawn; the roosters crowed, the spirits fled, and the last temple stayed unfinished. The furious prince cursed her into stone, and she became the Durga image in the Shiva temple. The tale was composed centuries after the temples, probably under the Mataram Sultanate.

The real builders were Hindu kings of Central Java. Rakai Pikatan most likely started the complex, and some historians read it as a Hindu answer to the Buddhist temples of Borobudur and Sewu. The Shivagrha inscription of 856 gives 12 November as the day the Shiva temple was inaugurated; its original name meant the House of Shiva. The Shiva tower rises 47 metres in a walled compound of 240 structures, with a three-metre statue of Shiva Mahadeva in its inner chamber and separate temples for Brahma and Vishnu. The same inscription records a public works project to move a river beside the temple, identified as the Opak, onto a north-south course along the outer wall; experts suggest this was meant to protect the site from Merapi lahars.

The Javanese court moved to East Java in the 930s and the temples were abandoned, for reasons that are not clear; a major earthquake in the sixteenth century brought them down. In 1733 a Dutch East India Company employee travelling to Kartasura described the ruins as Brahmin temples that looked like a mountain of stones. After Mataram was divided in 1755, the ruins and the Opak became the border between Yogyakarta and Surakarta. Nicolaus Engelhard, the Dutch governor on Java's northeast coast, saw them in 1803 and two years later ordered the site cleared, measured and drawn.
zh:
爪哇村民用一个公主与千座神庙的故事解释普兰巴南神庙。传说班东·邦多沃索王子杀了巨人国王波科，想娶他的女儿琼格朗公主（意为「苗条的少女」）。公主出了个办不到的难题：一夜之间造起一千座神庙。王子借精灵之力造好了999座。公主在东方点起火堆，让侍女们像拂晓时那样舂米；公鸡啼了，精灵四散而逃，最后一座神庙没有建成。暴怒的王子把她诅咒成石头，她就成了湿婆庙里的难近母像。这个故事比神庙晚了几百年，大概成形于马打兰苏丹国时期。

真正的建造者是中爪哇的印度教国王。这组神庙很可能由拉凯·皮卡坦始建，一些史家认为它是印度教对婆罗浮屠和附近的佛教寺院塞武的回应；856年的《湿瓦格里哈铭文》记载湿婆庙在11月12日落成，原名意为「湿婆之家」。湿婆主塔高47米，立在围有240座建筑的庙院中央；内殿供奉三米高的湿婆·摩诃提婆像，另有梵天与毗湿奴的神庙。同一篇铭文还记载了一项改移庙旁河流的工程，这条河被认为是奥帕克河，新河道沿外墙呈南北走向；专家推测是为了保护神庙免受默拉皮火山泥流侵袭。

930年代王廷迁往东爪哇，神庙被废弃，原因不明；16世纪的一场大地震使它们倒塌。1733年，一名前往卡尔塔苏拉的荷兰东印度公司职员在日记中把废墟称作「婆罗门寺庙」，说它们像一座石头堆成的山。1755年马打兰分裂后，神庙废墟与奥帕克河成了日惹和梭罗的边界。1803年，荷兰人在爪哇东北岸的长官尼古劳斯·恩格尔哈德到访，两年后下令清理遗址、丈量并绘图。

en:
Bete Giyorgis stands alone in a pit cut down into volcanic tuff, a trench 25 metres square and 30 deep; the only way in is a narrow man-made canyon that spirals down and turns into a tunnel near the church. Ethiopian tradition says King Gebre Mesqel Lalibela had a vision in which he was told to build it, and accounts name both Saint George and God as the one who gave the order. It is among the last built of the eleven rock-hewn churches of Lalibela. French archaeologists found that the workmen shaped each detail as they went down into the rock, carving inside and outside together and clearing rubble through the windows with picks and hammers. Legend says angels helped them by day and carried on working at night.

When the churches were cut is disputed. David Buxton's chronology runs the work on into the fourteenth century, while David Phillipson argues that three churches began as Aksumite works between 600 and 800. A local historian credits Queen Meskel Kibra with Biete Abba Libanos, built as a memorial to her husband. Biete Golgotha Mikael is said to hold the king's tomb, and dust from it, given out by the priest, is believed to heal the sick; Francisco Álvares, who went twice in the 1520s, swore that all he wrote of the churches was true, because he feared no one would believe him.

Fra Mauro's Venetian map of 1457–59 names the place 'Lalabeda'. In 1531 Ahmad al-Ghazi laid waste to the district. His chronicler, the Futuh al-Habasha, says he gathered the monks and lit a fire in one church, saying 'Let one of yours and one of ours enter there'; a nun threw herself on the flames and was pulled out by his soldiers. Richard Pankhurst doubts the story, since the Royal Chronicles do not mention it. The Portuguese soldier Miguel de Castanhoso, who left Ethiopia in 1544, wrote that the Moors tried to destroy the churches with crowbars and gunpowder and did no damage at all.
zh:
拉利贝拉岩石教堂群中的圣乔治教堂独自立在一个凿入火山凝灰岩的深坑中央，坑长宽各25米、深30米；只有一条人工窄峡盘旋向下，临近教堂时变成隧道，才能进去。埃塞俄比亚的说法是，格布雷·梅斯克尔·拉利贝拉王得到异象，受命建造这座教堂，下令者有的说是圣乔治，有的说是上帝。它是拉利贝拉十一座岩凿教堂中最晚建成的几座之一。法国考古学者发现，工匠是边往下凿边做细部，内外同时雕琢，碎石从窗口运走，用的是铁镐和锤子。传说天使白天帮工匠干活，夜里还继续凿。

这些教堂凿于何时，说法不一。戴维·巴克斯顿的年表认为工程一直延续到14世纪；戴维·菲利普森则认为其中三座教堂最早是600至800年间阿克苏姆时代的工程。一位当地历史学家把阿巴·利巴诺斯教堂归于王后梅斯克尔·基布拉，说那是她为丈夫修的纪念堂。各各他·米卡埃尔教堂相传葬着国王，墓上的尘土由教士分发，据信能治病；弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯1520年代去过两次，他发誓自己所写的一切都是真的，因为怕别人不信。

1457至1459年的威尼斯弗拉·毛罗地图把这个地方写作「拉拉贝达」。1531年艾哈迈德·格拉兹蹂躏了这一带。他的编年史《征服阿比西尼亚》说，他召集僧人，在一座教堂里点起火，说「你们一个，我们一个，进去」；一名修女投身火中，被他的士兵拉了出来。理查德·潘克赫斯特对此存疑，因为王室编年史没有提到。1544年离开埃塞俄比亚的葡萄牙军人米格尔·德·卡斯塔尼奥索写道，摩尔人想用撬棍和火药毁掉这些教堂，却没能损坏分毫。

en:
Aymara legend placed Tiwanaku at the centre of the world, and the Jesuit Bernabe Cobo recorded its old name, taypiqala, 'stone in the centre'. In Inca belief, Lake Titicaca was where the creator Viracocha made the sun, the moon and the first people. When Pedro Cieza de Leon visited in 1549, he noted that the ruins belonged to a time before the Incas. The ceremonial centre lies on the Altiplano 21 kilometres south-east of the lake, at nearly 3,900 metres. Its masons quarried red sandstone ten kilometres away and green andesite on the Copacabana peninsula across the lake; one theory is that andesite blocks of over 40 tons were taken some 90 kilometres over the water on reed boats. At Pumapunku lies the largest stone on the site, estimated at 131 tonnes. The Gate of the Sun, about three metres tall and four wide, was carved from a single block of some ten tons; a central figure holding a spear-thrower is flanked by 48 attendants, and some have claimed the carvings form a calendar, though without firm evidence. The walls of the sunken temple are set with 175 stone heads, no two alike, and the 7.3-metre Bennett monolith was found there.

The city had collapsed around 1000, but the ruins remained a holy place, and it is said that the Incas who came to them were amazed. When the Spanish arrived, Cobo reported, one gateway and one 'window' still stood upright on a platform at Pumapunku. The stepped Akapana pyramid was looted from Inca times onward, and a deep looters' trench runs from its centre to its eastern side.
zh:
艾马拉传说把蒂亚瓦纳科放在世界的中心，耶稣会士贝尔纳维·科沃记下了它的旧名「塔伊皮卡拉」，意为「中心之石」。印加人相信，创世神维拉科查是在的的喀喀湖造出太阳、月亮和最初的人。1549年谢萨·德·莱昂来到这里，他注意到这些遗迹属于印加人之前的年代。仪式中心坐落在高原上，在的的喀喀湖东南21公里，海拔近3900米。石匠从10公里外采来红砂岩，又从湖对岸的科帕卡巴纳半岛采来绿色安山岩；有一种说法认为，四十多吨重的安山岩巨石是用芦苇船在湖上运了约90公里。普玛彭古有遗址里最大的一块石料，估重131吨。太阳门高约3米、宽4米，用整块约十吨重的石头雕成，中央手持投矛器的神像两侧排着48个侍从，有人主张雕刻是一种历法，但没有确凿证据。半地下神殿的墙面上嵌着175颗石首，彼此都不相同，7.3米高的贝内特石碑就在这座神殿中发现。

这座城约在1000年已经衰落，遗址却一直是圣地，据说来到这里的印加人为之惊叹。科沃记载，西班牙人到来时，普玛彭古的一座平台上仍有一道石门和一扇「窗」直立着。阶梯状的阿卡帕纳金字塔自印加时代起就遭劫掠，一道盗宝人挖的深沟从它的中心通到东侧。

en:
Vlad the Impaler of Wallachia passed through the Bran Gorge several times, but most historians agree that he never lived in Bran Castle, which belonged to Kronstadt, a city hostile to him. It was once believed that he was held prisoner here after the Hungarians captured him; historians conclude that his prison was a fortress in Budapest. The castle stands on a rock at the Transylvanian end of the Rucăr-Bran pass, on a historic road between Transylvania and Wallachia. In the early thirteenth century the Teutonic Order, to which Andrew II had given the Burzenland, built a wooden fort called Dietrichstein near the pass, and it was later destroyed. In November 1377 Louis I allowed the Saxons of Kronstadt to build a stone fortress there at their own cost and with their own masons, promising that the customs post would move from Rucăr to Bran if Wallachia came into his hands. Unlike many castles of the time it was no noble family's seat: it was built almost exclusively for defence and for the protection of the German colonists.

In 1395 Sigismund of Luxembourg used Bran as his base for a raid into Wallachia that drove out Vlad the Usurper, a rival of his vassal Mircea the Elder, and later gave Mircea the castle. Before 1444 it had also served against the Turks. In 1427 it passed from Kronstadt to the Hungarian crown, which paid for strengthening it, and in 1498 the crown leased it back to the city. It held off a Wallachian siege in 1529, and in 1593 self-igniting gunpowder destroyed its powder tower. In 1612 it was handed over without a fight to Prince Gabriel Báthory, and Gabriel Bethlen later had the south tower added. Nicolae Pătrașcu, the son of Michael the Brave, besieged it without success, and in 1789 it was besieged again by a Turkish army said to number 5,000 and held out.
zh:
瓦拉几亚的穿刺公弗拉德曾几次穿过布兰峡谷，但多数历史学家认为他从没在布兰城堡住过，因为城堡属于对他怀有敌意的喀琅施塔特。人们曾以为他被匈牙利人俘虏后关在这里，历史学家的结论是他被关押在布达佩斯的一座要塞。城堡踞在布兰山口特兰西瓦尼亚一侧的岩石上，山口路是特兰西瓦尼亚通往瓦拉几亚的一条古道。13世纪初，匈牙利国王安德烈二世把布尔岑兰赐给条顿骑士团，骑士团在山口附近修了一座名叫迪特里希施泰因的木堡，后来被毁。1377年11月，路易一世准许喀琅施塔特的撒克逊人自费、用自己的工匠在此修建石堡，并许诺若瓦拉几亚落入他手中，就把税关从鲁卡尔迁到布兰。和当时许多城堡不同，它不是哪家贵族的宅邸，几乎完全是为了防御和保护德意志移民而建。

1395年，西吉斯蒙德以布兰为基地攻入瓦拉几亚，赶走了篡位者弗拉德，此人是他的附庸老米尔恰的对手；后来西吉斯蒙德把这座城堡交给了米尔恰。1444年之前，它还抵御过土耳其人。1427年城堡由喀琅施塔特转入匈牙利王室，王室出资加固；1498年王室又把它租给这座城市。它在1529年顶住瓦拉几亚军队的围攻，1593年火药自燃，炸毁了火药塔。1612年，城堡未经战斗就交给加布里埃尔·巴托里亲王，加博尔·贝特伦后来下令加建南塔。勇敢者米哈伊的儿子尼古拉·珀特拉斯库来围攻，没有得手；1789年，一支据称有五千人的土耳其军队再次围城，仍被挡了回去。

en:
The largest of Norway's surviving stave churches stands in Heddal: three towers, two side aisles, built wholly of Scots pine, twenty metres long and twenty-six high.
