Local legend says it went up in three days. Five Heddal farmers had decided to build a church, and one of them, Raud Rygi, met a stranger who offered to do it. The price: Raud must fetch the sun and the moon down from the sky, give his life's blood, or guess the stranger's name. All the materials arrived the first night and the spire rose the second. Afraid for his life, Raud wandered out to the hill Svintruberget and heard a song from inside the mountain, saying that Finn would come tomorrow with the moon, the sun and a Christian heart. The builder was a troll named Finn. At the handover Raud put his arms round a pillar as if to straighten it and said, 'Hey Finn, this pillar isn't straight!' The troll left in haste, and could never again bear church bells. The same troll, the legend adds, built Nidaros Cathedral, Avaldsnes Church and Lund Cathedral.

The age of the real building is not settled. A runic inscription in the chancel is dated to 1167 and read as a consecration inscription; tree-ring dating puts important parts in the middle of the 1200s, some older and some younger, and the usual estimate is around 1200. It was dedicated to the Virgin Mary. After the Reformation it fell into serious disrepair, and in the 1600s it was repaired and given a low flat ceiling. In 1723 the crown sold the churches of Norway to pay off its Great Northern War debts, and Heddal passed to a private owner who had to keep it up. In 1814 it was one of more than three hundred parish churches used as polling stations for Norway's first national elections: the electors chosen here later met those of the whole county to pick the men who would write the constitution at Eidsvoll.
zh:
海达尔木板教堂是挪威现存最大的木板教堂，立在海达尔：三座塔，两条侧廊，通体用欧洲赤松建成，长20米，高26米。当地传说，这座教堂是三天盖成的。海达尔的五个农民决意建一座教堂，其中的劳德·吕吉遇到一个愿意承建的陌生人。条件是：劳德要么从天上取来太阳和月亮，要么献出自己的心头血，要么猜出这个陌生人的名字。第一夜材料全部运齐，第二夜尖塔竖了起来。劳德怕丢性命，在田野里游荡，走到斯温特鲁山，听见山里传出一首歌，唱的是明天芬恩要带着月亮、太阳和一颗基督徒的心来。原来承建的是一个叫芬恩的山妖。交工那天，劳德抱住一根柱子，像要把它扶直，说：「喂，芬恩，这根柱子不直！」山妖匆匆离去，此后再也受不了教堂的钟声。传说里还说，尼达罗斯大教堂、阿瓦兹内斯教堂和隆德大教堂也是这个山妖盖的。

真实建筑的年代并无定论。圣坛上有被定在1167年的如尼文铭文，释读为祝圣铭文；年轮测定显示重要部分建于13世纪中期，有些更早，有些更晚；对整座教堂通行的估计是1200年前后。教堂奉祀圣母马利亚。宗教改革后，教堂年久失修，17世纪修缮时加了低矮的平顶。1723年，王室为偿还大北方战争的债务，出售挪威各地的教堂，海达尔教堂转到一位私人业主手里，由他负责维护。1814年，它是全挪威三百多座充当投票站的教区教堂之一，参加挪威第一次全国性选举：在这里选出的选举人，随后与全郡的选举人会合，选出前往埃兹沃尔制定宪法的代表。

en:
The Great Mosque at Divrigi is celebrated for its portals, three of them, each decorated differently and none in the same style as another. The north portal in particular is carved in dense high relief, and the west portal carries a double-headed eagle, the emblem of Sultan Kayqubad. According to the Turkish wikipedia, when the afternoon sun falls on the entrance, the shadows form the profile of a standing man, and it is believed to be a man reading the Quran and praying. An inscription over the north portal gives the date 626 AH (1228-9) and names the patron Ahmadshah ibn Sulayman, a ruler of the Divrigi branch of the Mengucekids. The hospital inscription calls the building a dar al-shifa, a house of healing, and names its founder as Turan Malik, daughter of Fakhr al-Din Bahramshah of Erzincan. The same architect signed the interior of both buildings: Khurramshah ibn Mughith, from Ahlat.

Inside the mosque, stone piers carry vaults that differ from aisle to aisle, and a light dome stands over the central aisle. The ebony minbar is carved with bands of thuluth script and stars, and an inscription dates it to 1243 and names a craftsman from Tiflis. The hospital shares the mosque's south wall. Four iwans open around a covered court with a light dome and a small pool, and the overflow from the pool runs out through a channel around it. A tomb chamber in the hospital has a window onto the mosque. In 1398 Bayezid I took the castle above the complex, and in 1401 he had to leave it to the Mamluks, who still held it in 1444. Inscriptions record several major restorations between the fifteenth and nineteenth centuries.
name_zh: 迪夫里伊医院和清真寺
zh:
迪夫里伊医院和清真寺中的大清真寺以大门闻名：一共三座，装饰各不相同，风格也不统一。北门尤其雕得密集，是深浮雕，西门上有双头鹰，那是苏丹凯库巴德的徽记。据土耳其文维基，午后阳光照到门口时，影子会勾出一个站立的男人侧影，当地相信那是一个在诵读《古兰经》、做礼拜的人。北门的铭文纪年为伊历626年（1228至1229年），写明施主是艾哈迈德沙赫·本·苏莱曼，门居杰克王朝迪夫里伊一系的统治者。医院的铭文称这座建筑为「达尔·舍法」，即疗愈之院，创建者是埃尔津詹的法赫尔丁·巴赫拉姆沙赫之女图兰·梅莱克。两座建筑的内部都留有同一位建筑师的签名：来自阿赫拉特的胡拉姆沙赫·本·穆吉斯。

清真寺内，石柱支撑着各排拱廊上互不相同的拱顶，中间的殿上有一座采光穹顶。乌木敏拜尔刻着苏鲁斯体书带和星形纹，铭文纪年1243年，署名的匠人来自第比利斯。医院与清真寺共用南墙，四座伊旺围着带采光穹顶的内庭，庭心有一方小水池，池中溢出的水沿一道水渠绕池流出。医院里有一间陵墓室，窗口朝向清真寺。1398年，巴耶济德一世夺取了建筑群上方的城堡，1401年不得不把它让给马穆鲁克，1444年仍在马穆鲁克手中。铭文记载，15至19世纪间它曾多次大修。

en:
Herodotus says that about 600 BC the pharaoh Necho II began a canal through the Wadi Tumilat to link the Nile with the Red Sea. He was told that 120,000 men died on the work, though the figure is thought to be exaggerated, and an oracle warned Necho that others would profit from it, so the digging stopped. Darius I of Persia is credited with finishing it. On the granite stelae he set up beside it he boasted that ships went from Egypt through this canal to Persia, and Herodotus says two triremes could pass in it with oars extended and that the trip took four days, though Aristotle, Strabo and Pliny the Elder say Darius never finished. Ptolemy II, Trajan and the Arab commander Amr ibn al-As each had it dug out again. An Irish monk named Fidelis sailed on it from the Nile to the Red Sea in the early 700s, and in 767 the caliph al-Mansur is said to have had it closed to keep supplies from reaching his opponents in Arabia.

After the Portuguese opened the sea route round Africa, Venetian leaders contemplated a waterway from the Red Sea to the Nile to bring the spice trade back, and negotiated with the Mamluks until the Ottoman conquest of Egypt in 1517 ended the plan. The Ottoman grand vizier Sokollu Mehmed Pasha wanted a canal so that the Mediterranean and Red Sea fleets could join, but it was judged too expensive. Napoleon's scholars and engineers searched northern Egypt in 1798 and 1799 and mapped the remains of an ancient canal in the Description de l'Égypte. As emperor Napoleon thought of a north-south canal, but gave it up because of a mistaken belief, drawn from fragmentary survey measurements, that the Red Sea stood 8.5 metres higher than the Mediterranean. Ferdinand de Lesseps's Suez Canal opened on 17 November 1869.
zh:
据希罗多德所说，公元前600年左右，法老尼科二世开始沿图米拉特干河开渠，沟通尼罗河与红海。他听说有十二万人死于这项工程，不过这个数字被认为夸大了；又有神谕警告尼科二世，他人将因此得益，工程便停了下来。一般认为是波斯王大流士一世完成了它。他在渠畔立起的花岗岩石碑上夸耀：船只从埃及经这条运河驶往波斯。希罗多德说，渠里两艘三列桨船可以并排伸桨通过，全程要走四天；但亚里士多德、斯特拉波和老普林尼都说大流士没有完工。托勒密二世、图拉真和阿拉伯统帅阿慕尔·伊本·阿斯先后都命人重新疏浚。一位名叫菲德利斯的爱尔兰修士，8世纪上半叶曾乘船从尼罗河驶到红海；767年哈里发曼苏尔据说下令封渠，不让物资运到阿拉伯的反对者手里。

葡萄牙人打通绕过非洲的海路之后，威尼斯的领袖们想挖一条连接红海与尼罗河的水道，把香料贸易拉回来，还与马穆鲁克谈判，直到1517年奥斯曼征服埃及，计划作罢。奥斯曼大维齐尔索库鲁·穆罕默德帕夏想开一条运河，好让地中海和红海的舰队合在一起，但被认为耗费过大。拿破仑的学者和工程师1798至1799年在埃及北部搜寻，把一条古运河的遗迹画进了《埃及志》。称帝后的拿破仑考虑过开一条南北向的运河，却因一个错误的看法放弃了：根据零碎的测量数据，他们以为红海比地中海高出8.5米。1869年11月17日，雷赛布主持的苏伊士运河通航。

en:
The Shwedagon is the golden stupa on Singuttara Hill above Dagon, the most sacred pagoda in Burma. Its founding legend says that two merchants, Tapussa and Bhallika, met the Buddha at Bodh Gaya and gave him rice cake and honey, and became his first lay disciples. He gave them eight hairs from his head, and they presented the hairs to King Okkalapa of Dagon, who enshrined them in a stupa on this hill; the legend puts this in the Buddha's lifetime. The stupa is said to keep relics of all four Buddhas of this age: the staff of Kakusandha, the water strainer of Konagamana, a scrap of Kassapa's robe and the eight hairs of Gautama.

The brick spire is sheathed in gold plates fixed over the masonry with traditional rivets. Monarchs, beginning with Queen Shin Saw Pu, and people from all over the country have given gold to keep it covered, and stalls on the eastern and southern approaches sell gold leaf. Four flights of steps climb the hill, each entrance guarded by a pair of giant leogryphs. Pilgrims circle clockwise from one directional shrine to the next, then find their own birth-day post among the eight planetary posts, Sunday's garuda through Saturday's naga, and pour water over the Buddha image there. In the month of Tabaung the hill holds the country's largest pagoda festival, from the new moon to the full.

Inscriptions from the reign of Dhammazedi list repairs going back to 1436; Queen Shin Saw Pu raised the stupa to 40 metres and gilded it, and by the early 1500s the Shwedagon was the most famous pilgrimage site in Burma. In 1779 King Singu gave the Maha Gandha, a twenty-three-ton bronze bell, which was hung in a pavilion on the northwest of the platform. In 1796 Hiram Cox, the British envoy to the Burmese court, kept to the custom by not visiting the pagoda at all rather than take off his shoes.
zh:
大光金塔（瑞德宫大金塔）在大光的辛古塔拉山上，是缅甸最神圣的佛塔。据建塔传说，商人提谓和波利在菩提迦耶遇见佛陀，以糕饼和蜂蜜供佛，成为最早的在家弟子。佛陀赐给他们八根头发，二人把佛发献给大光的奥加拉巴王，国王把佛发供进这座山上的塔里，传说此事发生在佛陀在世之时。塔里相传供有当世四佛的圣物：拘楼孙佛的杖、拘那含佛的滤水囊、迦叶佛的衣片和释迦牟尼的八根头发。

砖塔通体覆着以传统铆钉固定的金板。历代君主从信绍布女王起，加上全国各地的民众，都向塔布施黄金来维持这层金装；东、南两道台阶旁的摊子出售金箔。四道台阶通上山顶，每个入口各立一对巨型狮形神兽。香客顺时针绕塔，依次走过四方佛龛，再到八根星柱中找到自己的生辰柱，从周日的迦楼罗到周六的龙，在柱前向佛像浇水。德榜月从朔到望，山上举行全国最盛大的佛塔节。

达摩悉提时代的碑铭列出了早至1436年的历次修缮；信绍布女王把塔加高到40米并贴了金；到16世纪初，大光金塔已是缅甸最有名的朝圣地。1779年，辛古王布施了二十三吨重的铜钟摩诃甘达，铜钟挂在平台西北角的钟亭里。1796年，出使缅甸朝廷的英国使节考克斯为了不脱鞋，干脆没有去参拜这座塔，以此遵守当地的规矩。

en:
The Gomateshwara statue is visible from about thirty kilometres away. It stands on the hill called Vindhyagiri at Shravanabelagola in the Kannada country: a 57-foot image of the Jain saint Bahubali, cut from a single block of granite. Chavundaraya, minister and commander of the Western Ganga kings, commissioned it in 981; the Prakrit inscription at its base, dated to that year, praises the king who funded the work and the general who raised the image for his mother. Tradition says his mother Kalala Devi dreamed of a colossal Gomateshwara and vowed not to eat until the dream came true. The figure stands naked and motionless, with no support from the thigh upward; an anthill rises behind it, and a snake and a creeper wind round the legs and arms and end in flowers and berries on the upper arms.

Bahubali, son of the first tirthankara Rishabhanatha and brother of the emperor Bharata, is said to have given up his kingdom after a contest with his brother and stood motionless in meditation for twelve years, with climbing plants growing around his legs, until he attained omniscience. Every twelve years the Mahamastakabhisheka, the great head-anointing, renews the image. Devotees pour 1,008 vessels of water from scaffolding built around the colossus, then sugarcane juice, milk and saffron, and scatter turmeric, sandalwood powder, flower petals and gold and silver flowers over it.

A legend tells how Chavundaraya's first anointing failed. The milk and the other liquids he poured from hundreds of pots would not flow below the navel, until a poor old woman appeared holding milk in half the shell of a gullikayi fruit, and the liquid ran from head to foot. Chavundaraya saw his pride and tried again, and this time it ran. One derivation of the name Belagola links it to the eggplant (gullakayi) of this story, against the usual reading 'white pond'.
zh:
从约三十公里外就能望见巴胡巴利雕像（戈马泰什瓦拉）。它立在卡纳达地区什拉瓦纳贝拉戈拉的温迪亚吉里山上，是一尊57英尺高的耆那教圣者巴胡巴利像，由整块花岗岩雕成。西恒伽诸王的宰相兼统帅查文达拉亚于981年下令雕造；像座下的普拉克里特铭文即作于是年，称颂出资的国王，也记下这位将军为母亲立像的经过。相传他的母亲卡拉拉·黛维梦见一尊巨大的戈马泰什瓦拉像，发誓梦想不成就不进食。雕像赤裸不动，大腿以上没有任何支撑；身后是一座蚁冢，一条蛇和一根藤蔓缠绕双腿和双臂，在上臂顶端开出花朵、结出浆果。

巴胡巴利是初代祖师勒舍婆那陀之子、皇帝婆罗多的兄弟，相传他在与兄弟的较量后舍弃王国，以站姿入定十二年，藤蔓缠上双腿，最终证得一切智。每隔十二年，人们举行大灌顶玛哈玛斯塔卡比谢卡，为这尊像沐浴：信众在巨像四周搭起脚手架，从上面倾下一千零八罐水，再浇上甘蔗汁、牛奶和藏红花，并撒上姜黄、檀香粉、花瓣，以及金银花朵。

传说查文达拉亚第一次灌顶就出了岔子。他用几百只罐子盛的牛奶和其他液汁，流到肚脐就流不下去，直到一位穷老妇出现，用半只古利卡伊果的壳盛着牛奶，液汁才从头一直流到脚。查文达拉亚明白自己心存傲慢，重新来过，这一回液汁畅流无阻。贝拉戈拉一名通常解作「白池」，另有一说把它同这个故事里的茄子（古拉卡伊）联系起来。

en:
Of all the carving on the temples of Khajuraho, the famous love-making couples make up only about a tenth. The rest shows apsaras putting on make-up and knotting their girdles, musicians, potters and farmers. By the twelfth century the Chandela kings had built 85 sandstone temples here in Bundelkhand, spread over twenty square kilometres; about 25 survive. Most went up in the tenth and early eleventh centuries. The largest, the Kandariya Mahadeva, dated to 1025-1050, was built for Shiva by Vidyadhara to celebrate his success over Mahmud of Ghazni, whose siege of Kalinjar ended in a truce and an exchange of gifts. It rises over a hundred feet under a spire of 84 miniature spires, and its walls carry more than 870 statues. The masons used no mortar: blocks of up to twenty tons are joined by mortise and tenon and held by their own weight. Jain temples stand in an eastern group beside the Hindu ones.

By 1444 the Chandelas had lost their kingdom to Delhi in 1202 and moved their seat to the forts of Mahoba, Kalinjar and Ajayagarh, and Khajuraho had shrunk to a small village. Ibn Battuta, who travelled in India in the fourteenth century, called the place Kajarra and wrote of temples whose idols Muslims had mutilated, and of yogis with matted locks as long as their bodies, yellow from fasting, whom Muslim visitors came to for lessons. At the plain Matangeshvara temple, a lingam two and a half metres high stands on a platform 7.6 metres across; the tradition is that the sage Matanga appeared there in the form of a lingam and mastered the god of love. In 1495 Sikandar Lodi's campaign of temple destruction reached Khajuraho and damaged some temples, but its remoteness protected the rest. Over the centuries the forest overgrew them, until in 1819 the military surveyor C. J. Franklin 'rediscovered' the group for the British.
zh:
克久拉霍神庙的雕刻里，最出名的欢爱造像只占全部的约十分之一。其余是描眉、系腰带的飞天，乐师、陶工和农夫。到12世纪，昌德拉诸王在本德尔肯德一带建起85座砂岩神庙，分布在二十平方公里的土地上，现存约25座，多数建于10世纪至11世纪初。最大的坎达里亚·摩诃提婆神庙供奉湿婆，据说建于1025至1050年间，维迪亚达拉为庆祝战胜加兹尼的马哈茂德而建；马哈茂德围攻卡林贾尔，最后以休战、互赠礼物收场。神庙高逾百英尺，塔尖由84座小塔堆叠而成，墙上雕像超过870尊。工匠不用灰浆：重达二十吨的石块靠榫卯相接，以自重相压。耆那教神庙集中在东群，与印度教庙并立。

1444年，昌德拉人已在1202年失去王国，退守马霍巴、卡林贾尔和阿贾伊加尔等堡垒，克久拉霍缩成一个小村庄。摩洛哥人伊本·白图泰14世纪游历印度，把这里叫作「卡贾拉」，记下被穆斯林毁损的神像，还有头发长如身躯、因苦修而面色发黄的瑜伽修行者，连穆斯林也来向他们求教。形制素朴的马坦盖什瓦拉神庙里，一根高二点五米的林伽立在直径7.6米的台座上；相传圣者马坦加在此化作林伽，降伏了爱神。1495年，西坎达尔·洛迪毁庙之举到了克久拉霍，损坏了几座神庙，其余因地处偏远而得以保全。此后丛林逐年漫过神庙，直到1819年英国军事测绘员富兰克林「重新发现」了这组建筑。

en:
Local legend says that anyone who tries to count the columns of the Great Mosque of Uqba goes blind. There are more than five hundred in the mosque, 414 of them in the prayer hall, in marble, granite and porphyry, taken from ancient sites such as Carthage, Sbeitla and Chemtou. The mosque stands in the north-east of the medina, founded with the city in 670 by the Arab general Uqba ibn Nafi and given its present form by the Aghlabids in the ninth century. Its square minaret, 31.5 metres tall and built about 836, is the oldest minaret still standing in the Islamic world and became a model in North Africa and al-Andalus. Around the mihrab are set 139 lustre tiles of the ninth century, and beside it stands a minbar of about 862 made of more than three hundred carved pieces of teak imported from India, the oldest pulpit preserved in Islam. Maliki scholars taught in the mosque. Local tradition holds that seven pilgrimages to it equal one pilgrimage to Mecca, which is why some call Kairouan the fourth holiest city of Islam. Non-Muslims, who had lived in the city in the early eleventh century, were later forbidden to settle there.

Near the mosque stand the other monuments of the holy city. The Mosque of the Three Doors, founded in 866, has three arched doorways under Kufic inscriptions. The Zawiya of Sidi Sahib holds the tomb of Abu Zama al-Balawi, a companion of the Prophet who, according to legend, kept three hairs of Muhammad's beard; the present buildings date from the seventeenth century. Outside the medina walls lie the Aghlabid basins, a settling basin and a great storage basin with a total capacity of 68,800 cubic metres. After the Banu Hilal conquest of 1057 brought the city's decline, the Great Mosque was repaired: the Hafsids added the domed Bab Lalla Rihana to its eastern wall in 1293, and under the Muradid beys the ceiling boards were repainted in 1618-19. In 1727 the Anglican priest Thomas Shaw wrote that it was thought the most beautiful and sacred building in the Berber lands, with an almost unbelievable number of granite columns.
zh:
当地传说，试图数清欧格白大清真寺柱子的人会瞎眼。寺中柱子有五百多根，礼拜殿里就有414根，有大理石、花岗岩和斑岩的，取自迦太基、斯贝特拉、舍姆图等古代遗址。清真寺在老城东北部，670年由阿拉伯将领欧格白·伊本·纳菲随建城一同奠基，9世纪阿格拉布王朝时定下现存面貌。方形宣礼塔高31.5米，约836年建成，是伊斯兰世界现存最古老的宣礼塔，后来成了北非和安达卢西亚宣礼塔的范本。米哈拉布四周镶着9世纪的139块金属光泽琉璃砖；旁边是约862年设置的讲经台，用三百多块雕花的印度柚木拼成，是伊斯兰世界保存下来的最古老的讲经台。马立克派学者在寺中讲学。当地相传，到这座寺朝拜七次，抵得上去一次麦加朝觐，所以有人称凯鲁万为伊斯兰教第四圣城。曾在11世纪初住在城里的非穆斯林，后来被禁止在城中定居。

离清真寺不远，立着凯鲁万圣城的其他建筑。三门清真寺建于866年，有三道拱门，门上是库法体铭文。西迪萨希卜扎维亚里有先知圣门弟子艾布·宰迈·巴拉维的陵墓，传说他珍藏了三根穆罕默德的胡须；现存建筑属17世纪。老城墙外是阿格拉布蓄水池，包括一座沉淀池和一座大蓄水池，总容量68800立方米。1057年希拉尔部落攻占此城，凯鲁万走向衰落，大寺后来得到修缮：哈夫斯王朝1293年在东墙添建带穹顶的拉拉·里哈娜门，穆拉德朝贝伊在1618至1619年重新彩绘了天花木板。1727年，英国教士托马斯·肖写道，人们认为它是柏柏尔之地最美、最神圣的建筑，寺中花岗岩柱子之多，几乎令人难以置信。

en:
Aït Benhaddou climbs a hill above the Ounila River in the High Atlas in terraces, and the upper floors of its tall tower-houses are decorated with geometric patterns in raw brick. It is a ksar, a fortified Berber village, on the former caravan route between the Sahara and Marrakesh, one of the main trans-Saharan trade routes. The road crossed the mountains at the Tizi n'Tichka pass, one of the few ways over the range, and the ksar kept a caravanserai for the caravans. The hill was fortified as early as the eleventh century, in Almoravid times, and local tradition says the village is named for Amghar Ben Haddou, the chief who ruled the place then. None of its present buildings is believed to be older than the seventeenth century, but they were raised by the same methods that had been used here for centuries.

Houses, mosque and granary are grouped inside a defensive wall with corner towers and a gate, and winding lanes and steps join the terraces. The lower storeys are rammed earth and the upper ones lighter adobe, to reduce the load on the walls. The material needs constant maintenance, and a ksar left to itself can begin to crumble within a few decades. At the top of the hill stand the remains of the agadir, a fortified collective granary where the inhabitants kept their possessions; below are the mosque, the caravanserai, a public square, the shrine of the marabout Sidi Ali ou Amer, and a Muslim cemetery and a Jewish cemetery. French sources call the stream at the foot of the hill the Oued Maleh, the Salt River: its water is too salty to drink.
zh:
阿伊特本哈杜城顺大阿特拉斯山中乌尼拉河畔的山坡层层而起，高大塔楼住宅的上层用生砖嵌出几何纹样。这是一座柏柏尔人的设防堡村（当地称克萨尔），位于从撒哈拉通往马拉喀什的旧商队路上，那是跨撒哈拉贸易的主要路线之一。这条路在提什卡山口翻越大山，那是阿特拉斯山脉少数几条通道之一，堡村里设有供商队投宿的客馆。早在11世纪穆拉比特王朝时期，这座山头已经设防；当地相传，堡村的名字来自当时统治此地的头人阿姆加尔·本·哈杜。现存建筑据信没有早于17世纪的，但用的仍是这里几百年传下来的工法。

民居、清真寺和粮仓全挤在一道护墙之内，墙角立着角楼，墙上开有城门，蜿蜒的小巷和台阶把各层台地连起来。底层是夯实的泥土，上层改用较轻的土坯，以减轻墙身承重。这种材料必须不断维护，堡村一旦无人照看，几十年内就会开始倾颓。山顶是阿加迪尔的遗迹，即设防的集体粮仓，居民把财物存在里面；山下有清真寺、客馆、一处公共广场、圣徒西迪·阿里·乌·阿米尔的墓祠，还有一片穆斯林墓地和一片犹太人墓地。法文资料把山脚下的河叫作马利赫干河，意即咸水河，河水太咸，不能饮用。

en:
Five missions stood in a chain down the San Antonio River, each a walled compound of stone and adobe with chapel, friary, granary, workshops and Indian quarters. The first and northernmost, San Antonio de Valero, later called the Alamo, was entrusted to the Franciscan Antonio de San Buenaventura y Olivares by Governor Martín de Alarcón on 1 May 1718. Alarcón wanted a waystation between the settlements on the Rio Grande and the isolated missions of East Texas, and he built a presidio a mile to the north. Valero soon filled with refugees from the closed East Texas missions, and in 1720 Antonio Margil founded San José five miles to the south. In 1731 three more missions were moved from East Texas to the river: Concepción, San Juan and Espada.

These were farms and fortresses at once. In 1745 a hundred mission Indians drove off three hundred Apaches who had surrounded the presidio, and walls later went up around Valero's Indian quarters, probably after the massacre at the San Sabá mission. By 1744 more than 300 converts lived at Valero, and it fed and clothed itself from 2,000 cattle and 1,300 sheep and fields of corn, beans and cotton. The friars built seven gravity-fed ditches, dams and at least one aqueduct, a 15-mile network that irrigated about 3,500 acres. Concepción's stone church was covered with brightly painted frescoes inside and out. Valero's church, begun in 1744, collapsed in the late 1750s; its replacement was meant to have three storeys, a dome and two bell towers, but only the first two levels were finished.

Folklore says that the Rose Window of San José, carved in 1775, was the work of a Spanish craftsman, Pedro Huizar, and was dedicated to his sweetheart Rosa, who died at sea on her way from Spain to join him. Valero was secularized in 1793 and San José's lands were given to its Indians the next year. In 1803 the Second Flying Company of San Carlos de Parras, from Álamo de Parras, moved into the empty Valero compound, and the place probably took the name Alamo from it.
zh:
圣安东尼奥布道区的五座布道站沿圣安东尼奥河排成一串，都是石墙土坯围起的院落，有礼拜堂、修院、粮仓、作坊和信徒居室。最北、最早的一座是圣安东尼奥·德·巴莱罗（后来通称阿拉莫），1718年5月1日由总督马丁·德·阿拉尔孔正式交给方济各会修士安东尼奥·德·圣布埃纳文图拉·伊·奥利瓦雷斯。阿拉尔孔要在里奥格兰德沿岸的定居点和偏远的东得克萨斯布道站之间设一个中转站，还在北面一英里处建了一座要塞。巴莱罗很快挤满了从关闭的东得克萨斯布道站逃来的难民，1720年安东尼奥·马吉尔便在南面五英里处另建圣何塞。1731年，又有三座布道站从东得克萨斯迁到河边：孔塞普西翁、圣胡安和埃斯帕达。

这里既是农庄，也是堡垒。1745年，一百名布道站信徒击退了包围要塞的三百名阿帕奇人；后来巴莱罗的信徒居住区外筑起围墙，大概是因为圣萨瓦布道站遭到屠杀。到1744年，巴莱罗住着三百多名信徒，靠两千头牛、一千三百只羊和玉米、豆子、棉花田自给衣食。修士们修了七条依靠重力引水的水渠、若干堤坝和至少一座渡槽，水渠网长15英里，灌溉约3500英亩土地。孔塞普西翁的石砌教堂里外都绘有鲜艳的壁画。巴莱罗的教堂1744年动工，1750年代末倒塌；重建的教堂原计划三层、带穹顶和两座钟塔，最后只建成了下面两层。

民间传说，圣何塞的玫瑰窗刻于1775年，出自西班牙工匠佩德罗·惠萨尔之手，献给他的恋人罗莎，她从西班牙赶来与他会合，在海上丧生。1793年巴莱罗被世俗化，次年圣何塞的土地交给了当地信徒。1803年，来自阿拉莫德帕拉斯的圣卡洛斯德帕拉斯第二飞行连进驻空置的巴莱罗院落，这个地方的名字「阿拉莫」大概就来自这支连队。

en:
Erdene Zuu was built from the stones of a dead capital: its halls went up beside the ruins of Karakorum, with stone taken from the old Mongol city. Abtai Sain Khan of the Khalkha had it built in 1585, after he met the Third Dalai Lama. The first three halls, the Gurvan Zuu, were finished the next year and are dedicated to the Buddha's youth, his teaching and his old age; they stand on high white marble platforms under tiled roofs. The Dalai Lama did not come to the consecration himself and sent a Sakya lama, and the Sakya tradition kept a long influence here. The protector of the house was Gombo-Gur, a form of Mahakala. The enclosure was meant to be ringed with 108 stupas, the number of beads on a Buddhist rosary, and the wall of stupas was finished in 1806.

For its first hundred years it was the family monastery of the Tusheet khans, and Zanabazar, Abtai's great-grandson and the first Jebtsundamba, often came to study and perform rituals. In 1688 Galdan's Dzungars invaded the Khalkha lands and came near three times without sacking the monastery, but it was left almost empty, and the few people nearby pulled down its wooden fence for firewood. When the Dzungars came again in 1731, the decisive battle with Qing troops was fought close by. A Mongol legend says that the statue of Gombo-Gur drove the Dzungar soldiers out of the main hall, the stone lions at the entrance roared, and the soldiers fled to the Orkhon and drowned; the Yongzheng Emperor is said to have granted the river a prince's title and 300 liang of silver a year. In 1745 a novice named Bunia tried several times to fly from the roof with a parachute-like device of his own invention; he was tried and severely punished, and died of it. Abbot Dagvadorj restored the monastery with Qing money in 1776, and in 1799 the Stupa of Awakening was built, with over a hundred thousand small images and the ashes of Abtai Khan sealed inside. At its height the enclosure held sixty-two halls.
zh:
额尔德尼昭（光显寺）是用一座死去的都城的石头建起来的：殿宇立在哈拉和林的废墟旁，用的是这座蒙古旧都的石料。喀尔喀的阿巴岱赛音汗在会见三世达赖喇嘛之后，于1585年建寺。最早的三座佛殿「固尔班召」次年落成，分别供奉少年、说法和晚年的佛陀，建在高大的白色大理石台基上，覆着瓦顶。达赖喇嘛没有亲自主持开光，派来一位萨迦派喇嘛，萨迦派的影响在这里延续了很久。寺院的护法是大黑天的一种化身贡布固尔。外围原计划环以108座佛塔，按佛珠之数定下，这道塔墙到1806年建成。

最初一百年，这里是土谢图汗的家庙。阿巴岱的曾孙、第一世哲布尊丹巴扎那巴扎尔常来此读经做法。1688年，噶尔丹的准噶尔人侵入喀尔喀，三度逼近寺院而没有洗劫，但寺里几乎没了人，附近的居民把木栅栏拆去当柴烧。1731年准噶尔人再度来犯，与清军的决战就在寺院附近。蒙古传说称，贡布固尔的神像把准噶尔兵赶出了大殿，门口的石狮发出吼声，敌兵逃向鄂尔浑河溺毙；据说雍正帝为此封这条河为郡王，每年赐银300两。1745年，一位名叫布尼亚的小喇嘛用自制的类似降落伞的装置多次从寺顶试飞，被审判并重罚，伤重而死。住持丹巴达尔扎1776年用清朝拨款重修寺院，1799年建成菩提塔，塔内封藏十万余尊小佛像和阿巴岱汗的骨灰。极盛之时，围墙之内共有六十二座殿堂。

en:
Ivan of Rila, the first Bulgarian hermit, lived in a cave in the Rila mountains with no possessions at all; legend says wild animals came freely to him and birds landed in his hands. His disciples founded the monastery in the valley of the Rilska river, and almost every tsar of the Second Bulgarian Empire made large donations to it. The present site is the work of Hreljo, a local lord with the title of protosebastos, who re-erected the monastery here in the first half of the fourteenth century. His fortress tower of the mid-1330s is topped by the small chapel of the Transfiguration. In 1378 Tsar Ivan Shishman issued the Rila charter, signed and sealed in gold, giving the monastery twenty villages with their lands. After the Ottomans came, the house was poorly fortified and often raided, yet in 1402 the government itself ordered the kadi of Kyustendil to confirm its old rights.

The monastery was destroyed in the middle of the fifteenth century and rebuilt at its end by three brothers from Dupnitsa, with donations from the Russian Orthodox Church, the Rossikon monastery on Mount Athos and Mara Brankovic, the Serbian despot's daughter and widow of Sultan Murad II. Through her influence the relics of Ivan, which had lain in Tarnovo since 1194, came back to Rila in 1469, and the monk Vladislav the Grammarian wrote of the translation. The monks also guard the Osenovitsa icon of the Virgin, which they hold to be miraculous; it is said to date from the twelfth century and to contain relics of 32 saints. On 16 August 1778 about thirty Albanian raiders burned the monastery for the third time, sparing only the tower and the church. The best-known treasure is the cross the monk Rafail carved from a single piece of wood 81 by 43 centimetres: 104 religious scenes and 650 miniature figures, cut with fine burins under magnifying lenses over at least twelve years, and completed in 1802, when the monk lost his sight. In 1819 eight hundred regular Ottoman troops surrounded the rebuilt monastery and looted it.
zh:
里拉修道院的创建者圣伊凡·里拉是保加利亚第一位隐修士，住在里拉山里的岩洞中，一无所有；相传野兽会主动走近他，飞鸟落在他手上。他的弟子在里尔斯卡河谷里创建了修道院，第二保加利亚帝国几乎每一位沙皇都向它捐赠巨款。现址是领有「首席显贵」头衔的地方领主赫雷廖（Hreljo）在14世纪上半叶重建的。他在1330年代中期筑起防御塔，塔顶是窄小的主显圣容堂。1378年，沙皇伊凡·希什曼颁下金印封缄的《里拉诏书》，把二十座村庄连同土地一并赐给修道院。奥斯曼人到来后，修道院防御薄弱，常遭劫掠，但1402年政府反而下令丘斯滕迪尔的卡迪确认它的旧有权利。

修道院在15世纪中期被毁，世纪末由杜普尼察的三兄弟重建，捐施来自俄罗斯正教会、阿索斯山的罗斯人修道院，以及塞尔维亚专制公之女、穆拉德二世的遗孀玛拉·布兰科维奇。靠她的影响，自1194年起存放在塔尔诺沃的圣伊凡遗骨于1469年迎回里拉，修士弗拉迪斯拉夫（Vladislav Gramatik）把这次迁移写成文书。寺里还供奉奥西诺维察圣母像，修士们相信它有神迹，据说画于12世纪，内嵌32位圣徒的遗物。1778年8月16日，约三十名阿尔巴尼亚人劫掠者第三次放火，只有塔和教堂幸存。寺中最有名的珍藏是修士拉法伊尔用一整块长81厘米、宽43厘米的木头雕成的十字架：104个宗教场景、650个微型人像，用细刻刀就着放大镜刻了至少十二年，1802年完工，这时修士失明了。1819年，八百名奥斯曼正规军包围并洗劫了重建后的修道院。

en:
The palace was built around a 66-centimetre Buddha of green stone, clothed in gold, which is called the Emerald Buddha although it is jade or jasper. According to one account of its discovery, in 1434 lightning struck a chedi at Chiang Rai, and the abbot later noticed that the stucco on the nose of the Buddha inside had flaked off, showing green stone beneath. In one version of the legend, when the king of Lan Na wanted it in Chiang Mai, the elephant carrying it three times insisted on going to Lampang instead, which was taken as a divine sign. The image later passed to Chiang Mai, Luang Prabang and Vientiane. In 1779 the Siamese general Chao Phraya Chakri looted Vientiane and took it home, then seized the throne himself and became Rama I.

Work on the palace began on 6 May 1782, when Rama I moved the capital across the Chao Phraya from Thonburi to Bangkok. The site had held a Chinese community, which he ordered to move south of the new city walls, in the area of Bangkok's Chinatown. Short of materials and money, the builders made the first palace entirely of wood, surrounded by a simple log palisade, and in June the king crossed the river to live in it. Masonry replaced the timber over the next few years. His men went upstream to Ayutthaya, destroyed by the Burmese in 1767, and dismantled forts, walls and the old royal palaces for bricks, though they took none from the temples; barges carried the bricks down to Bangkok.

The plan followed the royal palace at Ayutthaya. Walls, gates and forts divided the grounds into the Outer Court for government offices, the Middle Court for throne halls, and the Inner Court reserved for women. The royal chapel, Wat Phra Kaew, stood in the northeast corner and has no quarters for monks. In 1785 the Emerald Buddha was moved to it with great pomp, and Rama I held a full traditional coronation the same year. Rama II later extended the palace south to the wall of Wat Pho, enlarging it to 218,400 square metres.
zh:
曼谷大皇宫是围绕一尊66厘米高的绿色石佛建起的。佛像身披金饰，称玉佛，其实是软玉或碧玉。据一种说法，1434年清莱一座佛塔遭雷击，住持后来发现塔里那尊佛像鼻子上的灰泥剥落，露出了绿色的石头。有一种传说是，兰那国王想把它迎到清迈，驮着佛像的大象三次不肯前行，偏要走向南邦，人们便当作神意。此后玉佛先后到过清迈、琅勃拉邦和万象。1779年，暹罗将领昭披耶却克里洗劫万象，把玉佛带回，随后夺取王位，即拉玛一世。

大皇宫1782年5月6日动工，当时拉玛一世把都城从吞武里迁过湄南河，来到曼谷。宫址原是一个华人社区，他下令把这些人迁到新城墙外以南，即曼谷唐人街一带。缺料又缺钱，最初的宫殿全用木头，外围只立一圈木栅，6月国王渡河入住。几年里砖石陆续取代了木构。他的人马溯河而上，到1767年毁于缅甸之手的阿瑜陀耶，拆取堡垒、城墙和旧王宫的砖，但没有动寺庙里的砖，再用驳船顺流运到曼谷。

布局参照阿瑜陀耶的王宫。墙垣、宫门和堡垒把宫城分成三部分：外朝设官署，中朝安置王座殿，内廷只供女眷居住。东北角是王家寺院玉佛寺，寺中没有僧寮。1785年，玉佛被隆重迎入寺中，同年拉玛一世举行完整的传统加冕礼。拉玛二世后来把宫城向南扩到卧佛寺墙下，面积增至21.84万平方米。
